And they began therefore to devour the bulls, and behold: all the children of the earth began to tremble and to be terrified before them and to flee.</p>

### Chapter 87 <span class="chap-roman">(LXXXVII)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">Appearance of seven white men (the angels).</p>

<p class="v">1. And I saw them again beginning to strike one another, and to devour one another, and the earth began to cry out. 2. Then I lifted up my eyes again toward the sky, and I saw in a vision, and behold: there came out of the sky beings resembling white men, and four came out of that place, and three (others) with them. 8. Now these three who came out last took me by the hand, and lifted me up above the earthly generation, and carried me to a high place and showed me a tower raised (above) the earth, and all the hills were small (beside it). 4. And they said to me: "Remain here until you have seen everything that will happen to these elephants, these camels and these asses, and to the stars, and to the heifers, and to them all."</p>

### Chapter 88 <span class="chap-roman">(LXXXVIII)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">The good angels punish the fallen angels.</p>

<p class="v">1. And I saw one of the four who had come out first, seize the first star that had fallen from the sky, and bind it hand and foot, and cast it into an abyss, and this abyss was narrow and deep, steep and dark. 2. Then one of them drew the sword and gave it to the elephants, the camels and the asses, and they began to strike one another, and the whole earth trembled because of them. 3. And as I was watching (still) in a vision, behold, one of the four who had come out cast... from the sky, and all the great stars whose sexual member was like that of horses were gathered together and taken, and he (the angel) bound them all hand and foot, and cast them into an abyss of the earth.</p>

### Chapter 89 <span class="chap-roman">(LXXXIX)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">History of the world since Noah. — The seventy shepherds of Israel.</p>

<p class="v">1. Then one of the four went to that white bull and taught him a secret without his trembling. He had been born a bull, and he became a man, and he built for himself a great ship and dwelt in it; and three bulls dwelt with him in that ship, and it was covered over above them.</p>

<p class="v">2. I lifted up my eyes again toward the sky and I saw a high roof, and on that roof seven cataracts, and these cataracts flowed into an enclosure (in masses) of abundant waters. 3. And I saw again, and behold, springs opened up on the ground in that vast enclosure, and this water began to boil and to rise above the ground, and I saw (still) this enclosure until (finally) its whole surface was covered by the water. 4. And the water and the darkness and the mist increased above it. And I saw the height of this water; and this water rose above this enclosure, and it spread over the enclosure, and it remained upon the ground.</p>

<p class="v">5. All the bulls of this enclosure were gathered together, until I saw them submerged, swallowed up and annihilated in this water. 6. And the ship floated upon the water; but all the bulls and the elephants and the camels and the asses were swallowed up in the earth with all the four-footed beasts, and I could no longer see them; and they could not come out, and they were destroyed and submerged in the abyss.</p>

<p class="v">7. And again I saw in a vision, until these cataracts disappeared from this high roof, (until) the fissures of the earth were leveled and (until) other abysses opened. 8. And the water began to descend there, until the earth was uncovered, and the ship rested upon the earth, and the darkness withdrew, and there was light.</p>

<p class="v">9. Then the white bull who had become a man came out of that ship, and the three bulls with him; and one of the three bulls was white, he resembled that (first) bull, and one of them was red as blood; and one, black. And this white bull withdrew from them.</p>

<p class="v">10. And they began to beget wild beasts and birds. And there was a multitude of every kind: lions, leopards, dogs, wolves, hyenas, wild boars, foxes, squirrels, wild pigs, falcons, vultures, sparrowhawks, eagles and ravens. And in the midst of them was born a white bull. 11. And they began to bite one another; then the white bull, who had been born in their midst, begot a wild ass and a white bull with him, and the wild ass grew. 12. Then the bull that had been begotten by the (white bull) begot a black boar and a white sheep. And that one begot many boars, and the sheep begot twelve sheep.</p>

<p class="v">13. And when these twelve sheep had grown, they delivered one of them to some asses, and these asses in turn delivered this sheep to wolves, and the sheep grew up in the midst of the wolves. 14. Then the Lord brought the eleven sheep to dwell with her and to graze with her in the midst of the wolves. And they multiplied and became many flocks of sheep.</p>

<p class="v">15. Now the wolves began to fear them and to oppress them, even to causing their young to perish, and to casting their young into a great stream of water. And the sheep began to cry out concerning their young and to complain to their Lord.</p>

<p class="v">16. But one sheep who had escaped the wolves fled and went to the wild asses. And I saw the sheep lament, and cry out, and beseech their Lord with all their strength, until the Lord of the sheep came down at the voice of the sheep, from his high sanctuary, and came to them and made them graze.</p>

<p class="v">17. And he called the sheep that had fled from the midst of the wolves, and he spoke to it about the wolves, that it should charge them no longer to touch the sheep. 18. And the sheep went to the wolves at the Lord's command, and another sheep came to meet it and walked with it. And they went and entered both together into the assembly of the wolves, and they spoke to them and charged them not to touch the sheep from then on. 19. And from then on, I saw that the wolves oppressed the sheep more harshly and with all their strength, and the sheep cried out. 20. And their Lord came to the sheep, and he began to strike these wolves, and the wolves began to lament. But the sheep were silent and from then on they cried out no more.</p>

<p class="v">21. And I saw the sheep come out from among the wolves, and the eyes of the wolves were darkened. And these wolves went out pursuing the sheep with all their strength. 22. But the Lord of the sheep walked with them, leading them, and all his sheep followed him, and his face was resplendent, glorious and terrible to see. 23. And the wolves began to pursue these sheep, until they had overtaken them near a pool of water. 24. But this pool of water opened, and the water stood on one side and on the other before them and (before) their Lord who showed them the way and stood between them and the wolves. 25. And as these wolves no longer saw the sheep, they walked through the midst of this pool of water; and the wolves pursued the sheep, and they ran after them, these wolves, into this pool of water. 26. But when they saw the Lord of the sheep, they turned to flee before his face. But this pool of water closed again, and it suddenly resumed its natural position, and it filled with water, and it rose until it covered these wolves. 27. And I saw until all the wolves who were pursuing the sheep had perished, and were submerged.</p>

<p class="v">28. And the sheep withdrew from this water and went into a desert without water or grass. And they began to open their eyes and to see. And I saw the Lord of the sheep make them graze and give them water and grass, and this sheep walk and guide them.</p>

<p class="v">29. Now this sheep climbed to the summit of that (sic) high rock, and the Lord of the sheep sent it to them. 30. Then I saw the Lord of the sheep standing before them; and his aspect was grand, terrible and mighty, and all the sheep saw him and they feared before his face. 31. And all feared and trembled before him, and they cried out to that sheep (which was) with them, [the second sheep who was in their midst]: "We cannot stand before our Lord, nor look at him." 32. Now the sheep who guided them returned and climbed to the summit of that rock. And the eyes of the sheep began to grow dark, and they strayed out of the way that it had shown them; but this sheep did not know it.</p>

<p class="v">33. Then the Lord of the sheep grew angry with them with great anger, and this sheep learned (of the defection of the other sheep); it came down from the summit of the rock and it came to the sheep, and it found that most of them had darkened eyes and were straying. 34. And on seeing it, they feared and trembled before its face and they wanted to return to their folds. 35. But this sheep took with it other sheep, and it went to the sheep that had strayed, and it began to kill them, and the sheep feared before its face. And this sheep brought back the sheep that had strayed, and they returned to their folds.</p>

<p class="v">36. And I saw in this vision until this sheep became a man and built a house for the Lord of the sheep, and it brought all the sheep into this house.</p>

<p class="v">37. And I saw until this sheep, who had joined the sheep that guided the sheep, fell asleep. And I saw until all the great sheep had perished, and small ones rose up in their place, and they entered into a pasture, and they approached a stream of water. 38. Then the sheep that guided them, who had become a man, was separated from them and fell asleep; and all the sheep sought it and raised great cries over it. 39. And I saw until they ceased crying over this sheep.</p>

<p class="v">Then they crossed this stream of water, and there came (other) sheep who guided them in place of those who had fallen asleep after having guided them. 40. And I saw the sheep until they entered into a beautiful region and into a pleasant and splendid land. And I saw these sheep until they were satisfied, and this house was in their midst in the pleasant land. 41. Now sometimes their eyes opened and sometimes they were blinded, until another sheep arose and guided them. And it brought them all back, and their eyes opened. 42. Now the dogs, the foxes and the wild boars began to devour these sheep until the Lord of the sheep raised up [another sheep], a ram from among them, who guided them. 43. And this ram began to strike here and there these dogs, these foxes and these wild boars, until he had made them all perish.</p>

<p class="v">44. Then the eyes of this sheep opened, and it saw that the ram who was in the midst of the sheep had lost his honor and that he was beginning to strike these sheep and to trample them underfoot and to conduct himself unworthily. 45. Then the Lord of the sheep sent the sheep to another sheep and raised it to the rank of ram to lead the sheep in place of the ram who had lost his honor. 46. And it went to it, and it spoke to it in secret, and it raised up this ram and made it judge and shepherd of the sheep. Now during all these (events) the dogs oppressed the sheep. 47. But the first ram pursued this second ram, and this second ram arose and fled before it. And I saw until these dogs had struck down the first ram.</p>

<p class="v">48. Then this second ram arose and led the [small] sheep, and this ram begot many sheep, then fell asleep. And a small sheep became a ram in its place, and it was the judge and the leader of the sheep. 49. And these sheep grew and multiplied, and all these dogs, foxes and wild boars were afraid and fled far from it. But this ram struck and killed all the beasts, and these beasts no longer had any power in the midst of the sheep, and they no longer stole anything at all from them. 50. And this house became great and spacious, and it was built for these sheep, &lt;and&gt; a tower, high and great, was built upon the house for the Lord of the sheep. And this house was low, and the tower high and lofty. And the Lord of the sheep stood upon this tower, and a table laden (with offerings) was placed before him.</p>

<p class="v">51. Then I saw these sheep stray again and go in a multitude of ways, and abandon their house. And the Lord of the sheep called from among them some sheep and sent them to the sheep; but the sheep began to kill them. 52. Now one of them was saved and was not killed, and it leaped and it cried out concerning the sheep, and they wanted to kill it. But the Lord of the sheep saved it from the hands of the sheep and made it go up and sit beside me. 53. And he sent still more sheep to these sheep to announce (his word) to them and to weep over them. 54. And afterward I saw them abandon the house of the Lord and his tower. They strayed in everything and their eyes were blinded. And I saw the Lord of the sheep make a great slaughter of them in their pastures, until these sheep had (again) called down this slaughter and given up their place. 55. And he abandoned them to the lions, to the leopards, to the wolves, to the hyenas, to the foxes and to all the beasts, and these wild beasts began to tear these sheep apart. 56. Then I saw him abandon their house and their tower and deliver them all (the sheep) to the lions, that they might tear them apart and devour them, — [to all the beasts.]</p>

<p class="v">57. And I began to cry out with all my strength, and to call upon the Lord of the sheep, and I showed him that the sheep were being devoured by all the wild beasts. 58. But he was silent as he watched them, and he rejoiced that they were being eaten, devoured and carried off; and he abandoned them as prey to all the beasts.</p>

<p class="v">59. Then he called seventy shepherds and he delivered these sheep to them to make them graze. And he said to the shepherds and to their servants: "Let each of you henceforth make the sheep graze, and everything that I shall command you, do it. 60. I will deliver them to you in (a fixed) number and I will tell you which ones must perish, and those, make them perish." — And he delivered these sheep to them.</p>

<p class="v">61. Then he called another and said to him: "Consider and see everything that the shepherds do to these sheep, for they make more of them perish than I have commanded them. 62. And (for) every excess and loss that will be the work of the shepherds, write down how many they make perish by my order, and how many they make perish of their own accord. Write down to their account every loss of each shepherd. 63. Then read the number before me: how many they will have made perish, and how many had been delivered to them for destruction, so that this may be a testimony to me against them, so that I may know the whole conduct of the shepherds, that I may measure them and see what they do, whether or not they hold to the order that I have given them. 64. But let them not know it, and do not make it known to them and do not warn them, but write down every destruction of the shepherds, one by one, in its time, and bring it all up before me."</p>

<p class="v">65. And I saw until the time when these shepherds made (the sheep) graze, (each) in his time, and began to kill and to make perish more (sheep) than they had been ordered, and to deliver these sheep to the lions. 66. And the lions and the leopards ate and devoured most of the sheep, and the wild boars ate along with them, and they burned this tower and they overturned this house. 67. And I grieved very greatly over the tower, because this house of the sheep had been overturned, and from then on I could no longer see whether these sheep were entering into this house. 68. And the shepherds and their servants delivered these sheep to all the wild beasts that they might devour them, and (of) everything (that) each of them in his time had received in (a fixed) number, it was written (for) each of them by the other, in a book, how many of them he had made perish. 69. Now each one killed and made perish more than had been fixed for them, and I began to weep and to lament over these sheep.</p>

<p class="v">70. And I saw likewise in a vision the one who was writing, how he wrote down each (sheep) that had been destroyed by these shepherds day by day, and he brought and laid down his whole book, and he showed the Lord of the sheep everything that each of them had done and everything that each of them had taken away, and everything that he had delivered to destruction. 71. And the book was read in the presence of the Lord of the sheep, and he took the book from his hand, and he read it, sealed it and laid it down.</p>

<p class="v">72. And after this, I saw that the shepherds made (the sheep) graze for twelve hours, and behold: three of these sheep returned, and they arrived and entered, and they began to rebuild everything that had fallen of this house, but the wild boars prevented them, and they could not do it (this time). 73. Then they began again to build as before, and they raised up this tower which was called the high tower, and they began again to place a table before the tower, but all the bread that was (placed) there was defiled and unclean. 74. And over all this the eyes of these sheep were blinded, and they did not see, and their shepherds likewise, and he (the Lord of the sheep) delivered them for a greater destruction to their shepherds, who trampled the sheep underfoot and devoured them.</p>

<p class="v">75. And the Lord of the sheep kept silent until all the sheep were scattered in the desert and were mingled with them (the wild animals), and they (the shepherds) did not deliver them from the hand of the beasts. 76. And the one who had written the book brought it, showed it and read it to the Lord of the sheep, and he besought him on their behalf and addressed a request to him, showing him the whole conduct of the shepherds, and bearing witness before him against all the shepherds. 77. And taking his book, he laid it down beside him (the Lord of the sheep) and he went out.</p>
### Chapter 90 <span class="chap-roman">(XC)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">Continuation of the history of the seventy shepherds and of the last times of Israel. — The messianic times and the final judgment.</p>

<p class="v">1. And I saw until the time when thirty-five shepherds had thus fed (the sheep), and each of them fulfilled (his charge) in his time, as the first ones had, and others received them into their hands, that they might feed them in their time, each shepherd in his time.</p>

<p class="v">2. After this, in a vision, I saw all the birds of heaven coming: the eagles, the vultures, the hawks, and the ravens; and the eagles led all the birds, and they began to devour those sheep and to put out their eyes and to devour their flesh. 3. And the sheep cried out because their flesh was being devoured by the birds. And I looked, and I lamented in my sleep over the shepherd who was feeding the sheep.</p>

<p class="v">4. And I saw until those sheep had been devoured by the dogs, by the eagles, and by the hawks, who left them absolutely no flesh, nor skin, nor sinew, until they had nothing left but bones, and their bones fell upon the earth, and the sheep grew fewer.</p>

<p class="v">5. And I saw until the time when twenty-three shepherds had fed (the sheep) and had each, in his time, completed fifty-eight periods. 6. And behold: lambs were born of those white sheep, and they began to open their eyes and to see, and to bleat unto the sheep. 7. But the sheep did not bleat back to them and did not give ear to their word, but they were utterly deaf, and their eyes were blinded exceedingly and more and more.</p>

<p class="v">8. And I saw in vision the ravens swoop down upon those lambs and seize one of those lambs, and they tore the sheep to pieces and devoured them.</p>

<p class="v">9. And I saw until horns grew upon those lambs, and the ravens made their horns fall off. And I saw until a great horn grew on one of those sheep, and their eyes were opened. 10. And it (the sheep) saw them, and their eyes were opened; and it cried out to the sheep, and the rams saw it and all ran to it. 11. And despite this, all those eagles, those vultures, those ravens, and those hawks still ravaged the sheep, swooping down upon them and devouring them. And the sheep kept silent, and the rams lamented and cried out.</p>

<p class="v">12. Then those ravens joined battle and fought with it (the sheep), and they wanted to take away its horn, but they could not. 13. And I watched them until the shepherds, the eagles, the vultures, and the hawks came upon the scene; they called to the ravens to break that ram's horn, and they fought and struggled with him, and he fought with them, and he cried out for someone to come to his aid.</p>

<p class="v">14. And I saw the man come who had written down the names of the shepherds and who had brought (the book) before the Lord of the sheep, and he helped him and saved him, and showed him everything. He came down to the aid of that ram. 15. And I saw the Lord of the sheep come to it in fury, and all who saw him fled, and they all fell into darkness (as they fled) from before his face.</p>

<p class="v">16. All the eagles, vultures, ravens, and hawks assembled, and they brought with them all the wild sheep, and they all came together and helped one another to break that ram's horn to pieces. 17. And I saw that man who had written the book at the Lord's command open the book of the destruction that those last twelve shepherds had wrought, and show before the Lord of the sheep that they had destroyed far more than their predecessors. 18. And I saw until the Lord of the sheep came to them, and he took in his hand the rod of his wrath, and he struck the earth, and the earth split open, and all the beasts and the birds of heaven fell away from those sheep and were swallowed up in the earth, which closed over them.</p>

<p class="v">19. And I saw until a great sword was given to the sheep, and the sheep went forth against all the wild beasts to kill them, and all the beasts and the birds of heaven fled from before their face.</p>

<p class="v">20. And I saw until a throne was set up on the pleasant land, and the Lord of the sheep sat upon it, and he (an angel) took all the sealed books and opened those books before the Lord of the sheep. 21. And the Lord called those first seven white men, and commanded that there be brought before him, beginning with the first star that went before them, those stars whose sexual member was like the sexual member of horses [and the first star that fell first]. And they brought them all before him. 22. Then he spoke to that man who was writing before him, one of the seven white men, and he said to him: "Take these seventy shepherds, to whom I had delivered the sheep, and who, after receiving them, slaughtered far more than I had commanded them." 23. And behold: I saw them all bound in chains, and they all stood before him.</p>

<p class="v">24. And the judgment fell first upon the stars, and they were judged, and they were found sinners, and they went away into the place of punishment, and they were cast into a deep place, full of burning fire and filled with a pillar of fire. 25. Then those seventy shepherds were judged and were found sinners, and they too were cast into that abyss of fire. 26. And I saw at that time a similar pit, full of fire, open in the midst of the earth. And those blinded sheep were brought, and they were all judged and found sinners, and cast into that abyss of fire, and they burned. Now this pit was to the right of that house. 27. And I saw those sheep burning, and their bones (themselves) burned.</p>

<p class="v">28. And I rose up to see, until he folded up that old house, and all its pillars were carried away; and all the beams as well as the ornaments of that house were folded up with them, and they were carried away and cast into a place to the right of the earth. 29. And I saw until the Lord of the sheep brought a new house, greater and higher than the first, and set it up in the place of the first, which had been folded up. And all its pillars were new, and its ornaments new; and it was greater than the first old (house) which he had carried away, and all the sheep were within it.</p>

<p class="v">30. And I saw all the sheep that remained, and all the animals that were on the earth, and all the birds of heaven, prostrate themselves, worship those sheep, entreat them, and obey their every word. 31. Then those three who were clothed in white took me by the hand — they were the ones who had first taken me up — and with the hand of that ram holding me, they made me go up and made me sit in the midst of the sheep, before the judgment took place. 32. And those sheep were all white, and their fleece was full and pure. 33. And all those that had perished and had been scattered, and all the wild beasts and all the birds of heaven, gathered together in that house, and the Lord of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to his house.</p>

<p class="v">34. And I saw until they (the sheep) laid down the sword that had been given to the sheep, and they brought it back into the house, and it was sealed in the presence of the Lord; and all the sheep were called into that house, but it could not hold them. 35. And the eyes of them all were opened, and they saw well, and there was not one among them that did not see. 86. And I saw that this house was great and spacious and utterly full.</p>

<p class="v">37. And I saw that a white bull was born, and its horns were great, and all the wild beasts and all the birds of heaven feared it and entreated it at all times. 38. And I saw until all their kinds were changed, and they all became white bulls, and the first among them became a buffalo [and this buffalo was a great animal], and it had upon its head great black horns, and the Lord of the sheep rejoiced over it and over all the bulls. 39. And I was lying in the midst of them, and I awoke after having seen everything.</p>

<p class="v">40. And such is the vision that I saw while I was lying down; then I awoke, and I blessed the Lord of justice, and I gave him glory. 41. After this I shed abundant tears, and my tears did not stop until I could bear it no longer: when I looked, they flowed over what I saw, for all shall come and shall be fulfilled; and all the deeds of men were shown to me, one after another. 42. And that night I remembered my first dream, and I wept and was troubled about it because I had seen this vision.</p>

<p class="v">PART FIVE</p>

<p class="v">BOOK OF EXHORTATION AND OF THE CURSE</p>

<p class="v">(Chap. XCI-CV)</p>

<p class="v">______</p>

### Chapter 91 <span class="chap-roman">(XCI)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">Enoch's exhortations to his children. — Predictions concerning the punishment of sinners.</p>

<p class="v">1. Now therefore, my son Methuselah, summon to me your brothers, gather around me all the children of your mother, for a voice calls me and a spirit has been poured out upon me, that I may show you all that shall befall you unto eternity.</p>

<p class="v">2. And thereupon Methuselah went to summon all his brothers to him (Enoch), and he gathered his kinsfolk. 3. And he (Enoch) spoke to all the children of justice and said: Hear, children of Enoch, all the words of your father, and give good ear to the voice of my mouth, for it is you whom I exhort, and I say to you: Beloved, love truth and walk in it. 4. And do not draw near to truth with a double heart, do not associate with those who have a double heart, but walk in justice, O my children: it will itself lead you in the good ways, and justice will be your companion. 5. For, I see it, the state of violence grows greater upon the earth, and so a great punishment shall be accomplished upon the earth; all injustice shall be consumed and shall be cut off at its roots, and its whole edifice shall perish. 6. Injustice shall begin again to be accomplished upon the earth, and it shall contain twice as many works of injustice, oppression, and sin! 7. But when, in every work, injustice, sin, blasphemy, and violence have grown, when perversity, crime, and impurity have grown, a great punishment shall come from heaven upon all this, and the holy Lord shall come forth in fury with a scourge to execute judgment upon the earth. 8. In those days, violence shall be cut off at its root, and the roots of injustice as well as (those of) deceit, and they shall be destroyed under the heavens. 9. And all the idols of the heathen and (their) temple shall be given over to the burning fire. They shall be driven out from all the earth and cast into the torment of fire, and they shall be destroyed by wrath and by a terrible torment, which shall be eternal. 10. Then the righteous shall arise from their sleep, and wisdom also shall arise and be given to them.</p>

<p class="v">[11. Then the roots of injustice shall be cut off, and sinners shall perish by the sword; the impious shall be cut off in every place, and those who devise violence and those who commit blasphemy shall perish by the sword.]</p>

<p class="v">18. And now I will tell you, O my children, and show you the ways of justice and those of violence; and I will show you again how you shall know what must come to pass.</p>

<p class="v">19. And now listen to me, my children, and walk in the paths of justice, and do not go in the paths of violence, for all those who walk in the way of injustice shall perish forever.</p>

### Chapter 92 <span class="chap-roman">(XCII)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">Reward of the righteous. Destruction of sinners.</p>

<p class="v">1. Writing composed by Enoch. Enoch therefore wrote all this doctrine of wisdom — the object of the praise of all men and the judge of all the earth — for all my children who dwell upon the earth and for the future generations who shall do good and peace. 2. Let not your spirit be saddened concerning the times, for the Great and the Holy One has appointed days for everything. 3. And the righteous one shall awaken from his sleep; he shall rise up and advance in the ways of justice, and all his ways and his course shall be in eternal virtue and clemency. 4. He (the Great and the Holy One) will be gracious to the righteous one, he will give him eternal justice, and he will give him power, and he (the righteous one) shall be in virtue and in justice, and he shall walk in an eternal light. 5. But sin shall be lost in darkness forever; it shall therefore appear no more from this day unto eternity.</p>

### Chapter 93 <span class="chap-roman">(XCIII)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">Apocalypse of the weeks. Enoch's predictions concerning the ten weeks that shall pass from his birth until the end of the times.</p>

<p class="v">1. [Then Enoch taught, and he began to speak according to the books. 2. And Enoch said: Concerning the children of justice, concerning the elect of the world, and concerning the plant of equity, here is what I will tell you and make known to you, my children, I, Enoch, according as it has been revealed to me by a vision of the heavens, and as I have learned it by the voice of the holy angels, and as I have understood it by the tablets of heaven. 3. Enoch therefore began to speak according to the writings, and said: I, the seventh, was born in the first week, while right and justice still endured. 4. And after me, in the second, a great evil shall arise; bad faith shall abound, and in it (this week) shall take place the first consummation, and then a man shall be saved. And after that (week) is finished, injustice shall grow, and he (God) will make a law for sinners. 5. And then, in the third week, toward its end, a man shall be chosen as a plant of righteous judgment, and after that he shall grow into a plant of justice 10 for eternity. 6. And then, in the fourth week, at its end, the visions of the holy and the righteous shall appear, and a law for generation after generation and an enclosure shall be prepared for them. 7. And then, in the fifth week, at its end, a house of glory and dominion shall be built for eternity. 8. And then, in the sixth week, those who live in it shall all be blinded, and the heart of all of them shall fall into impiety, far from wisdom, and then a man shall go up (to heaven), and at the end of that (week) the house of dominion shall be consumed by fire, and then the whole race of mighty root shall be scattered. 9. And then, in the seventh week, a perverse generation shall arise; numerous shall be its works, but all its works (shall be) abomination. 10. And at the end of that (week), the righteous elect of the plant of eternal justice shall be chosen, that there may be given to them sevenfold the knowledge of all his (God's) creation.</p>

<p class="v">[11. For who among the children of men can hear the voice of the Holy One without being troubled by it, and who can think his thought, and who can contemplate all the works of heaven? 12. Who is he that can see heaven, and who is he that can know the work of heaven? And how would he see a soul or a spirit, and could he speak of it, or go up and see all their extremities, and understand them or act as they do. 13. And who among the children of men can understand what is the breadth and the length of the earth, and to whom have all (their) measures been shown? 14. Or is there a man who can know the length of heaven as well as its height, upon what (foundation) it is established, how great is the number of the stars, and where all the lights rest? ]</p>

<p class="v">XCI, 12-17 (see p. 240, note)</p>

<p class="v">[12. And then there shall be another week, the eighth; it shall be that of justice; a sword shall be given to it that judgment and justice may be executed upon the oppressors, and sinners shall be delivered into the hands of the righteous. 13. And toward its end (of the eighth week), they (the righteous) shall acquire houses because of their justice; and a house shall be built for the great King, in eternal splendor. 14. And after that, in the ninth week, the judgment of justice shall be revealed to the whole universe, and all the works of the impious shall vanish from all the earth, and the world shall be inscribed for perdition, and all men shall see the ways of good. 15. And after that, in the tenth week, in (its) seventh part, shall take place the great eternal judgment, in which he shall execute vengeance in the midst of the angels. 16. And the first heaven shall vanish and pass away, and a new heaven shall appear, and all the powers of the heavens shall shine eternally sevenfold brighter. 17. And after that (shall come) numerous weeks which shall pass innumerable, eternal, in goodness and in justice, and from then on sin shall no more be named unto eternity.]</p>

### Chapter 94 <span class="chap-roman">(XCIV)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">Exhortations to the righteous. Curses against the impious.</p>

<p class="v">1. Now therefore I say to you, my children, love justice and walk in it, for the ways of justice are worthy to be followed, but the ways of iniquity shall pass away and vanish suddenly. 2. To certain men of the (future) generation shall be revealed the ways of violence and of death, and they shall keep away from them and shall not follow them. 3. And now to you, the righteous, I say: do not go in an evil way, nor in the ways of death; and do not draw near them, lest you perish. 4. But seek and choose for yourselves justice and an excellent life, and walk in the paths of peace, that you may live and be happy. 5. And keep my word in the thought of your heart, and let it not be erased from your heart; for I know that sinners will tempt men to change wisdom into evil, no place will be found for it (wisdom), and no trial shall diminish.</p>

<p class="v">6. Woe to those who build iniquity and oppression and lay their foundation on fraud, for they shall be overthrown suddenly, and there shall be no peace for them. 7. Woe to those who build their houses through sin, for they shall be torn from all their foundations, and they shall fall by the sword, and those who possess gold and silver shall perish suddenly in the judgment.</p>

<p class="v">8. Woe to you, the rich, because you trust in your riches; you shall be deprived of them, because you did not remember the Most High in the days of your riches. 9. You have committed blasphemy and iniquity; you are ripe for the day of the shedding of blood, for the day of darkness, and for the day of the great judgment.</p>

<p class="v">10. Thus I say to you and announce to you that he who created you will overthrow you, and there shall be no pity upon your ruin, and your creator will rejoice in your destruction. 11. And your righteous ones in those days shall be a reproach to sinners and to the impious.</p>

### Chapter 95 <span class="chap-roman">(XCV)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">Enoch's sorrow. — Further curses.</p>

<p class="v">1. Who will grant my eyes to become a cloud of water? And I will weep over you, and I will pour out my tears like a cloud of water, and I will relieve the sorrow of my heart.</p>

<p class="v">2. Who gave you leave to do hatred and evil? Therefore judgment shall overtake you, you sinners.</p>

<p class="v">3. Do not fear sinners, O righteous ones, for the Sovereign of the universe will deliver them once more into your hands, that you may render judgment against them, as it pleases you.</p>

<p class="v">4. Woe to you, who cast anathemas that cannot be broken! The remedy is far from you because of your sin!</p>

<p class="v">5. Woe to you, who repay evil to your neighbor, for you shall receive according to your works!</p>

<p class="v">6. Woe to you, witnesses of falsehood, and to those who weigh out injustice, for you shall perish suddenly!</p>

<p class="v">7. Woe to you, sinners, because you persecute the righteous, for you yourselves shall be delivered up and persecuted by injustice, and its yoke shall weigh heavily upon you!</p>

### Chapter 96 <span class="chap-roman">(XCVI)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">Grounds for hope for the righteous, for fear for sinners.</p>

<p class="v">1. Have confidence, O righteous ones, for sinners shall soon be annihilated before you, and you shall have over them whatever power you desire. 2. And on the day of the affliction of sinners, your little ones shall rise up and soar like eagles, your nest shall be higher than (that of) the vulture; like the squirrel, you shall climb and penetrate forever into the caverns of the earth and into the clefts of the rocks, far from the face of the wicked, who shall groan and weep over you like sirens. 3. Fear not, therefore, you who suffer, for there shall be a remedy for you, a clear light shall shine for you, and from heaven you shall hear the voice of rest.</p>

<p class="v">4. Woe to you, sinners, because your riches give you the appearance of the righteous, but your heart convicts you that you are sinners, and this word shall testify against you, to recall your iniquities. 5. Woe to you who devour the flower of the wheat and drink the strength of the principle of the spring, and who in your strength trample the humble underfoot. 6. Woe to you who drink water at all times, for suddenly you shall receive your reward: you shall be consumed and dried up, because you have forsaken the spring of life.</p>

<p class="v">7. Woe to you who commit injustice, fraud, and blasphemy: against you there shall be a memorial for evil. 8. Woe to you, the mighty, who by violence oppress the righteous, for the day of your destruction is coming; in those days, at the time of your punishment, there shall be for the righteous many good days.</p>

### Chapter 97 <span class="chap-roman">(XCVII)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">Woe to those who commit injustice and who possess ill-gotten riches.</p>

<p class="v">1. Have confidence, you righteous, because sinners shall be given over to shame, and they shall be annihilated on the day of iniquity. 2. You shall know, (sinners,) that the Most High remembers your destruction, and that the angels of heaven rejoice at your destruction. 3. What will you do, sinners, and where will you flee on that day of judgment, when you hear the sound of the prayer of the righteous? 4. You shall be like those against whom this word shall testify: "You were the accomplices of sinners." 5. And in those days the prayer of the righteous shall reach the Lord, and for you the days of your judgment shall come. 6. All your words of injustice shall be read before the Great and the Holy One, your face shall be covered with confusion, and every work founded on injustice shall be rejected. 7. Woe to you, sinners, who are in the midst of the sea or on dry land: the memory of them shall be fatal to you. 8. Woe to you who possess silver and gold (acquired) through injustice! You say: "We are rich, we have fortune, and we possess all that we have desired. 9. And now let us carry out our plans, for we have accumulated money, our treasuries are full of it like water, and numerous are the laborers of our houses." 10. Like water also your illusions shall flow away, for your riches shall not remain with you; but suddenly they shall fly away far from you, because it was through injustice that you acquired them all, and you yourselves shall be delivered up to a great curse.</p>

### Chapter 98 <span class="chap-roman">(XCVIII)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">Evil deeds are known to God: woe to fools and to sinners.</p>

<p class="v">Evil deeds are known to God: woe to fools and to sinners. 1. And now, I, I swear to you, wise and foolish, that you shall see many things upon the earth. 2. For you, men, you put on yourselves more ornaments than a woman and more colors than a virgin; in empire, in greatness and in power, and in silver and gold, purple, honors, and fine foods, they pour out like water. 3. Because they have neither doctrine nor wisdom, for this reason they shall be lost together with their goods and with all their splendor and their honors; and in shame, in slaughter, and in great poverty their spirit shall be cast into a furnace of fire.</p>

<p class="v">4. I swear to you, sinners, that just as a mountain has (never) become and will never become a servant, nor a hill a maidservant, so sin was not sent upon the earth; but men made it of themselves, and they who have committed it shall be under a great curse. 5. And barrenness was not given (by nature) to woman, but it is because of the work of her hands that she dies without children. 6. I swear to you, sinners, by the Holy One and the Great One, that all your evil work is manifest in the heavens, and that there is no work of violence in you that is hidden and secret. 7. And do not think in your spirit and do not say in your heart that you did not know and that you did not see that every sin is written every day in heaven in the presence of the Most High. 8. From now on you shall know that all the violence that you commit is written down every day until the day of your judgment.</p>

<p class="v">9. Woe to you, fools, for you shall be lost through your folly; you have done evil against the wise, and happiness shall not come to you. 10. And now, know that you are ready for the day of ruin, and hope not at all to live, O sinners; but you shall pass away and die, for you know no ransom, for you are ready for the day of the great judgment and for the day of affliction and of the great misery (reserved) for your spirit.</p>

<p class="v">11. Woe to you, thick of heart, who do evil and eat blood: from where do you eat so well, and drink, and fill yourselves? From all the good things that the Most High Lord has accumulated upon the earth; therefore you shall have no peace.</p>

<p class="v">12. Woe to you who cherish iniquity; why do you promise yourselves happiness? Know that you shall be delivered into the hands of the righteous: they shall cut off your head and put you to death, and they shall have no pity on you.</p>

<p class="v">13. Woe to you who rejoice in the affliction of the righteous, for no grave shall be dug for you.</p>

<p class="v">14. Woe to you who declare the word of the righteous to be vain, for there is no hope of life for you.</p>

<p class="v">15. Woe to you who write words of falsehood and words of the impious, for they write their lies so that they may be listened to and the rest forgotten: they shall have no peace at all, but they shall die a sudden death.</p>

### Chapter 99 <span class="chap-roman">(XCIX)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">Woe to the impious, to the transgressors of the law, to idolaters, etc. Happiness of those who walk in the way of justice.</p>

<p class="v">1. Woe to those who commit impieties and who praise and glorify the word of falsehood: you shall be destroyed, and you shall not have a life of happiness.</p>

<p class="v">2. Woe to those who change the words of truth and transgress the eternal law, and make themselves, what they were not, sinners: upon the earth they shall be trodden underfoot.</p>

<p class="v">3. In those days prepare yourselves, O righteous, to recall your prayers and to set them as witnesses before the angels, that they may remind the Most High of the sin of sinners.</p>

<p class="v">4. In those days, the nations shall be stirred up, and the families of the nations shall rise up on the day of destruction. 5. And in those days those who are reduced to misery shall go forth and tear their children apart and cast them away; and their sons shall fall far from them, and they shall cast away their nursing children, and they shall not return to them, and they shall have no pity on their beloved ones.</p>

<p class="v">6. Again, I swear to you, sinners, that sin is ripe for the day when blood shall not cease (to flow). 7. And those who worship stone, and those who make images of gold and silver, of wood and clay, and those who worship evil spirits and demons and every kind of idol, without discernment, no help shall come to them from these. 8. They fall into impiety because of the folly of their heart, and their eyes are darkened by the faintheartedness of their heart and by the vision of their dreams. 9. Through these they commit impiety and they tremble, for they have done all their works in falsehood and have worshiped stone; therefore they shall be lost in the twinkling of an eye.</p>

<p class="v">10. And in those days, happy are all those who receive the word of wisdom and understand it, who practice the ways of the Most High and walk in the way of his justice, and (who) do not commit impiety with the impious, for they shall be saved.</p>

<p class="v">11. Woe to you who extend evil even to your kin, for you shall be put to death in Sheol.</p>

<p class="v">12. Woe to you who use a measure of sin and fraud and who pour out bitterness upon the earth, for because of this they shall be consumed.</p>

<p class="v">13. Woe to you who build your houses by the labor of others: all their materials are bricks and stones of sin; I tell you, you shall have no peace at all.</p>

<p class="v">14. Woe to those who repudiate the measure and the eternal inheritance of their fathers, and whose soul clings to idols, for there shall be no rest for them.</p>

<p class="v">15. Woe to those who commit injustice and lend their aid to violence, and who slaughter their companions until the day of the great judgment. 16. For he shall cast your glory to the ground, and he shall put evil into your hearts, and he shall stir up his wrath, and his spirit shall destroy you all by the sword, and all the righteous and the holy shall remember your sin.</p>

### Chapter 100 <span class="chap-roman">(C)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">Sinners shall exterminate one another. On the day of the great judgment, the angels shall watch over the righteous, while sinners shall go to burn in a furnace of fire.</p>

<p class="v">1. And in those days, in a single place, fathers shall be struck down together with their sons, and brothers shall fall together with their kin in death, until their blood flows like a river. 2. For man shall not withhold his hand from killing his son and the son of his son, and the sinner shall not withhold his hand from (killing) his beloved brother: from dawn until sunset they shall slaughter one another. 3. And the horse shall advance until its breast (is bathed) in the blood of sinners, and the chariot until its upper part is submerged.</p>

<p class="v">4. And in those days, the angels shall go down to a hidden place; they shall gather into a single spot all those who brought sin down (upon the earth); and on that day of judgment, the Most High shall rise up to render the great judgment in the midst of sinners. 5. And he shall give guardians from among the holy angels to all the righteous and the holy; they shall keep them as the apple of the eye until he consumes all evil and all sin; and if the righteous sleep a long sleep, they shall have nothing to fear.</p>

<p class="v">6. And wise men shall see the truth, and the children of the earth shall understand all the words of this book, and they shall recognize that their riches cannot save them in the ruin of their sin.</p>

<p class="v">7. Woe to you, sinners, if you afflict the righteous on the day of terrible anguish, and (if) you burn them in fire: you shall receive the reward of your works.</p>

<p class="v">8. Woe to you, thick of heart, who stay awake to devise evil: terror shall seize you, and no one shall come to your aid.</p>

<p class="v">9. Woe to you, sinners, for the word of your mouth and for the work of your hands which your impiety has done: in a furnace of flame you shall burn,</p>

<p class="v">10. And now know that your deeds shall be sought out by the angels in heaven, and by the sun, by the moon, and by the stars, because of your sin, for on earth you render judgment against the righteous. 11. And every cloud and mist and dew and rain shall testify against you, for they shall all refuse to fall upon you, and they shall be mindful of your sins. 12. Offer, then, gifts to the rain, that it may not refuse to fall upon you, and to the dew, if it will accept from you gold and silver, that it may fall. 13. When the frost and the snow shall descend upon you, their cold and all the whirlwinds of snow and all their torments, in those days you shall not be able to stand before them.</p>

### Chapter 101 <span class="chap-roman">(CI)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">Exhortation to the fear of the Almighty: all nature trembles before him, except sinners.</p>

<p class="v">1. Children of heaven, consider heaven and all the work of the Most High, and tremble before him, and do not do evil in his presence. 2. If he shuts the window of heaven and keeps the rain and the dew from falling upon the earth because of you, what will you do? 3. And if he sends his wrath against you because of all your works, there will be no entreating him, for you utter against his justice proud and shameless words; therefore you shall have no peace.</p>

<p class="v">4. And do you not see the pilots of ships, how their ships are tossed by the waves and shaken by the winds, and fall into danger? 5. And because of this, they fear that all their fine riches may go into the sea with them, and they think nothing good in their heart; (they think) that the sea will devour them and that they will perish in it. 6. Is not the whole sea, and all its waters, and all its motion, the work of the Most High? And has he not set his seal upon all its action (of the sea), and has he not chained it entirely within the sand? 7. At his rebuke it trembles and dries up, and all its fish perish along with all that it contains, and you, sinners, who are upon the earth, you do not fear him at all! 8. Has he not made heaven and earth and all that they contain? And who has given knowledge and wisdom to all those who move upon the earth and in the sea? 9. Do not the pilots of ships fear the sea, and yet sinners do not fear the Most High!</p>

### Chapter 102 <span class="chap-roman">(CII)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">Terror of the last days. The apparent misfortune of the righteous.</p>

<p class="v">1. In those days, if he casts upon you a terrible fire, where will you flee, and how will you save yourselves? And if he hurls his word against you, will you not be dismayed and will you not tremble? 2. And all the luminaries shall be seized with great fear, and the whole earth shall be dismayed, shall tremble, and shall be troubled. 3. And all the angels shall carry out their mission, and they shall wish to hide themselves before the great glory, and the children of the earth shall tremble and be troubled; but you, sinners, you shall be eternally cursed, and there shall be no peace for you.</p>

<p class="v">4. Fear not, you souls of the righteous, and have confidence, you who died in justice. 5. And do not be saddened because your soul has gone down into Sheol in sorrow, and because your flesh did not receive, during your life, according to your virtue; but rather (it went down into Sheol) on a day when you had become (as it were) sinners, and on the day of the curse and of punishment. 6. When you die, sinners say of you: "As we have died, the righteous have died, and what profit have they gained from their works? 7. Behold, like us they have died in sorrow and in darkness, and what do they have more than we? From now on we are equal. 8. And what will they carry away, and what will they see in eternity? For behold, they too have died, and from now on they shall never see the light again."</p>

<p class="v">9. I say to you: You, sinners, it is enough for you to eat and drink, to plunder and to sin, to strip men bare and acquire riches, and to see happy days. 10. Have you not seen what the end of the righteous has been? No violence was found in them until their death. 11. And yet they perished, and they were as though they had never been, and their souls went down into Sheol in affliction.</p>

### Chapter 103 <span class="chap-roman">(CIII)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">Solution of the apparent riddle that is the life of the righteous. Further objections of sinners.</p>

<p class="v">1. But now I swear to you, righteous ones, by the glory of the Great One, of the Glorious One, and of the Mighty One in dominion, and by his greatness I swear to you: 2. I myself know the mystery, I have read it upon the tablets of heaven, and I have seen the writing of the holy ones, and I have found it written and engraved concerning them (the righteous) 3. that all good and joy and honor has been prepared and written down for the souls of those who died in justice, and that many good things shall be given to you as a reward for your labors, and that your lot shall be better than that of the living. 4. And your souls, you who died in justice, shall live and rejoice and exult, and they shall not perish, your souls, and their memory shall not (pass away) from before the face of the Great One throughout all the generations of the world; from now on you shall no longer fear their dishonor.</p>

<p class="v">5. Woe to you who die, sinners, if you die in the wealth of your sins, and those who resemble you say of you: "Happy are these sinners! They have seen all their days. 6. And now they have died in happiness and in riches, and they did not see affliction and murder during their life; they died in glory, and no judgment was rendered against them during their life."</p>

<p class="v">7. You shall know that your souls will be made to go down into Sheol; there they shall be wretched, and their affliction shall be great. 8. And your soul shall enter into darkness and into bonds and into a burning flame, there where the great punishment shall take place, and the great punishment shall last throughout all the generations of the world; woe to you, for you shall have no peace.</p>

<p class="v">9. Do not say of the righteous and the good who are alive: "In the days of their life they labored much, and they saw every affliction, they experienced numerous evils, and they were consumed and diminished, and their soul grew small. 10. They are lost, and they have found no one to help them, not even with a word, and in nothing; they are overwhelmed with sorrow, and they are lost, and they do not hope to see life from one day to the next. 11. They hoped to be the head, and they are the tail. They have suffered while laboring, and they do not enjoy the fruit of their labor; they are the food of sinners, and the wicked have made their yoke heavy upon them. 12. Those who hate them and those who strike them have dominated them; and before those who hate them they have bowed their heads, and these have had no pity on them. 13. They wished to withdraw from them, to flee and find rest, and they found no place to flee to and escape them. 14. And they accused them before the princes in their affliction, and they cried out against those who devour them, but they pay no attention to their cry and do not wish to listen to their voice. 15. They help those who despoil and devour them and those who have diminished their number, and they hide their violence, and they do not remove from upon them the yoke of those who devour them, scatter them, and kill them; they hide their murder, and they do not remember that they (the wicked) raised their hands against them."</p>
### Chapter 104 <span class="chap-roman">(CIV)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">Assurances given to the righteous. An apostrophe to sinners and to falsifiers of the word of truth.</p>

<p class="v">1. I swear it to you: in heaven the angels remember you for good, in the presence of the glory of the Great One; and your names are written in the presence of the glory of the Great One. 2. Hope, for at first you were afflicted with misfortune and suffering, but now you shall shine like the luminaries of heaven. You shall shine and you shall appear, and the gate of heaven shall be opened before you. 3. And in your cry, cry out for justice and it shall appear to you, for all your affliction shall be sought out upon the princes and upon all those who have helped those who despoil you. 4. Hope, and do not give up your hope, for you shall enjoy great joy like the angels of the heavens. 5. What will you do? You shall not have to hide yourselves on the day of the great judgment, you shall not be found sinners, and the eternal judgment shall take place far from you for all the generations of the world. 6. And now do not fear, O righteous ones, when you see sinners grow strong and prosperous in their way, and do not associate with them, but keep away from their violence, for you shall have a part in the lot of the host of heaven.</p>

<p class="v">7. For you say, you sinners: "Do not search out and do not write down all our sins." — All your sins are written down every day. 8. And now I will show you that the light and the darkness, the day and the night, see all your sins.</p>

<p class="v">9. Do not be impious in your hearts, do not lie, do not alter the word of truth and do not accuse of falsehood the word of the Holy One and of the Great One, and do not prize your idols, for all your lies and all your impieties shall not be imputed to you as righteousness, but as great sin. 10. And now I know this mystery: sinners shall alter and greatly distort the word of truth, and they shall utter evil words, and they shall lie and they shall invent great falsehoods, and they shall write books upon their own words. 11. But if they write all my word according to the truth, in their own tongues, and do not alter and do not abridge my words, but write everything according to the truth, all that I attested from the beginning concerning them, (in that case) 12. I know another mystery: the books shall be given to the righteous and to the wise, to bring them joy and truth and great wisdom. 13. The books shall be given to them, and they shall believe in them and shall rejoice in them, and they shall receive the reward, all the righteous who shall have learned from them all the ways of truth.</p>

### Chapter 105 <span class="chap-roman">(CV)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">God commands the righteous to make known the wisdom of Enoch's writings.</p>

<p class="v">1. In those days the Lord commanded (the righteous) to call the children of the earth and to bear witness to them of their wisdom: "Show it to them, for you are their guides, as well as the rewards (that shall take place) over all the earth. 2. [For I and my son shall be united with them forever in the ways of truth during their life], and you shall have peace. Rejoice, children of truth! Amen."</p>

### Appendix — The Birth of Noah {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">Chapters 106-107 in the usual numbering, from the translation published by J.-P. Migne (1856)</p>

<p class="footer-note">The transcription of Martin's text ends at chapter 105. The following account, present in the Ethiopian manuscripts, is given here in the older French translation collected by Migne, where it bears the number CV. The brief final chapter (108), "another writing of Enoch," absent from several manuscripts, exists in no public-domain French translation: there Enoch promises the persecuted humble the light and the promised throne, while the sinners cry out in the darkness.</p>

<p class="v">1. After some time, Methuselah, my son, gave a wife to his son Lamech.</p>

<p class="v">2. She, having conceived, brought into the world a child whose flesh was white as snow, and red as a rose; whose hair was white and long as wool, and whose eyes were of surpassing beauty. No sooner had he opened them than he flooded the whole house with light, as with the very brightness of the sun.</p>

<p class="v">3. And no sooner had he been received from the hands of the midwife than he opened his mouth, telling of the wonders of the Lord. Then Lamech, his father, filled with astonishment, went to find Methuselah, and told him that he had a son who did not resemble other children at all. "This is not a man," he said, "it is an angel of heaven; assuredly, he is not of our kind."</p>

<p class="v">4. His eyes are bright as the rays of the sun, his face is illumined; he does not appear to be of me, but of an angel.</p>

<p class="v">5. I fear indeed that this prodigy is the omen of some event upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">6. And now, O my father, I beg you to go find Enoch, my ancestor, and ask him for the explanation, for he makes his dwelling with the angels.</p>

<p class="v">7. Having heard his son's words, Methuselah came to find me at the ends of the earth, for he knew that I was there, and he called me.</p>

<p class="v">8. At his voice I hastened to him, and I said to him: Here I am, my son; why have you come to find me?</p>

<p class="v">9. And he answered me: A great event brings me to you; a wonder difficult to understand, the explanation of which I have come to ask of you.</p>

<p class="v">10. Listen then, O my father, and know that my son Lamech has just had a son who does not resemble him at all, and who does not appear to belong to the race of men. He is whiter than snow, redder than the rose; his hair is whiter than wool, and his eyes cast forth rays like the sun; when he opens them, he fills the house with light.</p>

<p class="v">11. And immediately after he came forth from the hands of the midwife, he opened his mouth and blessed the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">12. His father Lamech, frightened by this wonder, hastened to me, not believing that this child was his, but that he was born of an angel of heaven; and behold, I have come to you so that you may reveal to me the truth of this mystery.</p>

<p class="v">13. Then I, Enoch, answered him: The Lord is about to do a new work upon the earth. I have seen it in a vision. I have spoken to you of the time of my father Jared, of those who, born of heaven, had nevertheless transgressed the word of the Lord. Behold, they committed iniquity, and they transgressed the ordinances, and dwelt with the wives of men, and begot with them an infamous posterity.</p>

<p class="v">14. For this crime, a great catastrophe shall come upon the earth; a flood shall inundate it and devastate it for a year.</p>

<p class="v">15. This child who is born to you shall alone survive this great cataclysm, with his three sons. When all mankind is destroyed, he alone shall be saved.</p>

<p class="v">16. And his descendants shall beget upon the earth giants, born not of the spirit, but of the flesh. The earth shall therefore be chastised, and all corruption shall be washed away. Therefore, teach your son Lamech that the son who is born to him is truly his son; let him call him by the name Noah, because he shall be a survivor for you. He and his sons shall have no part in the corruption, and shall keep themselves from the sins that shall cover the face of the earth. Unfortunately, after the flood, iniquity shall be still greater than before; for I know what must come to pass; the Lord himself has revealed to me all its mysteries, and I have been able to read it in the tables of heaven.</p>

<p class="v">17. I have read there that generations shall succeed generations, until the holy race arises, until crime and iniquity disappear from the face of the earth, until all partake of righteousness.</p>

<p class="v">18. And now, my son, go and announce to your son Lamech,</p>

<p class="v">19. That the child who is born to him is truly his son, and that there is no deceit in his birth.</p>

<p class="v">20. And when Methuselah had heard the words of his father Enoch, who had revealed to him all the mysteries, he returned full of confidence, and called the child by the name Noah, because he was to be the consolation of the earth after the great catastrophe.</p>

<p class="v">21. Here is another book that Enoch wrote for his son Methuselah, and for those who are to come after him, so that they might preserve, as he did, the word and the simplicity of their ways. You who suffer, wait patiently for the moment when the sinners shall have disappeared, and the power of the wicked shall have been annihilated; wait until sin has vanished from the earth; for their names shall be blotted out of the holy books, their race shall be destroyed, and their spirits shall be tormented. They shall cry out, they shall lament in an invisible desert, and shall burn in a fire that shall never be consumed. There too I beheld what seemed a cloud, which my eyes could not penetrate; for from its lower part one could not make out its upper part. There I also saw the flame of a burning fire, like unto shining mountains, driven by a whirlwind and pushed to the right and to the left.</p>

<p class="v">22. And I questioned one of the holy angels who was with me, and I said to him: What is this splendor? It is not heaven that I see, it is evidently the flame of a vast hearth; I hear cries of pain, cries of despair.</p>

<p class="v">23. And he answered: There, in this place that you see, are tormented the spirits of sinners and blasphemers, of those who conducted themselves ill, who perverted what God had spoken by the mouth of his prophets. For the list of their names and of their evil works is kept in heaven; and the angels take note of it, and they know the punishments reserved for them; they also know what is reserved for those who have crucified their flesh, and who were persecuted by wicked men; for those who loved their God, who did not set their affection on gold and silver, who, far from surrendering their bodies to the pleasures of this world, tormented their bodies with voluntary sufferings.</p>

<p class="v">24. To those who, from the day of their birth, have not coveted earthly riches, but have regarded themselves as a traveling spirit upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">25. Such was their conduct, and yet God tried them well! But their spirits were always found pure and innocent, and ready to bless the Lord; I have recorded in my books all the rewards they shall have merited, for having loved heavenly things more than themselves. This is what God says: When they were persecuted by the wicked, covered with reproaches and insults, they did not cease to praise me. Now I will raise their spirits to the abode of light; I will transform those who were born in darkness, and who did not claim for themselves the glory that their faith had merited for them.</p>

<p class="v">26. I will lead into the abode of splendors those who love my name, I will make them sit upon thrones of glory, and I will make them thrill with eternal joy; for the judgment of God is full of equity.</p>

<p class="v">27. He will give these faithful ones a blessed dwelling; as for those who were born in darkness, they shall see themselves cast down into darkness, while the righteous shall enjoy happiness beyond measure. The sinners, seeing them, shall utter cries of despair, while the righteous shall live in splendor and glory, and shall experience forever the truth of the promises of a God whom they loved.</p>

<p class="v">End of the vision of the prophet Enoch. May the blessing and the grace of the Lord descend upon those who love him. So be it.</p>

# Part Two <SEP> The Book of Jubilees

<p class="part-sub">Mäshafä Kufalé, "the Little Genesis" — a French translation based on the text established by R. H. Charles (1902)</p>

On Sinai, "the angel of the presence" dictates to Moses the history of the world from creation to the Passover,
divided into jubilees of forty-nine years. The Book of Jubilees is a solemn rewriting of Genesis:
in it we learn the name of Cain's wife, the Feast of Weeks celebrated by Noah, the war of the kings against Jacob,
and why the 364-day calendar is that of heaven. Written in Hebrew in the 2nd century BCE
(fifteen manuscripts found at Qumran), it has survived complete only in Ge'ez, where the Ethiopian Church reads it
as Scripture. The italicized summaries at the head of each chapter are those of the Charles edition.

### Chapter 1 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Moses receives the tables of the law and the instructions concerning past and future history that he is to record in a book, 1-4. Apostasy of Israel, 5-9. Captivity of Israel and Judah, 10-13. Return of Judah and rebuilding of the temple, 15-18. Prayer of Moses for Israel, 19-21. God's promise to redeem them and to dwell with them, 22-5, 28. Moses is commanded to write the future history of the world (the Book of Jubilees?), 26. And an angel to write the law, 27. This angel takes the heavenly chronological tablets to dictate them to Moses, 29.</p>

<p class="v">This is the account of the division of the days of the law and of the testimony, of the events of the years, of their (years') weeks, of their jubilees throughout all the years of the world, as the Lord said to Moses on Mount Sinai when he went up to receive the tables of the law and of the commandments, according to the voice of God when he said to him: "Go up to the top of the mountain."</p>

<p class="v">1. And it came to pass in the first year of the exodus of the children of Israel out of Egypt, in the third month, on the sixteenth day of the month, [2450 Anno Mundi] that God spoke to Moses, saying: "Come up to me on the mountain, and I will give you two tables of stone of the law and of the commandment which I have written, that you may teach them."</p>

<p class="v">2. And Moses went up onto the mountain of God, and the glory of the LORD abode upon Mount Sinai, and a cloud overshadowed it for six days.</p>

<p class="v">3. And he called Moses on the seventh day out of the midst of the cloud, and the appearance of the glory of the LORD was like a flaming fire on the top of the mountain.</p>

<p class="v">4. And Moses remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights, and God taught him the former and the latter history of the division of all the days of the law and of the testimony.</p>

<p class="v">5. And He said: "Incline your heart to every word that I shall tell you on this mountain, and write them in a book, so that their generations may see how I have not abandoned them because of all the evil they have done in transgressing the covenant which I establish between me and you for their generations today on Mount Sinai."</p>

<p class="v">6. "And thus it shall come to pass that when all these things happen to them, they shall acknowledge that I am more righteous than they in all their judgments and in all their deeds, and they shall acknowledge that I have truly been with them."</p>

<p class="v">7. "And write for yourself all these words that I declare to you today, for I know their rebellion and their stiffness of neck, before I bring them into the land which I swore to their fathers, to Abraham and to Isaac and to Jacob, saying: I will give to your posterity a land flowing with milk and honey.</p>

<p class="v">8. "And they shall eat and be filled, and they shall turn to strange gods, to (gods) who cannot deliver them from any of their tribulation; and this testimony shall be heard as a witness against them. For they shall forget all my commandments, (even) everything that I command them, and they shall walk after the gentiles, and after their uncleanness and after their shame, and shall serve their gods, and this shall be to them an offense and a tribulation, an affliction and a snare.</p>

<p class="v">9. "And many shall perish and be taken prisoner and shall fall into the hands of the enemy, because they have forsaken my ordinances and my commandments, and the feasts of my covenant, and my sabbaths, and my holy place which I have sanctified for myself in their midst, and my tabernacle and my sanctuary, which I have sanctified for myself in the midst of the land, that I might establish my name there and that it might dwell there."</p>

<p class="v">10. "And they shall make for themselves high places, and groves, and graven images, and they shall worship each his own (graven image), so as to go astray, and they shall sacrifice their children to demons and to all the works of the error of their heart.</p>

<p class="v">11. "And I will send them witnesses, that I may testify against them, but they will not listen, and will also kill the witnesses, and they will persecute those who seek the law, and they will abrogate and change everything so as to do evil in my sight.</p>

<p class="v">12. "And I will hide my face from them, and I will deliver them into the hands of the gentiles for captivity, for a prey, and to be devoured, and I will remove them from the midst of the land, and I will scatter them among the gentiles.</p>

<p class="v">13. "And they will forget all my law and all my commandments and all my judgments, and will go astray regarding the new moons, the sabbaths, the feasts, the jubilees, and the ordinances."</p>

<p class="v">14. "And after that they shall turn to me from among the gentiles with all their heart and with all their soul and with all their strength, and I will gather them from the midst of all the gentiles, and they shall seek me, so that they shall find me when they seek me with all their heart and with all their soul.</p>

<p class="v">15. "And I will reveal to them abundant peace with righteousness, and I will remove for them the plant of uprightness, with all my heart and with all my soul, and they shall be a blessing and not a curse, and they shall be the head and not the tail."</p>

<p class="v">16. "And I will build my sanctuary in their midst, and I will dwell with them, and I will be their God and they shall be my people in truth and righteousness."</p>

<p class="v">17. "And I will not abandon them nor let them fall, for I am the LORD, their God.</p>

<p class="v">18. And Moses fell upon his face and prayed and said: "O Lord my God, do not abandon your people and your inheritance to wander in the error of their heart, and do not deliver them into the hands of their enemies, the gentiles, lest they dominate over them and incite them to sin against you.</p>

<p class="v">19. "Let your mercy, O Lord, be lifted up upon your people, and create in them an upright spirit, and do not let the spirit of Beliar rule over them, to accuse them before you and ensnare them out of all the paths of righteousness, so that they perish from before your face.</p>

<p class="v">20. "But they are your people and your inheritance, whom you delivered by your great power from the hands of the Egyptians: create in them a clean heart and a holy spirit, and let them no longer be ensnared in their sins," forever.</p>

<p class="v">21. And the Lord said to Moses: "I know their contrariness, their thoughts, and their stiffness of neck, and they will not be obedient until they confess their own sin and that of their fathers."</p>

<p class="v">22. "And after that they shall turn to me in all uprightness and with all their heart and with all their soul, and I will circumcise the foreskin of their heart and the foreskin of the heart of their posterity, and I will create in them a holy spirit, and I will purify them so that they shall not turn away from me from this day and forever.</p>

<p class="v">23. "And their souls shall cling to me and to all my commandments, and they shall fulfill my commandments, and I will be their Father and they shall be my children."</p>

<p class="v">24. "And they shall all be called children of the living God, and every angel and every spirit shall know, yes, they shall know that these are my children, and that I am their Father in uprightness and righteousness, and that I, their Father, love them."</p>

<p class="v">25. "And write for yourself all these words that I declare to you on this mountain, the first and the last, which shall come to pass in all the divisions of the days, in the law and in the testimony and in the weeks and the jubilees, forever, until I come down and dwell with them for all eternity.</p>

<p class="v">26. And He said to the angel of the presence: "Write for Moses from the beginning of creation until my sanctuary is built among them for all eternity."</p>

<p class="v">27. "And the LORD will appear in the sight of all, and all shall know that I am the God of Israel and the father of all the children of Jacob, and the king of Mount Zion for eternity. And Zion and Jerusalem shall be holy."</p>

<p class="v">28. And the angel of the presence, who walked before the camp of Israel, took the tables of the divisions of the years — from the time of creation — of the law and of the testimony of the weeks of the jubilees, according to the individual years, according to the total number of the jubilees [according to the individual years], from the day of the [new] creation, when the heavens and the earth shall be renewed, and all their creation according to the powers of the heavens, and according to all the creation of the earth, until the sanctuary of the Lord is made in Jerusalem on Mount Zion, and all the luminaries are renewed for healing, peace, and blessing for all the elect of Israel, and so that it may be from that day and unto all the days of the earth.</p>

### Chapter 2 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">The account of the twenty-two distinct acts of creation over the six days, 1-16. Institution of the sabbath: its observance by the highest angels, with whom Israel is afterward to be associated, 17-32. (Cf. Gen. i-ii. 3.)</p>

<p class="v">1.
