And the angel of the presence spoke to Moses according to the word of the Lord, saying: Write the complete history of the creation, how in six days the Lord God finished all his works and all that he created, and observed the sabbath on the seventh day, and sanctified it for all ages, and appointed it as a sign of all his works.</p>

<p class="v">2. For on the first day he created the heavens which are above, and the earth, and the waters, and all the spirits that minister before him — the angels of the presence, and the angels of sanctification, and the angels [of the spirit of fire and the angels] of the spirit of the winds, and the angels of the spirit of the clouds, and of darkness, and of snow, and of hail and of frost, and the angels of the voices, and of the thunder and of the lightning, and the angels of the spirits of cold and of heat, and of winter and of spring and of autumn and of summer, and of all the spirits of his creatures which are in the heavens and on the earth, (he created) the abysses and the darkness, evening (and night), and the light, dawn and day, which he prepared in the knowledge of his heart.</p>

<p class="v">3. And thereupon we saw his works, and we praised him, and we gave praise before him because of all his works; for he created seven great works on the first day.</p>

<p class="v">4. And on the second day he created the firmament in the midst of the waters, and the waters were divided on that day — half of them went up above and the other half went down beneath the firmament (which was) in the midst, upon the face of the whole earth. And that was the only work he created on the second day.</p>

<p class="v">5. And on the third day he commanded the waters to pass from the surface of the whole earth into one place, and the dry land to appear.</p>

<p class="v">6. And the waters did as he had commanded them, and they withdrew from the surface of the earth into one place outside that firmament, and the dry land appeared.</p>

<p class="v">7. And on that day he created for them all the seas according to their separate gathering-places, and all the rivers, and the gatherings of the waters in the mountains and over all the earth, and all the lakes, and all the dew of the earth, and the seed that is sown, and everything that grows, and the fruit-bearing trees, and the trees of the woods, and the garden of Eden, in Eden, and all the plants after their kind.</p>

<p class="v">8. These four great works God created on the third day. And on the fourth day he created the sun, the moon, and the stars, and set them in the firmament of heaven, to give light upon all the earth, and to rule over the day and the night, and to divide the light of heaven from the darkness.</p>

<p class="v">9. And God made the sun a great sign upon the earth for days, and for sabbaths, and for months, and for feasts, and for years, and for sabbaths of years, and for jubilees, and for all the seasons of the years.</p>

<p class="v">10. And it divides the light from the darkness, [and] for prosperity, that all things which sprout and grow upon the earth might prosper.</p>

<p class="v">11. These three kinds he made on the fourth day. And on the fifth day he created the great sea monsters in the depths of the waters, for these were the first things of flesh that were created by his hands, the fish and everything that moves in the waters, and everything that flies, the birds and all their kinds.</p>

<p class="v">12. And the sun rose above them to make them prosper, and above all that was upon the earth, all that grows out of the earth, all the fruit-bearing trees, and all flesh.</p>

<p class="v">13. These three kinds he created on the fifth day. And on the sixth day he created all the animals of the earth, and all cattle, and everything that moves upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">14. And after all this he created man, a man and a woman he created them, and gave him dominion over everything that is upon the earth and in the seas, and over everything that flies, and over the beasts and over the cattle, and over everything that moves upon the earth, and over all the earth, and over all this he gave him dominion.</p>

<p class="v">15. And these four kinds he created on the sixth day. And there were in all twenty-two kinds.</p>

<p class="v">16. And he finished all his work on the sixth day, everything that is in the heavens and on the earth, and in the seas and in the abysses, and in the light and in the darkness, and in everything.</p>

<p class="v">17. And he gave us a great sign, the day of the sabbath, so that we should work six days, but keep sabbath from all work on the seventh day.</p>

<p class="v">18. And all the angels of the presence and all the angels of sanctification, these two great classes, he commanded us to observe the sabbath with him in heaven and on earth.</p>

<p class="v">19. And he said to us: Behold, I will separate for myself a people from among all the peoples, and these shall keep the sabbath day, and I will sanctify them for myself as my people, and I will bless them; as I have sanctified the sabbath day and sanctify it for myself, so will I bless them, and they shall be my people and I will be their God.</p>

<p class="v">20. And I have chosen the seed of Jacob from among all that I have seen, and have written him down as my firstborn son, and have sanctified him for myself forever and ever; and I will teach them the sabbath day, that they may keep sabbath thereon from all work.</p>

<p class="v">21. And thus he created therein a sign according to which they should keep sabbath with us on the seventh day, to eat and to drink, and to bless him who created all things, as he blessed and sanctified for himself a people above all peoples, and that they should keep sabbath together with us.</p>

<p class="v">22. And he caused his commandments to ascend as a sweet-smelling savor acceptable before him continually. . .</p>

<p class="v">23. There were twenty-two heads of mankind from Adam to Jacob, and twenty-two kinds of work were made until the seventh day; this is blessed and holy, and the former also is blessed and holy; and the one serves with the other unto sanctification and blessing.</p>

<p class="v">24. And to this one (Jacob and his posterity) it was granted that they should always be the blessed and holy ones of the first testimony and of the first law, even as he had sanctified and blessed the sabbath day on the seventh day.</p>

<p class="v">25. He created the heaven and the earth and everything that he created in six days, and God sanctified the seventh day for all his works; therefore he ordained concerning it that whoever should do any work thereon should die, and that whoever should defile it should surely die.</p>

<p class="v">26. Therefore command the children of Israel to observe this day, that they may sanctify it, that they may do no work thereon, and that they may not defile it, for it is more holy than all other days.</p>

<p class="v">27. And whoever profanes it shall surely die, and whoever does any work thereon shall surely die eternally, so that the children of Israel may observe this day throughout their generations, and may not be uprooted from the land; for it is a holy day and a blessed day.</p>

<p class="v">28. And whoever observes it and keeps sabbath thereon from all his work shall be holy and blessed continually, like us.</p>

<p class="v">29. Declare and say to the children of Israel the law of this day, both that they should keep sabbath thereon, and that they should not forsake it in the error of their heart; (and) that it is not lawful to do thereon any improper work, to seek thereon their own pleasure, and that they should not prepare thereon anything to be eaten or drunk, and (that it is not lawful) to draw water thereon, or bring in or take out thereon through their gates any burden which they had not prepared for themselves on the sixth day in their dwellings.</p>

<p class="v">30. And they shall not bring in nor take out from house to house on that day; for that day is more holy and more blessed than any jubilee day among the jubilees; on this day did we keep sabbath in the heavens before it was made known to any flesh to keep sabbath thereon on the earth.</p>

<p class="v">31. And the Creator of all things blessed it, but he did not sanctify all peoples and all nations to keep sabbath thereon, but Israel alone: to them alone did he grant to eat and to drink and to keep sabbath thereon upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">32. And the Creator of all things blessed this day which he had created for blessing, and holiness, and glory above all days.</p>

<p class="v">33. This law and testimony were given to the children of Israel as a law forever for their generations.</p>

### Chapter 3 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Adam names all the creatures, 1-3. Creation of Eve and promulgation of the levitical laws of purification, 4-14. Adam and Eve in Paradise: their sin and their expulsion, 15-29. Law of covering one's shame enacted, 30-2. Adam and Eve dwell at Êldâ, 32-5. (Cf. Gen. ii. 18-25, iii.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And on the six days of the second week we brought, according to the word of God, to Adam all the beasts, and all the cattle, and all the birds, and everything that moves on the earth, and everything that moves in the water, according to their kinds and according to their types: the beasts on the first day; the cattle on the second day; the birds on the third day; and everything that moves on the earth on the fourth day; and that which moves in the water on the fifth day.</p>

<p class="v">2. And Adam gave names to them all, each by its respective name, and as he called them, so was their name.</p>

<p class="v">3. And during these five days, Adam saw all these men and women, according to all the kinds that were on the earth, but he was alone and found no helper for himself.</p>

<p class="v">4. And the Lord said to us: "It is not good that this man should be alone: let us make him a helper."</p>

<p class="v">5. And the LORD our God caused a deep sleep to fall upon him, and he slept, and he took for the woman one rib from among his ribs, and this rib was the origin of the woman from among his ribs, and he built up the flesh in its place, and he built the woman.</p>

<p class="v">6. And he awoke Adam from his sleep, and on awaking he arose on the sixth day, and he brought her to him, and he knew her, and said to her: "This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called [my] wife, because she was taken from her husband."</p>

<p class="v">7. Therefore man and woman shall be one, and therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother and cleave to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.</p>

<p class="v">8. In the first week Adam was created, and the rib, his wife; in the second week he showed her to him; and for this reason the commandment was given to keep women in their uncleanness, for a male seven days, and for a female twice seven days.</p>

<p class="v">9. And after Adam had completed forty days in the land where he had been created, we brought him into the garden of Eden to till it and to keep it, but they brought his wife in on the eightieth day, and after that she entered the garden of Eden.</p>

<p class="v">10. And for this reason the commandment is written on the heavenly tablets concerning her who bears a child: "If she bears a male, she shall remain in her uncleanness seven days according to the first week of days, and thirty-three days shall she remain in the blood of her purifying for many days, and she shall not touch any hallowed thing, nor enter into the sanctuary, until she has completed these days which are enjoined in the case of a male child."</p>

<p class="v">11. "But if it is a female, she shall remain in her uncleanness two weeks of days, according to the first two weeks, and sixty-six days in the blood of her purifying, and they shall be in all eighty days." . .</p>

<p class="v">12. And when she had completed these eighty days, we brought her into the garden of Eden, for it is more holy than all the earth besides, and every tree that is planted in it is holy.</p>

<p class="v">13. Therefore it was prescribed for her who bears a male or a female, the law of those days, that she should not touch any hallowed thing, nor enter into the sanctuary, until these days for the male or female child are completed.</p>

<p class="v">14. This is the law and the testimony which were written for Israel, that they should observe it continually.</p>

<p class="v">15. And in the first week of the first jubilee, [1-7 in the morning] Adam and his wife were in the garden of Eden for seven years, tilling it and keeping it, and we gave him work, and we bade him do everything that was necessary and fitting for the tilling of the ground.</p>

<p class="v">16. And he tilled (the garden), and was naked and did not know it, and was not ashamed, and he protected the garden from the birds, the beasts, and the cattle, and gathered its fruit, and ate thereof, and set aside the residue for himself and for his wife [and set aside what was kept].</p>

<p class="v">17. And after the completion of the seven years that he had completed there, seven years exactly, [8 in the morning] and in the second month, on the seventeenth day (of the month), the serpent came and approached the woman, and the serpent said to the woman: Has God commanded you not to eat of all the trees of the garden?</p>

<p class="v">18. And she said to him: Of all the fruit of the trees of the garden, God has said to us: Eat; but of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God has said to us: You shall not eat of it, and you shall not touch it, lest you die.</p>

<p class="v">19. And the serpent said to the woman: You shall not surely die; for God knows that on the day you eat of it, your eyes shall be opened, and you shall be like gods, and you shall know good and evil.</p>

<p class="v">20. And the woman saw that the tree was pleasant and pleasing to the sight, and that its fruit was good to eat, and she took of it and ate.</p>

<p class="v">21. And when she had first covered her shame with fig leaves, she gave some to Adam and he ate, and his eyes were opened, and he saw that he was naked.</p>

<p class="v">22. And he took fig leaves and sewed them together, and made himself an apron, and covered his shame.</p>

<p class="v">23. And God cursed the serpent, and was angry with it forever. . .</p>

<p class="v">24. And he was angry with the woman, because she had listened to the voice of the serpent and had eaten; and he said to her: "I will greatly multiply your sorrow and your pains: in sorrow you shall bring forth children, and your return shall be to your husband, and he shall rule over you."</p>

<p class="v">25. And he also said to Adam: Because you have listened to the voice of your wife, and have eaten of the tree of which I commanded you not to eat, cursed be the ground because of you: thorns and thistles shall it bring forth for you, and you shall eat your bread in the sweat of your face, until you return to the earth from which you were taken; for you are earth, and to earth you shall return.</p>

<p class="v">26. And he made them tunics of skin, and clothed them, and sent them out of the garden of Eden.</p>

<p class="v">27. And on the day that Adam went out from the Garden, he offered as a sweet-smelling offering, frankincense, galbanum, stacte, and spices, in the morning at the rising of the sun, from the day when he covered his shameful body.</p>

<p class="v">28. And on that day the mouth of all the beasts, and of the cattle, and of the birds, and of everything that walks and of everything that moves, was closed, so that they could no longer speak, for they had all spoken with one another with one lip and one tongue.</p>

<p class="v">29. And he sent out from the garden of Eden all flesh that was in the garden of Eden, and all flesh was scattered according to its kinds and according to its types, into the places that had been created for them.</p>

<p class="v">30. And to Adam alone he gave (something) to cover his shame, from among all the beasts and cattle.</p>

<p class="v">31. Therefore it is prescribed on the heavenly tablets, concerning all those who know the judgment of the law, that they must cover their shame, and must not uncover themselves as the gentiles uncover themselves.</p>

<p class="v">32. And at the new moon of the fourth month, Adam and his wife went out of the garden of Eden, and they dwelt in the land of Elda, in the land of their creation.</p>

<p class="v">33. And Adam called the name of his wife Eve.</p>

<p class="v">34. And they had no son until the first jubilee, [8 in the morning] and after that he knew her.</p>

<p class="v">35. Now he tilled the ground as he had been instructed in the garden of Eden.</p>

### Chapter 4 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Cain and Abel and the other children of Adam, 1-12. Enos, Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared, 13-15. Enoch and his history, 16-25. Four sacred places, 26. Methuselah, Lamech, Noah, 27, 28. Death of Adam and Cain, 29-32. Shem, Ham, and Japheth, 32. (Cf. Gen. iv-v.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the third week of the second jubilee [64-70 AM] she gave birth to Cain, and in the fourth [71-77 AM] she bore Abel, and in the fifth [78-84 AM] she gave birth to her daughter Âwân.</p>

<p class="v">2. And in the first (year) of the third jubilee [99-105 AM], Cain killed Abel because (God) accepted the sacrifice of Abel and did not accept the offering of Cain.</p>

<p class="v">3. And he killed him in the fields; and his blood cried out from the earth to heaven, complaining that he had killed him.</p>

<p class="v">4. And the LORD rebuked Cain because of Abel, because he had killed him, and he made him a fugitive on the earth because of the blood of his brother, and he cursed him upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">5. And for this reason it is written on the heavenly tables: Cursed is he who strikes his neighbor treacherously, and let all who have seen and heard say: So be it; and let him who saw it and did not declare it be cursed like the other.</p>

<p class="v">6. And for this reason we declare, when we present ourselves before the Lord our God, all the sins that are committed in heaven and on earth, in the light and in the darkness, and everywhere.</p>

<p class="v">7. And Adam and his wife mourned for Abel four weeks of years, [99-127 AM] and in the fourth year of the fifth week [130 AM] they became joyful again, and Adam knew his wife again, and she bore him a son, and he called his name Seth; for he said: "GOD has raised up for us a second seed on the earth in place of Abel; for Cain killed him."</p>

<p class="v">8. And in the sixth week [134-40 AM] he begot his daughter Azûrâ.</p>

<p class="v">9. And Cain took Awân, his sister, as wife, and she bore him Enoch at the end of the fourth jubilee. [190-196 AM] And in the first year of the first week of the fifth jubilee, [197 AM] houses were built upon the earth, and Cain built a city and called it by the name of his son Enoch.</p>

<p class="v">10. And Adam knew Eve, his wife, and she bore nine more sons.</p>

<p class="v">11. And in the fifth week of the fifth jubilee [225-31 AM] Seth took Azûrâ his sister as wife, and in the fourth (year of the sixth week) [235 AM] she bore him Enos.</p>

<p class="v">12. He began to call upon the name of the Lord on the earth.</p>

<p class="v">13. And in the seventh jubilee, in the third week [309-15 AM], Enos took Nôâm his sister as wife, and she bore him a son in the third year of the fifth week, and he called his name Kenan.</p>

<p class="v">14. And at the end of the eighth jubilee [325, 386-3992 A.M.] Kenan took Mûalêlêth his sister as wife, and she bore him a son in the ninth jubilee, in the first week, in the third year of that week, [395 AM] and he called his name Mahalalel.</p>

<p class="v">15. And in the second week of the tenth jubilee [449-55 in the morning] Mahalalel took as wife DinaH, daughter of Barakiel, daughter of his father's brother, and she bore him a son in the third week of the sixth year, [461 A.M.] and he called his name Jared, for in his days the angels of the Lord came down upon the earth, those who are called the Watchers, that they might instruct the children of men, and that they might do judgment and uprightness upon the earth. Earth.</p>

<p class="v">16. And in the eleventh jubilee [512-18 in the morning] Jared took for himself a wife, and her name was Baraka, the daughter of Râsûjâl, a daughter of his father's brother, in the fourth week of that jubilee, [522 in the morning] and she bore him a son in the fifth week, in the fourth year of the jubilee, and he called his name Enoch.</p>

<p class="v">17. And he was the first among men born on the earth who learned writing, and knowledge, and wisdom, and who wrote down in a book the signs of heaven according to the order of their months, so that men might know the seasons of the years according to the order of their separate months.</p>

<p class="v">18. And he was the first to write a testimony, and he bore witness to the sons of men among the generations of the earth, and recounted the weeks of the jubilees, and made known to them the days of the years, and set in order the months, and recounted the sabbaths of the years, as we made them known to him.</p>

<p class="v">19. And what was, and what he would see in a vision of his sleep, as it would happen to the children of men throughout their generations until the day of judgment; he saw and understood everything, and wrote his testimony, and placed the testimony on earth for all the children of men and for their generations.</p>

<p class="v">20. And in the twelfth jubilee, [582-88] in the seventh week thereof, he took for himself a wife, and her name was Edna, the daughter of Danel, the daughter of his father's brother, and in the sixth year of this week [587 AM] she bore him a son, and he called him Methuselah.</p>

<p class="v">21. And he was moreover with the angels of God for six jubilees of years, and they showed him everything that is on the earth and in the heavens, the rule of the sun, and he wrote down everything.</p>

<p class="v">22. And he bore witness against the Watchers, who had sinned with the daughters of men; for these had begun to unite themselves, so as to be defiled, with the daughters of men, and Enoch testified against them all.</p>

<p class="v">23. And he was taken from among the children of men, and we led him into the garden of Eden in majesty and honor, and behold, there he writes down the condemnation and judgment of the world, and all the wickedness of the children of men.</p>

<p class="v">24. And because of this, (God) brought the waters of the flood upon all the land of Eden; for there he was placed as a sign, and that he might testify against all the children of men, that he might recount all the deeds of the generations until the day of condemnation.</p>

<p class="v">25. And he burned the incense of the sanctuary, sweet spices acceptable before the LORD on the mountain.</p>

<p class="v">26. For the LORD has four places on the earth: the garden of Eden, and the mountain of the East, and this mountain on which you are today, Mount Sinai, and Mount Zion, which shall be sanctified in the new creation for a sanctification of the earth; through it the earth shall be sanctified from all (its) guilt and its uncleanness throughout the generations of the world.</p>

<p class="v">27. And in the fourteenth jubilee [652 AM] Methuselah took as wife Edna, daughter of Azrial, daughter of his father's brother, in the third week, in the first year of that week, [701-7 AM] and he begot a son and called his name Lamech.</p>

<p class="v">28. And in the fifteenth jubilee, in the third week, Lamech took a wife, and her name was Betenos, daughter of Baraki'il, daughter of his father's brother, and in that week she bore him a son, and he called his name Noah, saying: "This one shall comfort me for my sorrow and for all my labor, and for the ground which the LORD has cursed."</p>

<p class="v">29. And at the end of the nineteenth jubilee, in the seventh week, in the sixth year [930 AM] thereof, Adam died, and all his sons buried him in the land of his creation, and he was the first to be buried in the earth.</p>

<p class="v">30. And he lacked seventy years of a thousand years; for a thousand years are as one day in the testimony of the heavens, and for this reason it was written concerning the tree of knowledge: "On the day that you eat of it, you shall die." For this reason he did not complete the years of that day; for he died during it.</p>

<p class="v">31. At the end of this jubilee, Cain was killed after him in the same year; for his house fell upon him and he died in the midst of his house, and he was killed by its stones; for with a stone he had killed Abel, and by a stone he was killed in a righteous judgment.</p>

<p class="v">32. For this reason it was ordained on the heavenly tablets: "With the instrument with which a man kills his neighbor, he shall be killed; in the manner he wounded him, in like manner they shall deal with him."</p>

<p class="v">33. And in the twenty-fifth [1205 AM] jubilee, Noah took for himself a wife, and her name was \`Emzârâ, the daughter of Râkê'êl, the daughter of his father's brother, in the first year of the fifth week [1207 AM]: and in the third year she bore him Shem, in the fifth year [1209 AM] she bore him Ham, and in the first year of the sixth week [1212 AM] she bore him Japheth.</p>
### Chapter 5 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">The Angels of God take the daughters of men to wife, 1. Corruption of all creation, 2-3. Punishment of the fallen angels and their children, 4-9a. The last judgment announced, 9b-16. The Day of Atonement, 17-18. The flood announced, Noah builds the ark, the flood, 19-32. (Cf. Gen.vi-viii.19.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And it came to pass when the children of men began to multiply on the face of the earth and daughters were born to them, that the angels of God saw them in a certain year of this jubilee, that they were fair to look upon; and they took to themselves wives of all whom they chose, and they bore unto them sons, and they were giants.</p>

<p class="v">2. And lawlessness increased on the earth and all flesh corrupted its way, both men and cattle and beasts and birds and everything that walks on the earth — all corrupted their ways and their order, and they began to devour one another, and lawlessness increased on the earth, and every imagination of the thoughts of all men was thus continually evil.</p>

<p class="v">3. And God looked upon the earth, and behold it was corrupt, and all flesh had corrupted its order, and all who were on the earth had done every kind of evil in his sight.</p>

<p class="v">4. And he said he would destroy man and all flesh upon the face of the earth which he had created.</p>

<p class="v">5. But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">6. And against the angels whom he had sent upon the earth he was exceedingly angry, and he gave command to root them out of all their dominion, and he commanded us to bind them in the depths of the earth, and behold, they are bound in the midst of them and are kept separate.</p>

<p class="v">7. And against their sons a command went forth from before his face that they should be smitten with the sword and be removed from under heaven.</p>

<p class="v">8. And he said, "My spirit shall not always dwell on man; for they also are flesh, and their days shall be a hundred and twenty years.</p>

<p class="v">9. And he sent his sword among them that each should slay his neighbor, and they began to slay one another until they all fell by the sword and were destroyed from the earth.</p>

<p class="v">10. And their fathers were witnesses (of their destruction), and after this they were bound in the depths of the earth for ever, until the day of the great condemnation, when judgment shall be executed on all those who have corrupted their ways and their works before the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">11. And he destroyed them all from their places, and there was not left one of them whom he did not judge according to all his wickedness.</p>

<p class="v">12. And he made for all his works a new and righteous nature, so that they should not sin in their whole nature for ever, but should all be righteous each in his kind for all time.</p>

<p class="v">13. And the judgment of all is ordained and written in righteousness on the heavenly tablets, even (the judgment of) all who depart from the path which is ordained for them to walk in; and if they do not walk therein, judgment is written down for every creature and for every kind.</p>

<p class="v">14. And there is nothing in heaven, or on earth, or in the light, or in the darkness, or in Sheol, or in the depths, or in the place of darkness (that is not judged); and all their judgments are ordained, written, and engraved.</p>

<p class="v">15. He will judge all, the great according to his greatness, and the small according to his smallness, and each according to his way.</p>

<p class="v">16. And he is not one who regards the person of man, nor one who accepts gifts, if he says he will execute judgment on each. If anyone has given all that is on the earth, he will not regard the other gifts or the person (of anyone), and will accept nothing at his hand, for he is a righteous judge.</p>

<p class="v">17. [And concerning the children of Israel it has been written and ordained: If they turn to him in righteousness, he will forgive all their transgressions and pardon all their sins.</p>

<p class="v">18. It is written and ordained that he will show mercy to all who turn from all their guilt once a year.]</p>

<p class="v">19. And as for all who corrupted their ways and their thoughts before the flood, no man's person was accepted save that of Noah alone; for his person was accepted on behalf of his sons, whom (God) saved from the waters of the flood on his account; for his heart was righteous in all his ways, according to what had been commanded regarding him, and he had not departed from anything that was commanded him.</p>

<p class="v">20. And the LORD said that he would destroy everything that was on the earth, both men and cattle, and</p>

<p class="v">21. the beasts, and the birds of heaven, and everything that moves on the earth. And he commanded Noah to make himself an ark, that he might save himself from the waters of the flood.</p>

<p class="v">22. And Noah made the ark in all points as he had been commanded, in the twenty-seventh jubilee of years, in the fifth week, in the fifth year (at the new moon of the first month). [1307 AM]</p>

<p class="v">23. And he entered in the sixth (year), [1308 AM] in the second month, on the new moon of the second month, until the sixteenth; and he entered, with all that we had brought to him, into the ark, and the Lord closed it from outside on the evening of the seventeenth.</p>

<p class="v">24. And the LORD opened the seven floodgates of heaven,</p>

<p class="v">And the mouths of the fountains of the great deep, seven mouths in number.</p>

<p class="v">25. And the floodgates began to pour down water from heaven for forty days and forty nights,</p>

<p class="v">And the fountains of the deep also sent up waters, until the whole world was full of water.</p>

<p class="v">26. And the waters increased upon the earth:</p>

<p class="v">The waters rose fifteen cubits above all the high mountains,</p>

<p class="v">And the ark was lifted up above the earth,</p>

<p class="v">And it moved upon the surface of the waters.</p>

<p class="v">27. And the water prevailed upon the surface of the earth for five months — a hundred and fifty days.</p>

<p class="v">28. And the ark went and rested on the top of Lubar, one of the mountains of Ararat.</p>

<p class="v">29. And (on the new moon) in the fourth month, the fountains of the great deep were closed and the floodgates of heaven were closed; and on the new moon of the seventh month, all the mouths of the abysses of the earth opened, and the water began to descend into the depths.</p>

<p class="v">30. And on the new moon of the tenth month, the tops of the mountains became visible, and on the new moon of the first month, the earth became visible.</p>

<p class="v">31. And the waters disappeared from off the earth in the fifth week, in the seventh year [1309 AM], and on the seventeenth day of the second month, the earth was dry.</p>

<p class="v">32. And on the twenty-seventh day he opened the ark and sent out from it beasts, cattle, birds, and everything that moves.</p>

### Chapter 6 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Noah's sacrifice, 1-3 (cf. Gen. vii.20-2). God's covenant with Noah, the eating of blood forbidden, 4-10 (cf. Gen. ix.1-17). Moses commanded to renew this law against the eating of blood, 11-14. The bow set in the clouds for a sign, 15-16. The Feast of Weeks instituted, the history of its observance, 17-22. The feast of new moons, 23-8. Division of the year into 364 days, 29-38.</p>

<p class="v">1. And on the new moon of the third month he went forth from the ark and built an altar on that mountain.</p>

<p class="v">2. And he made atonement for the earth, and took a kid and made atonement by its blood for all the guilt of the earth; for everything that was on it had been destroyed, save what was in the ark with Noah.</p>

<p class="v">3. And he placed the fat thereof on the altar, and he took an ox, and a goat, and a sheep and kids, and salt, and a turtledove, and the young of a dove, and he placed a burnt offering on the altar, and poured thereon an offering mingled with oil, and sprinkled wine and scattered frankincense over everything, and caused a sweet savor to rise up, pleasing before the LORD.</p>

<p class="v">4. And the LORD smelled the sweet savor, and he made a covenant with him that there should not be a flood again to destroy the earth; that all the days of the earth, seedtime and harvest should never cease; that cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night, should not change their order nor ever cease.</p>

<p class="v">5. 'And you, be fruitful and multiply on the earth, and become numerous upon it, and be a blessing upon it.' I will put your fear and your dread upon everything that is on the earth and in the sea.'</p>

<p class="v">6. 'And behold, I have given you all beasts, and all birds, and everything that moves on the earth, and the fish in the waters, and everything that serves you for food; as the green herbs, I have given you everything to eat.</p>

<p class="v">7. "But you shall not eat flesh, nor life, nor blood; for the life of all flesh is in the blood, lest the blood of your lives be required. At the hand of every man, at the hand of every (beast), I will require the blood of man.</p>

<p class="v">8. "Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed, for he was made man in the image of God."</p>

<p class="v">9. 'And you, be fruitful and multiply on the earth.'</p>

<p class="v">10. And Noah and his sons swore not to eat any blood that was in any flesh, and he made a covenant before the LORD God for ever throughout all the generations of the earth, in this month.</p>

<p class="v">11. For this reason he told you that you should make in this month a covenant with the children of Israel on the mountain, with an oath, and that you should sprinkle blood upon them because of all the words of the covenant which the Lord made with them for ever.</p>

<p class="v">12. And this testimony is written concerning you that you should observe it continually, so that you should not eat on any day the blood of beasts, birds, or cattle throughout all the days of the earth, and the man who eats the blood of beast or of cattle or of birds throughout all the days of the earth, he and his seed shall be rooted out of the land.</p>

<p class="v">13. And you shall command the children of Israel not to eat blood, so that their names and their seed may be continually before the LORD our God.</p>

<p class="v">14. And as for this law there is no limit of days, for it is for ever. They shall keep it throughout their generations, so that they may continue to intercede for you with blood before the altar; every day, at every hour of morning and evening, they shall seek your forgiveness perpetually before the LORD, so as to keep it and not be rooted out.</p>

<p class="v">15. And he gave to Noah and his sons a sign that there should be no more a flood upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">16. He set his bow in the cloud for a sign of the eternal covenant that there should be no more a flood upon the earth to destroy it all the days of the earth.</p>

<p class="v">17. For this reason it is ordained and written on the heavenly tablets that they should celebrate the feast of weeks in this month, once a year, in order to renew the covenant every year.</p>

<p class="v">18. And this whole feast was celebrated in heaven from the day of creation until the days of Noah — twenty-six jubilees and five weeks of years [1309-1659 AM]: and Noah and his sons observed it for seven jubilees and one week of years, until the day of Noah's death, and from the day of Noah's death his sons did away with it until the days of Abraham, and they ate blood.</p>

<p class="v">19. But Abraham observed it, and Isaac and Jacob and his children observed it until your days, and in your time the children of Israel forgot it until you celebrated it anew on this mountain.</p>

<p class="v">20. And you shall command the children of Israel to observe this feast in all their generations; it is a commandment for them: one day in the year, in this month, they shall celebrate the feast.</p>

<p class="v">21. For it is the feast of weeks and the feast of first fruits: this feast is twofold and of a double nature: according to what is written and engraved concerning it, celebrate it.</p>

<p class="v">22. For I have written it in the book of the first law, in that which I have written for you, that you should celebrate it in its season, one day in the year, and I have explained to you its sacrifices, that the children of Israel should remember it and celebrate it throughout their generations in this month, one day every year.</p>

<p class="v">23. And on the new moon of the first month, and on the new moon of the fourth month, and on the new moon of the seventh month, and on the new moon of the tenth month, these are the days of remembrance, and the days of the seasons in the four divisions of the year. These are written and ordained as a testimony for ever.</p>

<p class="v">24. And Noah ordained them for himself as feasts for the generations for ever, so that they thus became a memorial for him.</p>

<p class="v">25. And on the new moon of the first month he was commanded to make himself an ark, and on that day the earth became dry, and he opened (the ark) and saw the earth.</p>

<p class="v">26. And on the new moon of the fourth month, the mouths of the depths of the abyss below were closed. And on the new moon of the seventh month, all the mouths of the abysses of the earth opened, and the waters began to descend into them.</p>

<p class="v">27. And on the new moon of the tenth month, the tops of the mountains appeared, and Noah rejoiced.</p>

<p class="v">28. And for this reason he ordained them for himself as feasts of remembrance for ever, and thus are they ordained.</p>

<p class="v">29. And they placed them on the heavenly tablets, each having thirteen weeks; from one to another (passes) their memorial, from the first to the second, and from the second to the third, and from the third to the fourth.</p>

<p class="v">30. And all the days of the commandment shall be fifty-two weeks of days, and (these) shall make up the entire year. Thus it is engraved and ordained on the heavenly tablets.</p>

<p class="v">31. And there is no neglecting (this commandment) for a single year or from year to year.</p>

<p class="v">32. And command the children of Israel that they observe the years according to this reckoning — three hundred and sixty-four days, and (these) shall constitute a complete year, and they shall not disturb its time from its days and from its feasts; for everything shall come to pass in them according to their testimony, and they shall not leave out any day nor disturb any feast.</p>

<p class="v">33. But if they neglect them and do not observe them according to his commandment, then they will disturb all their seasons, and the years will be dislodged from this (order), [and they will disturb the seasons and the years will be dislodged], and they will neglect their ordinances.</p>

<p class="v">34. And all the children of Israel will forget and will not find the way of the years, and will forget the new moons, the seasons, and the sabbaths, and they will err with regard to the whole order of the years.</p>

<p class="v">35. For I know, and henceforth I will declare it to you, and it is not of my own will; for the book (a lie) is written before me, and on the heavenly tablets the division of days is ordained, lest they forget the feasts of the covenant and walk according to the feasts of the nations after their error and after their ignorance.</p>

<p class="v">36. For there will surely be those who make observations of the moon, how it disturbs the seasons and comes in from year to year ten days too soon.</p>

<p class="v">37. For this reason the years will come upon them in which they will disturb (the order), and make an abominable (day) the day of testimony, and an unclean day a feast day, and they will confound all the days, the holy with the unclean, and the unclean day with the holy; for they will err with regard to the months, the sabbaths, the feasts, and the jubilees.</p>

<p class="v">38. For this reason I command you and testify to you, so that you may testify to them; for after your death your children will disturb them, so that they will not make the year three hundred and sixty-four days only, and for this reason they will err with regard to the new moons, the seasons, the sabbaths, and the feasts, and they will eat every kind of blood with every kind of flesh.</p>

### Chapter 7 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Noah plants a vineyard and offers a sacrifice, 1-5. He becomes drunk and exposes himself, 6-9. The curse of Canaan and the blessing of Shem and Japheth, 10-12 (cf. Gen. ix.20-8). The sons and grandsons of Noah and their cities, 13-19. Noah teaches his sons the causes of the flood and exhorts them to avoid eating blood and killing, to observe the law concerning fruit trees, and to let the land lie fallow every seventh year, as Enoch had commanded, 20-39.</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the seventh week, in the first year [1317 AM] of this jubilee, Noah planted vines on the mountain on which the ark had rested, named Lubar, one of the mountains of Ararat, and they produced fruit in the fourth year, [1320 AM] and he kept their fruit, and gathered it that year in the seventh month.</p>

<p class="v">2. And he made wine of it, and put it in a vessel, and kept it until the fifth year, [1321 AM] until the first day, on the new moon of the first month.</p>

<p class="v">3. And he celebrated that festal day with joy, and he made a burnt offering to the LORD — a young bull and a ram, and seven sheep, each a year old, and a kid — that he might thus make atonement for himself and his sons.</p>

<p class="v">4. And he first prepared the kid, and he put a little of its blood on the flesh that was on the altar which he had made, and he placed all the fat on the altar where he made the burnt offering, and the bull and the ram and the sheep, and he placed all their flesh on the altar.</p>

<p class="v">5. And he placed thereon all their offerings mingled with oil, and afterward he sprinkled wine on the fire which he had previously kindled on the altar, and he placed frankincense on the altar and caused a sweet savor to rise up, pleasing before the Lord his God.</p>

<p class="v">6. And he rejoiced and drank of this wine, he and his children, with joy.</p>

<p class="v">7. And it was evening, and he went into his tent, and being drunk he lay down and slept, and uncovered himself in his tent while he slept.</p>

<p class="v">8. And Ham saw Noah his father naked, and went out and told his two brothers outside.</p>

<p class="v">9. And Shem took a garment and arose, he and Japheth, and they put the garment on their shoulders and went backward and covered the shame of their father, and their faces were turned away.</p>

<p class="v">10. And Noah awoke from his sleep and knew all that his youngest son had done to him, and he cursed his son and said: "Cursed be Canaan! He shall be a slave to his brothers."</p>

<p class="v">11. And he blessed Shem, and said: 'Blessed be the Lord, the God of Shem, and Canaan shall be his servant.'</p>

<p class="v">12. 'God will enlarge Japheth, and God will dwell in the dwelling of Shem, and Canaan shall be his servant.'</p>

<p class="v">13. And Ham knew that his father had cursed his youngest son, and he was displeased that he had cursed his son, and he separated from his father, he and his sons with him, Cush and Mizraim and Put and Canaan.</p>

<p class="v">14. And he built himself a city and called its name after the name of his wife Ne'elatama'uk.</p>

<p class="v">15. And Japheth saw it, and became jealous of his brother, and he too built himself a city, and he called its name after the name of his wife 'Adataneses.</p>

<p class="v">16. And Shem dwelt with his father Noah, and he built a city near his father on the mountain, and he too called its name after the name of his wife Sedeqetelebab.</p>

<p class="v">17. And behold, these three cities are near Mount Lubar: Sedeqetelebab facing the mountain on the east; and Na'eltama'uk on the south; 'Adatan'es toward the west.</p>

<p class="v">18. And these are the sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, and Arpachshad — this (son) was born two years after the flood — and Lud, and Aram.</p>

<p class="v">19. The sons of Japheth: Gomer and Magog and Madai and Javan, Tubal and Meshech and Tiras: these are the sons of Noah.</p>

<p class="v">20. And in the twenty-eighth jubilee [1324-1372 AM] Noah began to impose upon the sons of his sons the ordinances and the commandments, and every judgment that he knew, and he exhorted his sons to observe righteousness, and to cover the shame of their flesh, and to bless their Creator, and to honor father and mother, and to love their neighbor, and to guard their souls from fornication, uncleanness, and all iniquity.</p>

<p class="v">21. For it was on account of these three things that the flood came upon the earth, namely, on account of the fornication wherein the Watchers, against the law of their ordinances, went whoring after the daughters of men and took to themselves wives of all whom they chose: and they made the beginning of uncleanness.</p>

<p class="v">22. And they begot sons, the Naphidim, and they were all unlike one another, and they devoured one another: and the giants killed the Naphil, and the Naphil killed the Eljo, and mankind the Eljo, and one another.</p>

<p class="v">23. And every one sold himself to commit iniquity and to shed much blood, and the earth was filled with iniquity.</p>

<p class="v">24. And after this they sinned against the beasts and the birds, and against everything that moves and walks on the earth; and much blood was shed on the earth, and every imagination and desire of men continually imagined vanity and evil.</p>

<p class="v">25. And the LORD destroyed everything from off the face of the earth; because of the wickedness of their deeds, and because of the blood which they had shed in the midst of the earth, he destroyed everything.</p>

<p class="v">26. And we were left, I and you, my sons, and everything that had entered with us into the ark, and behold, I see your deeds before me, that you are not walking in righteousness, for you have begun to walk in the path of destruction, and you separate yourselves from one another, and you are envious of one another, and (it comes about) that you are not in harmony, my sons, each with his brother.</p>

<p class="v">27. For I see, and behold, the demons have begun their seductions against you and against your children, and now I fear on your account that after my death you will shed the blood of men upon the earth, and that you too will be destroyed from the face of the earth.</p>

<p class="v">28. For whoever sheds the blood of man, and whoever eats the blood of any flesh whatsoever, shall all be destroyed from the earth.</p>

<p class="v">29. And no man who eats blood, or who sheds the blood of man on the earth, shall be left, nor shall there be left to him any seed or descendant living under heaven; for they shall go down into Sheol, and they shall descend into the place of condemnation, and into the darkness of the abyss shall they all be carried off by a violent death.</p>

<p class="v">30. No blood shall be seen upon you from all the blood there shall be on any day when you have killed beasts or cattle or anything that flies upon the earth, and do a good deed for your souls by covering that which has been shed upon the face of the earth.</p>

<p class="v">31. And you shall not be like him who eats with blood, but take heed that no one eat blood before you: cover the blood, for thus have I been commanded to testify to you and your children, together with all flesh.</p>

<p class="v">32. And do not allow the soul to be eaten with the flesh, so that your blood, which is your life, may not be required at the hand of any flesh that sheds it upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">33. For the earth will not be clean from the blood which has been shed upon it; for only through the blood of him who shed it will the earth be purified throughout all its generations.</p>

<p class="v">34. And now, my children, listen: practice judgment and righteousness, that you may sow righteousness over the whole face of the earth, and that your glory may be lifted up before my God, who saved me from the waters of the flood.</p>

<p class="v">35. And behold, you will build yourselves cities, and plant therein every plant that is upon the earth, and above all, every fruit-bearing tree.</p>

<p class="v">36. For three years the fruit of everything that is eaten shall not be gathered; and in the fourth year their fruit shall be accounted holy [and they shall offer the first fruits], acceptable before the Most High God, who created the heavens and the earth and all things. Let them offer abundantly the first fruits of the wine and of the oil (as) first fruits on the altar of the Lord, who receives it, and let what remains be eaten by the servants of the house of the Lord before the altar which receives it.)</p>

<p class="v">37. And in the fifth year, make the release, that you may release it with justice and uprightness, and you will be righteous, and everything that you plant will prosper.</p>

<p class="v">38. For thus did Enoch, the father of your father, command Methuselah his son, and Methuselah his son commanded Lamech, and Lamech commanded me all that his fathers had commanded him.</p>

<p class="v">39. And I also will give you commandments, my sons, as Enoch commanded his son in the earlier jubilees: while he was yet living, the seventh in his generation, he commanded and testified to his son and to the sons of his son until the day of his death.</p>

### Chapter 8 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Kainam discovers an inscription concerning the sun and the stars, 1-4. His sons, 5-8 years. The sons of Noah and Noah divide the earth, 10-11. The inheritance of Shem, 12-21: that of Ham, 22-4: that of Japheth, 25-30. (Cf. Gen. x.)</p>

<p class="v">1. In the twenty-ninth jubilee, in the first week, [1373 AM] at the beginning thereof, Arpachshad took to himself a wife, and her name was Rasu'eja, the daughter of Susan, the daughter of Elam, and she bore him a son in the third year of this week, [1375 AM] and he called his name Kainam.</p>

<p class="v">2. And the son grew, and his father taught him writing, and he went to seek a place where he might seize a city for himself.</p>

<p class="v">3. And he found a writing which former (generations) had engraved on the rock, and he read what was thereon, and he transcribed it, and he sinned on account of it; for it contained the teaching of the Watchers, according to which they observed the omens of the sun, and the moon, and the stars in all the signs of heaven.</p>

<p class="v">4. And he wrote it down and said nothing about it; for he was afraid to speak of it to Noah, lest he should be angry with him on account of it.</p>

<p class="v">5. And in the thirtieth jubilee, [1429 AM] in the second week, in the first year thereof, he took to himself a wife, and her name was Melka, the daughter of Madai, the son of Japheth, and in the fourth year [1432 AM] thereof he begot a son and called his name Shelah; for he said, 'Truly I have been sent.'</p>

<p class="v">6. [And he was born in the fourth year], and Shelah grew, and took to himself a wife, and her name was Mu'ak, the daughter of Kesed, his father's brother, in the thirty-first jubilee, in the fifth week, in the first year [1499 AM] thereof.</p>

<p class="v">7. And she bore him a son in the fifth year [1503 AM], and he called his name Eber; and he took to himself a wife, and her name was 'Azurad, daughter of Nebrod, in the thirty-seventh century, the second jubilee, the seventh week, in the third year. [1564 AM]</p>

<p class="v">8. And in the sixth year [1567 AM] she bore him a son, and he called his name Peleg; for in the days when he was born the children of Noah began to divide the earth among themselves: for this reason he called his name Peleg.</p>

<p class="v">9. And they divided it secretly among themselves, and told it to Noah.</p>

<p class="v">10. And it came to pass in the beginning of the thirty-third jubilee [1569 AM] that they divided the earth into three parts, for Shem, Ham, and Japheth, according to the inheritance of each, in the first year of the first week, when one of us who had been sent was with them.</p>

<p class="v">11. And he called his sons, and they drew near to him, they and their children, and he divided the earth into lots, of which his three sons were to take possession, and they stretched forth their hands and took the writing from the bosom of Noah their father.</p>

<p class="v">12. And there came forth on the writing, as the lot for Shem, the middle of the earth which he should take as an inheritance for himself and for his sons for the generations of eternity, from the middle of the mountain range of Rafa, from the mouth of the water of the river Tina, and his portion goes toward the west through the middle of this river, and it extends until it reaches the water of the abysses, out of which this river goes forth and pours its waters into the sea, and this river flows into the great sea. And everything toward the north belongs to Japheth, and everything toward the south belongs to Shem.</p>

<p class="v">13. And it extends until it reaches Karaso: this is in the bosom of the tongue which looks toward the south.</p>

<p class="v">14. And his portion extends along the great sea, and it extends in a straight line until it reaches the west of the tongue which looks toward the south: for this sea is called the tongue of the Egyptian Sea.</p>

<p class="v">15. And from here it turns toward the south, toward the mouth of the great sea, on the border of its waters, and it extends to the west as far as 'Afra, and it extends until it reaches the waters of the river Gihon, and to the south of the waters of Gihon, to the banks of this river.</p>

<p class="v">16. And it extends toward the east, until it reaches the garden of Eden, to the south thereof, [to the south] and from the east of the whole land of Eden and of all the east, it turns toward the east and continues until it reaches the east of the mountain named Rafa, and descends to the bank of the mouth of the river Tina.</p>

<p class="v">17. This portion was drawn by lot for Shem and his sons, that they should possess it for ever, for his generations, for ever.</p>

<p class="v">18. And Noah rejoiced that this portion had come out for Shem and for his sons, and he remembered all that he had spoken with his mouth in the prophecy; for he had said: "Blessed be the Lord God of Shem, and may the Lord dwell in the dwelling of Shem."</p>

<p class="v">19. And he knew that the garden of Eden is the holy of holies and the dwelling of the LORD, and Mount Sinai the center of the desert, and Mount Zion the center of the navel of the earth: these three were created as holy places facing one another.</p>

<p class="v">20. And he blessed the God of gods, who had put the word of the LORD in his mouth, and the LORD for ever.</p>

<p class="v">21. And he knew that a blessed portion and a blessing had come to Shem and to his sons for the generations for ever: the whole land of Eden, and the whole land of the Red Sea, and the whole land of the East and of India, and upon the Red Sea and its mountains, and all the land of Bashan, and all the land of Lebanon and the islands of Kaftur, and all the mountains of Sanir and Amana, and the mountains of Asshur in the north, and all the land of Elam, of Asshur, of Babel, of Susan and of Madai, and all the mountains of Ararat, and all the region beyond the sea, which is beyond the mountains of Asshur, toward the north, a blessed and spacious land, and everything in it is very good.</p>

<p class="v">22. And for Ham came forth the second portion, beyond the Gihon, toward the south, to the right of the Garden, and it extends toward the south, and it extends to all the mountains of fire, and it extends toward the west to the sea of 'Atel, and it extends toward the west until it reaches the sea of Ma'uk — that (sea) into which descends everything that is not destroyed.</p>

<p class="v">23. And it extends toward the north to the boundaries of Gadir, and it extends to the border of the waters of the sea, to the waters of the great sea, until it approaches the river Gihon, and runs along the river Gihon until it reaches the right of the garden of Eden.</p>

<p class="v">24. And this is the land which was allotted to Ham, as the portion which he was to occupy for ever, for himself and his sons, for their generations for ever.</p>

<p class="v">25. And for Japheth came forth the third portion beyond the river Tina, to the north of the mouth of its waters, and it extended northeast to the whole region of Gog and all the land east thereof.</p>

<p class="v">26. And it extends from the north toward the north, and it extends toward the mountains of Qelt toward the north, and toward the sea of Ma'uk, and it extends to the east of Gadir as far as the region of the waters of the sea.</p>

<p class="v">27. And it extends until it approaches the west of Fara and turns back toward 'Aferag, and it extends toward the east to the waters of the sea of Me'at.</p>

<p class="v">28. And it extends northeast to the region of the river Tina, until it approaches the boundary of its waters toward Mount Rafa, and it turns toward the north.</p>

<p class="v">29. This is the land that was allotted to Japheth and his sons, as the portion of his inheritance which he was to possess for himself and his sons, for their generations and for ever: five great islands and a great land in the north.</p>

<p class="v">30. But it is cold, and the land of Ham is hot, and the land of Shem is neither hot nor cold, but it is a mixture of cold and heat.</p>

### Chapter 9 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Subdivision of the three portions among the grandchildren of Noah. Among the children of Ham, 1: those of Shem, 2-6: those of Japheth, 7-13. Oath taken by the sons of Noah, 14-15.</p>

<p class="v">1. And Ham divided (the land) among his sons, and the first portion came forth for Cush toward the east, and to the west of him for Mizraim, and to the west of him for Put, and to the west of him [and to the west] to the west thereof] on the sea for Canaan.</p>

<p class="v">2. And Shem also divided (the land) among his sons, and the first portion came forth for Ham and his sons, to the east of the river Tigris until it approaches the east, all the land of India, and on the Red Sea on its coast, and the waters of Dedan, and all the mountains of Mebri and Ela, and all the land of Susan, and everything on the side of Pharnak, to the Red Sea and the river Tina.</p>

<p class="v">3. And for Asshur came forth the second portion, all the land of Asshur and Nineveh and Shinar and to the border of India, and it rises and runs along the river.</p>

<p class="v">4. And for Arpachshad came forth the third portion, all the land of the region of the Chaldees to the east of the Euphrates, bordering on the Red Sea, and all the waters of the desert near the tongue of the sea which looks toward Egypt, all the land of Lebanon and Sanir and 'Amana to the border of the Euphrates.</p>

<p class="v">5. And for Aram came forth the fourth portion, all the land of Mesopotamia between the Tigris and the Euphrates, to the north of the Chaldees, to the border of the mountains of Asshur and the land of Arara.</p>

<p class="v">6. And the fifth portion came forth for Lud, the mountains of Asshur and everything pertaining to them until it reaches the Great Sea, and until it reaches the east of Asshur his brother.</p>

<p class="v">7. And Japheth also divided the land of his inheritance among his sons.</p>

<p class="v">8. And the first portion came forth for Gomer, to the east, from the north side to the river Tina; and in the north there came forth for Magog all the inner parts of the north until it reaches the sea of Meat.</p>

<p class="v">9. And for Madai came forth, as his portion that he should possess, from the west of his two brothers to the islands and to the coasts of the islands.</p>

<p class="v">10. And for Javan came forth the fourth portion, every island and the islands that are toward the border of Lud.</p>

<p class="v">11. And for Tubal came forth the fifth portion, in the middle of the tongue which approaches the border of the portion of Lud, to the second tongue, to the region beyond the second tongue, to the third tongue.</p>

<p class="v">12. And for Meshech came forth the sixth portion, all the region beyond the third tongue until it approaches the east of Gadir.</p>

<p class="v">13. And for Tiras came forth the seventh portion, four great islands in the midst of the sea, which extend to the portion of Ham [and the islands of Kamaturi were drawn by lot for the sons of Arpachshad as his inheritance].</p>

<p class="v">14. And thus the sons of Noah divided (the land) among their sons in the presence of Noah their father, and he bound them all by an oath, invoking a curse on whoever sought to seize the portion which had not fallen to him by his lot.</p>

<p class="v">15. And they all said: "So be it; so be it for themselves and their sons for ever throughout their generations until the day of judgment, on which the Lord God will judge them by the sword and by fire for all the unclean wickedness of their errors, with which they have filled the earth with transgression, uncleanness, fornication, and sin.</p>

### Chapter 10 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">The evil spirits lead astray the sons of Noah, 1-2. Noah's prayer, 3-6. Mastema is permitted to keep a tenth of his subject spirits, 7-11. Noah is taught the use of herbs by the angels to withstand the demons, 12-14. Noah dies, 15-17. Building of Babel and the confusion of tongues, 18-27. Canaan seizes Palestine, 29-34. Madai receives Media, 33-6.</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the third week of this jubilee, the unclean demons began to lead astray the children of the sons of Noah, and to lead them astray and destroy them.</p>

<p class="v">2. And the sons of Noah came to Noah their father, and they told him about the demons who were leading astray and blinding and killing the sons of his sons.</p>

<p class="v">3. And he prayed before the LORD his God, and said:</p>

<p class="v">'God of the spirits of all flesh, who has shown me mercy</p>

<p class="v">And has saved me and my sons from the waters of the flood,</p>

<p class="v">And has not caused me to perish as you caused the sons of perdition to perish;</p>

<p class="v">For your grace has been great toward me,</p>

<p class="v">And your mercy toward my soul has been great;</p>

<p class="v">Let your grace be lifted up upon my sons,</p>

<p class="v">And let not the evil spirits rule over them</p>

<p class="v">Lest they destroy them from the earth.</p>

<p class="v">4. But bless me and my sons, that we may grow, and multiply, and fill the earth.</p>

<p class="v">5. And you know how your Watchers, the fathers of these spirits, acted in my days: and as for these spirits who are alive, imprison them and hold them fast in the place of condemnation, and let them not bring destruction upon the son of your servant, my God; for these are malignant and created to destroy.</p>

<p class="v">6. And let them not have dominion over the spirits of the living; for you alone can exercise dominion over them. And let them have no more power over the sons of the righteous, henceforth and for ever.</p>

<p class="v">7. And the LORD our God commanded us to bind them all.</p>

<p class="v">8. And the chief of the spirits, Mastema, came and said: 'Lord, Creator, let some of them remain before me, and let them listen to my voice, and do all that I shall tell them; for if some of them are not left to me, I shall not be able to execute the power of my will upon the sons of men; for these are for corruption and leading astray before my judgment, for great is the wickedness of the sons of men.</p>

<p class="v">9. And he said: 'Let a tenth part of them remain before him, and let nine parts descend into the place of condemnation.'</p>

<p class="v">10. And to one of us he commanded that we should teach Noah all their medicines; for he knew that they would not walk in uprightness, nor strive in righteousness.</p>

<p class="v">11. And we acted according to all his words: we bound all the malignant evil ones in a place of condemnation, and we left a tenth of them so that they might be subject before Satan on the earth.</p>

<p class="v">12. And we explained to Noah all the remedies for their diseases, together with their seductions, and how he could heal them with the herbs of the earth.</p>

<p class="v">13. And Noah wrote down all things in a book, just as we instructed him concerning every kind of medicine. Thus the evil spirits were prevented from (harming) the sons of Noah.</p>

<p class="v">14. And he gave everything that he had written to Shem, his eldest son; for he loved him exceedingly above all his sons.</p>

<p class="v">15. And Noah slept with his fathers, and was buried on Mount Lubar, in the land of Ararat.</p>

<p class="v">16. He completed nine hundred and fifty years in his life, nineteen jubilees and two weeks and five years. [1659 AM]</p>

<p class="v">17. And in his life on earth he surpassed the children of men, except Enoch, because of the righteousness in which he was perfect. For Enoch's office was ordained to bear witness to the generations of the world, so that he should recount all the deeds of generation to generation, until the day of judgment.</p>

<p class="v">18. And in the thirty-third jubilee, in the first year of the second week, Peleg took to himself a wife, whose name was Lomna, daughter of Sinaar, and she bore him a son in the fourth year of this week, and he called his name Reu; for he said: "Behold, the children of men have become evil through the wicked purpose of building for themselves a city and a tower in the land of Shinar."</p>

<p class="v">19. For they departed from the land of Ararat toward the east, to Shinar; for in his days they built the city and the tower, saying: "Come, let us go up thus to heaven."</p>

<p class="v">20. And they began to build, and in the fourth week they made bricks with fire, and the bricks served them for stone, and the clay with which they cemented them together was asphalt which comes out of the sea and out of the springs of water in the land of Shinar.</p>

<p class="v">21. And they built it: forty-three years [1645-1688 AM] they were building it; its breadth was 203 bricks, and the height (of a brick) was the third of one; its height amounted to 5,433 cubits and 2 palms, and (the extent of one wall was) thirteen stades (and of the other thirty stades).</p>

<p class="v">22. And the Lord our God said to us: "Behold, they are one people, and this they have begun to do, and now nothing will be withheld from them. Come, let us go down and confound their language, so that they may not understand one another's language, and that they may be scattered into cities and nations, and that a single purpose shall no longer remain among them until the day of judgment.</p>

<p class="v">23. And the Lord went down, and we went down with him to see the city and the tower which the children of men had built.</p>

<p class="v">24. And he confounded their language, and they no longer understood one another, and they then ceased to build the city and the tower.</p>

<p class="v">25. For this reason the whole land of Shinar is called Babel, because the LORD there confounded all the language of the children of men, and from there they were scattered into their cities, each according to his language and his nation.</p>

<p class="v">26. And the LORD sent a mighty wind against the tower and overthrew it upon the earth. And behold, it was between Asshur and Babylon, in the land of Shinar, and they called its name "Overthrow."</p>

<p class="v">27. In the fourth week, in the first year [1688 AM] at the beginning thereof, in the thirty-fourth jubilee, were they scattered from the land of Shinar.</p>

<p class="v">28. And Ham and his sons entered the land which he was to occupy, and which he had acquired as his portion in the land of the south.</p>

<p class="v">29. And Canaan saw that the land of Lebanon as far as the river of Egypt was very good, and he did not enter the land of his inheritance to the west (that is, toward) the sea, and he dwelt in the land of Lebanon, on the east and on the west, from the border of the Jordan and from the border of the sea.</p>

<p class="v">30. And Ham, his father, and Cush and Mizraim his brothers said to him: "You have settled in a land which is not yours and which was not allotted to us by lot: do not do this; for if you do this, you and your sons will fall in the land and be cursed through sedition; for by sedition you have settled, and by sedition your children will fall, and you will be rooted out for ever.</p>

<p class="v">31. "Do not dwell in the dwelling of Shem; for it fell to Shem and his sons by their lot.</p>

<p class="v">32. "You are cursed, and you will be cursed more than all the sons of Noah, by the curse by which we bound ourselves by oath in the presence of the holy judge and in the presence of Noah our father."</p>

<p class="v">33. But he did not listen to them, and he dwelt in the land of Lebanon from Hamath to the entrance of Egypt, he and his sons until this day.</p>

<p class="v">34. And for this reason this land is named Canaan.</p>

<p class="v">35. And Japheth and his sons went toward the sea and dwelt in the land of their portion, and Madai saw the land by the sea and it did not please him, and he asked a portion from Ham, Asshur, and Arpachshad, his wife's brother, and he dwelt until this day in the land of Media, near his wife's brother.</p>

<p class="v">36. And he called his dwelling and that of his sons Media, after the name of their father Madai.</p>
### Chapter 11 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Reu and Serug, 1 (cf. Gen. xi.20, 21). The rise of war, the shedding of blood, the drinking of blood, and idolatry, 2-7. Nahor and Terah, 8-14 (cf. Gen. xi.22-30). Abram's knowledge of God and his marvelous deeds, 15-24.</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the thirty-fifth jubilee, in the third week of the first year [1681 AM] of it, Reu took for himself a wife, and her name was 'Ôrâ, the daughter of 'Ûr, the son of Kesed, and she bore him a son, and he called his name Sêrôh, in the seventh year of this week of this jubilee. [1687 AM]</p>

<p class="v">2. And the sons of Noah began to war upon one another, to take one another captive, and to slay one another, and to shed the blood of men upon the earth, and to eat blood, and to build strong cities, and walls, and towers, and individuals began to exalt themselves above the nation, and to lay the foundations of kingdoms, and to make war people against people, and nation against nation, and city against city, and all began to do evil, and to acquire weapons, and to teach war to their sons, and they began to seize cities and to sell slaves, men and women.</p>

<p class="v">3. And 'Ûr, son of Kesed, built the city of 'Ara in Chaldea, and gave it the name of his own name and of his father's name. And they made themselves molten images, and each worshipped the idol, the molten image which they had made for themselves, and they began to make graven images and unclean likenesses, and evil spirits helped them and led them astray into committing transgression and impurity.</p>

<p class="v">4. And the prince Mastêmâ strove to bring about all this, and he sent other spirits, those who were placed under his hand, to commit every kind of evil and sin, and every kind of transgression, to corrupt and destroy, and to shed blood upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">5. It is for this reason that he called the name of Sêrôh, Serug, for everyone turned to every kind of sin and transgression.</p>

<p class="v">6. And he grew up and dwelt at Ur in Chaldea, near the father of his wife's mother, and he worshipped idols, and he took a wife in the thirty-sixth jubilee, in the fifth week, in the first year of it, [1744 AM] and she was named Melka, the daughter of Kaber, the daughter of his father's brother.</p>

<p class="v">7. And she bore him Nahor, in the first year of this week, and he grew up and dwelt at Ur in Chaldea, and his father taught him the researches of the Chaldeans, for divining and augury according to the signs of heaven.</p>

<p class="v">8. And in the thirty-seventh jubilee, in the sixth week, in the first year of it, [1800 AM] he took for himself a wife, and she was named 'Ijaska, daughter of Nestag of the Chaldeans.</p>

<p class="v">9. And she bore him Terah in the seventh year of this week. [1806 AM]</p>

<p class="v">10. And the prince Mastêmâ sent ravens and birds to devour the seed that was sown in the land, so as to destroy the land and rob the children of men of their labors. Before they could plow the seed in, the ravens picked it up from the surface of the ground.</p>

<p class="v">11. And it is for this reason that he called his name Terah, because the ravens and the birds reduced them to misery and devoured their seed.</p>

<p class="v">12. And the years began to be barren, on account of the birds, and they devoured all the fruit of the trees: it was only with great effort that they were able to save a little of all the fruits of the earth in their days.</p>

<p class="v">13. And in this thirty-ninth jubilee, in the second week of the first year, [1870 AM] Terah took for himself a wife, and she was named 'Edna, the daughter of Abram, the daughter of his father's sister. And in the seventh year of this week [1876 AM], she bore him a son, and he called him Abram, after the name of his mother's father;</p>

<p class="v">14. for he had died before his daughter had conceived a son.</p>

<p class="v">15. And the child began to perceive the errors of the earth, how everyone went astray after graven images and after impurity, and his father taught him to write, and he was two weeks of years old, [1890 AM] and he separated himself from his father, so that he might not worship idols with him.</p>

<p class="v">16. And he began to pray to the Creator of all things, that he might save him from the errors of the children of men, and that his portion might not fall into error after impurity and vileness.</p>

<p class="v">17. And the time of sowing came, to sow seed upon the land, and they all went out together to guard their seed against the ravens, and Abram went out with those who went, and the child was a boy of fourteen years.</p>

<p class="v">18. And a cloud of ravens came to devour the seed, and Abram ran to meet them before they settled on the ground, and cried out to them before they settled on the ground to devour the seed, and said, "Do not come down: return to the place from which you came," and they turned back.</p>

<p class="v">19. And he made the clouds of ravens turn back that day seventy times, and of all the ravens in the whole land where Abram was, not a single one settled there.</p>

<p class="v">20. And all who were with him throughout the land saw him cry out, and all the ravens turned back, and his name became great throughout the land of the Chaldeans.</p>

<p class="v">21. That year, all who wished to sow came to him, and he accompanied them until the time of sowing was ended. They sowed their land, and that year they brought home enough grain, and ate, and were satisfied.</p>

<p class="v">22. And in the first year of the fifth week [1891 AM] Abram taught those who made instruments for oxen, the craftsmen in wood, and they made a vessel above the ground, facing the frame of the plow, so that the seed might be placed upon it, and the seed would fall from it onto the plowshare, and be hidden in the earth, and they no longer feared the ravens.</p>

<p class="v">23. And in this way they made vessels above the ground on all the frames of the plows, and they sowed and plowed all the land, as Abram had commanded them, and they no longer feared the birds.</p>

### Chapter 12 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Abram seeks to turn Terah away from idolatry, 1-8. Marries Sarai, 9. Haran and Nahor, 9-11. Abram burns the idols: death of Haran, 12-14 (cf. Gen. xi.28). Terah and his family go to Haran, 15. Abram observes the stars and prays, 16-21. Is bidden to go to Canaan, and blessed, 22-4. Given the power to speak Hebrew, 25-7. Leaves Haran for Canaan, 28-31. (Cf. Gen. xi.31-xii.3.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And it came to pass, in the sixth week, in the seventh year of it, [1904 AM] that Abram said to Terah, his father, saying, "Father!"</p>

<p class="v">2. And he said, "Here am I, my son." And he said,</p>

<p class="v">"What help and what profit have we from these idols that you worship,</p>

<p class="v">And before which you bow down?</p>

<p class="v">3. For there is no spirit in them,</p>

<p class="v">For they are dumb, deceitful forms of the heart.</p>

<p class="v">Do not worship them:</p>

<p class="v">4. Worship the God of heaven,</p>

<p class="v">Who makes the rain and the dew fall upon the earth</p>

<p class="v">And does everything upon the earth,</p>

<p class="v">And he created everything by his word,</p>

<p class="v">And all life comes from before his face.</p>

<p class="v">5. Why do you worship things that have no spirit in them?</p>

<p class="v">For they are the work of (men's) hands,</p>

<p class="v">And you carry them upon your shoulders,</p>

<p class="v">And you have no help from them,</p>

<p class="v">But they are a great shame to those who make them,</p>

<p class="v">And a deceit of the heart to those who worship them:</p>

<p class="v">Do not worship them."</p>
