<p class="v">6. And his father said to him, "I too know it, my son, but what shall I do with a people who have made me serve before them?</p>

<p class="v">7. And if I tell them the truth, they will kill me; for their soul cleaves to them, to worship and honor them.</p>

<p class="v">8. Keep silent, my son, lest they kill you." And he spoke these words to his two brothers, and they were angry with him, and he kept silent.</p>

<p class="v">9. And in the fortieth jubilee, in the second week of the seventh year, Abram took for himself a wife, and she was named Sarai, the daughter of his father, and she became his wife.</p>

<p class="v">10. And Haran, his brother, took a wife in the third year of the third week, [1928 AM] and she bore him a son in the seventh year of this week, [1932 AM] and he called his name Lot.</p>

<p class="v">11. And Nahor, his brother, took a wife.</p>

<p class="v">12. And in the sixtieth year of Abram's life, that is, the fourth week, the fourth year of it, [1936 AM] Abram rose up in the night and burned the house of the idols, and he burned everything that was in the house, and no one knew it.</p>

<p class="v">13. And they rose up in the night and sought to save their gods from the midst of the fire.</p>

<p class="v">14. And Haran hurried to save them, but the fire blazed up over him, and he was burned in the fire, and he died at Ur in Chaldea before Terah his father, and they buried him at Ur in Chaldea.</p>

<p class="v">15. And Terah went out from Ur in Chaldea, he and his sons, to go to the land of Lebanon and to the land of Canaan, and he dwelt in the land of Haran, and Abram dwelt with Terah, his father, at Haran two weeks of years.</p>

<p class="v">16. And in the sixth week, in the fifth year of it, [1951 AM] Abram sat up the whole night, at the new moon of the seventh month, to observe the stars from evening to morning, so as to see what the character of the year would be as regards the rains, and he was alone as he sat and watched.</p>

<p class="v">17. And a word came into his heart, and he said, "All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and the sun, are all in the hand of the Lord. Why do I search them out?</p>

<p class="v">18. If he wills, he makes it rain, morning and evening;</p>

<p class="v">And if he desires, he withholds it,</p>

<p class="v">And everything is in his hands."</p>

<p class="v">19. And he prayed that night, and said,</p>

<p class="v">"My God, God Most High, you alone are my God,</p>

<p class="v">And it is you and your dominion that I have chosen.</p>

<p class="v">And you have created all things,</p>

<p class="v">And everything is the work of your hands.</p>

<p class="v">20. Deliver me from the hands of the evil spirits who rule over the thoughts of the hearts of men,</p>

<p class="v">And let them not lead me astray from you, my God.</p>

<p class="v">And establish me and my seed forever,</p>

<p class="v">That we may not go astray from now on and forevermore."</p>

<p class="v">21. And he said, "Shall I return to Ur of the Chaldeans, who seek my face, so that I may go back to them, or shall I remain here in this place? Make the right way prosper before you in the hands of your servant, that he may accomplish it, and that I may not walk in the deceit of my heart, O my God."</p>

<p class="v">22. And he finished speaking and praying, and behold, the word of the Lord was sent to him through me, saying, "Arise from your country, and from your kindred, and from your father's house, to a land that I will show you, and I will make of you a great and numerous nation.</p>

<p class="v">23. And I will bless you</p>

<p class="v">And I will make your name great,</p>

<p class="v">And you shall be blessed upon the earth,</p>

<p class="v">And in you shall all the families of the earth be blessed,</p>

<p class="v">And I will bless those who bless you,</p>

<p class="v">And curse those who curse you.</p>

<p class="v">24. And I will be your God, you and your son, and your son's son, and all your posterity: fear nothing, from now on and for all the generations of the earth, I am your God."</p>

<p class="v">25. And the Lord God said, "Open his mouth and his ears, that he may hear and speak with his mouth, with the tongue that has been revealed"; for it had ceased from the mouth of all the children of men since the day of the fall (of Babel).</p>

<p class="v">26. And I opened his mouth, and his ears and his lips, and I began to speak with him in Hebrew, in the tongue of creation.</p>

<p class="v">27. And he took the books of his fathers, and these were written in Hebrew, and he copied them out, and from then on he began to study them, and I made known to him what he could not (understand), and he studied them during the six rainy months.</p>

<p class="v">28. And it came to pass in the seventh year of the sixth week [1953 AM] that he spoke to his father and told him that he was leaving Haran to go to the land of Canaan, to see it and to return to him.</p>

<p class="v">29. And Terah, his father, said to him, "Go in peace:</p>

<p class="v">May the eternal God make your way smooth.</p>

<p class="v">And may the Lord [be with you, and] keep you from all harm,</p>

<p class="v">And grant you grace, mercy, and favor before those who see you,</p>

<p class="v">And may none of the children of men have power over you to do you harm;</p>

<p class="v">Go in peace."</p>

<p class="v">30. "And if you see a land pleasing in your eyes to dwell in, then arise and bring me to you, and take with you Lot, the son of Haran your brother, as your own son: may the LORD be with you.</p>

<p class="v">31. And Nahor, your brother, will go with me until you return in peace, and we will all go together with you."</p>

### Chapter 13 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Abram journeys from Haran to Shechem in Canaan, from there to Hebron, and from there into Egypt, 1-14a. Returns to Canaan, where Lot separates from him; receives the promise of Canaan and goes to Hebron, 14b-21. Chedorlaomer's attack on Sodom and Gomorrah: Lot taken captive, 22-4. Law of tithes promulgated, 25-9. (Cf. Gen. xii.4-10, 15-17, 19-20; xiii.11-18; xiv.8-14; 21-4.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And Abram departed from Haran, and he took Sarai his wife, and Lot, the son of his brother Haran, into the land of Canaan, and he entered into Asshur, and went to Shechem, and dwelt near a lofty oak.</p>

<p class="v">2. And he looked, and behold, the land was very pleasant, from the entrance of Hamath to the lofty oak.</p>

<p class="v">3. And the LORD said to him, "I will give this land to you and to your posterity."</p>

<p class="v">4. And he built an altar there, and offered upon it a burnt offering to the LORD, who had appeared to him.</p>

<p class="v">5. And he departed from there toward the mountain . . . Bethel on the west and Ai on the east, and he pitched his tent there.</p>

<p class="v">6. And he looked, and behold, the land was very broad and beautiful, and everything grew there: vines, fig trees, and pomegranates, oaks and holm-oaks, and terebinths and oil trees, and cedars, and cypresses and date palms, and all the trees of the fields, and there was water upon the mountains.</p>

<p class="v">7. And he blessed the LORD, who had brought him out of Ur in Chaldea and had brought him into this land.</p>

<p class="v">8. And it came to pass, in the first year, in the seventh week, at the new moon of the first month, [1954 AM] that he built an altar on that mountain and called upon the name of the Lord: "You, the eternal God, are my God."</p>

<p class="v">9. And he offered upon the altar a burnt offering to the LORD, that he might be with him and not forsake him all the days of his life.</p>

<p class="v">10. And he departed from there and journeyed toward the south, and he came to Hebron — and Hebron was built at that time — and he dwelt there two years, and he departed from there to the land of the south, to Bealoth, and there was a famine in the land.</p>

<p class="v">11. And Abram entered Egypt in the third year of the week, and he dwelt in Egypt five years before his wife was taken from him.</p>

<p class="v">12. It was at that time that Tanis, in Egypt, was built, seven years after Hebron.</p>

<p class="v">13. And it came to pass, when Pharaoh seized Sarai, Abram's wife, that the LORD struck Pharaoh and his house with great plagues on account of Sarai, Abram's wife.</p>

<p class="v">14. And Abram was very glorious because of his possessions of sheep, oxen, donkeys, horses, camels, menservants and maidservants, and silver and gold in abundance. And Lot, his brother's son also, was rich.</p>

<p class="v">15. And Pharaoh restored Sarai, Abram's wife, and sent him out of the land of Egypt, and he went to the place where he had pitched his tent at the beginning, to the place of the altar, with Ai to the east and Bethel to the west, and he blessed the LORD his God, who had brought him back in peace.</p>

<p class="v">16. And it came to pass, in the forty-first jubilee, in the third year of the first week, [1963 AM] that he returned to that place and offered a burnt offering there, and called upon the name of the Lord, and said, "You, the God Most High, are my God forever and ever."</p>

<p class="v">17. And in the fourth year of this week [1964 AM] Lot separated from him, and Lot dwelt at Sodom, and the men of Sodom were exceedingly sinful.</p>

<p class="v">18. And he was grieved in his heart that his brother's son had separated from him, for he had no children.</p>

<p class="v">19. In the year that Lot was taken captive, the LORD said to Abram, after Lot had separated from him, in the fourth year of this week, "Lift up your eyes from the place where you dwell, to the north and to the south, and to the west and to the east.</p>

<p class="v">20. For all the land that you see, I will give to you and to your posterity forever, and I will make your posterity like the sand of the sea; even if a man could count the dust of the earth, your posterity would not fail to be numbered."</p>

<p class="v">21. "Arise, walk through the land, in its length and in its breadth, and see it all; for I will give it to your posterity." And Abram departed to Hebron, and dwelt there.</p>

<p class="v">22. And that year Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, and Amraphel, king of Shinar, and Arioch, king of Ellasar, and Tergal, king of the nations, killed the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Sodom fled, and many fell wounded in the valley of Siddim, beside the Salt Sea.</p>

<p class="v">23. And they took Sodom, Adam, and Zeboim captive, and they also captured Lot, the son of Abram's brother, and all his goods, and they went toward Dan.</p>

<p class="v">24. And someone who had escaped came and told Abram that his brother's son had been taken captive, and (Abram) armed his servants . . .</p>

<p class="v">25. . . . for Abram and for his posterity, a tenth of the firstfruits to the Lord, and the Lord ordained it as an ordinance forever, that they should give it to the priests who served before him, that they should possess it forever.</p>

<p class="v">26. And for this law there is no limit of days; for he has ordained that the generations should give to the LORD forever a tenth of everything, of the seed, the wine, the oil, the cattle, and the sheep.</p>

<p class="v">27. And he gave it to his priests, that they might eat and drink with joy before him.</p>

<p class="v">28. And the king of Sodom came to him and bowed down before him, and said, "Our lord Abram, give us the souls that you have saved, but let the spoil be yours."</p>

<p class="v">29. And Abram said to him, "I lift up my hands to God Most High, that from a thread to a sandal-strap I will take nothing that is yours, lest you should say, 'I have made Abram rich'; except what the young men have eaten, and the share of the men who went with me, Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. Let these take their share."</p>

### Chapter 14 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Abram receives the promise of a son and of countless posterity, 1-7. Offers a sacrifice and is told that his posterity shall be in Egypt, 8-17. God's covenant with Abram, 18-20. Hagar bears Ishmael, 21-4. (Cf. Gen. xv.; xvi.1-4, 11.)</p>

<p class="v">1. After these things, in the fourth year of this week, at the new moon of the third month, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a dream, saying, "Fear nothing, Abram; I am your shield, and your reward shall be exceedingly great."</p>

<p class="v">2. And he said, "Lord, Lord, what will you give me, since I am going hence without children, and the son of Masek, the son of my handmaid, is Dammasek Eliezer: he shall be my heir, and to me you have given no seed."</p>

<p class="v">3. And he said to him, "This one shall not be your heir, but he who shall come forth from your own body shall be your heir."</p>

<p class="v">4. And he brought him outside and said to him, "Look toward heaven and count the stars, if you are able to count them."</p>

<p class="v">5. And he looked toward heaven, and saw the stars. And he said to him, "So shall your posterity be."</p>

<p class="v">6. And he believed in the LORD, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.</p>

<p class="v">7. And he said to him, "I am the LORD who brought you out of Ur in Chaldea, to give you this land of the Canaanites, that you might possess it forever; and I will be God to you and to your posterity after you."</p>

<p class="v">8. And he said, "Lord, Lord, by what shall I know that I shall inherit it?"</p>

<p class="v">9. And he said to him, "Take me a heifer of three years, and a goat of three years, and a sheep of three years, and a turtledove and a pigeon."</p>

<p class="v">10. And he took all these in the middle of the month, and he dwelt near the oak of Mamre, which is near Hebron.</p>

<p class="v">11. And he built an altar there, and sacrificed all these; and he poured out their blood upon the altar, and divided them in the middle, and laid them opposite one another; but the birds he did not divide.</p>

<p class="v">12. And the birds fell upon the pieces, and Abram drove them away, and did not let the birds touch them.</p>

<p class="v">13. And it came to pass, when the sun went down, that a trance fell upon Abram, and behold! a horror of great darkness fell upon him, and it was said to Abram, "Know for certain that your posterity shall be strangers in a land that is not theirs, and they will enslave them and afflict them four hundred years."</p>

<p class="v">14. "And I will also judge the nation to which they shall be enslaved, and after that they shall come out with great possessions."</p>

<p class="v">15. "And you shall go in peace to your fathers, and you shall be buried in a good old age."</p>

<p class="v">16. "But in the fourth generation they shall return here, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full."</p>

<p class="v">17. And he awoke from his sleep, and he arose, and the sun had gone down; and there was a flame, and behold! a smoking furnace, and a flame of fire passed between the pieces.</p>

<p class="v">18. And on that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, "I will give to your posterity this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates: the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites, the Perizzites, the Rephaim, the Phakorites, the Hivites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites."</p>

<p class="v">19. And the day passed, and Abram offered the pieces, and the birds, and their fruit offerings and their drink offerings, and the fire consumed them.</p>

<p class="v">20. And on that day we made a covenant with Abram, as we had made it with Noah in this month; and Abram renewed for himself the feast and the ordinance forever.</p>

<p class="v">21. And Abram rejoiced and made known all these things to Sarai his wife; and he believed that he would have seed, but she did not bear it.</p>

<p class="v">22. And Sarai counseled her husband Abram, and said to him, "Go in to Hagar, my Egyptian handmaid; it may be that I shall build up a posterity for you through her."</p>

<p class="v">23. And Abram listened to the voice of Sarai his wife, and said to her, "Do so." And Sarai took Hagar her handmaid, the Egyptian, and gave her as a wife to Abram her husband.</p>

<p class="v">24. And he went in to her, and she conceived and bore him a son, and he called his name Ishmael, in the fifth year of this week [1965 AM]; and it was the eighty-sixth year of Abram's life.</p>

### Chapter 15 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Abram celebrates the feast of firstfruits, 1-2: his name is changed and circumcision instituted, 3-14. Sarai's name changed, and Isaac promised, 15-21. Abraham, Ishmael, and all his household circumcised, 22-4. Circumcision an eternal ordinance, 25, 26. Israel shares this honor with the highest angels, who were created circumcised, 27-9. Israel subject to God alone: the other nations to angels, 30-2. Israel's future unfaithfulness, 33-4. (Cf. Gen. xvii.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the fifth year of the fourth week of this jubilee, [1979 AM] in the third month, in the middle of the month, Abram celebrated the feast of the firstfruits of the grain harvest.</p>

<p class="v">2. And he offered to the LORD new offerings upon the altar, the firstfruits of the produce, a heifer, a goat, and a lamb, upon the altar, as a burnt offering to the LORD; he offered their fruit offerings and their drink offerings upon the altar with incense.</p>

<p class="v">3. And the LORD appeared to Abram and said to him, "I am God Almighty; walk before me, and be perfect."</p>

<p class="v">4. "And I will make my covenant between me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly."</p>

<p class="v">5. And Abram fell on his face, and God spoke with him, and said,</p>

<p class="v">6. "Behold, my ordinance is with you,</p>

<p class="v">And you shall be the father of many nations.</p>

<p class="v">7. And your name shall no longer be called Abram,</p>

<p class="v">But your name, from now on and forever, shall be Abraham.</p>

<p class="v">For I have made you the father of many nations.</p>

<p class="v">8. And I will make you exceedingly great,</p>

<p class="v">And I will make nations of you,</p>

<p class="v">And kings shall come forth from you.</p>

<p class="v">9. And I will establish my covenant between me and you, and your posterity after you, throughout their generations, for an everlasting covenant, that I may be a God to you and to your posterity after you.</p>

<p class="v">10. (And I will give to you, and to your posterity after you) the land where you have sojourned, the land of Canaan, that you may possess it forever, and I will be their God."</p>

<p class="v">11. And the LORD said to Abraham, "And as for you, keep my covenant, you and your posterity after you; and circumcise every male among you, and circumcise your foreskins, and it shall be a sign of an everlasting covenant between me and you.</p>

<p class="v">12. And you shall circumcise the child on the eighth day, every male throughout your generations, whether born in the house, or bought with money from any foreigner, whom you have acquired and who is not of your posterity."</p>

<p class="v">13. "He who is born in your house shall surely be circumcised, and those whom you have bought with money shall be circumcised, and my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting ordinance."</p>

<p class="v">14. "And the uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin on the eighth day, that soul shall be cut off from his people, for he has broken my covenant."</p>

<p class="v">15. And God said to Abraham, "As for Sarai your wife, her name shall no longer be called Sarai, but Sarah shall be her name."</p>

<p class="v">16. "And I will bless her, and I will give you a son by her, and I will bless him, and he shall become a nation, and kings of nations shall come forth from him."</p>

<p class="v">17. And Abraham fell on his face and rejoiced, and said in his heart, "Shall a son be born to him who is a hundred years old, and shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?"</p>

<p class="v">18. And Abraham said to God, "O that Ishmael might live before you!"</p>

<p class="v">19. And God said, "Yes, and Sarah too shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac, and I will establish my covenant with him, an everlasting covenant, and for his posterity after him."</p>

<p class="v">20. "And as for Ishmael also, I have heard you, and behold, I will bless him, and make him great, and multiply him exceedingly, and he shall beget twelve princes, and I will make him a great nation."</p>

<p class="v">21. "But I will establish my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah shall bear you, at this season, next year."</p>

<p class="v">22. And he ceased speaking with him, and God went up from Abraham.</p>

<p class="v">23. And Abraham did as God had told him, and he took Ishmael his son, and all who were born in his house and whom he had bought with his money, all the males of his house, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin.</p>

<p class="v">24. And on that very day Abraham was circumcised, and all the men of his house, and those born in the house, and all whom he had bought with money from the children of the stranger, were circumcised with him.</p>

<p class="v">25. This law is for all generations forever, and there is no circumcising of days, nor omitting a single day out of the eight days; for it is an everlasting ordinance, ordained and written on the heavenly tablets.</p>

<p class="v">26. And whoever is born, the flesh of whose foreskin is not circumcised on the eighth day, does not belong to the children of the covenant that the LORD made with Abraham, but to the children of destruction; and there is no sign on him that he belongs to the Lord, but he is destined to be destroyed and slain from the earth, and to be rooted out of the earth, for he has broken the covenant of the LORD our God.</p>

<p class="v">27. For all the angels of the presence and all the angels of sanctification were created thus from the day of their creation, and before the angels of the presence and the angels of sanctification he sanctified Israel, that they might be with him and with his holy angels.</p>

<p class="v">28. And you shall command the children of Israel, and they shall observe the sign of this covenant throughout their generations as an everlasting ordinance, and they shall not be rooted out of the land.</p>

<p class="v">29. For the commandment is ordained as a covenant, that they should observe it forever among all the children of Israel.</p>

<p class="v">30. As for Ishmael, and his sons, and his brothers, and Esau, the LORD did not bring them near, and he did not choose them merely because they are children of Abraham, because he knew them, but he chose Israel to be his people.</p>

<p class="v">31. And he sanctified them, and gathered them from among all the children of men; for there are many nations and many peoples, and they all belong to him, and over all of them he has set spirits with authority to lead them astray from him.</p>

<p class="v">32. But over Israel he set no angel or spirit, for he alone is their ruler, and he will preserve them and require them at the hand of his angels and his spirits, and at the hand of all his powers, so that he may preserve them and bless them, and that they may be his and he theirs from now on and forever.</p>

<p class="v">33. And now I announce to you that the children of Israel will not remain faithful to this ordinance, and they will not circumcise their sons according to all this law; for in the very flesh of their circumcision they will omit this circumcision of their sons, and all of them, sons of Beliar, will leave their sons uncircumcised as they were born.</p>

<p class="v">34. And there will be great wrath from the LORD against the children of Israel, because they have forsaken his covenant, and turned away from his word, and provoked and blasphemed, inasmuch as they do not observe the ordinance of this law; for they have treated their members like the Gentiles, so that they may be expelled and rooted out of the land. And there will be no more forgiveness for them [so that there may be pardon and forgiveness] for all the sin of this eternal error.</p>

### Chapter 16 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Angels appear to Abraham at Hebron, and Isaac again promised, 1-4. Destruction of Sodom, and deliverance of Lot, 5-9. Abraham at Beersheba: birth and circumcision of Isaac, whose posterity was to be God's portion, 10-19. Institution of the feast of Tabernacles, 20-31. (Cf. Gen. xviii.1, 10, 12; xix.24, 29, 33-7; xx.1, 4, 8; xxi.1-4.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And at the new moon of the fourth month we appeared to Abraham, at the oak of Mamre, and we spoke with him, and we announced to him that a son would be given to him by Sarah his wife.</p>

<p class="v">2. And Sarah laughed, for she had heard that we had spoken these words with Abraham, and we reproved her, and she was afraid and denied that she had laughed at these words.</p>

<p class="v">3. And we told her the name of her son, as his name is ordained and written on the heavenly tablets, namely Isaac,</p>

<p class="v">4. And that when we returned to her at an appointed time, she would have conceived a son.</p>

<p class="v">5. And in this month the LORD executed his judgments upon Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Zeboim, and all the region of the Jordan, and he burned them with fire and brimstone, and destroyed them, as they are to this day, just as [lo] I have declared to you all their works, that they are wicked and exceedingly sinful, that they defile themselves and commit fornication in their flesh, and commit impurity upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">6. And in the same way, God will execute judgment upon the places where men have acted according to the impurity of the Sodomites, as with the judgment of Sodom.</p>

<p class="v">7. But Lot we saved, for God remembered Abraham, and sent him out from the midst of the overthrow.</p>

<p class="v">8. And he and his daughters committed upon the earth a sin such as had not been on the earth from the days of Adam until his time, for the man lay with his daughters.</p>

<p class="v">9. And behold, it was commanded and engraved concerning all his posterity, on the heavenly tablets, that they should be removed and rooted out, and that a judgment should be executed upon them like the judgment of Sodom, and that no posterity of that man should be left on earth on the day of condemnation.</p>

<p class="v">10. And in that month, Abraham departed from Hebron, and went and dwelt between Kadesh and Shur, in the mountains of Gerar.</p>

<p class="v">11. And in the middle of the fifth month, he departed from there and dwelt at the well of the Oath.</p>

<p class="v">12. And in the middle of the sixth month, the LORD visited Sarah and did for her as he had said, and she conceived.</p>

<p class="v">13. And she bore a son in the third month, and in the middle of the month, at the time of which the LORD had spoken to Abraham, at the feast of the firstfruits of the harvest, Isaac was born.</p>

<p class="v">14. And Abraham circumcised his son on the eighth day: he was the first to be circumcised according to the covenant that is established forever.</p>

<p class="v">15. And in the sixth year of the fourth week, we came to Abraham, at the well of the Oath, and we appeared to him [as we had told Sarah that we would return to her, and that she would have conceived a son.</p>

<p class="v">16. And we returned in the seventh month, and found Sarah with child before us] and we blessed him, and announced to him all the things that had been decreed concerning him: that he should not die until he had begotten six more sons, and should see them before he died; but that in Isaac his name and his posterity should be called:</p>

<p class="v">17. And that all the posterity of his other sons should be Gentiles, and should be counted with the Gentiles; but of the sons of Isaac, one alone should become a holy posterity, and should not be counted among the Gentiles.</p>

<p class="v">18. For he was to become the portion of the Most High, and all his posterity had fallen into the possession of God, that it might become for the LORD a people for his own possession above all the nations, and that it might become a kingdom and priests and a holy nation.</p>

<p class="v">19. And we departed, and announced to Sarah all that we had told him, and they both rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.</p>

<p class="v">20. And he built there an altar to the LORD who had delivered him and who was making him rejoice in the land of his sojourning, and he celebrated a feast of joy in this month, seven days, near the altar that he had built at the well of the Oath.</p>

<p class="v">21. And he built tents for himself and for his servants at this feast, and he was the first to celebrate the feast of tabernacles upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">22. And during these seven days he brought to the altar each day a burnt offering to the LORD, two oxen, two rams, seven sheep, and one goat, as a sin offering, that he might thereby atone for himself and for his seed.</p>

<p class="v">23. And as a thank offering, seven rams, seven kids, seven sheep, and seven goats, and their fruit offerings and their drink offerings; and he burned all the fat upon the altar, a choice offering to the LORD, of a pleasing odor.</p>

<p class="v">24. And morning and evening he burned fragrant substances, frankincense and galbanum, and stacte, and nard, and myrrh, and spices, and costum; he offered all these seven, crushed, mixed together in equal parts, and pure.</p>

<p class="v">25. And he celebrated this feast for seven days, rejoicing with all his heart and with all his soul, he and all who were in his house, and there was no stranger with him, nor anyone uncircumcised.</p>

<p class="v">26. And he blessed his Creator, who had made him in his generation, for he had made him according to his good pleasure; for he knew and understood that from him would be born the plant of righteousness for the eternal generations, and from him a holy seed, that it might become like him who had made all things.</p>

<p class="v">27. And he blessed and rejoiced, and he called this feast by the name of the feast of the Lord, a joy pleasing to God Most High.</p>

<p class="v">28. And we blessed him forever, and all his posterity after him, throughout all the generations of the earth, because he celebrated this feast in its season, according to the testimony of the heavenly tablets.</p>

<p class="v">29. Therefore it is written on the heavenly tablets concerning Israel, that they shall celebrate the feast of tabernacles with joy for seven days, in the seventh month, which shall be pleasing before the LORD, a perpetual statute for their generations, every year.</p>

<p class="v">30. And for this there is no limit of days; for it is ordained forever for Israel that they should celebrate it, and dwell in tents, and set crowns upon their heads, and take leafy boughs and willows from the brook.</p>

<p class="v">31. And Abraham took branches of palm trees, and the fruit of good trees, and each day, going around the altar with the branches seven times a day in the morning, he praised and gave thanks to his God for everything, with joy.</p>

### Chapter 17 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Expulsion of Hagar and Ishmael, 1-14. Mastêmâ proposes that God require Abraham to sacrifice Isaac, in order to test his love and obedience: the ten trials of Abraham, 15-18. (Cf. Gen. xxi.8-21.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the first year of the fifth week, Isaac was weaned in this jubilee, [1982 AM] and Abraham made a great feast in the third month, on the day his son Isaac was weaned.</p>

<p class="v">2. And Ishmael, son of Hagar the Egyptian, was before Abraham his father, in his place, and Abraham rejoiced and blessed God because he had seen his sons and had not died childless.</p>

<p class="v">3. And he remembered the words that had been spoken to him on the day Lot separated from him, and he rejoiced because the LORD had given him seed upon the earth to inherit the land, and he blessed with all his mouth the Creator of all things.</p>

<p class="v">4. And Sarah saw Ishmael playing and dancing, and Abraham rejoicing with great joy, and she became jealous of Ishmael, and said to Abraham, "Drive out this handmaid and her son, for the son of this handmaid shall not inherit with my son Isaac."</p>

<p class="v">5. And the matter was grievous in Abraham's sight, on account of his handmaid and on account of his son, that he should drive them away from him.</p>

<p class="v">6. And God said to Abraham, "Do not let it be grievous to you on account of the child and the handmaid; in all that Sarah has said to you, listen to her words and do them, for it is in Isaac that your name and your posterity shall be called."</p>

<p class="v">7. "But as for the son of this handmaid, I will make of him a great nation, for he is of your posterity."</p>

<p class="v">8. And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread and a bottle of water, and placed them on the shoulders of Hagar and the child, and sent her away.</p>

<p class="v">9. And she departed and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba, and the water in the bottle was spent, and the child was thirsty, and could go no further, and fell down.</p>

<p class="v">10. And his mother took him and cast him under an olive tree, and went and sat down over against him, a bowshot away; for she said, "Let me not see the death of my child," and as she sat, she wept.</p>

<p class="v">11. And an angel of God, one of the holy ones, said to her, "Why do you weep, Hagar? Arise, take the child and hold him in your hand, for God has heard your voice, and has seen the child."</p>

<p class="v">12. And she opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water, and she went and filled her skin with water, and gave her child a drink, and she rose up and went on toward the wilderness of Paran.</p>

<p class="v">13. And the child grew and became an archer, and God was with him, and his mother took him a wife from among the daughters of Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">14. And she bore him a son, and he called his name Nebaioth; for she said, "The LORD was near me when I called upon him."</p>

<p class="v">15. And it came to pass, in the seventh week, in the first year of it, [2003 AM] in the first month of this jubilee, on the twelfth day of this month, that there were voices in heaven concerning Abraham, that he was faithful in all that he had been told, and that he loved the Lord, and that in every affliction he was faithful.</p>

<p class="v">16. And the prince Mastêmâ came and said before God, "Behold, Abraham loves Isaac his son, and delights in him above all else; command him to offer him as a burnt offering upon the altar, and you shall see whether he will carry out this command, and you shall know whether he is faithful in everything in which you test him."</p>

<p class="v">17. And the LORD knew that Abraham was faithful in all his afflictions; for he had tested him through his country and through famine, and he had tested him through the riches of kings, and he had tested him again through his wife, when she was taken from him, and through circumcision; and he had tested him through Ishmael and Hagar his handmaid, when he sent them away.</p>

<p class="v">18. And in everything with which he had tested him, he was found faithful, and his soul was not impatient, nor was he slow to act; for he was faithful, and a friend of the Lord.</p>
### Chapter 18 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">The sacrifice of Isaac: Mastêmâ put to shame, 1-13. Abraham blessed anew: returns to Beer Sheba, 14-19. (Cf. Gen. XXII. 1-19.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And God said to him, "Abraham, Abraham"; and he said, "Here I am."</p>

<p class="v">2. And He said, "Take your beloved son whom you love, Isaac, and go into the heights, and offer him upon one of the mountains that I will show you."</p>

<p class="v">3. And he rose early in the morning and saddled his donkey, and took with him his two young men and Isaac his son, and he split the wood for the burnt offering, and he came to the place on the third day, and he saw the place from afar.</p>

<p class="v">4. And he came to a well of water, and he said to his young men, "Remain here with the donkey, and I and the boy will go (yonder), and when we have worshiped, we will return to you."</p>

<p class="v">5. And he took the wood for the burnt offering and laid it upon Isaac his son, and he took in his hand the fire and the knife, and the two of them went together to that place.</p>

<p class="v">6. And Isaac said to his father, "Father"; and he said, "Here I am, my son." And he said to him, "Here is the fire, the knife, and the wood; but where is the sheep for the burnt offering, father?"</p>

<p class="v">7. And he said, "God will provide himself a sheep for the burnt offering, my son." And he drew near to the place of the mountain of God.</p>

<p class="v">8. And he built an altar, and laid the wood upon the altar, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him upon the wood that was upon the altar, and stretched out his hand to take the knife to slay Isaac his son.</p>

<p class="v">9. And I stood before him, and before the prince Mastêmâ, and the LORD said, "Tell him not to lay his hand upon the child, nor to do anything to him, for I have shown that he fears the LORD."</p>

<p class="v">10. And I called to him from heaven, and said to him, "Abraham, Abraham"; and he was terrified and said, "Here I am."</p>

<p class="v">11. And I said to him, "Do not lay your hand upon the child, and do nothing to him; for now I have shown that you fear the LORD, and that you have not refused me your son, your firstborn."</p>

<p class="v">12. And the prince Mastêmâ was put to shame; and Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a ram was caught . . . by its horns, and Abraham went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.</p>

<p class="v">13. And Abraham called that place "The LORD Has Seen," so that it is said, on the mountain the LORD has seen: that is Mount Zion.</p>

<p class="v">14. And the Lord called Abraham by his name a second time from heaven, as He made us appear to speak to him in the name of the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">15. And He said, "I have sworn by myself," says the LORD,</p>

<p class="v">"Because you have done this thing,</p>

<p class="v">And you have not refused me your son, your beloved son,</p>

<p class="v">That in blessing I will bless you,</p>

<p class="v">And in multiplying I will multiply your seed</p>

<p class="v">As the stars of heaven, and as the sand that is on the shore of the sea.</p>

<p class="v">And your posterity shall inherit the cities of its enemies,</p>

<p class="v">16. And in your posterity shall all the nations of the earth be blessed;</p>

<p class="v">Because you have obeyed my voice,</p>

<p class="v">And I have shown to all that you are faithful to me in everything I have told you:</p>

<p class="v">Go in peace."</p>

<p class="v">17. And Abraham went to his young men, and they rose up and went together to Beer Sheba, and Abraham [2010 AM] dwelt near the Well of the Oath.</p>

<p class="v">18. And he celebrated this feast every year, seven days with joy, and he called it the feast of the Lord according to the seven days during which he went and returned in peace.</p>

<p class="v">19. And accordingly it was ordained and written on the heavenly tablets concerning Israel and its posterity that they should observe this feast for seven days with the joy of the feast.</p>

### Chapter 19 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Abraham's return to Hebron. Death and burial of Sarah, 1-9. Marriage of Isaac and second marriage of Abraham. Birth of Esau and Jacob, 10-14. Abraham commends Jacob to Rebecca and blesses him, 15-31. (Cf. Gen. xxiii.1-4, 11-16; xxiv.15; xxv.1-2, 25-7; xiii. 16.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the first year of the first week of the forty-second jubilee, Abraham returned and dwelt opposite Hebron, which is Kirjath Arba, for two weeks of years.</p>

<p class="v">2. And in the first year of the third week of this jubilee, the days of Sarah's life were fulfilled, and she died at Hebron.</p>

<p class="v">3. And Abraham went to mourn for her and buried her, and we tried [to see] whether his spirit was patient and whether he was not indignant in the words of his mouth; and he was found patient in this and was not troubled.</p>

<p class="v">4. For with patience of spirit he conferred with the children of Heth, to the intent that they should give him a place in which to bury his dead.</p>

<p class="v">5. And the LORD gave him favor before all who saw him, and he besought the sons of Heth gently, and they gave him the land of the double cave, opposite Mamre, that is, Hebron, for four hundred pieces of silver.</p>

<p class="v">6. And they besought him, saying, "We will give it to you for nothing"; but he would not take it from them for nothing, for he gave them the price of the place, the money in full, and he bowed down before them twice, and after that he buried his dead in the double cave.</p>

<p class="v">7. And all the days of Sarah's life were one hundred and twenty-seven years, that is, two jubilees and four weeks and one year: these are the days of the years of Sarah's life.</p>

<p class="v">8. This is the tenth trial by which Abraham was tried, and he was found faithful, patient in spirit.</p>

<p class="v">9. And he did not say a single word concerning the rumor that went about in the land, that God had said He would give it to him and to his posterity after him, and he asked there for a place to bury his dead; for he was found faithful and was recorded on the heavenly tablets as the friend of God.</p>

<p class="v">10. And in the fourth year of this, he took a wife for his son Isaac, and she was called Rebecca [2020 AM] [the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor, the brother of Abraham], the sister of Laban and the daughter of Bethuel; and Bethuel was the son of Melca, who was the wife of Nahor, the brother of Abraham.</p>

<p class="v">11. And Abraham took a third wife, and she was called Keturah, from among the daughters of his servants, for Hagar had died before Sarah. And she bore him six sons, Zimram, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah, in two weeks of years.</p>

<p class="v">12. And in the sixth week, in the second year, Rebecca bore to Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau,</p>

<p class="v">13. and [2046 AM] Jacob was a smooth and upright man, and Esau was fierce, a man of the field and hairy, and Jacob dwelt in tents.</p>

<p class="v">14. And the young men grew, and Jacob learned to write; but Esau did not learn it, for he was a man of the field and a hunter, and he learned war, and all his deeds were fierce.</p>

<p class="v">15. And Abraham loved Jacob, but Isaac loved Esau.</p>

<p class="v">16. And Abraham saw the deeds of Esau, and he knew that it was in Jacob that his name and his posterity would be called; and he called Rebecca and gave her commandments concerning Jacob, for he knew that she (too) loved Jacob much more than Esau.</p>

<p class="v">17. And he said to her:</p>

<p class="v">My daughter, watch over my son Jacob,</p>

<p class="v">For he shall be in my place on the earth,</p>

<p class="v">And for a blessing in the midst of the children of men,</p>

<p class="v">And for the glory of all the posterity of Shem.</p>

<p class="v">18. For I know that the Lord will choose him to be His people of possession, above all the peoples that are upon the face of the earth.</p>

<p class="v">19. And behold, Isaac my son loves Esau more than Jacob, but I see that you truly love Jacob.</p>

<p class="v">20. Increase yet more your kindness toward him,</p>

<p class="v">And let your eyes be upon him with love;</p>

<p class="v">For he shall be henceforth to us a blessing on the earth and for all the generations of the earth.</p>

<p class="v">21. Let your hands be strong</p>

<p class="v">And let your heart rejoice in your son Jacob;</p>

<p class="v">For I have loved him far more than all my sons.</p>

<p class="v">He shall be blessed for ever,</p>

<p class="v">And his seed shall fill the whole earth.</p>

<p class="v">22. If a man can number the sand of the earth,</p>

<p class="v">His posterity also shall be numbered.</p>

<p class="v">23. And all the blessings with which the LORD has blessed me and my posterity shall belong forever to Jacob and to his posterity.</p>

<p class="v">24. And in his posterity my name shall be blessed, and the name of my fathers, Shem, and Noah, and Enoch, and Mahalalel, and Enos, and Seth, and Adam.</p>

<p class="v">25. And these shall serve</p>

<p class="v">To lay the foundations of heaven,</p>

<p class="v">And to strengthen the earth,</p>

<p class="v">And to renew all the lights that are in the firmament.</p>

<p class="v">26. And he called Jacob before the eyes of Rebecca his mother, and kissed him, and blessed him, and said:</p>

<p class="v">27. "Jacob, my beloved son, whom my soul loves, may God bless you from the height of the firmament, and may He give you all the blessings with which He blessed Adam, Enoch, Noah, and Shem; and all that He has told me, and all that He has promised to give me, may He make it cleave to you and to your posterity forever, according to the days of heaven above the earth.</p>

<p class="v">28. "And the spirits of Mastêmâ shall not rule over you nor over your posterity to turn you away from the Lord, who is your God henceforth and forever."</p>

<p class="v">29. "And may the Lord God be to you, and you, the firstborn son, a father, and to the people forever."</p>

<p class="v">30. "Go in peace, my son." And the two of them went out together from Abraham.</p>

<p class="v">31. And Rebecca loved Jacob with all her heart and with all her soul, far more than Esau; but Isaac loved Esau far more than Jacob.</p>

### Chapter 20 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Abraham exhorts his sons and the sons of his sons to practice righteousness, to observe circumcision, and to abstain from uncleanness and idolatry, 1-10. Sends them away with gifts, 11. Dwellings of the Ishmaelites and the sons of Keturah, 12-13. (Cf. Gen. XXV. 5-6.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the forty-second jubilee, in the first year of the seventh week, Abraham called Ishmael, [2052 (2045?) AM] and his twelve sons, and Isaac and his two sons, and the six sons of Keturah, and their sons.</p>

<p class="v">2. And he commanded them to observe the way of the Lord; that they should practice righteousness, love each his neighbor, and act in this way among all men; so that each of them should walk in such a manner toward the others as to exercise judgment and righteousness on the earth.</p>

<p class="v">3. That they should circumcise their sons, according to the covenant which He had made with them, and that they should not turn aside to the right or to the left from all the paths that the LORD had commanded us; and that we should keep ourselves from all fornication and uncleanness, [and renounce among us all fornication and uncleanness].</p>

<p class="v">4. And if a woman or a maidservant among you gives herself to fornication, burn her with fire, and let her not commit fornication with him according to their eyes and their heart; and let them not take for wives the daughters of Canaan; for the seed of Canaan shall be rooted out of the land.</p>

<p class="v">5. And he told them of the judgment of the giants and the judgment of the Sodomites, how they had been judged because of their wickedness and had died because of their fornication, their uncleanness, and their mutual corruption through fornication.</p>

<p class="v">6. "And keep yourselves from all fornication and uncleanness,</p>

<p class="v">And from all pollution of sin,</p>

<p class="v">Lest you make our name a curse,</p>

<p class="v">And your whole life a hissing,</p>

<p class="v">And all your sons be destroyed by the sword,</p>

<p class="v">And you become accursed like Sodom,</p>

<p class="v">And all your remnant like the sons of Gomorrah.</p>

<p class="v">7. I beg you, my sons, love the God of heaven</p>

<p class="v">And cleave to all His commandments.</p>

<p class="v">And do not walk after their idols and after their uncleannesses,</p>

<p class="v">8. And do not make for yourselves gods of cast or graven metal;</p>

<p class="v">For they are vanity,</p>

<p class="v">And there is no spirit in them;</p>

<p class="v">For they are the work of (men's) hands,</p>

<p class="v">And all who trust in them trust in nothing.</p>

<p class="v">9. Do not serve them and do not worship them,</p>

<p class="v">But serve God Most High and worship Him continually:</p>

<p class="v">And hope always in His face,</p>

<p class="v">And practice integrity and righteousness before Him,</p>

<p class="v">That He may take pleasure in you and grant you His mercy,</p>

<p class="v">And send rain upon you morning and evening,</p>

<p class="v">And bless all your works that you have done on the earth,</p>

<p class="v">And bless your bread and your water,</p>

<p class="v">And bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your land,</p>

<p class="v">And the herds of your cattle and the flocks of your sheep.</p>

<p class="v">10. And you shall be a blessing on the earth,</p>

<p class="v">And all the nations of the earth shall desire you,</p>

<p class="v">And bless your sons in my name,</p>

<p class="v">That they may be blessed as I am.</p>

<p class="v">11. And he gave to Ishmael and his sons, and to the sons of Keturah, gifts, and sent them away from Isaac his son, and he gave everything to Isaac his son.</p>

<p class="v">12. And Ishmael and his sons, and the sons of Keturah and their sons, went away together and dwelt from Paran to the entrance of Babylon, in all the land that is toward the east, facing the desert.</p>

<p class="v">13. And these mingled with one another, and their name was called Arabs and Ishmaelites.</p>

### Chapter 21 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">The last words of Abraham to Isaac concerning idolatry, the eating of blood, the offering of various sacrifices, and the use of salt, 1-11. Also concerning the wood to be used for sacrifice and the duty of washing before sacrifice and covering the blood, etc., 12-25.</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the sixth year of the seventh week of this jubilee, Abraham called Isaac his son, and [2057 (2050?) AM] commanded him, saying, "I have grown old, and I do not know the day of my death, and I am full of my days.</p>

<p class="v">2. "And behold, I am one hundred and seventy-five years old, and throughout all the days of my life I have remembered the Lord and sought with all my heart to do His will and to walk uprightly in all His ways."</p>

<p class="v">3. "My soul has hated idols (and I have despised those who served them, and I have given my heart and my spirit) so that I might do the will of Him who created me."</p>

<p class="v">4. "For He is the living God, and He is holy and faithful, and He is righteous above all, and with Him there is no acceptance of persons (of men) nor any acceptance of gifts; for God is righteous and He executes His judgment upon all who transgress His commandments and despise His covenant.</p>

<p class="v">5. "And you, my son, observe His commandments, His ordinances, and His judgments, and do not walk after abominations, nor after graven images, nor after molten images.</p>

<p class="v">6. "And do not eat any blood of animals, nor of cattle, nor of any bird that flies in the sky.</p>

<p class="v">7. "And if you kill a victim as a pleasing peace offering, kill it and pour its blood upon the altar, and all the fat of the offering upon the altar with fine flour and the meal offering mingled with oil and its drink offering — offer them all together upon the altar of burnt offerings; it is a sweet savor before the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">8. "And you shall offer the fat of the thank offering upon the fire that is on the altar, and the fat that is on the belly, and all the fat of the entrails and of the two kidneys, and all the fat that is upon them, and you shall remove the loins and the liver together with the kidneys.</p>

<p class="v">9. "And offer all this, of pleasing odor, acceptable before the LORD, with its meal offering and with its drink offering, of pleasing odor, the bread of the offering to the LORD."</p>

<p class="v">10. And eat its flesh on that day and on the second day, and let not the sun go down upon it on the second day until it is eaten, and let nothing remain for the third day; for it is not acceptable [for it is not approved], and let none eat of it any more, and all who eat of it shall bring sin upon themselves; for thus have I found it written in the books of my forefathers, in the words of Enoch and in the words of Noah.</p>

<p class="v">11. "And you shall sprinkle salt upon all your oblations, and let not the salt of the covenant be lacking from all your oblations before the LORD.</p>

<p class="v">12. "And as for the wood for the sacrifices, take heed that you bring no (other) wood for the altar besides these: cypress, laurel, almond, fir, pine, cedar, savin, fig, olive, myrrh, laurel, aspalathus.</p>

<p class="v">13. "And lay upon the altar, under the sacrifice, these kinds of wood whose appearance has been tested, and do not lay upon it split or dark wood, (but) hard and clean wood, without blemish, of sound and new growth; and do not lay old wood upon it, [for its fragrance is gone] for there is no longer any fragrance in it as before.</p>

<p class="v">14. "Besides these kinds of wood there is no other that you shall place (upon the altar), for its fragrance is dispersed, and the odor of its fragrance does not rise to heaven.</p>

<p class="v">15. "Observe this commandment and do it, my son, that you may be upright in all your actions.</p>

<p class="v">16. And be at all times pure in your body, and wash yourself with water before you approach to offer upon the altar, and wash your hands and your feet before you approach the altar; and when you have finished sacrificing, wash your hands and your feet again.</p>

<p class="v">17. "And let no blood appear upon you or upon your garments; be on your guard, my son, against blood, be exceedingly on your guard; cover it with dust.</p>

<p class="v">18. "And do not eat blood, for it is the soul; do not eat blood at all.</p>

<p class="v">19. "And do not accept gifts for the blood of man, lest it be shed unpunished, without judgment; for it is shed blood that makes the earth sin, and the earth cannot be cleansed of the blood of man except by the blood of him who shed it.</p>

<p class="v">20. "And do not accept any gift or present for the blood of man: blood for blood, that you may be accepted before the LORD, God Most High; for He is the defense of the good, and that you may be preserved from all evil, and that He may save you from every kind of death.</p>

<p class="v">21. I see, my son,</p>

<p class="v">That all the works of the children of men are sin and wickedness,</p>

<p class="v">And all their deeds are uncleanness, abomination, and defilement,</p>

<p class="v">And there is no righteousness in them.</p>

<p class="v">22. Take heed, lest you walk in their ways</p>

<p class="v">And tread their paths,</p>

<p class="v">And sin a sin unto death before God Most High.</p>

<p class="v">Otherwise He will hide His face from you</p>

<p class="v">[And] give you over into the hands of your transgression,</p>

<p class="v">And I will root you out of the land, and your seed from under the heavens,</p>

<p class="v">And your name and your posterity will perish from all the earth.</p>

<p class="v">23. Turn away from all their deeds and from all their uncleannesses,</p>

<p class="v">And observe the ordinance of God Most High,</p>

<p class="v">And do His will and be upright in all things.</p>

<p class="v">24. And He will bless you in all your deeds,</p>

<p class="v">And will cause to spring from you a plant of righteousness on all the earth, in all the generations of the earth,</p>

<p class="v">And my name and your name will not be forgotten forever under heaven.</p>

<p class="v">25. Go, my son, in peace.</p>

<p class="v">May God Most High, my God and your God, strengthen you to do His will,</p>

<p class="v">And may He bless all your posterity and the remnant of your posterity for all generations and forever, with all righteous blessings,</p>

<p class="v">That you may be a blessing on all the earth.</p>

<p class="v">26. And he went out from his presence rejoicing.</p>

### Chapter 22 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Isaac, Ishmael, and Jacob celebrate the feast of first fruits at Beer Sheba with Abraham, 1-5. Abraham's prayer, 6-9. The last words of Abraham and the blessings of Jacob, 10-30.</p>

<p class="v">1. And it came to pass in the first week of the forty-fourth jubilee, in the second year, that is, the year in which Abraham died, that Isaac and Ishmael came out from the Well of the Oath to celebrate the feast of weeks, that is, the feast of the first fruits of the harvest, with Abraham their father, and Abraham rejoiced because his two sons had come.</p>

<p class="v">2. For Isaac had many possessions at Beer Sheba, and Isaac was accustomed to go and see his possessions and return to his father.</p>

<p class="v">3. And in those days Ishmael came to see his father, and the two of them gathered together, and Isaac offered a burnt sacrifice, and presented it upon the altar of his father which he had made at Hebron.</p>

<p class="v">4. And he offered a thank offering and made a joyful feast before Ishmael his brother. And Rebecca made new cakes with the new grain, and gave them to Jacob her son to bring to Abraham his father, from the first fruits of the land, that he might eat and bless the Creator of all things before his death.</p>

<p class="v">5. And Isaac also sent by the hand of Jacob to Abraham a better thank offering, that he might eat and drink.</p>

<p class="v">6. And he ate and drank, and blessed God Most High,</p>

<p class="v">Who created heaven and earth,</p>

<p class="v">Who created all the fatness of the earth,</p>

<p class="v">And gave it to the children of men</p>

<p class="v">That they might eat and drink and bless their Creator.</p>

<p class="v">7. "And now I give You thanks, my God, because You have let me see this day: behold, I am one hundred and seventy-five years old, an old man and full of days, and all my days peace has been granted me.</p>

<p class="v">8. "The sword of the adversary has not overcome me in all that You have given me and to my children, all the days of my life until this day.</p>

<p class="v">9. "My God, may Your mercy and Your peace be upon Your servant and upon the posterity of his sons, that they may be for You a chosen nation and an inheritance among all the nations of the earth, henceforth for all the days of the generations of the earth, unto all ages.</p>

<p class="v">10. And he called Jacob and said, "My son Jacob, may the God of all bless you and strengthen you to do righteousness and His will before Him, and may He choose you and your posterity, that you may become a people for His inheritance according to His will forever.</p>

<p class="v">11. "And you, my son Jacob, come near and kiss me." And he came near and kissed him, and he said:</p>

<p class="v">'Blessed be my son Jacob</p>

<p class="v">And all the sons of God Most High, throughout all ages:</p>

<p class="v">May God give you a seed of righteousness;</p>

<p class="v">And may He sanctify some of your sons in the midst of all the earth;</p>

<p class="v">May the nations serve you,</p>

<p class="v">And all the nations bow down before your posterity.</p>

<p class="v">12. Be strong before men,</p>

<p class="v">And exercise your authority over all the posterity of Seth.</p>

<p class="v">So shall your ways and those of your sons be justified,</p>

<p class="v">That they may become a holy nation.</p>

<p class="v">13. May God Most High give you all the blessings</p>

<p class="v">With which He blessed me</p>

<p class="v">And with which He blessed Noah and Adam;</p>

<p class="v">May they rest upon the sacred head of your seed from generation to generation forever.</p>

<p class="v">14. And may He cleanse you from all unrighteousness and all uncleanness,</p>

<p class="v">That all your transgressions may be forgiven you, which you have committed through ignorance.</p>

<p class="v">And may He strengthen you,</p>

<p class="v">And bless you.</p>

<p class="v">And may you inherit all the earth,</p>

<p class="v">15. And may He renew His covenant with you,</p>

<p class="v">That you may be to Him a nation for His inheritance for all ages,</p>

<p class="v">And that He may be to you and to your posterity a God in truth and righteousness throughout all the days of the earth.</p>

<p class="v">16. And you, my son Jacob, remember my words,</p>

<p class="v">And observe the commandments of Abraham your father:</p>

<p class="v">Separate yourself from the nations,</p>

<p class="v">And do not eat with them:</p>

<p class="v">And do not act according to their works,</p>

<p class="v">And do not become their associate;</p>

<p class="v">For their works are unclean,</p>

<p class="v">And all their ways are a pollution, an abomination, and an uncleanness.</p>

<p class="v">17. They offer their sacrifices to the dead</p>

<p class="v">And they worship evil spirits,</p>

<p class="v">And they eat upon the graves,</p>

<p class="v">And all their works are but vanity and nothingness.</p>

<p class="v">18. They have no heart to understand</p>

<p class="v">And their eyes do not see what their works are,</p>

<p class="v">And how they err in saying to a piece of wood, "You are my god,"</p>

<p class="v">And to a stone, "You are my lord and you are my deliverer."</p>

<p class="v">[And they have no heart.]</p>

<p class="v">19. And as for you, my son Jacob,</p>

<p class="v">May God Most High help you</p>

<p class="v">And may the God of heaven bless you</p>

<p class="v">And turn you away from their uncleanness and from all their error.</p>

<p class="v">20. Beware, my son Jacob, of taking a wife from any posterity of the daughters of Canaan;</p>

<p class="v">For all its seed is to be rooted out of the earth.</p>

<p class="v">21. For, because of the transgression of Ham, Canaan went astray,</p>

<p class="v">And all his seed shall be destroyed from off the earth, and all that remains of it,</p>

<p class="v">And none of his descendants shall be saved in the day of judgment.</p>

<p class="v">22. And as for all worshipers of idols and the profane</p>

<p class="v">(b) There shall be no hope for them in the land of the living;</p>

<p class="v">(c) And there shall be no remembrance of them on the earth;</p>

<p class="v">(c) For they shall go down into Sheol,</p>

<p class="v">(d) And they shall go to the place of condemnation,</p>

<p class="v">As the children of Sodom were taken away from the earth</p>

<p class="v">So shall all who worship idols be driven out.</p>

<p class="v">23. Fear nothing, my son Jacob,</p>

<p class="v">And be not afraid, O son of Abraham!</p>

<p class="v">May God Most High preserve you from destruction,</p>

<p class="v">And from all the paths of error, may He deliver you.</p>

<p class="v">24. "I built this house for myself, that I might set my name upon it on the earth: [it is given to you and to your posterity forever], and it shall be called the house of Abraham; it is given to you and to your posterity forever; for you shall build my house and establish my name before God forever: your posterity and your name shall endure through all the generations of the earth.</p>

<p class="v">25. And he ceased commanding him and blessing him.</p>

<p class="v">26. And the two of them lay down together upon one bed, and Jacob slept in the bosom of Abraham, his father's father, and he kissed him seven times, and his affection and his heart rejoiced over him.</p>

<p class="v">27. And he blessed him with all his heart and said, "God Most High, the God of all and the Creator of all, who brought me out of Ur of the Chaldees that He might give me this land to inherit it forever, and that I might establish a holy seed, blessed be the Most High forever.</p>

<p class="v">28. And he blessed Jacob and said, "My son, for whom I rejoice with all my heart and with all my affection, may your grace and your mercy rest forever upon him and upon his posterity.</p>

<p class="v">29. "And do not abandon him, and do not despise him henceforth unto the days of eternity, and let your eyes be open upon him and upon his posterity, that you may preserve him, bless him, and sanctify him as a nation for your inheritance;</p>

<p class="v">30. "And bless him with all your blessings from henceforth unto all the days of eternity, and renew your covenant and your grace with him and with his posterity according to all your good pleasure for all the generations of the earth."</p>

### Chapter 23 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">The death and burial of Abraham, 1-8 (cf. Gen. xxv.7-10). Decreasing years and increasing corruption of mankind: the messianic woes: universal strife: the faithful rise in arms to bring back the unfaithful: Israel invaded by the sinners of the Gentiles, 11-25. Renewed study of the law and renewal of mankind: the messianic kingdom: the blessed immortality of the righteous, 26-31.</p>

<p class="v">1. And he placed two fingers of Jacob upon his eyes, and he blessed the God of gods, and he covered his face and stretched out his feet and slept the sleep of eternity, and was gathered to his fathers.</p>

<p class="v">2. And through all this, Jacob lay in his bosom, and did not know that Abraham, his father's father, was dead.</p>

<p class="v">3. And Jacob awoke from his sleep, and behold, Abraham was cold as ice, and he said, "Father, father"; but no one spoke, and he knew that he was dead.</p>

<p class="v">4. And he rose from his bosom and ran to tell Rebecca his mother; and Rebecca went to Isaac in the night and told him what was happening. And they went together, and Jacob with them, and he had a lamp in his hand, and when they had entered, they found Abraham dead.</p>

<p class="v">5. And Isaac fell upon his father's face, wept, and kissed him.</p>

<p class="v">6. And voices were heard in the house of Abraham, and Ishmael his son arose, and went to Abraham his father, and wept over Abraham his father, he and all the house of Abraham, and they wept with great weeping.</p>

<p class="v">7. And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the double cave, near Sarah his wife, and they mourned him forty days, all the men of his house, and Isaac and Ishmael, and all their sons, and all the sons of Keturah in their place; and the days of mourning for Abraham were completed.</p>

<p class="v">8. And he lived three jubilees and four weeks of years, one hundred and seventy-five years, and fulfilled the days of his life, being old and full of days.</p>

<p class="v">9. For the days of the lives of the forefathers were nineteen jubilees; and after the flood they began to grow fewer than nineteen jubilees, and to decrease in jubilees, and to grow old quickly, and to be filled with their days because of the manifold tribulations and the wickedness of their ways, except for Abraham.</p>

<p class="v">10. For Abraham was perfect in all his deeds toward the Lord, and pleasing in righteousness all the days of his life; and behold, he did not complete four jubilees in his life, when he had grown old because of wickedness and was full of his days.</p>

<p class="v">11. And all the generations that shall arise from this time until the day of the great judgment shall grow old quickly, before they have completed two jubilees, and their knowledge shall forsake them because of their old age; and from off the earth, all their knowledge shall vanish.</p>

<p class="v">12. And in those days, if a man lives a jubilee and a half, it will be said of him, "He lived long," and most of his days are pains, sorrows, and tribulations, and there is no peace:</p>

<p class="v">13. For calamity upon calamity, and wound upon wound, and tribulation upon tribulation, and evil tidings upon evil tidings, and sickness upon sickness, and all evil judgments such as these, one with another, sickness and overthrow, and snow and frost, and ice, and fever, and chills, and torpor, and famine, and death, and the sword, and captivity, and every kind of calamity and pain.</p>

<p class="v">14. And all this shall come upon a wicked generation, that transgresses upon the earth: their works are uncleanness and fornication, and pollution and abominations.</p>

<p class="v">15. Then they will say, "The days of the forefathers were many (indeed), up to a thousand years, and they were good; but behold, the days of our life, if a man has lived many, are seventy years, and if he is strong, eighty years, and these are evil, and there is no peace in the days of this wicked generation."</p>

<p class="v">16. And in that generation the sons shall convict their fathers and their elders of sin and unrighteousness, and of the words of their mouth and the great wickedness which they commit, and concerning their forsaking of the covenant which the LORD made between them and Him, that they should observe and do all His commandments, His ordinances, and all His laws, without turning aside to the right or to the left.</p>

<p class="v">17. For all have done evil, and every mouth speaks iniquity, and all their works are uncleanness and abomination, and all their ways are pollution, uncleanness, and destruction.</p>

<p class="v">18. Behold, the earth shall be destroyed because of all their works, and there shall be neither seed of the vine nor oil; for their works are altogether faithless, and they shall all perish together, beasts, cattle, birds, and all the fish of the sea, because of the children of men.</p>

<p class="v">19. And they shall strive one with another, the young with the old, and the old with the young, the poor with the rich, the small with the great, and the beggar with the prince, because of the law and the covenant; for they have forgotten the commandments, the covenants, the feasts, the months, the sabbaths, the jubilees, and all the judgments.</p>

<p class="v">20. And they shall stand up (with bows and) with swords and fight to bring them back into the way; but they shall not return until much blood has been shed one after another upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">21. And those who have escaped shall not turn back from their wickedness to the way of righteousness, but they shall all exalt themselves unto deceit and wealth, so that each one takes all that belongs to his neighbor, and they shall call themselves by a great name, but not in truth nor in righteousness, and they shall defile the holy of holies with their uncleanness and the corruption of their defilement.</p>

<p class="v">22. And a great punishment shall come upon the deeds of that generation from the LORD, and He shall give them over to the sword, to judgment, to captivity, and to plunder and devouring.</p>

<p class="v">23. And He shall stir up against them the sinners of the Gentiles, who have neither mercy nor compassion, and who will respect no one's person, neither old nor young, nor anyone, for they are more wicked and stronger to do evil than all the children of men.</p>

<p class="v">And they shall deal violently with Israel and transgress against Jacob,</p>

<p class="v">And much blood shall be shed upon the earth,</p>

<p class="v">And there shall be no one to gather them nor anyone to bury them.</p>

<p class="v">24. In those days they shall cry aloud,</p>

<p class="v">And call and pray to be saved from the hand of the sinners, the Gentiles;</p>

<p class="v">But no one shall be saved.</p>

<p class="v">25. And the heads of the children shall be white with gray hair,</p>

<p class="v">And a child of three weeks shall appear old as a man of a hundred years,</p>

<p class="v">And their stature shall be destroyed by tribulation and oppression.</p>

<p class="v">26. And in those days the children shall begin to study the laws,</p>

<p class="v">And to seek out the commandments,</p>

<p class="v">And to return to the way of righteousness.</p>

<p class="v">27. And the days shall begin to grow and increase among these children of men</p>

<p class="v">Until their days approach a thousand years.</p>

<p class="v">And there shall be a greater number of years than the number of days before.</p>

<p class="v">28. And there shall be no old man,</p>

<p class="v">Nor one who is not (un)satisfied with his days,</p>

<p class="v">For all shall be as children and youths.</p>

<p class="v">29. And they shall complete all their days and live in peace and in joy,</p>

<p class="v">And there shall be neither Satan nor any evil destroyer;</p>

<p class="v">For all their days shall be days of blessing and healing.</p>

<p class="v">30. And at that time the LORD will heal His servants,</p>

<p class="v">And they shall rise up and see great peace,</p>

<p class="v">And drive out their adversaries.</p>

<p class="v">And the righteous shall see and give thanks,</p>

<p class="v">And rejoice with joy for ever and ever,</p>

<p class="v">And he shall see all their judgments and all their curses upon their enemies.</p>

<p class="v">31. And their bones shall rest in the earth,</p>

<p class="v">And their spirits shall know great joy,</p>

<p class="v">And they shall know that it is the LORD who executes judgment,</p>

<p class="v">And shows mercy to hundreds and thousands and to all who love Him.</p>

<p class="v">32. And you, Moses, write these words; for thus are they written, and they inscribe them on the heavenly tablets for a testimony for the generations forever.</p>

### Chapter 24 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Isaac at the Well of Vision, 1 (cf. Gen. xxv. 11). Esau sells his birthright, 2-7 (cf. Gen. xxv.29-34).</p>

<p class="v">1. And it came to pass after the death of Abraham, that the LORD blessed Isaac his son, and he rose up from Hebron and went to dwell at the Well of Vision in the first year of the third week [2073 AM] of this jubilee, seven years.</p>

<p class="v">2. And in the first year of the fourth week, a famine began in the land, [2080 AM] besides the first famine that had occurred in the days of Abraham.</p>

<p class="v">3. And Jacob ate lentil pottage, and Esau came in from the fields hungry. And he said to Jacob his brother, "Give me some of that red pottage." And Jacob said to him, "Sell me your birthright, and I will give you bread and also some of this lentil pottage."</p>

<p class="v">4. And Esau said in his heart, "I shall die; of what use is this birthright to me?"</p>

<p class="v">5. And he said to Jacob, "I give it to you." And Jacob said, "Swear it to me today," and he swore to him.</p>

<p class="v">6. And Jacob gave bread and lentils to his brother Esau, and he ate until he was satisfied, and Esau despised his birthright; it is for this reason that Esau's name was called Edom, because of the red pottage that Jacob had given him in exchange for the birthright.</p>

<p class="v">7. And Jacob became the elder, and Esau fell from his dignity.</p>

<p class="v">8. And the famine spread over the land, and Isaac set out to go down to Egypt in the second year of this week, and went to the king of the Philistines at Gerar, to Abimelech.</p>

<p class="v">9. And the LORD appeared to him and said, "Do not go down to Egypt; dwell in the land that I will tell you, and sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and will bless you.</p>

<p class="v">10. For to you and to your posterity I will give all this land, and I will establish my oath which I made to Abraham your father, and I will multiply your posterity as the stars of heaven, and I will give to your posterity all this land.</p>

<p class="v">11. "And in your posterity all the nations of the earth shall be blessed, because your father obeyed my voice and kept my charges and my commandments, and my laws, and my ordinances, and my covenant; and now, obey my voice and dwell in this land."</p>

<p class="v">12. And he dwelt at Gerar three weeks of years.</p>

<p class="v">13. And Abimelech gave orders concerning him, [2080-2101 AM] and concerning all that belonged to him, saying, "Any man who touches him or anything that belongs to him shall surely die."</p>

<p class="v">14. And Isaac became strong among the Philistines, and he acquired many possessions, oxen and sheep, camels and donkeys, and a great household.</p>

<p class="v">15. And he sowed in the land of the Philistines and reaped a hundredfold, and Isaac became exceedingly great, and the Philistines envied him.</p>

<p class="v">16. All the wells that the servants of Abraham had dug during the life of Abraham, the Philistines had stopped up after the death of Abraham and had filled with earth.</p>

<p class="v">17. And Abimelech said to Isaac, "Go away from us, for you are much mightier than we are." And Isaac departed from there in the first year of the seventh week, and sojourned in the valleys of Gerar.</p>

<p class="v">18. And they dug again the wells of water that the servants of Abraham his father had dug, and that the Philistines had stopped up after the death of Abraham his father, and he gave them names as Abraham his father had named them.</p>

<p class="v">19. And the servants of Isaac dug a well in the valley and found living water, and the shepherds of Gerar quarreled with the shepherds of Isaac, saying, "The water is ours"; and Isaac called the name of the well "Perversity," because they had been perverse toward us.</p>

<p class="v">20. And they dug a second well, and they also strove for it, and he called its name "Enmity." And he rose up from there and they dug another well, and for this they did not strive, and he called its name "Room," and Isaac said, "Now the LORD has made room for us, and we have increased in the land."</p>

<p class="v">21. And he went up from there to the Well of the Oath in the first year of the first week of the forty-fourth jubilee.</p>

<p class="v">22. And the LORD appeared to him that night, at the new moon of the first month, and said to him, "I am the God of Abraham your father; fear nothing, for I am with you, I will bless you and will surely multiply your seed as the sand of the earth, for the sake of Abraham my servant."</p>

<p class="v">23. And he built there an altar which Abraham his father had built first, and he called upon the name of the LORD, and he offered a sacrifice to the God of Abraham his father.</p>

<p class="v">24. And they dug a well and found living water.</p>

<p class="v">25. And the servants of Isaac dug another well and found no water, and they went and told Isaac that they had found no water, and Isaac said, "I have sworn today to the Philistines and this thing has been declared to us."</p>

<p class="v">26. And he called the name of that place the Well of the Oath; for there he had sworn to Abimelech and to Ahuzzath his friend and to Phicol the prefect, or his host.</p>

<p class="v">27. And Isaac understood that day that under compulsion he had sworn to them to make peace with them.</p>

<p class="v">28.
