And Isaac, that day, cursed the Philistines and said, "Cursed be the Philistines until the day of wrath and indignation from among all the nations; may God make them a derision and a curse and an object of wrath and indignation in the hands of the sinners, the Gentiles, and in the hands of the Kittim.</p>

<p class="v">29. "And whoever escapes the sword of the enemy and of Kittim, may the righteous nation be rooted out by judgment from under heaven; for they shall be the enemies and adversaries of my children throughout their generations on the earth.</p>

<p class="v">30. And no remnant shall be left to them,</p>

<p class="v">Nor anyone who shall be saved on the day of the wrath of judgment;</p>

<p class="v">For destruction, extermination, and expulsion from the earth is (reserved for) all the seed of the Philistines,</p>

<p class="v">And there shall remain to these Caphtorim neither name nor seed upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">31. For though he ascend to heaven,</p>

<p class="v">From there he shall be brought down,</p>

<p class="v">And though he strengthen himself upon the earth,</p>

<p class="v">From there he shall be dragged,</p>

<p class="v">And though he hide himself among the nations,</p>

<p class="v">Even from there he shall be uprooted;</p>

<p class="v">And though he go down to Sheol,</p>

<p class="v">There also his condemnation shall be great,</p>

<p class="v">And there also he shall have no peace.</p>

<p class="v">32. And if he goes into captivity,</p>

<p class="v">Those who seek his life shall kill him on the way,</p>

<p class="v">And neither name nor posterity shall be left to him upon all the earth;</p>

<p class="v">For he shall go into everlasting curse.</p>

<p class="v">33. And thus it is written and engraved concerning him on the heavenly tablets, to be done to him on the day of judgment, that he may be rooted out of the earth.</p>
### Chapter 25 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Rebecca warns Jacob not to marry a Canaanite woman, 1-3. Jacob promises to marry a daughter of Laban despite Esau's urgent demands that he marry a Canaanite woman, 4-10. Rebecca blesses Jacob, 11-23. (Cf. Gen. xxviii.1-4.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the second year of this week, in this jubilee, Rebecca called Jacob her son, and spoke to him, saying, "My son, do not take a wife for yourself from among the daughters of Canaan, as Esau, your brother, has done, who took for himself two wives from among the daughters of Canaan, and they have embittered my soul by all their impure deeds; for all their deeds are fornication and lust, and there is no righteousness in them, for (their deeds) are evil."</p>

<p class="v">2. And as for me, my son, I love you exceedingly, and my heart and my affection bless you at every hour of the day and at every watch of the night.</p>

<p class="v">3. And now, my son, listen to my voice, and do your mother's will, and do not take a wife for yourself from among the daughters of this land, but only from the house of my father and the kindred of my father. You shall take a wife from the house of my father, and the Most High God will bless you, and your children shall be a righteous generation and a holy posterity.</p>

<p class="v">4. Then Jacob spoke to Rebecca, his mother, and said to her, "Behold, mother, I am nine weeks old, and I have neither known nor touched any woman, and I have not betrothed myself to any; I do not even think of taking a wife for myself from among the daughters of Canaan.</p>

<p class="v">5. "For I remember, mother, the words of Abraham, our father, for he commanded me not to take a wife from among the daughters of Canaan, but to take for myself a wife from the posterity of the house of my father and of my kindred."</p>

<p class="v">6. "I have heard it said before that Laban, your brother, has fathered daughters, and I have resolved to take a wife from among them."</p>

<p class="v">7. "And therefore I have kept myself in my mind from sinning or corrupting myself in all my ways, all the days of my life; for as concerning lust and fornication, Abraham, my father, gave me many commandments.</p>

<p class="v">8. "And despite all that he commanded me, for twenty-two years my brother has striven with me, and he has often spoken to me and said to me, 'My brother, take for a wife a sister of my two wives'; but I refuse to do as he does.</p>

<p class="v">9. "I swear before you, mother, that all the days of my life I will not take a wife from among the daughters of the posterity of Canaan, and that I will not act wickedly as my brother has done."</p>

<p class="v">10. "Fear nothing, mother; be assured that I will do your will, and that I will walk in uprightness, and that I will not corrupt my ways forever.</p>

<p class="v">11. And thereupon she lifted her face to heaven and stretched out the fingers of her hands, and opened her mouth and blessed the Most High God, who had created heaven and earth, and she gave him thanks and praise.</p>

<p class="v">12. And she said, "Blessed be the Lord God, and blessed be his holy name forever and ever, who has given me Jacob as a pure son and a holy posterity; for he is yours, and his posterity shall be yours continually and throughout all generations forever.</p>

<p class="v">13. "Bless him, Lord, and put in my mouth the blessing of righteousness, that I may bless him.</p>

<p class="v">14. And at that hour, when the spirit of righteousness descended into her mouth, she laid her two hands on the head of Jacob, and said:</p>

<p class="v">15. Blessed are you, Lord of righteousness and God of the ages</p>

<p class="v">And may he bless you beyond all the generations of men.</p>

<p class="v">May he give you, my son, the way of righteousness,</p>

<p class="v">And reveal righteousness to your posterity.</p>

<p class="v">16. And may he make your sons numerous during your life,</p>

<p class="v">And may they arise according to the number of the months of the year.</p>

<p class="v">And may their sons become numerous and great beyond the stars of heaven,</p>

<p class="v">And their number greater than the sand of the sea.</p>

<p class="v">17. And may he give them this good land — as he said he would give it forever to Abraham and to his posterity after him —</p>

<p class="v">And may they keep it as a possession forever.</p>

<p class="v">18. And may I see (born) to you, my son, blessed children during my life,</p>

<p class="v">And may all your seed be a blessed and holy seed.</p>

<p class="v">19. And as you have refreshed the spirit of your mother during her life,</p>

<p class="v">So does the womb of her who bore you bless you,</p>

<p class="v">[My affection] and my breasts bless you</p>

<p class="v">And my mouth and my tongue praise you greatly.</p>

<p class="v">20. Increase and spread over the earth,</p>

<p class="v">And may your posterity be perfect in the joy of heaven and earth forever;</p>

<p class="v">And may your seed rejoice,</p>

<p class="v">And in the great day of peace, may there be peace.</p>

<p class="v">21. And may your name and your posterity endure to all ages,</p>

<p class="v">And may the Most High God be their God,</p>

<p class="v">And may the God of righteousness dwell with them,</p>

<p class="v">And by them shall his sanctuary be built for all ages.</p>

<p class="v">22. Blessed be he who blesses you,</p>

<p class="v">And all flesh that curses you falsely, let it be cursed.</p>

<p class="v">23. And she embraced him, and said to him:</p>

<p class="v">'May the Lord of the world love you'</p>

<p class="v">"As the heart of your mother and her affection rejoice in you and bless you."</p>

<p class="v">And she ceased blessing.</p>

### Chapter 26 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. And in the seventh year of this week, Isaac called Esau, his elder son, and said to him, "I am old, my son, and behold, my eyes are dim so that I cannot see, and I do not know the day of my death.</p>

<p class="v">2. "And now, take your hunting weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out into the fields, and hunt and catch (game) for me, my son, and prepare me savory meat, such as my soul loves, and bring it to me, that I may eat, and that my soul may bless you before I die.</p>

<p class="v">3. But Rebecca heard Isaac speaking to Esau.</p>

<p class="v">4. And Esau went out early to the fields to hunt and catch (game) and bring it home to his father.</p>

<p class="v">5. And Rebecca called Jacob, her son, and said to him, "Behold, I have heard Isaac, your father, speaking to Esau, your brother, saying, 'Hunt for me, prepare me savory meat, and bring it to me,</p>

<p class="v">6. that I may eat and bless you before the LORD before I die.' And now, my son, obey my voice in what I command you: go to your flock and bring me two good kids, and I will make of them savory meat for your father, such as he loves, and you shall bring it to your father, that he may eat it and bless you before the LORD before he dies, and that you may be blessed.</p>

<p class="v">7. And Jacob said to Rebecca, his mother, "Mother, I will refuse nothing that my father would wish to eat and that would please him; only I fear, my mother, that he will recognize my voice and will want to touch me."</p>

<p class="v">8. "And you know that I am smooth, and that Esau, my brother, is hairy, and that I shall appear in his eyes as a wrongdoer, and that I shall do a deed that he did not command me to do, and he will be angry with me, and I shall bring upon myself a curse and not a blessing.</p>

<p class="v">9. And Rebecca, his mother, said to him, "Let your curse be upon me, my son; only obey my voice."</p>

<p class="v">10. And Jacob obeyed the voice of Rebecca, his mother, and went and fetched two good, fat kids, and brought them to his mother, and his mother made of them savory meat, such as he loved.</p>

<p class="v">11. And Rebecca took the goodly garments of Esau, her elder son, which were with her in the house, and clothed Jacob, her younger son, (with them), and she put the skins of the kids upon his hands and upon the exposed parts of his neck.</p>

<p class="v">12. And she put the meat and the bread that she had prepared into the hands of her son Jacob.</p>

<p class="v">13. And Jacob went to his father and said to him, "I am your son. I have done what you told me: rise up, sit, and eat of what I have caught, father, that your soul may bless me."</p>

<p class="v">14. And Isaac said to his son, "How have you found it so quickly, my son?"</p>

<p class="v">15. And Jacob said, "Because the LORD your God caused me to find it."</p>

<p class="v">16. And Isaac said to him, "Come near, and I will feel you, my son, whether you are my son Esau or not."</p>

<p class="v">17. And Jacob drew near to Isaac, his father, and he felt him and said, "The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau."</p>

<p class="v">18. And he did not discern him, because it was a dispensation from heaven to remove his power of perception, and Isaac did not discern him, for his hands were hairy like those of his brother Esau, so that he blessed him.</p>

<p class="v">19. And he said, "Are you my son Esau?" And he said, "I am your son"; and he said, "Come near to me, and I will eat of what you have caught, my son, that my soul may bless you."</p>

<p class="v">20. And he drew near to him, and he ate; and he brought him wine, and he drank.</p>

<p class="v">21. And Isaac, his father, said to him, "Come near and kiss me, my son."</p>

<p class="v">22. And he drew near and kissed him. And he smelled the smell of his garments, and he blessed him and said, "Behold, the smell of my son is like the smell of a full field that the LORD has blessed.</p>

<p class="v">23. And may the LORD give you of the dew of heaven</p>

<p class="v">And of the dew of the earth, and of plenty of grain and oil:</p>

<p class="v">Let the nations serve you,</p>

<p class="v">And the peoples bow down before you.</p>

<p class="v">24. Be lord over your brothers,</p>

<p class="v">And let your mother's sons bow down before you;</p>

<p class="v">And let all the blessings with which the Lord has blessed me and has blessed Abraham, my father,</p>

<p class="v">Be imparted to you and to your posterity forever:</p>

<p class="v">Cursed be he who curses you,</p>

<p class="v">And blessed be he who blesses you.</p>

<p class="v">25. And as soon as Isaac had finished blessing his son Jacob, and Jacob had gone out from Isaac, his father, he hid himself, and Esau, his brother, came in from his hunting.</p>

<p class="v">26. And he too prepared savory meat, and brought it to his father, and said to his father, "Let my father rise and eat of my venison, that your soul may bless me."</p>

<p class="v">27. And Isaac, his father, said to him, "Who are you?" And he said to him, "I am your firstborn, your son Esau: I have done what you commanded me."</p>

<p class="v">28. And Isaac was greatly astonished and said, "Who is he that hunted, caught, and brought it to me, and I ate of it all before you came, and I blessed him? (And) he shall indeed be blessed, and all his posterity forever.</p>

<p class="v">29. And it came to pass that when Esau heard the words of his father Isaac, he cried out with an exceedingly great and bitter cry, and said to his father, "Bless me, (even) me also, father.</p>

<p class="v">30. And he said to him, "Your brother came with cunning, and he has taken away your blessing." And he said, "Now I know why his name is called Jacob: behold, he has supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright, and now he has taken away my blessing.</p>

<p class="v">31. And he said, "Have you not reserved a blessing for me, father?" And Isaac answered and said to Esau:</p>

<p class="v">"Behold, I have made him your lord,</p>

<p class="v">And I have given him all his brothers for servants,</p>

<p class="v">And with plenty of grain, wine, and oil have I sustained him:</p>

<p class="v">And what shall I now do for you, my son?</p>

<p class="v">32. And Esau said to Isaac, his father:</p>

<p class="v">"Have you but one blessing, O father?</p>

<p class="v">Bless me, (even) me also, father.'</p>

<p class="v">33. And Esau lifted up his voice and wept. And Isaac answered and said to him:</p>

<p class="v">"Behold, far from the dew of the earth shall your dwelling be,</p>

<p class="v">And far from the dew of heaven above.</p>

<p class="v">34. And you shall live by your sword,</p>

<p class="v">And you shall serve your brother.</p>

<p class="v">And it shall come to pass, when you become great,</p>

<p class="v">And shake his yoke from off your neck,</p>

<p class="v">You shall sin a complete sin unto death,</p>

<p class="v">And your seed shall be rooted out from under heaven.</p>

<p class="v">35. And Esau threatened Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him, and he said in his heart, "Let the days of mourning for my father come now, that I may kill my brother Jacob."</p>

### Chapter 27 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Rebecca, alarmed by Esau's threats, urges Isaac to send Jacob to Mesopotamia, 1-12. Isaac comforts Rebecca at Jacob's departure, 13-18. Jacob's dream and vow at Bethel, 19-27. (Cf. Gen. xxviii.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And the words of Esau, her elder son, were told to Rebecca in a dream, and Rebecca sent and called Jacob, her younger son,</p>

<p class="v">2. and said to him, "Behold, Esau, your brother, will take vengeance on you by killing you.</p>

<p class="v">3. "Now therefore, my son, obey my voice, and rise up and flee to Laban, my brother, at Haran, and stay with him a few days until your brother's anger turns away and he removes his anger from you, and forgets all that you have done; then I will send and fetch you from there.</p>

<p class="v">4. And Jacob said, "I am not afraid; if he wants to kill me, I will kill him.</p>

<p class="v">5. But she said to him, "Let me not be deprived of my two sons in one day."</p>

<p class="v">6. And Jacob said to Rebecca, his mother, "Behold, you know that my father has grown old and cannot see, because his eyes are dim, and if I leave him it will be evil in his eyes, because I am leaving him and going away from you, and my father will grow angry and curse me. I will not go; when he sends me, then only will I go.</p>

<p class="v">7. And Rebecca said to Jacob, "I will go in and speak to him, and he will send you away."</p>

<p class="v">8. And Rebecca went in and said to Isaac, "I loathe my life because of the two daughters of Heth whom Esau has taken as wives; and if Jacob takes a wife like these from among the daughters of the land, to what purpose should I live, for the daughters of Canaan are evil.</p>

<p class="v">9. And Isaac called Jacob and blessed him, and charged him and said to him, "Do not take for yourself a wife from any of the daughters of Canaan;</p>

<p class="v">10. rise up and go to Mesopotamia, to the house of Bethuel, your mother's father, and take from there a wife from among the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.</p>

<p class="v">11. "And may God Almighty bless you and increase and multiply you, that you may become a company of nations, and give you the blessings of my father Abraham, to you and to your posterity after you, that you may inherit the land of your sojournings and all the land that God gave to Abraham: go, my son, in peace.</p>

<p class="v">12. And Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went to Mesopotamia, to Laban, the son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebecca, Jacob's mother.</p>

<p class="v">13. And it came to pass, after Jacob rose up to go to Mesopotamia, that the spirit of Rebecca was grieved after her son, and she wept.</p>

<p class="v">14. And Isaac said to Rebecca, "My sister, do not weep on account of Jacob, my son; for he goes in peace, and he shall return in peace.</p>

<p class="v">15. "The Most High God will preserve him from all evil and will be with him; for he will not forsake him all his days;</p>

<p class="v">16. "For I know that his ways will prosper in all things wherever he goes, until he returns to us in peace, and we see him in peace."</p>

<p class="v">17. "Fear nothing on his account, my sister, for he is on the right path and he is a perfect man; and he is faithful and will not perish. Do not weep.</p>

<p class="v">18. And Isaac comforted Rebecca on account of her son Jacob, and blessed him.</p>

<p class="v">19. And Jacob went out from the Well of the Oath to go to Haran in the first year of the second week of the forty-fourth jubilee, and he came to Luz on the mountains, that is, Bethel, at the new moon of the first month of this week, [21 h 15] and he came to that place in the evening and turned aside from the road to the west of the way that night: and he slept there; for the sun had set.</p>

<p class="v">20. And he took one of the stones of that place and put it (at his head) under the tree, and he was traveling alone, and he slept.</p>

<p class="v">21. And he dreamed that night, and behold, a ladder was set up on the earth, and its top reached to heaven, and behold, the angels of the Lord were going up and down upon it; and behold, the Lord stood upon it.</p>

<p class="v">22. And he spoke to Jacob and said, "I am the Lord, the God of Abraham, your father, and the God of Isaac; the land on which you are sleeping, I will give it to you and to your posterity after you.</p>

<p class="v">23. "And your posterity shall be as the dust of the earth, and you shall grow to the west and to the east, to the north and to the south, and in you and in your posterity shall all the families of the nations be blessed."</p>

<p class="v">24. "And behold, I will be with you, and I will keep you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land in peace; for I will not leave you until I have done all that I have told you.</p>

<p class="v">25. And Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, "Truly this place is the house of the LORD, and I did not know it." And he was afraid and said, "Dreadful is this place, which is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven."</p>

<p class="v">26. And Jacob rose early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put under his head and set it up as a pillar for a sign, and he poured oil upon it. And he gave that place the name Bethel; but the name of the place had at first been Luz.</p>

<p class="v">27. And Jacob made a vow to the Lord, saying, "If the Lord is with me and keeps me on the way that I am going, and gives me bread to eat and clothing to wear, so that I come back in peace to my father's house, then the LORD shall be my God, and this stone that I have set up as a pillar for a sign in this place shall be the house of the LORD, and of all that you give me, I will give you a tenth, my God.</p>

### Chapter 28 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Jacob marries Leah and Rachel, 1-10. His children by Leah and Rachel and by their handmaids, 11-24. Jacob seeks to leave Laban, 25; but stays for a set wage, 26-8. Jacob grows rich, 29-30. (Cf. Gen. xxix.1, 17, 18, 21-35; xxx.1-13, 17-22, 24, 25, 28, 32, 39, 43; xxxi.1, 2.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And he set out on his journey, and came to the land of the East, to Laban, the brother of Rebecca, and he stayed with him, and served him for Rachel, his daughter, a week.</p>

<p class="v">2. And in the first year of the third week [2122 AM], he said to him, "Give me my wife, for whom I have served you seven years"; and Laban said to Jacob, "I will give you your wife."</p>

<p class="v">3. And Laban made a feast, and took Leah, his elder daughter, and gave her to Jacob for a wife, and gave him Zilpah, her handmaid, for a handmaid; and Jacob did not know it, for he thought it was Rachel.</p>

<p class="v">4. And he went in to her, and behold, it was Leah; and Jacob was angry with Laban, and said to him, "Why have you dealt with me this way? Did I not serve you for Rachel and not for Leah? Why have you wronged me?</p>

<p class="v">5. Take your daughter, and I will go; for you have done me wrong." For Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah; for Leah's eyes were weak, but her form was very beautiful; but Rachel had beautiful eyes and a form that was fair and very beautiful.</p>

<p class="v">6. And Laban said to Jacob, "It is not so done in our country, to give the younger before the elder." And it is not right to do this; for so it is ordained and written on the heavenly tablets, that no one should give his younger daughter before the elder; but the elder is given first, and after her the younger. And whoever does this is condemned in heaven, and no one who does this is righteous, for this deed is evil before the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">7. And command the children of Israel not to do this; let them neither take nor give the younger before they have given the elder, for it is very wicked.</p>

<p class="v">8. And Laban said to Jacob, "Let the seven days of this one's feast pass, and I will give you Rachel, and you shall serve me another seven years, so that you may tend my flock as you did at the beginning, the previous week."</p>

<p class="v">9. And on the day when the seven days of Leah's feast were completed, Laban gave Rachel to Jacob, that he might serve him another seven years, and he gave Rachel Bilhah, the sister of Zilpah, as a handmaid.</p>

<p class="v">10. And he served another seven years for Rachel, for Leah had been given to him for nothing.</p>

<p class="v">11. And the LORD opened the womb of Leah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a son, and he called his name Reuben, on the fourteenth day of the ninth month, in the first year of the third week. [21 h 22]</p>

<p class="v">12. But Rachel's womb was closed, for the LORD saw that Leah was hated and Rachel was loved.</p>

<p class="v">13. And Jacob went in again to Leah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a second son, and he called his name Simeon, on the twenty-first of the tenth month, in the third year of this week. [21 h 24]</p>

<p class="v">14. And Jacob went in again to Leah, and she conceived and bore him a third son, and he called his name Levi, at the new moon of the first month of the sixth year of this week. [21 h 27]</p>

<p class="v">15. And Jacob returned to her, and she conceived and bore him a fourth son, and he called his name Judah, on the fifteenth of the third month, in the first year of the fourth week. [21 h 29]</p>

<p class="v">16. And because of all this, Rachel envied Leah, for she did not bear children, and she said to Jacob, "Give me children"; and Jacob said, "Have I withheld from you the fruit of your womb? Have I forsaken you?</p>

<p class="v">17. And when Rachel saw that Leah had borne Jacob four sons, Reuben and Simeon and Levi and Judah, she said to him, "Go in to Bilhah, my handmaid, and she shall conceive and bear me a son." (And she gave him Bilhah, her handmaid, for a wife.)</p>

<p class="v">18. And he went in to her, and she conceived and bore him a son, and he called his name Dan, on the ninth of the sixth month, in the sixth year of the third week. [21 h 27]</p>

<p class="v">19. And Jacob returned to Bilhah a second time, and she conceived and bore Jacob another son, and Rachel called his name Naphtali, on the fifth of the seventh month, in the second year of the fourth week. [21h30]</p>

<p class="v">20. And when Leah saw that she had become barren and had not borne children, she envied Rachel, and she too gave her handmaid Zilpah to Jacob for a wife, and she conceived and bore a son, and Leah called his name Gad, on the twelfth of the eighth month, in the third year of the fourth week. [21h31]</p>

<p class="v">21. And he returned to her, and she conceived and bore him a second son, and Leah called his name Asher, on the second of the eleventh month, in the fifth year of the fourth week. [21h33]</p>

<p class="v">22. And Jacob went in to Leah, and she conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Issachar, on the fourth of the fifth month, in the fourth year of the fourth week, [2132 AM] and she gave him to a nurse.</p>

<p class="v">23. And Jacob returned to her, and she conceived and bore two (children), a son and a daughter, and she called the son's name Zebulun and the daughter's name Dinah, on the seventh day of the seventh month, in the sixth year of the fourth week. [21h34]</p>

<p class="v">24. And the LORD had pity on Rachel, and opened her womb, and she conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Joseph, at the new moon of the fourth month, in the sixth year of this fourth week. [21h34]</p>

<p class="v">25. And at the time when Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, "Give me my wives and my sons, and let me go to my father Isaac, and let me build myself a house; for I have completed the years during which I served you for your two daughters, and I will go to my father's house.</p>

<p class="v">26. And Laban said to Jacob, "Stay with me for your wages, and tend my flock for me again, and take your wages."</p>

<p class="v">27. And they agreed between them that he would give him as wages those of the lambs and kids born black, spotted, and white, which should be his wages.</p>

<p class="v">28. And all the sheep bore lambs spotted, speckled, and black, marked in various ways, and they bore again lambs like themselves, and all those that were spotted belonged to Jacob, and those that were not belonged to Laban.</p>

<p class="v">29. And Jacob's possessions multiplied exceedingly, and he possessed oxen and sheep, donkeys and camels, and menservants and maidservants.</p>

<p class="v">30. And Laban and his sons envied Jacob, and Laban took back his sheep from him, and watched him with evil intent.</p>

### Chapter 29 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Jacob departs secretly, 1-4. Laban pursues him, 5-6. Covenant of Jacob and Laban, 7-8. Dwellings of the Amorites (formerly of the Rephaim) destroyed in the writer's time, 9-11. Laban departs, 12. Jacob is reconciled with Esau, 13. Jacob sends provisions of food to his parents four times a year at Hebron, 14-17, 19-20. Esau remarries, 18. (Cf. Gen. xxxi.3, 4, 10, 13, 19, 21, 23, 24, 46, 47; xxxii.22; xxxiii.10, 16.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And it came to pass that when Rachel had borne Joseph, Laban went to shear his sheep; for they were three days' journey distant from him.</p>

<p class="v">2. And Jacob saw that Laban had gone to shear his sheep, and Jacob called Leah and Rachel, and told them kindly that they should come with him to the land of Canaan.</p>

<p class="v">3. For he told them that he had seen it all in a dream, even all that had been told him, that he should return to his father's house, and they said, "Wherever you go, we will go with you."</p>

<p class="v">4. And Jacob blessed the God of Isaac, his father, and the God of Abraham, his father's father, and he arose and mounted his wives and his children, and took all his possessions and crossed the river, and came to the land of Gilead; and Jacob hid his intention from Laban and did not tell him.</p>

<p class="v">5. And in the seventh year of the fourth week, Jacob turned toward Gilead on the twenty-first of the first month. [2135 AM] And Laban pursued him and overtook Jacob in the mountain of Gilead on the thirteenth of the third month.</p>

<p class="v">6. And the LORD did not allow him to do harm to Jacob; for he appeared to him in a dream in the night. And Laban spoke with Jacob.</p>

<p class="v">7. And on the fifteenth of these days, Jacob made a feast for Laban and for all who accompanied him, and Jacob swore to Laban that day, and Laban also to Jacob, that neither would cross the mountain of Gilead to the other with evil intent.</p>

<p class="v">8. And he made there a heap for a witness; therefore the name of that place is called "The Heap of Testimony," after this heap.</p>

<p class="v">9. But formerly the land of Gilead was called the land of the Rephaim; for it was the land of the Rephaim, and there the Rephaim were born, giants whose height was ten, nine, eight, down to seven cubits.</p>

<p class="v">10. And their dwelling extended from the land of the children of Ammon to Mount Hermon, and the seats of their kingdom were Karnaim and Ashtaroth, and Edrei, and Misur, and Beon.</p>

<p class="v">11. And the LORD destroyed them because of the wickedness of their deeds; for they were very wicked, and the Amorites dwelt in their place, wicked and sinners, and there is no people today that has fully accomplished all its sins, and they have no longer a lifetime upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">12. And Jacob sent Laban away, and he departed to Mesopotamia, the land of the East, and Jacob returned to the land of Gilead.</p>

<p class="v">13. And he crossed the Jabbok on the eleventh of the ninth month. And that day Esau, his brother, came to him, and he was reconciled with him, and he left him for the land of Seir, but Jacob dwelt in tents.</p>

<p class="v">14. And in the first year of the fifth week of this jubilee [2136 AM], he crossed the Jordan, and dwelt beyond the Jordan, and he pastured his flocks from the Sea of the Heap as far as Bethshan, and as far as Dothan and as far as the forest of Akrabbim.</p>

<p class="v">15. And he sent to his father Isaac of all his goods, garments, and food, and meat, and drink, and milk, and butter, and cheese, and some dates from the valley.</p>

<p class="v">16. And to his mother Rebecca also, four times a year, between the periods of the months, between plowing and harvest, and between autumn and the rainy (season), and between winter and spring, at the tower of Abraham.</p>

<p class="v">17. For Isaac had returned from the Well of the Oath and had gone up to the tower of his father Abraham, and he dwelt there separated from his son Esau.</p>

<p class="v">18. For at the time when Jacob departed for Mesopotamia, Esau took for a wife Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael, and he gathered together all the flocks of his father and of his wives, and went up and dwelt on the mountain of Seir, and he left Isaac his father alone at the Well of the Oath.</p>

<p class="v">19. And Isaac went up from the Well of the Oath and dwelt in the tower of Abraham his father on the mountains of Hebron,</p>

<p class="v">20. And there Jacob sent, from time to time, all that he sent to his father and his mother, everything they needed, and they blessed Jacob with all their heart and with all their soul.</p>

### Chapter 30 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Dinah is carried off, 1-3. Massacre of the Shechemites, 4-6. Laws against intermarriage between Israel and the Gentiles, 7-17. Levi chosen for the priesthood on account of his slaughter of the Shechemites, 18-23. Dinah recovered, 24. Jacob's rebuke, 25-6. (Cf. Gen. xxxiii.18, xxxiv.2, 4, 7, 13-14, 25-30, xxxv.5.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the first year of the sixth week [2143 AM], he went up in peace to Salem, to the east of Shechem, in the fourth month.</p>

<p class="v">2. And there they took Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, into the house of Shechem, son of Hamor, the Hivite, prince of the land, and he lay with her and defiled her, and she was a young girl, a child of twelve years.</p>

<p class="v">3. And he begged his father and her brothers to give her to him as a wife. And Jacob and his sons were angered on account of the men of Shechem; for they had defiled Dinah, their sister, and they spoke to them with evil intent, and dealt deceitfully with them, and beguiled them.</p>

<p class="v">4. And Simeon and Levi came unexpectedly to Shechem and executed judgment on all the men of Shechem, and killed all the men they found there, and left not one. They killed them all in torment, because they had dishonored their sister Dinah.</p>

<p class="v">5. And let it not happen again henceforth that a daughter of Israel be defiled; for judgment is ordained in heaven against them, that they should destroy by the sword all the men of the Shechemites, because they had brought shame on Israel.</p>

<p class="v">6. And the LORD delivered them into the hands of the sons of Jacob, that they might exterminate them by the sword and execute judgment against them, and that it should not happen again in Israel that a virgin of Israel be defiled.</p>

<p class="v">7. And if anyone in Israel wishes to give his daughter or his sister to a man of the race of the Gentiles, he shall surely die, and he shall be stoned; for he has brought shame on Israel; and the woman shall be burned with fire, because she has dishonored the name of her father's house, and she shall be rooted out of Israel.</p>

<p class="v">8. And let there be found no adulterous woman nor impurity in Israel throughout all the days of the generations of the earth; for Israel is holy to the LORD, and whoever defiles it shall surely die: he shall be stoned with stones.</p>

<p class="v">9. For thus it has been ordained and written on the heavenly tablets concerning all the posterity of Israel: whoever defiles it shall surely die, and he shall be stoned with stones.</p>

<p class="v">10. And to this law there is neither limit of days, nor remission, nor any atonement; but the man who has defiled his daughter shall be rooted out from the midst of all Israel, because he has given of his seed to Moloch, and has wrought impiously so as to defile it.</p>

<p class="v">11. And you, Moses, command the children of Israel and exhort them not to give their daughters to the Gentiles, and not to take for their sons any of the daughters of the Gentiles, for this is abominable before the LORD.</p>

<p class="v">12. Therefore I have written for you, in the words of the law, all the deeds of the Shechemites that they committed against Dinah, and how the sons of Jacob said, "We will not give our daughter to a man who is uncircumcised, for that would be a reproach to us."</p>

<p class="v">13. And it is a reproach to Israel, to those who live and to those who take the daughters of the Gentiles; for this is unclean and abominable to Israel.</p>

<p class="v">14. And Israel shall not be free from this impurity if it has a wife from among the daughters of the Gentiles, or if it has given one of its daughters to a man who is of the Gentiles.</p>

<p class="v">15. For there shall be plague upon plague, and curse upon curse, and every judgment, plague, and curse shall come upon him: if he does this, or if he hides his eyes from those who commit impurity, or from those who profane the sanctuary of the Lord, or those who profane his holy name, (then) the whole nation together shall be judged for all the impurities and profanation of that man.</p>

<p class="v">16. And there shall be no respect of persons [and no regard for persons], and there shall be no acceptance from him of fruits, offerings, burnt offering, and fat, nor of any sweet-smelling savor, so as to accept the treatment of any man or woman in Israel who defiles the sanctuary.</p>

<p class="v">17. Therefore I have commanded you this, saying: Bear this testimony to Israel: see how the Shechemites and their sons behaved: how they were delivered into the hands of two sons of Jacob, and they killed them under torment, and this was (counted) to them for righteousness, and it was written down to them for righteousness.</p>

<p class="v">18. And the posterity of Levi was chosen for the priesthood and to be Levites, that they might serve before the LORD, as we do, continually, and that Levi and his sons might be blessed forever; for he was zealous to execute righteousness, judgment, and vengeance against all who rose up against Israel.</p>

<p class="v">19. And thus they inscribe in testimony on his behalf on the heavenly tablets blessing and righteousness before the God of all:</p>

<p class="v">20. And we remember the righteousness that the man accomplished during his life, at every season of the year; unto a thousand generations they will record it, and it shall come to him and to his descendants after him, and he has been recorded on the heavenly tablets as a friend and a righteous man.</p>

<p class="v">21. All this account I have written for you, and I have commanded you to tell the children of Israel that they should not commit sin, nor transgress the ordinances, nor break the covenant that has been ordained for them, (but) that they should fulfill it and be recorded as friends.</p>

<p class="v">22. But if they transgress and commit impurity in any way, they shall be inscribed on the heavenly tablets as adversaries, and they shall be blotted out of the book of life, and they shall be inscribed in the book of those who shall be destroyed and with those who shall be rooted out of the earth.</p>

<p class="v">23. And on the day when the sons of Jacob killed Shechem, a writing was written in their favor in heaven, saying that they had executed righteousness, integrity, and vengeance against the sinners, and it was written down for a blessing.</p>

<p class="v">24. And they brought Dinah, their sister, out of the house of Shechem, and they took captive all that belonged to Shechem, their sheep, and their oxen, and their donkeys, and all their wealth, and all their flocks, and brought it all to Jacob their father.</p>

<p class="v">25. And he reproached them because they had put the city to the sword, for he feared the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites and the Perizzites.</p>

<p class="v">26. And the fear of the LORD was upon all the cities that are around Shechem, and they did not rise up to pursue the sons of Jacob; for terror had fallen upon them.</p>

### Chapter 31 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Jacob goes to Bethel to offer a sacrifice, 1-3 (cf. Gen. xxxv.2-4, 7, 14). Isaac blesses Levi, 4-17, and Judah, 18-22. Jacob tells Isaac how God made him prosper, 24. Jacob goes to Bethel with Rebecca and Deborah, 26-30. Jacob blesses the God of his fathers, 31-2.</p>

<p class="v">1. And at the new moon of the month, Jacob spoke to all the people of his house, saying, "Purify yourselves and change your garments, and let us arise and go up to Bethel, where I made a vow to him on the day when I fled from Esau, my brother, because he was with me and brought me into this land in peace; and put away the foreign gods that are among you.</p>

<p class="v">2. And they gave up the foreign gods, and what they had in their ears and what they had on their necks, and the idols that Rachel had stolen from Laban, her father, and that she had given entirely to Jacob. And he burned them, and broke them, and destroyed them, and hid them under an oak that is in the land of Shechem.</p>

<p class="v">3. And he went up to Bethel at the new moon of the seventh month. And he built an altar at the place where he had slept, and he set up a pillar there, and he sent word to his father Isaac to come to him for his sacrifice, and also to his mother Rebecca.</p>

<p class="v">4. And Isaac said, "Let my son Jacob come, and let me see him before I die."</p>

<p class="v">5. And Jacob set out for his father Isaac and for his mother Rebecca, at the house of his father Abraham, and he took with him two of his sons, Levi and Judah, and he came to his father Isaac and to his mother Rebecca.</p>

<p class="v">6. And Rebecca came out of the tower, before her, to embrace Jacob and to kiss him; for her spirit had been roused when she heard, "Behold, Jacob, your son, has come"; and she embraced him.</p>

<p class="v">7. And she saw his two sons, and she recognized them, and said to him, "Are these your sons, my son?" And she embraced them, and kissed them, and blessed them, saying, "In you shall the posterity of Abraham be made illustrious, and you shall be a blessing on the earth.</p>

<p class="v">8. And Jacob went in to Isaac, his father, into the chamber where he lay, and his two sons were with him, and he took his father's hand, and bowing down, he kissed him, and Isaac clung to the neck of Jacob, his son, and wept on his neck.</p>

<p class="v">9. And the darkness left Isaac's eyes, and he saw the two sons of Jacob, Levi and Judah, and he said, "Are these your sons, my son? For they are like you."</p>

<p class="v">10. And he told him that they were truly his sons: "And you have truly seen that they are truly my sons."</p>

<p class="v">11. And they drew near to him, and he turned and embraced them and kissed them both together.</p>

<p class="v">12. And the spirit of prophecy descended into his mouth, and he took Levi by his right hand and Judah by his left.</p>

<p class="v">13. And he turned first to Levi, and began to bless him first, and said to him, "May the God of all, the Lord of all the ages, bless you and your children in all the ages.</p>

<p class="v">14. And may the Lord give to you and to your posterity greatness and great glory, and make you and your posterity, out of all flesh, draw near to him to serve in his sanctuary like the angels of the presence and like the holy ones. (Even) as they are, the posterity of your sons shall be for glory, greatness, and holiness, and may he make them great in all the ages.</p>

<p class="v">15. And they shall be judges and princes, and chiefs of all the posterity of the sons of Jacob;</p>

<p class="v">They shall speak the word of the Lord in righteousness,</p>

<p class="v">And they shall judge all his judgments in righteousness.</p>

<p class="v">And they shall recount my ways to Jacob</p>

<p class="v">And my paths to Israel.</p>

<p class="v">The blessing of the Lord shall be given in their mouth</p>

<p class="v">To bless all the seed of the beloved.</p>

<p class="v">16. Your mother called you Levi,</p>

<p class="v">And rightly did she call your name;</p>

<p class="v">You shall be joined to the Lord</p>

<p class="v">And be the companion of all the sons of Jacob;</p>

<p class="v">Let his table be yours,</p>

<p class="v">And you and your sons, eat of it;</p>

<p class="v">And may your table be full for all generations,</p>

<p class="v">And your food shall not fail in all the ages.</p>

<p class="v">17. And may all who hate you fall before you,</p>

<p class="v">And may all your adversaries be rooted out and perish;</p>

<p class="v">And blessed be he who blesses you,</p>

<p class="v">And cursed be every nation that curses you.</p>

<p class="v">18. And he said to Judah:</p>

<p class="v">"May the Lord give you strength and power</p>

<p class="v">To tread down all who hate you;</p>

<p class="v">You shall be prince, you and one of your sons, over the sons of Jacob;</p>

<p class="v">May your name and that of your sons spread abroad and pass through every land and every region.</p>

<p class="v">Then the Gentiles shall fear before your face,</p>

<p class="v">And all the nations shall tremble</p>

<p class="v">[And all the peoples shall tremble].</p>

<p class="v">19. In you shall be the help of Jacob,</p>

<p class="v">And in you is found the salvation of Israel.</p>

<p class="v">20. And when you sit on the throne of honor of your righteousness</p>

<p class="v">There shall be great peace for all the posterity of the sons of the beloved;</p>

<p class="v">Blessed be he who blesses you,</p>

<p class="v">And all who hate you, afflict you, and curse you</p>

<p class="v">Shall be rooted out and destroyed from the earth and shall be cursed.</p>

<p class="v">21. And turning, he embraced him again and kissed him, and rejoiced greatly; for he had truly seen the sons of Jacob, his son.</p>

<p class="v">22. And he went out from between his feet, and fell down and bowed before him, and he blessed them, and rested there with Isaac, his father, that night, and they ate and drank with joy.</p>

<p class="v">23. And he made the two sons of Jacob sleep, one on his right and the other on his left, and this was reckoned to him for righteousness.</p>

<p class="v">24. And Jacob told everything to his father during the night, how the LORD had shown him great mercy, and how he had made him prosper in all his ways and had protected him from all evil.</p>

<p class="v">25. And Isaac blessed the God of his father Abraham, who had not withdrawn his mercy and his righteousness from the sons of his servant Isaac.</p>

<p class="v">26. And in the morning, Jacob told his father Isaac the vow that he had made to the Lord, and the vision that he had seen, and that he had built an altar, and that everything was ready for the sacrifice that was to be made before the Lord as he had promised, and that he had come to set it upon a donkey.</p>

<p class="v">27. And Isaac said to Jacob, his son, "I cannot go with you; for I am old and cannot bear the journey: go, my son, in peace; for I am today a hundred and sixty-five years old; I can no longer travel; set your mother (on a donkey) and let her go with you.</p>

<p class="v">28. "And I know, my son, that you came for my sake, and blessed be this day on which you have seen me alive, and I too have seen you, my son."</p>

<p class="v">29. May you prosper and fulfill the vow that you have made; and do not delay your vow; for you will be called to account for the vow. Now therefore hasten to fulfill it, and may he be satisfied — he who made everything, and he to whom you made this vow.</p>

<p class="v">30. And he said to Rebecca, "Go with Jacob, your son"; and Rebecca departed with Jacob, her son, and Deborah with her, and they came to Bethel.</p>

<p class="v">31. And Jacob remembered the prayer with which his father had blessed him, and his two sons, Levi and Judah, and he rejoiced and blessed the God of his fathers, Abraham and Isaac.</p>

<p class="v">32. And he said, "Now I know that I have an eternal hope, and my sons also, before the God of all"; and thus it is ordained concerning both of them; and they record it as an eternal testimony on the heavenly tablets, how Isaac blessed them.</p>
### Chapter 32 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">The dream of Levi at Bethel, 1. Levi chosen for the priesthood, as the tenth son, 2-3. Jacob celebrates the feast of tabernacles and offers the tithe through Levi: also the second tithe, 4-9. Law of tithes ordained, 10-15. Visions of Jacob in which Jacob reads on the heavenly tablets his own future and that of his descendants, 16-26. Celebrates the eighty days of the feast of tabernacles, 27-9. Death of Deborah, 30 years. Birth of Benjamin and death of Rachel, 33-4. (Cf. Gen. xxxv.8,10, 11, 13, 16-20.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And he spent that night at Bethel, and Levi dreamed that they had ordained him and established him as priest of the Most High God, him and his sons forever; and he awoke from his sleep and blessed the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">2. And Jacob rose early in the morning, on the fourteenth of that month, and he gave the tithe of all that had come with him, both of men and of cattle, of gold and of all the vessels and garments, yes, he gave the tithe of everything.</p>

<p class="v">3. And in those days Rachel became pregnant with her son Benjamin. And Jacob counted his sons beginning from himself, and Levi fell into the Lord's portion, and his father clothed him in the garments of the priesthood and filled his hands.</p>

<p class="v">4. And on the fifteenth of that month he brought to the altar fourteen oxen from among the cattle, twenty-eight rams, forty-nine sheep, seven lambs, and twenty-one kids as a burnt offering on the altar of sacrifice, pleasing and of a sweet savor before God.</p>

<p class="v">5. This was his offering, in fulfillment of the vow he had made to give the tenth, together with their fruit offerings and their libations.</p>

<p class="v">6. And when the fire had consumed it, he burned incense upon the fire, upon the fire, and as a thank offering, two oxen, four rams, four sheep, four goats and two yearling sheep, and two kids; and he did so every day for seven days.</p>

<p class="v">7. And he and all his sons and his men ate there with joy for seven days, and blessed and gave thanks to the Lord, who had delivered him from all his tribulations, and had fulfilled his vow for him.</p>

<p class="v">8. And he gave the tithe of all the clean animals, and made a burnt offering, but he did not give the unclean animals to Levi, his son, and he gave him all the souls of men.</p>

<p class="v">9. And Levi exercised the priestly office at Bethel before Jacob his father, in preference to his ten brothers, and he was priest there, and Jacob fulfilled his vow: thus he gave the tithe to the LORD and sanctified it, and it became holy unto Him.</p>

<p class="v">10. And it is for this reason that it is ordained on the heavenly tablets as a law concerning the tithe, that the tithe should again be eaten before the Lord year by year, in the place where it is chosen for His name to dwell, and to this law there is no limit of days forever.</p>

<p class="v">11. This ordinance is written that it should be fulfilled year by year, in eating the second tithe before the Lord in the place where it shall have been chosen, and that nothing of it shall remain from that year to the next.</p>

<p class="v">12. For within its own year the grain shall be eaten until the days of the harvest of that year's grain, and the wine until the days of the wine, and the oil until the days of its season.</p>

<p class="v">13. And all that remains of it and grows old, let it be considered polluted; let it be burned with fire, for it is unclean.</p>

<p class="v">14. And let them eat it thus together in the sanctuary, and let them not let it grow old.</p>

<p class="v">15. And all the tithes of the oxen and sheep shall be consecrated to the LORD, and shall belong to His priests, who shall eat them before Him year by year; for thus it is ordained and engraved concerning the tithe on the heavenly tablets.</p>

<p class="v">16. And the following night, on the twenty-second day of that month, Jacob resolved to rebuild that place and to surround the court with a wall, and to sanctify it and make it holy forever, for himself and his children after him.</p>

<p class="v">17. And the LORD appeared to him during the night, blessed him, and said to him: "Your name shall not be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name."</p>

<p class="v">18. And He said to him again: "I am the LORD who created the heaven and the earth, and I will increase you and multiply you exceedingly, and kings shall come forth from you, and they shall judge everywhere that the foot of the sons of men has trodden.</p>

<p class="v">19. "And I will give to your posterity all the earth that is under the heavens, and they shall judge all the nations according to their desires, and after that they shall take possession of the whole earth and inherit it forever."</p>

<p class="v">20. And He finished speaking with him, and He withdrew from him, and Jacob watched until He had ascended into heaven.</p>

<p class="v">21. And he saw in a vision of the night, and behold, an angel descended from heaven with seven tablets in his hands, and he gave them to Jacob, and he read them and knew all that was written therein, that would happen to him and his sons throughout all the ages.</p>

<p class="v">22. And he showed him all that was written on the tablets, and said to him: "Do not build this place, do not make it an eternal sanctuary, and do not dwell here; for this is not the place. Go to the house of Abraham your father and dwell with Isaac your father until the day of your father's death.</p>

<p class="v">23. "For in Egypt you shall die in peace, and in that land you shall be buried with honor in the sepulcher of your fathers, with Abraham and Isaac.</p>

<p class="v">24. "Fear nothing, for as you have seen and read, so shall everything be; and write down everything as you have seen and read.</p>

<p class="v">25. And Jacob said: "Lord, how can I remember all that I have read and seen?" And He said to him: "I will remind you of everything."</p>

<p class="v">26. And he rose up, and he awoke from his sleep, and he remembered all that he had read and seen, and he wrote down all the words that he had read and seen.</p>

<p class="v">27. And he celebrated yet another day there, and he sacrificed there according to all that he had sacrificed on the previous days, and he called its name "Addition," for that day was added, and the previous days he called "The Feast."</p>

<p class="v">28. And thus it was made manifest that it should be so, and this is written on the heavenly tablets; therefore it was revealed to him that he should celebrate it and add it to the seven days of the feast.</p>

<p class="v">29. And its name was called Addition, because it was recorded among the days of the feasts, according to the number of the days of the year.</p>

<p class="v">30. And in the night, on the twenty-third of that month, Deborah, the nurse of Rebecca, died, and she was buried below the city, under the oak by the river, and he called the name of that place, "The River of Deborah," and the oak, "The Oak of the Mourning of Deborah."</p>

<p class="v">31. And Rebecca departed and returned to her house, to her father Isaac, and Jacob sent by her rams, sheep, and goats, that she might prepare a meal for her father as he desired.</p>

<p class="v">32. And he followed his mother until he arrived in the land of Kabratan, and he dwelt there.</p>

<p class="v">33. And Rachel bore a son in the night, and she called his name "Son of my sorrow"; for she suffered in bearing him; but his father called him Benjamin, on the eleventh of the eighth month, the first year of the sixth week of this jubilee. [2143 AM]</p>

<p class="v">34. And Rachel died there, and she was buried in the land of Ephrath, that is Bethlehem, and Jacob built a pillar upon Rachel's grave, on the road above her tomb.</p>

### Chapter 33 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Reuben sins with Bilhah, 1-9 (cf. Gen. xxxv.21, 22). Laws concerning incest, 10-20. Children of Jacob, 22. (Cf. Gen. xxxv.23-7.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And Jacob departed and dwelt to the south of Magdaladra'ef. And he went to his father Isaac, he and Leah his wife, at the new moon of the tenth month.</p>

<p class="v">2. And Reuben saw Bilhah, the maidservant of Rachel, his father's concubine, bathing in the water in a secret place, and he loved her.</p>

<p class="v">3. And he hid himself at night, and he entered the house of Bilhah [at night], and he found her asleep alone on a bed in her house.</p>

<p class="v">4. And he lay with her, and she awoke and saw, and behold, Reuben was lying with her in the bed, and she uncovered the edge of his covering and seized it, and cried out, and discovered that it was Reuben.</p>

<p class="v">5. And she was ashamed because of him, and she loosed her hand, and he fled.</p>

<p class="v">6. And she lamented exceedingly because of this thing, and told no one of it.</p>

<p class="v">7. And when Jacob returned and sought her, she said to him: "I am not pure for you, for I have defiled myself toward you; for Reuben has defiled me, and he lay with me in the night, and I was asleep, and I did not discover it until he uncovered my skirt and lay with me."</p>

<p class="v">8. And Jacob was exceedingly angry with Reuben, because he had lain with Bilhah, because he had uncovered his father's skirt.</p>

<p class="v">9. And Jacob did not approach her again, because Reuben had defiled her. And as for any man who uncovers his father's skirts, his deed is exceedingly evil, for it is abominable before the LORD.</p>

<p class="v">10. Therefore it is written and ordained on the heavenly tablets that a man shall not lie with his father's wife, and shall not uncover his father's covering, for this is unclean: they shall surely die together, the man who lies with his father's wife, and the woman also, for they have committed impurity upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">11. And there shall be nothing unclean before our God in the nation which He has chosen for Himself as a possession.</p>

<p class="v">12. And again it is written a second time: "Cursed be he who lies with his father's wife, for he has uncovered his father's shame"; and all the saints of the Lord said: "So be it; so be it."</p>

<p class="v">13. And you, Moses, command the children of Israel to observe this word; for it involves a sentence of death; and it is unclean, and there is no eternal atonement for the man who has committed this, but he must be put to death and killed, and stoned with stones, and uprooted from the midst of the people of our God.</p>

<p class="v">14. For it is not permitted to anyone who does so in Israel to remain alive a single day upon the earth, for he is abominable and unclean.</p>

<p class="v">15. And let it not be said: Reuben received life and pardon after lying with his father's concubine, and to her also, though she had a husband, and though her husband Jacob, his father, was still alive.</p>

<p class="v">16. For until that time the ordinance, the judgment, and the law had not been revealed in their fullness to all, but in your days it has been revealed as a law of seasons and days, and an eternal law for everlasting generations.</p>

<p class="v">17. And for this law there is no expiry of days, nor atonement for it, but they must both be uprooted from the midst of the nation: on the day they committed it, they shall kill them.</p>

<p class="v">18. And you, Moses, write it down for Israel, that they may observe it and act according to these words, and not commit a sin that leads to death; for the Lord our God is judge, He does not respect persons and accepts no gift.</p>

<p class="v">19. And tell them these words of the covenant, that they may hear them and observe them, and be on their guard concerning them, and that they may not be destroyed and uprooted from the land; for it is an impurity, an abomination, a defilement, and a pollution, all those who commit this upon the earth before our God.</p>

<p class="v">20. And there is no greater sin than the fornication which they commit upon the earth; for Israel is a holy nation unto the LORD its God, and a nation of inheritance, and a priestly and royal nation, and for His own possession; and such impurity shall not appear in the midst of the holy nation.</p>

<p class="v">21. And in the third year of this sixth week [2145 AM] Jacob and all his sons went to dwell in the house of Abraham, near Isaac his father and Rebecca his mother.</p>

<p class="v">22. And these are the names of the sons of Jacob: the firstborn Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, the sons of Leah; and the sons of Rachel, Joseph and Benjamin; and the sons of Bilhah, Dan and Naphtali; and the sons of Zilpah, Gad and Asher; and Dinah, daughter of Leah, the only daughter of Jacob.</p>

<p class="v">23. And they came and bowed down before Isaac and Rebecca, and when they saw them, they blessed Jacob and all his sons, and Isaac rejoiced exceedingly, for he saw the sons of Jacob, his youngest son, and he blessed them.</p>

### Chapter 34 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">War of the Amorite kings against Jacob and his sons, 1-9. Jacob sends Joseph to visit his brothers, 10. Joseph sold and taken to Egypt, 11-12 (cf. Gen. xxxvii.14, 17, 18, 25, 32-6). Death of Bilhah and Dinah, 15. Jacob mourns Joseph, 13, 14, 17. Institution of the Day of Atonement on the day the news of Joseph's death arrived, 18-19. Wives of the sons of Jacob, 20-1.</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the sixth year of this week of this forty-fourth jubilee [2148 AM] Jacob sent his sons to pasture their sheep, and his servants with them, in the pastures of Shechem.</p>

<p class="v">2. And the seven kings of the Amorites gathered together against them, to kill them, hiding under the trees, and to take their cattle as prey.</p>

<p class="v">3. And Jacob, Levi, Judah, and Joseph were in the house with Isaac their father; for his spirit was sad, and they could not leave him; and Benjamin was the youngest, and it was for this reason that he remained with his father.</p>

<p class="v">4. And there came the kings of Taphu and the kings of 'Aresa, and the kings of Seragan, and the kings of Selo, and the kings of Ga'as, and the king of Bethoron, and the king of Ma'anisakir, and all who dwell in those mountains (and) who dwell in the woods of the land of Canaan.</p>

<p class="v">5. And they announced this to Jacob, saying: "Behold, the kings of the Amorites have surrounded your sons and plundered their flocks."</p>

<p class="v">6. And he rose up from his house, he and his three sons and all his father's servants and his own servants, and he marched against them with six thousand men who bore the sword.</p>

<p class="v">7. And he killed them in the pastures of Shechem, and pursued those who fled, and killed them by the edge of the sword, and he killed 'Aresa and Taphu and Saregan and Selo and 'Amani-sakir and Ga'as, and he recovered his flocks.</p>

<p class="v">8. And he subdued them and imposed a tribute upon them, that they should pay him tribute, five fruit-products of their land, and he built Robel and Tamnatares.</p>

<p class="v">9. And he returned in peace, and made peace with them, and they became his servants, until the day when he and his sons went down into Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">10. And in the seventh year of this week [2149 AM], he sent Joseph from his house to inquire after the welfare of his brothers in the land of Shechem, and he found them in the land of Dothan.</p>

<p class="v">11. And they betrayed him and formed a plot against him to kill him, but changing their minds, they sold him to Ishmaelite merchants, and they brought him down into Egypt, and they sold him to Potiphar, Pharaoh's eunuch, chief of the cooks, priest of the city of Elew.</p>

<p class="v">12. And the sons of Jacob slaughtered a kid, and dipped Joseph's tunic in the blood, and sent it to Jacob their father, on the tenth of the seventh month.</p>

<p class="v">13. And he wept all night, for it had been brought to him in the evening, and he became feverish with mourning because of his death, and he said: "An evil beast has devoured Joseph"; and all the members of his household [wept with him that day, and they] were in mourning and grief with him all that day.</p>

<p class="v">14. And his sons and his daughter rose up to console him, but he refused to be consoled for his son.</p>

<p class="v">15. And on that day Bilhah learned that Joseph had perished, and she died mourning him, and she dwelt at Qafratef, and Dinah also, his daughter, died after the death of Joseph.</p>

<p class="v">16. And these three mournings fell upon Israel within a single month. And they buried Bilhah near the tomb of Rachel, and Dinah also, his daughter, they buried there.</p>

<p class="v">17. And he mourned Joseph for a year, and did not cease, for he said: "Let me go down to the grave mourning my son."</p>

<p class="v">18. Therefore it is ordained for the children of Israel to afflict themselves on the tenth of the seventh month, the day on which the news that made Jacob his father weep for Joseph arrived, so that they might make atonement for themselves with a kid on the tenth of the seventh month, once a year, for their sins; for they had grieved their father's affection for Joseph, his son.</p>

<p class="v">19. And this day has been appointed for them to afflict themselves for their sins, for all their transgressions, and for all their errors, so that they may purify themselves on that day, once a year.</p>

<p class="v">20. And after the death of Joseph, the sons of Jacob took wives. The name of Reuben's wife is 'Ada; and the name of Simeon's wife is 'Adlba'a, a Canaanite; and the name of Levi's wife is Melka, of the daughters of Aram, of the posterity of the sons of Terah; and the name of Judah's wife, Betasu'el, a Canaanite; and the name of Issachar's wife, Hezaqa; and the name of Zebulun's wife, Ni'iman; and the name of Dan's wife, "Egla"; and the name of Naphtali's wife, Rasu'u, of Mesopotamia; and the name of Gad's wife, Maka; and the name of Asher's wife, 'Ijona; and the name of Joseph's wife, Asenath, the Egyptian; and the name of Benjamin's wife, 'Ijasaka.</p>

<p class="v">21. And Simeon repented and took, like his brothers, a second wife from Mesopotamia.</p>

### Chapter 35 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Rebecca's warning to Jacob and his answer, 1-8. Rebecca asks Isaac to make Esau swear that he will not harm Jacob, 9-12. Isaac consents, 13-17. Esau swears the oath, as does Jacob, 18-26. Death of Rebecca, 27.</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the first year of the first week of the forty-fifth jubilee [2157 AM] Rebecca called Jacob, her son, and commanded him concerning his father and his brother, to honor them all the days of his life.</p>

<p class="v">2. And Jacob said: "I will do everything just as you have commanded me; for it will be to me an honor and a greatness, and a righteousness before the LORD, that I honor them.</p>

<p class="v">3. "And you also, mother, know from my birth until this day all my deeds and all that is in my heart, that I always think of the good of everyone."</p>

<p class="v">4. "And how should I not do what you have commanded me, to honor my father and my brother!"</p>

<p class="v">5. "Tell me, mother, what perversity you have seen in me, and I will turn away from it, and mercy shall be upon me."</p>

<p class="v">6. And she said to him: "My son, I have not seen in you, in all my days, any perverse deed, but (only) upright deeds. And yet I will tell you the truth, my son: I shall die this year, and I shall not survive beyond this year of my life; for I have seen in a dream the day of my death, that I shall not live beyond a hundred and fifty-five years; and behold, I have completed all the days of my life that I am to live.</p>

<p class="v">7. And Jacob mocked his mother's words, because his mother had told him that she was going to die; and she sat before him, in full possession of her strength, and she was not weakened in her strength; for she went in and out and saw, and her teeth were strong, and no sickness had touched her all the days of her life.</p>

<p class="v">8. And Jacob said to her: "Blessed am I, mother, if my days approach the days of your life, and if my strength remains with me as your strength; and you shall not die, for you are jesting with me in vain concerning your death.</p>

<p class="v">9. And she went to Isaac and said to him: "I make one request of you: make Esau swear that he will not harm Jacob, and that he will not pursue him with enmity; for you know Esau's thoughts, that they have been perverse from his youth, and that there is no goodness in him; for he desires, after your death, to kill him.</p>

<p class="v">10. "And you know all that he has done from the day Jacob his brother went to Haran until this day: how he has abandoned us with his whole heart and done us harm; he has seized your flocks and carried off before your eyes all your goods.</p>

<p class="v">11. "And when we implored and entreated him for what belonged to us, he behaved like a man who had pity on us."</p>

<p class="v">12. "And he is bitter against you because you have blessed Jacob your perfect and upright son; for there is no evil but only good in him, and since he came from Haran until this day, he has stolen nothing from us, for he always brings us everything in its season and rejoices with all his heart when we take from his hands, and he blesses us and has not separated himself from us since he came from Haran until this day, and he remains continually with us in the house, honoring us.</p>

<p class="v">13. And Isaac said to her: "I too know and see the deeds of Jacob, who is with us, how he honors us with all his heart; but formerly I loved Esau more than Jacob, because he was the firstborn; but now I love Jacob more than Esau, for he has committed many evil deeds, and there is no righteousness in him, for all his ways are injustice and violence, [and there is no righteousness around him.]"</p>

<p class="v">14. "And now my heart is troubled because of all his deeds, and neither he nor his posterity are to be saved, for they are the ones who will be destroyed from the earth and uprooted from under heaven, for he has forsaken the God of Abraham and has gone after his wives, after their impurity and after their error, he and his children.</p>

<p class="v">15. "And you command me to make him swear that he will not kill Jacob his brother; even if he swears, he will not keep his oath, and he will do no good but only evil.</p>

<p class="v">16. "But if he wishes to kill Jacob his brother, he will be delivered into Jacob's hands, and he will not escape his hands, [for he will fall into his hands.]"</p>

<p class="v">17. "And fear nothing on account of Jacob; for the guardian of Jacob is great, mighty, honored, and more praised than the guardian of Esau.</p>

<p class="v">18. And Rebecca sent to call Esau, and he came to her, and she said to him: "I have a request, my son, to make of you, and promise me you will grant it, my son.</p>

<p class="v">19. And he said: "I will do everything you tell me, and I will not refuse your request."</p>

<p class="v">20. And she said to him: "I ask you that on the day of my death, you take me and bury me near Sarah, the mother of your father, and that you and Jacob love one another, and that neither of you desire evil against the other, but mutual love only, and (thus) you shall prosper, my sons, and be honored in the midst of the land, and no enemy shall rejoice over you, and you shall be a blessing and a mercy in the eyes of all who love you.</p>

<p class="v">21. And he said: "I will do all that you have told me, and I will bury you, on the day you die, near Sarah, the mother of my father, as you have desired that her bones be near yours.</p>

<p class="v">22. "And Jacob, my brother, I will also love above all flesh; for I have no brother on all the earth but him alone: and it is no great merit to me if I love him; for he is my brother, and we were sown together in your body, and we came forth together from your womb, and if I do not love my brother, whom shall I love?</p>

<p class="v">23. "And I myself beg you to exhort Jacob concerning me and my sons, for I know that he will surely be king over me and over my sons, for on the day my father blessed him, he raised him above and set me lower.</p>

<p class="v">24. "And I swear to you that I will love him and that I will not desire evil against him all the days of my life, but that I will desire only good.</p>

<p class="v">25. And he swore to her concerning this whole matter. And she called Jacob before the eyes of Esau, and gave him the commandment according to the words she had spoken to Esau.</p>

<p class="v">26. And he said: "I will do your good pleasure; believe me, no evil shall come from me or from my sons against Esau, and I will be first in nothing except in love alone.</p>

<p class="v">27. And they ate and drank, she and her sons, that night, and she died that night, at the age of three jubilees and one week and one year, and her two sons, Esau and Jacob, buried her in the double cave near Sarah, the mother of their father.</p>

### Chapter 36 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Isaac gives instructions to his sons concerning his burial: exhorts them to love one another and makes them curse the destruction of whoever harms his brother, 1-11. Divides his possessions, giving the greater share to Jacob, and dies, 12-18. Leah dies: the sons of Jacob come to comfort him, 21-4.</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the sixth year of this week [2162 AM] Isaac called his two sons Esau and Jacob, and they came to him, and he said to them: "My sons, I am going the way of my fathers, to the eternal house where my fathers are.</p>

<p class="v">2. "Therefore, bury me near Abraham my father, in the double cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite, where Abraham bought a sepulcher for burial; in the sepulcher which I have dug for myself, bury me there.</p>

<p class="v">3. "And this I command you, my sons, to practice righteousness and integrity upon the earth, that the LORD may bring upon you all that the LORD has said He would do for Abraham and his posterity.</p>

<p class="v">4. "And love one another, my sons, your brothers, as a man loves his own soul, and let each seek in what way he may benefit his brother, and act together upon the earth; and let them love one another as their own soul.</p>

<p class="v">5. "And concerning the matter of idols, I command you and exhort you to reject them, to hate them, and not to love them, for they are full of deceit for those who worship them and for those who bow down before them.</p>

<p class="v">6. "Remember, my sons, the Lord God of Abraham your father, and how I too have worshiped Him and served Him in righteousness and in joy, so that He may multiply you and increase your posterity like the stars of heaven in multitude, and establish you upon the earth as a plant of righteousness that shall not be uprooted throughout all generations.</p>

<p class="v">7. "And now I am going to make you swear a great oath — for there is no oath greater than that by the glorious and honored and great and splendid and wonderful and mighty name, of Him who created the heavens and the earth and all things together, so that you may fear Him and worship Him.</p>

<p class="v">8. "And that each shall love his brother with affection and righteousness, and that no one shall desire evil against his brother from now on and forever, all the days of your life, so that you may prosper in all your deeds and not be destroyed.</p>

<p class="v">9. "And if one of you plots evil against his brother, know that from now on whoever plots evil against his brother shall fall into his hands, and shall be uprooted from the land of the living, and his posterity shall be destroyed from under heaven.</p>

<p class="v">10. "But on the day of turbulence, of execration, of indignation and of wrath, with a flaming and devouring fire, as it burned Sodom, so shall it burn his land and his city and all that belongs to him, and he shall be blotted out of the book of the discipline of the children of men, and shall not be recorded in the book of life, but in that which is destined for destruction, and he shall go into everlasting execration; so that their condemnation may be forever renewed in hatred and in execration and in wrath and in torment and in indignation and in plagues and in sickness forever.</p>

<p class="v">11. "I tell you this and testify to you, my sons, according to the judgment that will fall upon the man who wants to do evil to his brother.</p>

<p class="v">12. And he divided all his possessions between the two of them that day, and he gave the greater portion to the one who was the firstborn, and the tower and all that was around it, and all that Abraham possessed at the well of the oath.</p>

<p class="v">13. And he said: "This greater portion, I will give to the firstborn."</p>

<p class="v">14. And Esau said: "I have sold to Jacob, and I have given my birthright to Jacob; let it be given to him, and I have not a single word to say about it, for it is his."</p>

<p class="v">15. And Isaac said: "Let a blessing rest today upon you, my sons, and upon your posterity, for you have given me rest, and my heart is not grieved concerning the birthright, lest you should do evil because of it.</p>

<p class="v">16. "May the Most High God bless the man who practices righteousness, him and his posterity forever."</p>

<p class="v">17. And he finished giving them instructions and blessing them, and they ate and drank together before him, and he rejoiced because there was but one soul between them, and they went out from him, rested that day, and slept.</p>

<p class="v">18. And Isaac slept that day upon his bed, rejoicing; and he slept the eternal sleep, and died at the age of a hundred and eighty years. He had completed twenty-five weeks and five years; and his two sons Esau and Jacob buried him.</p>

<p class="v">19. And Esau departed for the land of Edom, to the mountains of Seir, and he dwelt there.</p>

<p class="v">20. And Jacob dwelt in the mountains of Hebron, in the tower of the land of his father Abraham's sojourning, and he worshiped the LORD with all his heart and according to the visible commandments, according as he had divided the days of his generations.</p>

<p class="v">21. And Leah, his wife, died in the fourth year of the second week of the forty-fifth jubilee, [2167 AM] and he buried her in the double cave near Rebecca his mother, to the left of the tomb of Sarah, his father's mother.</p>

<p class="v">22. And all his sons and his sons came to weep with him for Leah his wife, and to console him about her, for he mourned her, for he had loved her exceedingly after the death of Rachel her sister.</p>

<p class="v">23. For she was perfect and upright in all her ways and honored Jacob, and during all the time she lived with him, he did not hear a harsh word from her mouth, for she was gentle and peaceable, upright and honorable.</p>

<p class="v">24. And he remembered all the deeds she had done during her life, and he mourned her exceedingly; for he loved her with all his heart and with all his soul.</p>

### Chapter 37 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">The sons of Esau reproach him for his subordination to Jacob, and compel him to make war with the help of 4,000 mercenaries against Jacob, 1-15. Jacob rebukes Esau, 16-17. Esau's answer, 18-25.</p>

<p class="v">1. And on the day Isaac died, the father of Jacob and Esau, [2162 AM] the sons of Esau learned that Isaac had given the portion of the elder to his younger son Jacob, and they were very angry.</p>

<p class="v">2. And they disputed with their father, saying: "Why has your father given to Jacob the portion of the elder, and ignored you, though you are the elder and Jacob the younger?"</p>

<p class="v">3.
