And he said to them: "Because I sold my birthright to Jacob for a small dish of lentils, and on the day my father sent me to hunt and catch something and bring it to him to eat and bless me, he came by deceit, and I brought food and drink to my father, and my father blessed him and set him under his hand.</p>

<p class="v">4. "And now our father has made us swear, him and me, that we will not plot evil against one another, nor against his brother, and that we will continue in love and peace each with his brother, and that we will not make our ways corrupt."</p>

<p class="v">5. And they said to him: "We will not listen to you to make peace with him; for our strength is greater than his strength, and we are more powerful than he; we will go against him, we will kill him, and we will destroy him and his sons. And if you do not come with us, we will do you harm also."</p>

<p class="v">6. "And now listen to us: let us send to Aram and to Philistia and to Moab and Ammon, and choose for ourselves picked men who are eager for battle, and let us go against him and fight against him, and exterminate him from the earth before he becomes strong."</p>

<p class="v">7. And their father said to them: "Do not go and make war against him, lest you fall before him."</p>

<p class="v">8. And they said to him: "This is exactly your way of acting from your youth until this day, and you put your neck under his yoke."</p>

<p class="v">9. "We will not listen to these words." And they sent to Aram and to Aduram, to their father's friend, and they hired with them a thousand fighters, chosen men of war.</p>

<p class="v">10. And there came from Moab and from the children of Ammon, those who had been hired, a thousand chosen men, and from Philistia, a thousand chosen men of war, and from Edom and the Horites a thousand chosen fighters, and from Kittim, mighty men of war.</p>

<p class="v">11. And they said to their father: "Go out with them and lead them, or else we will kill you."</p>

<p class="v">12. And he was filled with anger and indignation, seeing that his sons were forcing him to march before them, to lead them against Jacob his brother.</p>

<p class="v">13. But then he remembered all the evil that was hidden in his heart against Jacob his brother; and he did not remember the oath he had sworn to his father and his mother not to plot any evil, all his life, against Jacob his brother.</p>

<p class="v">14. And despite all this, Jacob did not know that they were going to attack him to fight him, and he mourned Leah his wife, until they drew very near to the tower with four thousand warriors and chosen men of war.</p>

<p class="v">15. And the men of Hebron sent to tell him: "Behold, your brother has come against you to fight you, with four thousand girded with the sword, and they carry shields and weapons"; for they loved Jacob more than Esau. So they told him; for Jacob was a more generous and more merciful man than Esau.</p>

<p class="v">16. But Jacob did not believe it until they were very near the tower.</p>

<p class="v">17. And he shut the gates of the tower; and he stood upon the battlements and spoke to his brother Esau, and said: "Noble is the consolation with which you have come to console me for my wife who has died. Is this the oath that you swore to your father, and again to your mother, before their death? You have broken the oath, and at the moment you swore it to your father, you were condemned.</p>

<p class="v">18. Then Esau answered and said to him: "Neither the children of men nor the beasts of the earth have any oath of righteousness that they have sworn in swearing (a valid oath) forever; but every day they devise evil against one another, and how each may kill his adversary and his enemy.</p>

<p class="v">19. "And you hate me and my children forever. And there is no bond of brotherhood with you.</p>

<p class="v">20. "Hear these words that I declare to you,</p>

<p class="v">If the wild boar can change its skin and make its bristles as soft as wool,</p>

<p class="v">Or if it can sprout horns upon its head, like those of a stag or a sheep,</p>

<p class="v">Then will I observe the bond of brotherhood with you</p>

<p class="v">And if the breasts have separated from their mother, for you are not a brother to me.</p>

<p class="v">21. And if wolves make peace with lambs so as not to devour them nor do them violence,</p>

<p class="v">And if their heart is turned toward them for good,</p>

<p class="v">Then there will be peace in my heart toward you</p>

<p class="v">22. And if the lion becomes the friend of the ox and makes peace with him</p>

<p class="v">And if he is bound with him under the same yoke and plows with him,</p>

<p class="v">Then will I make peace with you.</p>

<p class="v">23. And when the raven becomes white as the raza,</p>

<p class="v">Then know that I have loved you</p>

<p class="v">And I will make peace with you</p>

<p class="v">You shall be uprooted,</p>

<p class="v">And your sons shall be uprooted,</p>

<p class="v">And there shall be no peace for you."</p>

<p class="v">24. And when Jacob saw that he was (so) wicked toward him with all his heart and all his soul, to the point of killing him, and that he had come leaping like the wild boar that comes upon the spear that pierces and kills it, and does not draw back before it;</p>

<p class="v">25. Then he told his own men and his servants to attack him, him and all his companions.</p>

### Chapter 38 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">War between Jacob and Esau. Death of Esau and the rout of his forces, 1-10. Edom reduced to servitude "unto this day," 11-14. Kings of Edom, 15-24. (Cf. Gen. xxxvi.31-9.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And after that Judah spoke to Jacob his father, and said to him: "Bend your bow, father, and send forth your arrows, and strike down the adversary and kill the enemy; and may you have the power, for we will not kill your brother, for he is like you, and he is like you — let us give him this honor."</p>

<p class="v">2. Then Jacob bent his bow and sent forth the arrow, and struck Esau his brother (in his right breast) and killed him.</p>

<p class="v">3. And he shot another arrow and struck 'Adoran the Aramean in the left breast, then drove him backward and killed him.</p>

<p class="v">4. Then the sons of Jacob went out, they and their servants, dividing themselves into groups on the four sides of the tower.</p>

<p class="v">5. And Judah went out at the head, and Naphtali and Gad with him, and fifty servants with him, on the south side of the tower, and they killed everyone they found before them, and not one of them escaped.</p>

<p class="v">6. And Levi, Dan, and Asher went out on the east side of the tower, and fifty men with them, and they struck down the fighters of Moab and Ammon.</p>

<p class="v">7. And Reuben, Issachar, and Zebulun went out on the north side of the tower, and fifty men with them, and they struck down the fighters of the Philistines.</p>

<p class="v">8. And Simeon, Benjamin, and Enoch, son of Reuben, went out on the west side of the tower, and fifty men with them, and they killed four hundred men of Edom and the Horites, valiant warriors; and six hundred fled, and four of the sons of Esau fled with them, and left their father slain, as he had fallen on the hill that is at Aduram.</p>

<p class="v">9. And the sons of Jacob pursued them as far as the mountains of Seir. And Jacob buried his brother on the hill that is at Aduram, and he returned to his house.</p>

<p class="v">10. And the sons of Jacob pressed hard upon the sons of Esau in the mountains of Seir, and bowed their necks, so that they became servants to the sons of Jacob.</p>

<p class="v">11. And they sent to their father to know whether they should make peace with them or kill them.</p>

<p class="v">12. And Jacob sent word to his sons that they should make peace, and they made peace with them, and placed upon them the yoke of servitude, so that they always paid tribute to Jacob and his sons.</p>

<p class="v">13. And they continued to pay tribute to Jacob until the day he went down into Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">14. And the sons of Edom have not been delivered from the yoke of servitude which the twelve sons of Jacob imposed upon them, unto this day.</p>

<p class="v">15. And these are the kings who reigned in Edom before any king reigned over the children of Israel, [unto this day] in the land of Edom.</p>

<p class="v">16. And Balak, son of Beor, reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Danaba.</p>

<p class="v">17. And Balak died, and Jobab, son of Zara of Boser, reigned in his place.</p>

<p class="v">18. And Jobab died, and 'Asam, of the land of Theman, reigned in his place.</p>

<p class="v">19. And 'Asam died, and 'Adath, son of Barad, who slew Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place, and the name of his city was Avith.</p>

<p class="v">20. And 'Adath died, and Salman, of 'Amaseqa, reigned in his place.</p>

<p class="v">21. And Salman died, and Saul of Ra'aboth by the river reigned in his place.</p>

<p class="v">22. And Saul died, and Ba'elunan, son of Achbor, reigned in his place.</p>

<p class="v">23. And Ba'elunan, son of Achbor, died, and 'Adath reigned in his place, and the name of his wife was Maitabith, daughter of Matarat, daughter of Metabedza'ab.</p>

<p class="v">24. These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom.</p>
### Chapter 39 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Joseph is set over Potiphar's house, 1-4. His purity and his imprisonment, 5-13. Imprisonment of Pharaoh's chief butler and chief baker, whose dreams Joseph interprets, 14-18. (Cf. Gen. xxxvii.2; xxxix.3-8, 12-15, 17-23; xl.1-5, 21-3; xli.1.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And Jacob dwelt in the land where his father sojourned, in the land of Canaan. These are the generations of Jacob.</p>

<p class="v">2. And Joseph was seventeen years old when he was taken down to the land of Egypt, and Potiphar, a eunuch of Pharaoh, the chief cook, bought him.</p>

<p class="v">3. And he set Joseph over all his house, and the blessing of the LORD came upon the house of the Egyptian for Joseph's sake, and the LORD prospered him in everything he did.</p>

<p class="v">4. And the Egyptian committed everything into Joseph's hands; for he saw that the Lord was with him, and that the Lord made him prosper in everything he did.</p>

<p class="v">5. And Joseph's appearance was comely [and his appearance was very comely], and his master's wife lifted up her eyes and saw Joseph, and she loved him and begged him to lie with her.</p>

<p class="v">6. But he did not give up his soul, and he remembered the Lord and the words that Jacob, his father, used to read among the words of Abraham, that no man should give himself to fornication with a woman who has a husband; that for him the punishment of death has been ordained in the heavens before the Most High God, and that the sin will be recorded against him in the eternal books continually before the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">7. And Joseph remembered these words and refused to lie with her.</p>

<p class="v">8. And she begged him for a year, but he refused and would not listen.</p>

<p class="v">9. But she embraced him and kept him in the house to force him to lie with her, and shut the doors of the house and held him fast; but he left his garment in her hands, broke through the door, and fled outside, away from her.</p>

<p class="v">10. And the woman saw that he would not lie with her, and she slandered him in the presence of her master, saying, "Your Hebrew servant, whom you love, sought to force me to lie with him; and when I raised my voice, he fled and left his garment in my hands when I held him, and he forced the door."</p>

<p class="v">11. And the Egyptian saw Joseph's garment and the broken door, and heard his wife's words, and cast Joseph into prison, in the place where the prisoners whom the king had imprisoned were kept.</p>

<p class="v">12. And he was there, in the prison; and the Lord gave Joseph favor in the eyes of the chief of the prison guards, and compassion before him, for he saw that the Lord was with him, and that the Lord made everything he did prosper.</p>

<p class="v">13. And he committed all things into his hands, and the chief of the prison guards knew nothing of what was in his charge, for Joseph did everything, and the Lord made it perfect.</p>

<p class="v">14. And he remained there two years. And at that time, Pharaoh, king of Egypt, was angry with his two eunuchs, the chief butler and the chief baker, and he put them under guard in the house of the chief cook, in the prison where Joseph was held.</p>

<p class="v">15. And the chief of the prison guards appointed Joseph to serve them; and he served before them.</p>

<p class="v">16. And they both had a dream, the chief butler and the chief baker, and they told it to Joseph.</p>

<p class="v">17. And as he had explained to them what would happen to them, Pharaoh restored the chief butler to his office, and put the (chief) baker to death, just as Joseph had interpreted it to them.</p>

<p class="v">18. But the chief butler forgot Joseph in the prison, although Joseph had told him what would happen to him, and he did not remember to inform Pharaoh how Joseph had told him, for he had forgotten.</p>

### Chapter 40 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Pharaoh's dreams and their interpretation, 1-4. Joseph's elevation and marriage, 5-13. (Cf. Gen. xli.1-5, 7-9, 14 ff., 25, 29-30, 34, 36, 38-43, 45-6, 49.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And in those days, Pharaoh had two dreams in one night concerning a famine that was to rage throughout the land, and he awoke from his sleep and called all the interpreters of dreams who were in Egypt, and the magicians, and told them his two dreams, and they could not declare them.</p>

<p class="v">2. And then the chief butler remembered Joseph and spoke of him to the king, and he brought him out of the prison, and he told his two dreams before him.</p>

<p class="v">3. And he said before Pharaoh that his two dreams were but one, and he said to him, "Seven years will come [in which there will be] abundance throughout all the land of Egypt, and after that seven years of famine, such a famine as there has not been in all the land."</p>

<p class="v">4. "And now, let Pharaoh appoint overseers throughout all the land of Egypt, and let them store up food in every city during the days of the years of abundance, and there will be food for the seven years of famine, and the land will not perish because of the famine, for it will be very severe."</p>

<p class="v">5. And the LORD gave Joseph favor and mercy in the eyes of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh said to his servants, "We shall not find a man as wise and discerning as this man, for the spirit of the Lord is with him."</p>

<p class="v">6. And he set him as second in all his kingdom, and gave him authority over all Egypt, and made him ride in Pharaoh's second chariot.</p>

<p class="v">7. And he clothed him in garments of fine linen, and put a gold chain around his neck, and (a herald) proclaimed before him, "'El 'El wa 'Abirer," and put a ring on his hand, and made him rule over all his house; he magnified him and said to him, "Only on the throne shall I be greater than you."</p>

<p class="v">8. And Joseph ruled over all the land of Egypt, and all Pharaoh's princes, and all his servants, and all who attended to the affairs of the king, loved him, for he walked in uprightness, for he was without pride or arrogance, and he had no respect of persons and accepted no gifts, but he judged all the inhabitants of the land with integrity.</p>

<p class="v">9. And the land of Egypt was at peace before Pharaoh because of Joseph, for the LORD was with him and granted him favor and mercy throughout all his generations before all who knew him and those who heard of him, and Pharaoh's kingdom was well ordered, and there was neither Satan nor any wicked person (within it).</p>

<p class="v">10. And the king called Joseph by the name Sephantiphanes, and he gave Joseph to wife the daughter of Potiphar, daughter of the priest of Heliopolis, the chief cook.</p>

<p class="v">11. And on the day when Joseph presented himself before Pharaoh, he was thirty years old [when he presented himself before Pharaoh].</p>

<p class="v">12. And in that year Isaac died. And it came to pass, as Joseph had said in the interpretation of his two dreams, as he had said, that there were seven years of abundance in all the land of Egypt, and the land of Egypt produced abundantly, one measure (yielding) eighteen hundred measures.</p>

<p class="v">13. And Joseph gathered food in every city until they were full of wheat, until they could no longer count it or measure it for its abundance.</p>

### Chapter 41 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">The sons of Judah and Tamar, 1-7. Judah's incest with Tamar, 8-18. Tamar gives birth to twins, 21-2. Judah is forgiven, because he sinned in ignorance and repented once he was found guilty, and because Tamar's marriage to his sons had not been consummated, 23-8. (Cf. Gen. xxxviii.6-18, 20-6, 29-30; xli.13.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the forty-fifth jubilee, in the second week, (and) the second year, [2165 AM] Judah took for his firstborn Er a wife from among the daughters of Aram, named Tamar.</p>

<p class="v">2. But he hated her and did not lie with her, because his mother was one of the daughters of Canaan, and he wanted to take a wife for himself from among his mother's kindred, but Judah, his father, would not permit it.</p>

<p class="v">3. And this Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked, and the LORD put him to death.</p>

<p class="v">4. And Judah said to Onan, his brother, "Go in to your brother's wife and perform toward her the duty of a husband's brother, and raise up seed for your brother."</p>

<p class="v">5. And Onan knew that the seed would not be his, (but) his brother's alone, and he went into his brother's wife's house, and spilled the seed on the ground, and he was wicked in the eyes of the Lord, and He slew him.</p>

<p class="v">6. And Judah said to Tamar, his daughter-in-law, "Remain in your father's house as a widow until Shelah, my son, is grown, and I will give you to him as wife."</p>

<p class="v">7. And he grew up; but Bedsu'el, Judah's wife, would not permit her son Shelah to marry. And Bedsu'el, Judah's wife, died [2168 AM] in the fifth year of that week.</p>

<p class="v">8. And in the sixth year, Judah went up to shear his sheep at Timnah. [2169 AM] And they said to Tamar, "Behold, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep."</p>

<p class="v">9. And she took off her widow's garments, and put on a veil, and adorned herself, and sat at the gate that is near the road to Timnah.</p>

<p class="v">10. And as Judah was going along, he found her and took her for a harlot, and he said to her, "Let me come in to you"; and she said to him, "Come in," and he went in.</p>

<p class="v">11. And she said to him, "Give me my wages"; and he said to her, "I have nothing in my hand except the ring that is on my finger, and my necklace, and my staff that is in my hand."</p>

<p class="v">12. And she said to him, "Give them to me until you send me my wages," and he said to her, "I will send you a kid"; and he gave them to her, and he went in to her, and she conceived by him.</p>

<p class="v">13. And Judah went to his sheep, and she went to her father's house.</p>

<p class="v">14. And Judah sent a kid by the hand of his shepherd, an Adullamite, and he did not find her; and he asked the men of the place, saying, "Where is the harlot who was here?" And they said to him, "There is no harlot here with us."</p>

<p class="v">15. And he returned and told him, and said that he had not found her: "I asked the men of the place, and they told me, 'There is no harlot here.'"</p>

<p class="v">16. And he said, "Let her keep them, lest we become a cause of ridicule." And when she had completed three months, it became evident that she was with child, and they told Judah, "Behold, Tamar, your daughter-in-law, is with child by harlotry."</p>

<p class="v">17. And Judah went to his father's house, and said to his father and his brothers, "Bring her out, and let them burn her, for she has committed impurity in Israel."</p>

<p class="v">18. And it came to pass, when she was brought out to be burned, that she sent to her father-in-law the ring, the necklace, and the staff, saying, "Discern to whom these belong, for it is by him that I am with child."</p>

<p class="v">19. And Judah acknowledged them and said, "Tamar is more righteous than I."</p>

<p class="v">20. "And therefore let them not burn her." And for this reason she was not given to Shelah, and he did not approach her again.</p>

<p class="v">21. And after this she bore two sons, Perez [2170 AM] and Zerah, in the seventh year of that second week.</p>

<p class="v">22. And then the seven years of fruitfulness of which Joseph spoke to Pharaoh were completed.</p>

<p class="v">23. And Judah acknowledged that the deed he had committed was evil, for he had lain with his daughter-in-law, and he deemed it odious in his eyes, and he acknowledged that he had transgressed and gone astray, for he had uncovered his son's garment, and he began to lament and to plead before the Lord because of his transgression.</p>

<p class="v">24. And we told him in a dream that it was forgiven him because he had pleaded fervently, and had lamented, and had not committed it again.</p>

<p class="v">25. And he received forgiveness because he turned away from his sin and his ignorance, for he had transgressed greatly before our God; and whoever does thus, whoever lies with his mother-in-law, let him be burned with fire, that he may burn in it, for there is upon them impurity and defilement — let them be burned with fire.</p>

<p class="v">26. And you shall command the children of Israel that there be no impurity among them, for whoever lies with his daughter-in-law or with his mother-in-law has committed an impurity; let the man who lay with her be burned with fire, and the woman also, and it will turn away wrath and punishment from Israel.</p>

<p class="v">27. And we told Judah that his two sons had not lain with her, and for this reason his posterity was established for a second generation and would not be uprooted.</p>

<p class="v">28. For, with a single-hearted intent, he had gone to seek a punishment, namely that, according to the judgment of Abraham, which he had commanded his sons, Judah had sought to burn her with fire.</p>

### Chapter 42 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Because of the famine, Jacob sends his sons to Egypt to procure grain, 1-4. Joseph recognizes them and detains Simeon, and asks them to bring Benjamin on their return, 5-12. Despite Jacob's reluctance, his sons take Benjamin with them on their second journey and are entertained by Joseph, 13-25. (Cf. Gen. xli.54, 56; xlii.7-9, 13, 17, 20, 24-5, 29-30, 34-8; xliii.1-2, 4-5, 8-9, 11, 15, 23, 26, 29, 34; xliv.1-2.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the first year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee, the famine began to fall upon the land, and the rain refused to fall upon the earth, for none fell at all.</p>

<p class="v">2. And the earth became barren, but in the land of Egypt there was food, for Joseph had gathered the seed of the land during the seven years of abundance and had preserved it.</p>

<p class="v">3. And the Egyptians came to Joseph that he might give them food, and he opened the storehouses where the grain of the first year was, and sold it to the people of the land for gold.</p>

<p class="v">4. (Now the famine was very great in the land of Canaan), and Jacob heard that there was food in Egypt, and he sent his ten sons to procure food for him in Egypt; but he did not send Benjamin, and (Jacob's ten sons) arrived (in Egypt) among those who were going there.</p>

<p class="v">5. And Joseph recognized them, but they did not recognize him, and he spoke to them and questioned them, and he said to them, "Are you not spies, and have you not come to explore the approaches to the land?" And he put them in a cell.</p>

<p class="v">6. And after that he released them again, and kept Simeon alone, and sent his nine brothers away.</p>

<p class="v">7. And he filled their sacks with wheat, and put their gold in their sacks, and they did not know it.</p>

<p class="v">8. And he commanded them to bring their young brother, for they had told him that their father was alive, and their young brother.</p>

<p class="v">9. And they went up from the land of Egypt and arrived in the land of Canaan; they told their father all that had happened to them, and how the lord of the land had spoken harshly to them and had seized Simeon until they should bring Benjamin.</p>

<p class="v">10. And Jacob said, "You have bereaved me of my children! Joseph is not here, and Simeon is not here either, and you would take Benjamin away. Your wickedness has come upon me."</p>

<p class="v">11. And he said, "My son will not go down with you, lest he fall ill; for their mother bore two sons, and one has perished, and you would take this one from me also. If by chance he should catch a fever on the way, you would bring down my old age with sorrow to the grave."</p>

<p class="v">12. For he saw that their money had been returned to each one in his sack, and for this reason he was afraid to send him.</p>

<p class="v">13. And the famine increased and grew severe in the land of Canaan and in all lands except the land of Egypt, for many of the children of the Egyptians had stored up their seed for food from the time they saw Joseph gathering seed together, and putting it in storehouses and preserving it for the years of famine.</p>

<p class="v">14. And the Egyptian people fed on it during the first year of their famine.</p>

<p class="v">15. But when Israel saw that the famine was very great in the land, and that there was no deliverance, he said to his sons, "Go back and procure food for us, that we may not die."</p>

<p class="v">16. And they said, "We will not go; if our youngest brother does not go with us, we will not go."</p>

<p class="v">17. And Israel saw that if he did not send him with them, they would all perish because of the famine.</p>

<p class="v">18. And Reuben said, "Deliver him into my hands, and if I do not bring him back to you, kill my two sons in place of his life."</p>

<p class="v">19. And he said to him, "He will not go with you." And Judah came near and said, "Send him with me, and if I do not bring him back to you, let me bear the blame before you all the days of my life."</p>

<p class="v">20. And he sent him with them in the second year of that week, on the first day of the month [2172 AM], and they arrived in the land of Egypt with all those who had gone there, and (they had) gifts in their hands: stacte, and almonds, and terebinth nuts, and pure honey.</p>

<p class="v">21. And they went and stood before Joseph, and he saw Benjamin his brother, and he knew him, and said to them, "Is this your youngest brother?" And they said to him, "It is he." And he said, "May the Lord show you grace, my son!"</p>

<p class="v">22. And he sent him into his house, and brought Simeon to them, and made a feast for them, and they presented to him the gift they had brought in their hands.</p>

<p class="v">23. And they ate before him, and he gave a portion to each of them, but Benjamin's portion was seven times greater than that of any of the others.</p>

<p class="v">24. And they ate and drank, then rose and stayed with their donkeys.</p>

<p class="v">25. And Joseph devised a plan by which he might know their thoughts, to see whether thoughts of peace prevailed among them, and he said to the steward who was over his house, "Fill all their sacks with food, and return their money into their vessels, and my cup, the silver cup from which I drink, put it in the youngest one's sack, and send them away."</p>

### Chapter 43 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Joseph's plan to test his brothers, 1-10. Judah's plea, 11-13. Joseph makes himself known to his brothers and sends them to fetch his father, 14-24. (Cf. Gen. xliv.3-10, 12-18, 27-8, 30-2; xlv.1-2, 5-9, 12, 18, 20-1, 23, 25-8.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And he did as Joseph had told him, and filled all their sacks with food for them, and put their money in their sacks, and put the cup in Benjamin's sack.</p>

<p class="v">2. And they set out early in the morning, and it came to pass that, when they had gone from there, Joseph said to the steward of his house, "Pursue them, run and seize them, saying, 'For good you have repaid me with evil; you have stolen the silver cup from which my lord drinks.' And bring back their youngest brother to me, and go fetch him quickly before I go to my seat of judgment."</p>

<p class="v">3. And he ran after them and spoke to them according to these words.</p>

<p class="v">4. And they said to him, "Far be it from your servants to do this and to steal any vessel from your lord's house; as for the money that we found in our sacks the first time, we, your servants, brought it back from the land of Canaan."</p>

<p class="v">5. "How then should we steal a vessel? Behold, we are ready to be searched together with our sacks, and wherever you find the cup, in the sack of any of us, let him be killed, and we and our donkeys will serve your lord."</p>

<p class="v">6. And he said to them, "No, the man in whose sack I find it, him alone will I take as a servant, and you shall return in peace to your home."</p>

<p class="v">7. And as he searched their vessels, beginning with the eldest and ending with the youngest, it was found in Benjamin's sack.</p>

<p class="v">8. And they tore their garments, and loaded their donkeys, and returned to the city and arrived at Joseph's house, and they all fell prostrate, face to the ground, before him.</p>

<p class="v">9. And Joseph said to them, "You have done evil." And they said, "What shall we say, and how shall we defend ourselves? Our lord has discovered the transgression of his servants; behold, we are our lord's servants, and our donkeys also."</p>

<p class="v">10. And Joseph said to them, "I also fear the LORD; as for you, go home, and let your brother be my servant, for you have done evil. Do you not know that a man delights in his cup as I do in this cup? And yet you have stolen it from me."</p>

<p class="v">11. And Judah said, "O my lord, let your servant, I pray you, speak a word in my lord's ear. Your servant's mother bore two brothers to our father: one went away, was lost, and was not found again, and he alone remains of his mother, and your servant our father loves him, and his life also is bound up with the life of this (boy)."</p>

<p class="v">12. "And it will come to pass that, when we go to your servant our father, and the boy is not with us, he will die, and we will bring down our father with sorrow to the grave."</p>

<p class="v">13. "Now let me, your servant, remain instead of the boy as a slave to my lord, and let the boy go with his brothers, for I pledged myself for him to your servant our father, and if I do not bring him back, your servant shall bear the blame before our father forever."</p>

<p class="v">14. And Joseph saw that they were all agreed in kindness with one another, and he could not restrain himself, and he told them that he was Joseph.</p>

<p class="v">15. And he spoke with them in the Hebrew language, fell upon their necks, and wept.</p>

<p class="v">16. But they did not recognize him, and they began to weep. And he said to them, "Do not weep over me, but hurry and bring me my father; and you see that it is my mouth that speaks, and that the eyes of my brother Benjamin see."</p>

<p class="v">17. "For behold, this is the second year of the famine, and there are still five years without harvest, or fruit of trees, or plowing."</p>

<p class="v">18. "Come down quickly, you and your households, that you may not perish by the famine, and that you may not be grieved because of your possessions, for the LORD sent me before you to set things in order, that many people might live."</p>

<p class="v">19. "And tell my father that I am still alive, and you see, you see that the LORD has established me as a father to Pharaoh, and as head of his house and of all the land of Egypt."</p>

<p class="v">20. "And tell my father of all my glory, and of all the wealth and the glory that the LORD has given me."</p>

<p class="v">21. And at the command from Pharaoh's mouth, he gave them chariots and provisions for the way, and he gave them all garments of many colors and money.</p>

<p class="v">22. And he sent to their father garments, money, and ten donkeys carrying wheat, and he sent them away.</p>

<p class="v">23. And they went up and told their father that Joseph was alive, that he measured out grain to all the nations of the earth, and that he was head of all the land of Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">24. And their father did not believe them, for he was beside himself in spirit; but when he saw the chariots that Joseph had sent, the life of his spirit returned, and he said, "It is enough for me if Joseph is alive; I will go down to see him before I die."</p>

### Chapter 44 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Jacob celebrates the feast of firstfruits, and, encouraged by a vision, goes down into Egypt, 1-10. Names of his descendants, 11-34. (Cf. Gen. xlvi.1-28.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And Israel set out from Haran, from his house, at the new moon of the third month, and he followed the road of the Well of the Oath, and he offered a sacrifice to the God of his father Isaac on the seventh of that month.</p>

<p class="v">2. And Jacob remembered the dream he had seen at Bethel, and he was afraid to go down into Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">3. And while he was thinking of sending word to Joseph to come to him, and that he would not go down, he remained there seven days, in case he might have a vision to know whether he should stay or go down.</p>

<p class="v">4. And he celebrated the feast of the harvest of the firstfruits with the old grain, for in all the land of Canaan there was not a handful of seed [in the land], for the famine was upon all the beasts, the cattle, and the birds, and upon man also.</p>

<p class="v">5. And on the sixteenth, the Lord appeared to him and said, "Jacob, Jacob"; and he said, "Here I am." And He said to him, "I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and Isaac; do not be afraid to go down into Egypt, for I will make of you a great nation. I will go down with you, and I will bring you up again, and in this land you shall be buried, and Joseph shall put his hands upon your eyes."</p>

<p class="v">6. "Fear nothing; go down into Egypt."</p>

<p class="v">7. And his sons rose up, and the sons of his sons, and they put their father and their possessions on chariots.</p>

<p class="v">8. And Israel rose up from the Well of the Oath on the sixteenth of that third month, and he went to the land of Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">9. And Israel sent Judah ahead of him to his son Joseph, to examine the land of Goshen, for Joseph had told his brothers that they should come and dwell there so as to be near him.</p>

<p class="v">10. And it was the best (land) of the land of Egypt, and near to him, for all of them and also for the cattle.</p>

<p class="v">11. And these are the names of the sons of Jacob who went to Egypt with Jacob their father.</p>

<p class="v">12. Reuben, the firstborn of Israel; and these are the names of his sons: Enoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi — five.</p>

<p class="v">13. Simeon and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul, the son of the Zephathite woman — seven.</p>

<p class="v">14. Levi and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari — four.</p>

<p class="v">15. Judah and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Shelah, Perez, and Zerah — four.</p>

<p class="v">16. Issachar and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Tola, and Puvah, and Jashub, and Shimron — five.</p>

<p class="v">17. Zebulun and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel — four.</p>

<p class="v">18. And these are the sons of Jacob and their sons whom Leah bore to Jacob in Mesopotamia — six — and their only sister, Dinah; and all the souls of the sons of Leah and their sons who went with Jacob their father into Egypt were twenty-nine, and with Jacob their father among them, they were thirty.</p>

<p class="v">19. And the sons of Zilpah, Leah's maidservant, Jacob's wife, who bore to Jacob Gad and Asher.</p>

<p class="v">20. And these are the names of their sons who went with him into Egypt. Sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon (and Eri), Areli, and Arodi — eight.</p>

<p class="v">21. And the sons of Asher: Jimnah, and Ishvah, (and Ishvi), and Beriah, and Serah, their only sister — six.</p>

<p class="v">22. All the souls were fourteen, and all those of Leah were forty-four.</p>

<p class="v">23. And the sons of Rachel, Jacob's wife: Joseph and Benjamin.</p>

<p class="v">24. And there were born to Joseph in Egypt, before his father came into Egypt, those whom Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis, bore to him: Manasseh and Ephraim — three.</p>

<p class="v">25. And the sons of Benjamin: Bela, and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, and Ehi, and Rosh, and Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard — eleven.</p>

<p class="v">26. And all the souls of Rachel were fourteen.</p>

<p class="v">27. And the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant, Jacob's wife, whom she bore to Jacob, were Dan and Naphtali.</p>

<p class="v">28. And these are the names of their sons who went with them into Egypt. And the sons of Dan were Hushim, Samon, and Asudi, and 'Ijaka, and Salomon — six.</p>

<p class="v">29. And they died in the year they entered Egypt, and only Dan Hushim remained.</p>

<p class="v">30. And these are the names of the sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, Shallum, and 'Iv.</p>

<p class="v">31. And 'Iv, who was born after the years of famine, died in Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">32. And all the souls of Rachel were twenty-six.</p>

<p class="v">33. And all the souls of Jacob who went into Egypt were seventy souls. These are his children and the children of his children, seventy in all, but five died in Egypt before Joseph and had no children.</p>

<p class="v">34. And in the land of Canaan, two sons of Judah died, Er and Onan, and they had no children, and the children of Israel buried those who perished, and they were counted among the seventy heathen nations.</p>

### Chapter 45 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Joseph receives Jacob, and gives him Goshen, 1-7. Joseph acquires all the land and its inhabitants for Pharaoh, 8-12. Jacob dies and is buried at Hebron, 13-15. His books given to Levi, 16. (Cf. Gen. xlvi.28-30; xlvii.11-13, 19, 20, 23, 24, 28; l.13.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And Israel entered the land of Egypt, into the land of Goshen, at the new moon of the fourth [2172 AM] month, in the second year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee.</p>

<p class="v">2. And Joseph went to meet his father Jacob, in the land of Goshen, and he fell upon his father's neck and wept.</p>

<p class="v">3. And Israel said to Joseph, "Now let me die, since I have seen you; and now blessed be the Lord God of Israel, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac, who has not withheld his mercy and his grace from his servant Jacob."</p>

<p class="v">4. "It is enough for me to have seen your face while I am still alive; yes, the vision I had at Bethel is true. Blessed be the Lord my God for ever and ever, and blessed be his name."</p>

<p class="v">5. And Joseph and his brothers ate bread before their father and drank wine, and Jacob rejoiced with very great joy because he saw Joseph eating with his brothers and drinking before him, and he blessed the Creator of all things, who had preserved him, and had kept his twelve sons for him.</p>

<p class="v">6. And Joseph had given his father and his brothers, as a gift, the right to dwell in the land of Goshen and at Rameses and in all the surrounding region, over which he ruled before Pharaoh. And Israel and his sons dwelt in the land of Goshen, the best part of the land of Egypt, and Israel was a hundred and thirty years old when he entered Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">7. And Joseph fed his father and his brothers, and their households, with bread, as much as sufficed them, for the seven years of famine.</p>

<p class="v">8. And the land of Egypt suffered because of the famine, and Joseph acquired all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh in exchange for food, and he took possession of the people and their cattle and everything, for Pharaoh.</p>

<p class="v">9. And the years of famine were completed, and Joseph gave the people of the land seed and food, that they might sow (the land) in the eighth year, for the river had flooded all the land of Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">10. For during the seven years of famine, it had not overflowed, and had watered only a few places on the banks of the river, but now it overflowed, and the Egyptians sowed the land, and it produced much wheat that year.</p>

<p class="v">11. And that was the first year of [2178 AM] the fourth week of the forty-fifth jubilee.</p>

<p class="v">12. And Joseph took a fifth of the grain of the harvest for the king, and left them four parts for food and for seed, and Joseph made this an ordinance for the land of Egypt, unto this day.</p>

<p class="v">13. And Israel lived seventeen years in the land of Egypt, and all the days that he lived were three jubilees, a hundred and forty-seven years, and he died in the fourth [2188 AM] year of the fifth week of the forty-fifth jubilee.</p>

<p class="v">14. And Israel blessed his sons before he died, and declared to them all that would happen to them in the land of Egypt; and he made known to them what would happen to them in the last days, and he blessed them, and gave Joseph two portions of the land.</p>

<p class="v">15. And he slept with his fathers, and was buried in the double cave in the land of Canaan, near Abraham, his father, in the tomb which he had dug for himself in the double cave in the land of Hebron.</p>

<p class="v">16. And he gave all his books and the books of his fathers to Levi, his son, that he might preserve them and renew them for his children, unto this day.</p>

### Chapter 46 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">The prosperity of Israel in Egypt, 1-2. The death of Joseph, 3-5. War between Egypt and Canaan, during which the bones of all the sons of Jacob except Joseph are buried at Hebron, 6-11. Egypt oppresses Israel, 12-16. (Cf. Gen. l.22, 25-6; Exod. i.6-14.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And it came to pass that after the death of Jacob, the children of Israel multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one heart, so that brother loved brother, and each one helped his brother, and they grew abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten [2242 AM] weeks of years, all the days of Joseph's life.</p>

<p class="v">2. And there was neither Satan nor any evil during all the days of Joseph's life that he lived after his father Jacob, for all the Egyptians honored the children of Israel throughout all the days of Joseph's life.</p>

<p class="v">3. And Joseph died at the age of a hundred and ten years; he lived seventeen years in the land of Canaan, and ten years he was a servant, and three years in prison, and eighty years he was under the king, ruling over all the land of Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">4. And he died, and all his brothers, and all that generation.</p>

<p class="v">5. And he commanded the children of Israel, before he died, to carry his bones with them when they went out of the land of Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">6. And he made them swear concerning his bones, for he knew that the Egyptians would not bring him back and bury him again in the land of Canaan, for Makamaron, king of Canaan, while he was dwelling in the land of Assyria, fought in the land of Canaan and slew the king of Egypt there, and pursued the Egyptians as far as the gates of Ermon.</p>

<p class="v">7. But he could not enter, for another, a new king, had become king of Egypt, and he was stronger than him, and he returned to the land of Canaan, and the gates of Egypt were shut, and none went out and none came into Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">8. And Joseph died in the forty-sixth jubilee, in the sixth week, in the second year, and he was buried in the land of Egypt, and [2242 AM] all his brothers died after him.</p>

<p class="v">9. And the king of Egypt went out to war against the king of Canaan [2263 AM] in the forty-seventh jubilee, in the second week, in the second year, and the children of Israel brought out all the bones of the children of Jacob, except the bones of Joseph, and they buried them in a field, in the double cave in the mountain.</p>

<p class="v">10. And most of them returned to Egypt, but a few of them remained in the mountains of Hebron, and Amram, your father, remained with them.</p>

<p class="v">11. And the king of Canaan was victorious over the king of Egypt, and he shut the gates of Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">12. And he devised an evil plan against the children of Israel to afflict them, and he said to the people of Egypt, "Behold, the people of the children of Israel have grown and multiplied more than we."</p>

<p class="v">13. "Come, let us deal wisely with them before they become too numerous, and let us afflict them with slavery before war strikes us and before they too fight against us; otherwise they will join our enemies and drive them out of our land, for their heart and their face are turned toward the land of Canaan."</p>

<p class="v">14. And he set overseers over them to afflict them with servitude; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications that had fallen in the cities of Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">15. And they made them serve with rigor, and the more they mistreated them, the more they grew and multiplied.</p>

<p class="v">16. And the people of Egypt held the children of Israel in abomination.</p>

### Chapter 47 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">The birth of Moses, 1-4. Adopted by Pharaoh's daughter, 5-9. He kills an Egyptian and flees (to Midian), 10-12. (Cf. Exod. i.22; ii.2-15.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the seventh week, in the seventh year, in the forty-seventh jubilee, your father went out [2303 AM] from the land of Canaan, and you were born in the fourth week, in the sixth year of that same [jubilee], in the [2330 AM] forty-eighth jubilee; it was the time of tribulation for the children of Israel.</p>

<p class="v">2. And Pharaoh, king of Egypt, commanded them to cast into the river all their male children that were born.</p>

<p class="v">3. And they cast them in for seven months, until the day of your birth.</p>

<p class="v">4. And your mother hid you for three months, and they spoke of her. And she made an ark for you, and covered it with pitch and asphalt, and placed it among the reeds on the bank of the river, and she put you there for seven days, and your mother came by night and nursed you, and by day Miriam, your sister, guarded you from the birds.</p>

<p class="v">5. And at that time, Tharmuth, Pharaoh's daughter, came to bathe in the river, and she heard your voice crying, and she told her maidservants to bring you out, and they brought you to her.</p>

<p class="v">6. And she took you out of the ark, and had compassion on you.</p>

<p class="v">7. And your sister said to her, "Shall I go and call you one of the Hebrew women to nurse and suckle this baby for you?"</p>

<p class="v">8. And she said (to her), "Go." And she went and called your mother Jochebed, and she gave her wages, and she nursed you.</p>

<p class="v">9. And afterward, when you were grown, they brought you to Pharaoh's daughter, and you became her son, and Amram, your father, taught you to write, and after you had completed three weeks, they brought you into the royal court.</p>

<p class="v">10. And you remained three weeks of years at the court until the time [2351-] when you went out from the royal court and saw an Egyptian striking your friend, who was [2372 AM] one of the children of Israel, and you killed him and hid him in the sand.</p>

<p class="v">11. And on the second day, you quarreled with two of the children of Israel, and you said to the one who was doing wrong, "Why do you strike your brother?"</p>

<p class="v">12. And he was angry and indignant, and said, "Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Do you intend to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?" And you were afraid, and you fled because of these words.</p>

### Chapter 48 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Moses returns from Midian to Egypt. Mastema seeks to kill him on the way, 1-3. The ten plagues, 4-11. Israel leaves Egypt: the destruction of the Egyptians at the Red Sea, 12-19. (Cf. Exod. ii.15; iv.19, 24; vii. ff.)</p>

<p class="v">1. And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you departed, and you dwelt (in [2372 AM] the land of Midian) five weeks and one year. And you returned to Egypt in the second week, in the second year, of the fiftieth jubilee.</p>

<p class="v">2. And you yourself know what he said to you on Mount Sinai, and what the prince Mastema desired to do to you when you were returning to Egypt (on the way, when you met him at the lodging place).</p>

<p class="v">3. Did he not seek with all his strength to kill you and to deliver the Egyptians from your hand, when he saw that you were sent to execute judgment and vengeance upon the Egyptians?</p>

<p class="v">4. And I delivered you from his hand, and you performed the signs and wonders that you had been sent to perform in Egypt against Pharaoh and against all his house, and against his servants and his people.</p>

<p class="v">5. And the LORD wrought great vengeance against them, for Israel's sake, and struck them with blood and frogs, lice and dog-flies, and malignant boils that broke out into sores; and their cattle with death; and with hail he destroyed everything that grew for them; and with locusts that devoured what was left by the hail; and with darkness; and (with the death) of the firstborn of men and animals, and of all their idols, the LORD took vengeance and burned them with fire.</p>

<p class="v">6. And everything was sent by your hand, that you might declare (these things) before they came to pass, and you spoke with the king of Egypt before all his servants and before his people.</p>

<p class="v">7. And everything happened according to your words; ten great and terrible judgments fell upon the land of Egypt, that you might execute your vengeance there for Israel.</p>

<p class="v">8. And the LORD did everything for the love of Israel, and according to his covenant, which he had established with Abraham, by which he would take vengeance on them, because they had reduced them to slavery by force.</p>

<p class="v">9. And the prince Mastema rose up against you and sought to deliver you into Pharaoh's hands, and he helped the Egyptian sorcerers,</p>

<p class="v">10. And they rose up and did before you the evils that we allowed them to do, but the remedies we did not allow to be done by their hands.</p>

<p class="v">11. And the LORD struck them with malignant ulcers, and they could not stand, for we destroyed them so that they could not perform a single sign.</p>

<p class="v">12. And despite all (these) signs and wonders, the prince Mastema was not ashamed, for he took courage and cried out to the Egyptians to pursue you with all the forces of the Egyptians, with their chariots and with their horses, and with all the armies of the peoples of Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">13. And I stood between the Egyptians and Israel, and we delivered Israel from his hand and from the hand of his people, and the LORD made them cross the sea as though it were dry land.</p>

<p class="v">14. And all the peoples he brought to pursue after Israel, the LORD our God cast into the midst of the sea, into the depths of the abyss, beneath the children of Israel, just as the people of Egypt had cast their children into the river; he took vengeance on a million of them, and a thousand strong and vigorous men were destroyed for the sake of a single infant of the children of your people whom they had cast into the river.</p>

<p class="v">15. And on the fourteenth day, and the fifteenth, and the sixteenth, and the seventeenth, and the eighteenth, the prince Mastema was bound and imprisoned behind the children of Israel, so that he could not accuse them.</p>

<p class="v">16. And on the nineteenth, we released them, that they might help the Egyptians and pursue the children of Israel.</p>

<p class="v">17. And he hardened their hearts and made them obstinate, and the LORD our God devised a plan to strike the Egyptians and cast them into the sea.</p>

<p class="v">18. And on the fourteenth, we bound him so that he could not accuse the children of Israel on the day when they asked the Egyptians for vessels and garments, vessels of silver, vessels of gold, and vessels of bronze, in order to plunder the Egyptians in exchange for the servitude into which they had forced them.</p>

<p class="v">19. And we did not bring the children of Israel out of Egypt empty-handed.</p>
### Chapter 49 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">The Passover: rules concerning its celebration. (Cf. Exodus XII.6, 9, 11, 13, 22-3, 30, 46; XV.22.)</p>

<p class="v">1. Remember the commandment which the LORD commanded thee concerning the Passover, that thou celebrate it in its season, on the fourteenth of the first month, that thou kill it before evening, and that they eat it at night on the 15th, in the evening, from the setting of the sun.</p>

<p class="v">2. For on that night — the beginning of the feast and the beginning of joy — you ate the Passover in Egypt, when all the powers of Mastema had been let loose to kill all the firstborn of the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh to the firstborn of the captive maidservant at the mill, and even the cattle.</p>

<p class="v">3. And this is the sign that the Lord gave them: In every house on whose lintels they saw the blood of a yearling lamb, into (that) house they were not to enter to slay, but were to pass over it, so that all who were in the house might be saved, because the sign of the blood was upon its lintels.</p>

<p class="v">4. And the powers of the LORD did everything according to what the LORD had commanded them, and they passed over all the children of Israel, and the plague did not come upon them to destroy from among them anyone, whether of the cattle, or a man, or a dog.</p>

<p class="v">5. And the plague was very grievous in Egypt, and there was not a house in Egypt where there was not a dead man, with weeping and lamentation.</p>

<p class="v">6. And all Israel ate the flesh of the paschal lamb and drank the wine, and praised, blessed, and gave thanks to the Lord, the God of their fathers, and was ready to go forth from the yoke of Egypt, and from the evil bondage.</p>

<p class="v">7. And remember this day all the days of thy life, and observe it from year to year, all the days of thy life, once a year, on its day, according to all its law, and do not put it off from day to day, or from month to month.</p>

<p class="v">8. For it is an everlasting ordinance, engraved on the heavenly tablets, concerning all the children of Israel, that they must observe it every year, on its day, once a year, throughout all their generations; and there is no limit of days, for it is ordained forever.</p>

<p class="v">9. And the man who is free from impurity and does not come to celebrate it at the time of its day, so as to bring an acceptable offering before the LORD, and to eat and drink before the LORD on the day of its feast, that man, who is clean and within reach, shall be cut off; because he did not offer the offering of the LORD at its appointed time, he shall bear his guilt upon himself.</p>

<p class="v">10. Let the children of Israel come and celebrate the Passover on the day of its appointed time, the fourteenth day of the first month, between the evenings, from the third part of the day until the third part of the night, for two parts of the day are given to the light and a third part to the evening.</p>

<p class="v">11. This is what the Lord has commanded thee, to observe it between the evenings.</p>

<p class="v">12. And it is not permitted to kill it during any period of the light, but during the period bordering on the evening, and let them eat it at the evening hour, until the third part of the night; and whatever remains of all its flesh from the third part of the night onward, let it be burned with fire.</p>

<p class="v">13. And they shall not cook it with water, nor eat it raw, but shall roast it on the fire; they shall eat it with diligence; they shall roast its head with the inward parts and its feet in the fire, and shall not break any bone of it; for no bone of the children of Israel shall be broken.</p>

<p class="v">14. Therefore the LORD has commanded the children of Israel to observe the Passover on the day of its appointed time, and they shall break no bone of it; for it is a feast day, and a commanded day, and there can be no passing from one day to another, nor from one month to another, without the day of its feast being observed.</p>

<p class="v">15. And thou shalt command the children of Israel to observe the Passover throughout their days, every year, once a year, on the day of its appointed time, and it shall come as an acceptable memorial before the LORD, and no plague shall come upon them to kill or strike, in the year that they celebrate the Passover in its time, in every respect according to its commandment.</p>

<p class="v">16. And they shall not eat it outside the sanctuary of the LORD, but before the sanctuary of the LORD, and all the people of the congregation of Israel shall celebrate it at the appointed time.</p>

<p class="v">17. And every man who comes to it on its day shall eat of it in the sanctuary of thy God, before the LORD, from the age of twenty years and upward; for thus it is written and ordained that they eat of it in the sanctuary of the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">18. And when the children of Israel enter into the land which they are to possess, into the land of Canaan, and set up the tabernacle of the LORD in the midst of the land, in one of their tribes, until the sanctuary of the LORD has been built in the land, let them come and celebrate the Passover in the midst of the tabernacle of the LORD, and let them slaughter it before the LORD from year to year.</p>

<p class="v">19. And in the days when the house shall be built in the name of the LORD, in the land of their inheritance, they shall go there and celebrate the Passover in the evening, at the setting of the sun, at the third part of the day.</p>

<p class="v">20. And they shall offer its blood on the threshold of the altar, and place its fat on the fire that is upon the altar, and they shall eat its flesh roasted with fire in the court of the house which has been sanctified in the name of the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">21. And they shall not be able to celebrate the Passover in their cities, nor in any other place than before the tabernacle of the LORD, or before his house where his name has dwelt; and they shall not stray from the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">22. And thou, Moses, command the children of Israel to observe the ordinances of the Passover, as it has been commanded thee; declare to them, every year and the day of its days, as well as the feast of unleavened bread, that they shall eat unleavened bread seven days, (and) that they shall observe its feast, and that they shall bring an offering every day during those seven days of the days of joy before the Lord on the altar of thy God.</p>

<p class="v">23. For you celebrated this feast in great haste when you came out of Egypt, until you entered the wilderness of Shur; for on the shore of the sea you completed it.</p>

### Chapter 50 {: .chap}

<p class="summary">Laws concerning the jubilees, 1-5, and the sabbath, 6-13.</p>

<p class="v">1. And after this law, I made known to thee the days of the sabbaths in the wilderness of Sin[ai], which is between Elim and Sinai.</p>

<p class="v">2. And I spoke to thee of the sabbaths of the land on Mount Sinai, and I spoke to thee of the jubilee years in the sabbaths of years; but I did not indicate to thee the year of it, until you enter the land which you are to possess.</p>

<p class="v">3. And the land also shall observe its sabbaths while they dwell in it, and they shall know the year of the jubilee.</p>

<p class="v">4. Therefore I have ordained for thee the year-weeks, the years, and the jubilees: there are forty-nine jubilees from the days of Adam until this day, [2410 AM] and one week and two years; and there are yet forty years to come (lit. 'distant') to learn the commandments [2450 AM] of the Lord, until they pass over into the land of Canaan, crossing the Jordan to the west.</p>

<p class="v">5. And the jubilees shall pass, until Israel is purified of all guilt of fornication, and of impurity, and of pollution, and of sin, and of error, and dwells with confidence in all the land, and there shall no longer be a Satan or any evil one, and the land shall be pure from that time forward forever.</p>

<p class="v">6. And this is the commandment concerning the sabbaths — I have written them for thee — and all the judgments of its laws.</p>

<p class="v">7. Six days shalt thou labor, but the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God. You shall do no work therein, you and your sons, your menservants and your maidservants, and all your cattle, and the stranger who is with you.</p>

<p class="v">8. And the man who does any work on it shall die: whoever profanes that day, whoever lies with (his) wife, or whoever says he will do something on it, that he will undertake a journey on it in respect of any buying or selling; and whoever draws water on it that he had not prepared on the sixth day, and whoever takes up a burden to carry it out of his tent or his house, shall die.</p>

<p class="v">9. You shall do no work on the sabbath day, except what you have prepared on the sixth day, so as to eat, to drink, to rest, and to keep the sabbath from all work on that day, and to bless the Lord your God, who has given you a feast day and a holy day; and a day of the holy kingdom for all Israel is this day among their days forever.</p>

<p class="v">10. For great is the honor that the LORD has given to Israel, to be able to eat, drink, and be satisfied on this feast day, and to rest from all the work that belongs to the labor of the children of men, except to burn incense and bring oblations and sacrifices before the Lord during the days and the sabbaths.</p>

<p class="v">11. This work alone shall be done on the sabbath days in the sanctuary of the LORD thy God; so that they may continually atone for Israel by sacrifices from day to day, as a memorial pleasing to the LORD, and that he may receive them always, from day to day, according to what has been commanded thee.</p>

<p class="v">12. And whoever does any work on it, or sets out on a journey, or cultivates (his) farm, whether in his house or in any other place, and whoever kindles a fire, or mounts an animal, or travels by boat on the sea, and whoever strikes or kills anything, or kills a beast or a bird, or whoever catches an animal or a bird or a fish, or whoever fasts or makes war on the days of the sabbath:</p>

<p class="v">13. The man who does any of these things on the sabbath day shall die, so that the children of Israel shall observe the sabbaths according to the commandments concerning the sabbaths of the land, as it is written on the tablets which he gave into my hands, that I should write for thee the laws of the seasons, and the seasons according to the division of their days.</p>

<p class="v">Here is completed the account of the division of the days.</p>

# Part Three <SEP> The Fourth Book of Esdras

<p class="part-sub">Ezra Sutuel — French translation collected by J.-P. Migne (1856)</p>

Thirty years after the destruction of Jerusalem, Ezra keeps watch and questions God: why does evil triumph?
The angel Uriel answers him with seven visions — the woman in mourning who becomes a city, the eagle with twelve wings,
the man who rises from the sea — up to the restoration of the burned Scriptures. Written in Hebrew around the year 100
of our era, this overwhelming apocalypse (it is from it that the "Requiem æternam" of the Latin liturgy comes,
4 Esd 2:34-35) is canonical in Ethiopia under the name <i>Ezra Sutuel</i>.

<p class="footer-note">The Ethiopian form of the book corresponds to chapters 3 to 14 below; chapters 1-2
and 15-16, transmitted through the Latin, are given so that the reader may have the entire book.</p>

### Chapter 1 <span class="chap-roman">(I)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. The second book of the prophet Ezra, son of Sarei, son of Azareus, son of Helcias, son of Sadanias, son of Sadoch, son of Achitob.</p>

<p class="v">2. Son of Achias, son of Phinees, son of Heli, son of Amerias, son of Asiel, son of Marimoth, son of Arna, son of Ozias, son of Borith, son of Abiseus, son of Phinees, son of Eleazar,</p>

<p class="v">3. Son of Araon, of the tribe of Levi; of Ezra, I say, who was a captive in the land of the Medes, under the reign of Artaxerxes, king of the Persians.</p>

<p class="v">4. The Lord addressed his word to me, and said:</p>

<p class="v">5. Go make known to my people what their sins are; and to their children, the iniquities they have committed against me, so that future generations may learn</p>

<p class="v">6. That they have been more wicked than their fathers; for they have forsaken me to sacrifice to strange gods.</p>

<p class="v">7. Was it not I who brought them out of Egypt and out of the house of bondage? Yet they have angered me, and they have not kept my ordinances.</p>

<p class="v">8. Tear out the hair of thy head and scatter it in all directions, as an omen of all the evils that shall fall upon them; because they have rejected my law, and because it is a rebellious people, without a yoke.</p>

<p class="v">9. How long shall I bear with them, whom I have showered with so many blessings?</p>

<p class="v">10. I overthrew many kings for their sake. I struck Pharaoh with his servants and all his army.</p>

<p class="v">11. I made all the nations flee before them. I scattered in the East the peoples of Tyre and Sidon, and the sword reaped all their enemies.</p>

<p class="v">12. Therefore, go find them and tell them on my behalf: Thus says the Lord:</p>

<p class="v">13. It is I who opened for you a passage through the midst of the waters, and who delivered to you strong cities, built from the earliest times. I gave you Moses for a leader, and Aaron for a high priest.</p>

<p class="v">14. I sent the pillar of fire to light you by night, and I performed before your eyes wonders without number; yet you have forgotten me, says the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">15. Thus says the Lord Almighty: I rained down quail in your midst as a sign of my protection. I marked out camps for you to entrench yourselves, and you filled them with your murmurings.</p>

<p class="v">16. In vain you called upon me against your enemies: they conquered you, and yet you have not ceased to murmur to this day.</p>

<p class="v">17. Where is the memory of my kindnesses? Did you not cry out to me when you were in the wilderness and hunger pressed upon you?</p>

<p class="v">18. Why did you say then: Have you brought us into this wilderness to make us die here? It would have been better for us to be the slaves of the Egyptians than to come and perish here.</p>

<p class="v">19. I was moved by your groanings. I gave you manna for food, and you ate the bread of angels.</p>

<p class="v">20. When you were pressed with thirst, was it not I who opened the rock and brought forth water from it in abundance? I gave you shelter under the shade of trees against the excessive heat of the sun.</p>

<p class="v">21. I put you in possession of a fertile land, and I made the Canaanites, the Perizzites, and the Philistines flee before you. What more then can I do for you, says the Lord?</p>

<p class="v">22. Thus says the Lord Almighty: When you were near the river of the Amorites, and in the heat of your thirst you blasphemed my name,</p>

<p class="v">23. I did not avenge those blasphemies with fire; but I sweetened for you the bitterness of the waters by having wood thrown into them.</p>

<p class="v">24. How then shall I treat thee, O Jacob, and thee, Judah? Thou wouldst not obey. I will go find other peoples. I will give them my name, and they will keep my ordinances:</p>

<p class="v">25. Since you have forsaken me, I will forsake you in turn. You will ask for mercy, and I will have no pity on you.</p>

<p class="v">26. You will call upon me, and I will not hear you; because you have dipped your hands in blood, and your feet are swift to commit murders.</p>

<p class="v">27. And it is not me that you have forsaken; but yourselves, says the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">28. Thus says the Lord Almighty: Have I not cared for you as a father cares for his son, a mother for her daughter, and a nurse for the child she suckles,</p>

<p class="v">29. So that you might be my people and my children, and that I might be your father and your God?</p>

<p class="v">30. I gathered you as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings. What then shall I do with you now? I will cast you away from before my face.</p>

<p class="v">31. When you offer me sacrifices, I will turn my eyes away from you. I hold in horror your feasts, your new moons, and your circumcisions.</p>

<p class="v">32. I sent you my servants the prophets, and after a thousand cruel outrages you put them to death; but I will require their blood of you again, says the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">33. Thus says the Lord Almighty: The land you inhabit shall become a desert. I will scatter you as the wind scatters the chaff.</p>

<p class="v">34. Your children shall leave no posterity, because they have despised my commandments and have done evil in my presence.</p>

<p class="v">35. And I will give your houses to a strange people who will believe in me without having heard my voice. It has not witnessed my wonders, and it will fulfill my ordinances.</p>

<p class="v">36. It has not been instructed by the prophets, and it will detest its iniquities.</p>

<p class="v">37. I promise to show grace to this new people, whose children shall be transported with joy; and who, not having seen me with the eyes of the body, shall nevertheless give faith to my words.</p>

<p class="v">38. And now, my brother, see this people that comes from the East, and consider what glory it is clothed with.</p>

<p class="v">39. I will give it for leaders Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Hosea, Amos, Micah, Joel, Obadiah, Jonah,</p>

<p class="v">40. Nahum, Habakkuk, Zephaniah, Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi, or the angel of the Lord.</p>

### Chapter 2 <span class="chap-roman">(II)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Thus says the Lord: I brought this people out of bondage, and gave them my law through the ministry of my prophets; but they would not listen to them, and they made void all the designs I had for them.</p>

<p class="v">2. She who bore them said to them: Withdraw from me, my children, for I am a widow and without help.</p>

<p class="v">3. I had raised you with joy, and your loss shall be for me a source of sorrow and tears, for you have sinned before the Lord your God, and have done evil in his sight.</p>

<p class="v">4. Of what help could I be to you now that I am widowed and forsaken? Withdraw, then, my children, and go bend the mercy of the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">5. And you, God, who are their Father, I call you to witness against these rebellious children who would not keep my covenant,</p>

<p class="v">6. So that you make them bear all the shame of it, that their mother be abandoned to plunder, and that nothing remain of their race.</p>

<p class="v">7. Let them be scattered and dispersed among the nations! Let their names be banished from off the earth, since they have despised my covenant.</p>

<p class="v">8. Woe to thee, Assyria, who serve as a refuge for the wicked! Perverse nation! Remember how I dealt with Sodom and Gomorrah,</p>

<p class="v">9. Those cities which are still sought beneath the heaps of ash and sulfur that cover them. Thus will I deal with those who have not listened to me, says the Lord Almighty.</p>

<p class="v">10. Thus says the Lord to Ezra: Go tell my people that I will give them the kingdom of Jerusalem which I had promised to Israel.</p>

<p class="v">11. I will cover them with a radiant glory, and they will dwell in those eternal dwellings that had been prepared for others.</p>

<p class="v">12. The tree of life will spread a pleasant fragrance around them, and they will no longer feel either labor or pain.</p>

<p class="v">13. Wait with patience, and you will at last enter into possession of this happiness. Pray that the course of the times be shortened; the kingdom is already prepared for you; watch, therefore.</p>

<p class="v">14. Take heaven and earth to witness; for I have destroyed evil, and I have created good, and I am he who lives, says the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">15. And you, mother, cherish your children, raise them with joy, make their feet firm as that of a pillar; for I have chosen you, says the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">16. I will raise the dead, I will bring them out of the tomb, and my name shall be known in Israel.</p>

<p class="v">17. Fear not, you, mother of these children; for I have chosen you, says the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">18. I will send to your aid my servants Isaiah and Jeremiah. It is by their counsel that I have sanctified and prepared for you twelve trees laden with all kinds of fruit;</p>

<p class="v">19. As many fountains from which flow milk and honey, with seven very high mountains, covered with roses and lilies; there I will fill your children with delights.</p>

<p class="v">20. Render justice to the widow and the orphan, relieve the needy, defend the fatherless, clothe those who are naked.</p>

<p class="v">21. Take care of him who is languishing and without strength, do not insult the lame, be the support of the crippled and the eye of the blind.</p>

<p class="v">22. Let the old man and the child be safe within your walls.</p>

<p class="v">23. When you find the dead, put them in the sepulchers, and seal their entrance, and I will give you the first place on the day of the resurrection.</p>

<p class="v">24. My people, wait, and be still; for the time of your rest shall come.</p>

<p class="v">25. And thou, like a mother full of tenderness, nourish thy children, and make firm their feet.</p>

<p class="v">26. None of the servants I have given thee shall perish; for I will require their number.</p>

<p class="v">27. Do not let thyself be cast down, because on the day of wrath and tribulations thou shalt be in joy and abundance, while others shall have for their portion only sadness and tears.</p>

<p class="v">28. The nations shall be jealous of thy happiness; but they shall be able to do nothing against thee, says the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">29. I will cover thee with my hands, and I will prevent thy children from being cast down into the abyss.</p>

<p class="v">30. Rejoice, then, mother, with thy children; for I will deliver you all, says the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">31. Remember those of thy children who are under the power of death. I will bring them out of the bowels of the earth, and I will have pity on them; for I am full of mercy, says the Lord Almighty.</p>

<p class="v">32. Hold thy children in thy arms until I come, and let me make them experience my mercy: for it is like those overflowing waters, and the spring of it shall never be exhausted.</p>

<p class="v">33. The Lord spoke to me, Ezra, on Mount Horeb. He commanded me to come find the children of Israel; but having presented myself before them, they rejected me, and despised the order of the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">34. Therefore I say to you, O nations who hear and listen to me: Live in expectation of your Shepherd; he will establish you in eternal rest, and he who is to come at the end of the ages is near.</p>

<p class="v">35. Prepare yourselves to receive in his reign the rewards he has destined for you; for an unfading light shall shine upon you throughout eternity.</p>

<p class="v">36. Flee this dark age. Hasten to enter into possession of this happiness that will fill you with joy; I call my Savior to witness it.</p>

<p class="v">37. Receive this precious gift; and in the transports of your joy, give thanks to him who has called you to the heavenly inheritance.</p>

<p class="v">38. Rise up, come forward, and consider the number of those who are invited to the feast of the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">39. They have freed themselves from the shadows of the age, and have received from the Lord radiant robes.</p>

<p class="v">40. Zion, gather all thy children, set apart those who are clothed in white, and who have fulfilled the law of the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">41. Their number is filled according to thy desires. Pray to the almighty God to sanctify thy people whom he has chosen from the beginning.</p>

<p class="v">42. I, Ezra, saw on Mount Zion a great multitude that I could not count, and they were all singing hymns to the praise of the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">43. In their midst there was a young man of tall stature, taller than the others, and he was placing crowns on the heads of all of them. I was astonished at this wonder.</p>

<p class="v">44. Then I questioned the angel, and said to him: Lord, who are these?</p>

<p class="v">45. And he said to me: These are they who have laid aside this mortal body to be clothed with immortality. They have confessed the name of God, and now they are crowned, and hold palms in their hands.</p>

<p class="v">46. And I said to the angel: Who is this young man who has placed crowns on their heads, and palms in their hands?</p>

<p class="v">47. And he answered me: It is the Son of God whom they confessed in the world; therefore I will fill with glory those who have generously fought for his name.</p>

<p class="v">48. Then the angel said to me: Go announce to my people the great things that the Lord has shown thee.</p>

### Chapter 3 <span class="chap-roman">(III)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. In the thirtieth year of the destruction of Jerusalem, I was in Babylon, and having sat down upon my bed, I felt troubled and weighed down with various thoughts,</p>

<p class="v">2. as I considered the desolation of Zion, and the great number of her children who were held captive in a foreign land.</p>

<p class="v">3. And in the cruel agitation I was in then, I addressed the Lord with words full of fear and reverence,</p>

<p class="v">4. and I said to him: Lord, sovereign ruler; you made your voice heard from the beginning of time. When you set the earth upon its foundations, you made your will known to those who dwelt in it.</p>

<p class="v">5. You gave Adam a mortal body, and he was the work of your hands: you breathed into him a breath of life, and he was animated in your presence.</p>
