<p class="v">6. You put him in the garden of delights, which you had planted with your hands before the earth had yet produced anything.</p>

<p class="v">7. You commanded him to walk in your ways; but he despised them, and at once you condemned him to death, along with all his descendants. From this first man came forth the tribes, the nations, the peoples, and men without number.</p>

<p class="v">8. They all walked according to the desires of their hearts. They did evil in your sight, and they despised your commandments.</p>

<p class="v">9. Then you flooded the earth with a deluge, you buried them themselves beneath the waters,</p>

<p class="v">10. And they found death in that flood, as Adam had found it in his transgression.</p>

<p class="v">11. Yet you saved Noah with his family, and from him came forth the race of the righteous.</p>

<p class="v">12. Men having imperceptibly multiplied, they spread over the earth to form there the peoples and the nations; but they carried iniquity further than those first men who perished by the flood.</p>

<p class="v">13. And as they were all sinners in your sight, you made choice of one of them, who was called Abraham.</p>

<p class="v">14. You loved him, and he was the sole keeper of your will.</p>

<p class="v">15. You made with him an everlasting covenant; and after promising him never to forsake his race, you made him father of Isaac, and from this son came afterward Esau and Jacob.</p>

<p class="v">16. You chose Jacob, and rejected Esau; and from Jacob was born a great people.</p>

<p class="v">17. When you brought his posterity out of Egypt, you led them to Mount Sinai.</p>

<p class="v">18. You bowed down the heavens, you made the earth sink, you shook the foundations of the world, the abysses trembled, and all nature was troubled.</p>

<p class="v">19. It was then that, to give your law to Jacob, and your covenant to Israel, you made your glory burst forth amid fire, tremblings, wind, and hail.</p>

<p class="v">20. But you did not remove the malice of their hearts, so that your law might bear its fruit in them.</p>

<p class="v">21. For the first Adam transgressed it in the malice of his heart, and he drew into his fall all those who came forth from him.</p>

<p class="v">22. The wound was never closed; and, since that time, man has always carried in his heart both the law and his inclination to violate it: for after losing the good that was in him, nothing remained to him as his portion but wickedness.</p>

<p class="v">23. At last, after several centuries, you raised up your servant David.</p>

<p class="v">24. You commanded him to build a city where your name would be invoked, and in which incense and sacrifices would be offered to you.</p>

<p class="v">25. This was observed for several years; but the people of this chosen city at last committed iniquity.</p>

<p class="v">26. They imitated in everything the conduct of Adam and of those who followed him: for they had, like them, malice in their hearts.</p>

<p class="v">27. And you delivered the holy city into the hands of your enemies.</p>

<p class="v">28. Are the peoples of Babylon, then, less sinful than we? And what have they done to deserve being the conquerors of Zion?</p>

<p class="v">29. Having come to Babylon, and having seen, in the thirtieth year of the captivity, the impieties and crimes without number that were being committed there, my heart was greatly troubled.</p>

<p class="v">30. When I considered that you spare sinners and the impious, that the enemies of your name triumph, and that, on the contrary, you destroy your people, without having given me any understanding of these misfortunes.</p>

<p class="v">31. Was this then what you had in store for us? And has Babylon committed fewer crimes than Zion?</p>

<p class="v">32. What other people than Israel has known you, and what other nation than that of Jacob has made a covenant with you?</p>

<p class="v">33. Zion, however, has received no reward as yet. Her labor has been without fruit. Yet I have traveled through all the nations; and although they live in forgetfulness of your name, they nevertheless enjoy a brilliant prosperity.</p>

<p class="v">34. Now, therefore, weigh in the same balance our iniquities and those of the inhabitants of this age, and you will recognize that Israel alone has glorified your name.</p>

<p class="v">35. For what interval have they placed between their crimes, and what nation has kept your commandments as we have?</p>

<p class="v">36. None has been faithful to them; and among us, you will find many who have observed them.</p>

### Chapter 4 <span class="chap-roman">(IV)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Then the angel who had been sent to me, and whose name was Uriel, answered me,</p>

<p class="v">2. and said to me: Thy heart has formed vain designs in this world, in claiming to understand the ways of the Most High.</p>

<p class="v">3. I said to him: What you say is true, my lord. He answered me: I am sent to show thee three things and to propose to thee three comparisons.</p>

<p class="v">4. If thou canst give me an account of one of the three, I will reveal to thee the way thou seekest, and the source of the malice of the heart.</p>

<p class="v">5. I said to him: Speak, my lord. And he said to me: Go, weigh fire, measure the wind, and call back the day that has passed.</p>

<p class="v">6. I answered him: What man could do what you require of me?</p>

<p class="v">7. Then he said to me: If I had asked thee how many caverns there are in the sea, how many springs in the abyss and above the firmament, and what are the outlets of paradise;</p>

<p class="v">8. Thou wouldst perhaps have answered me: I have not yet gone down into the abyss, nor into the depths of the earth, and I have never gone up to heaven.</p>

<p class="v">9. But I have questioned thee only about the wind and the fire, by which thou art always surrounded, and about the day through which thou hast passed; and thou canst not give me an account of these things.</p>

<p class="v">10. And he added: If thou canst not even know the things that are born with thee,</p>

<p class="v">11. How couldst thou understand the ways of the Most High, as well as the outward corruption of the age, such as it appears in my sight.</p>

<p class="v">12. I said to him then: It would have been more advantageous for us never to have existed, than to live thus in impiety, and to be wretched without knowing the cause of the evils that overwhelm us.</p>

<p class="v">13. The angel answered me: I was in the countryside, I drew near the forest, and the trees held counsel among themselves.</p>

<p class="v">14. They said: Come, let us go make war on the sea, that it may withdraw from before us, and that we may spread ourselves out.</p>

<p class="v">15. The waves of the sea also assembled, they held counsel, and said: Come, let us go flood the trees of the forests, and add them to our domain.</p>

<p class="v">16. But the forest saw its designs come to nothing; for fire drew near it, and it was consumed.</p>

<p class="v">17. It was the same with the designs of the waves of the sea. For the sand resisted them and held them back.</p>

<p class="v">18. If then thou wert made the judge of these contests, whom wouldst thou undertake to condemn or to justify?</p>

<p class="v">19. I said to him: They have indeed formed vain designs. The forests are born of the bowels of the earth, and the sea has its bed where it may roll its waves.</p>

<p class="v">20. And he answered me: Thou hast judged rightly; why hast thou not reasoned in the same way concerning thyself?</p>

<p class="v">21. Just as the earth is the place of the forests, and the sea that of the waves; so too those who are on the earth can understand only the things of the earth; thus those who dwell above the heavens alone understand the things that happen there.</p>

<p class="v">22. Then I said to him: I beg you, Lord, to give me understanding of these mysteries.</p>

<p class="v">23. For I have not claimed to fathom the things that are above us; but only those of which we are every day the sorrowful witnesses. Why has Israel become the reproach of all the earth, and why has the beloved people been delivered up to unbelieving nations? Why is the law of our fathers abolished, and why are the sacred books no longer to be found?</p>

<p class="v">24. Like feeble locusts, we pass our days in fright and in fear, and we are not worthy to obtain mercy.</p>

<p class="v">25. But will God forget his name, which he has established in our midst? This is what I have questioned you about.</p>

<p class="v">26. And he answered me: The more thou searchest these mysteries, the more they will excite thy wonder; for the age hastens toward its end with incredible speed.</p>

<p class="v">27. And it cannot understand the things that are reserved for the righteous in the times to come, because it is full of injustice and misery.</p>

<p class="v">28. As for the things about which thou questionest me: I will tell thee that evil has been sown over all the earth like a seed; but the time of its destruction has not yet come.</p>

<p class="v">29. If, then, the seed is not first scattered, and the place where the evil was sown is not destroyed, the good will bear no fruit there.</p>

<p class="v">30. For Adam bore from the beginning in his heart an unhappy seed. How many crimes has it not already produced, and how many will it not produce until the time of the harvest?</p>

<p class="v">31. Consider for thyself what fruit of impiety has not come forth from this fatal seed.</p>

<p class="v">32. And when the time comes to cut down these ears of grain without number, how great will be the abundance of that harvest?</p>

<p class="v">33. I said to him: How shall these things come to pass? When shall they happen? Why are our days short and subject to so many evils?</p>

<p class="v">34. And he answered me: Do not claim to fathom the secrets of the Most High; for however great thy efforts might be, they would be useless.</p>

<p class="v">35. Did not the souls of the righteous wish to learn these things from the very places where they are kept, when they said: How long shall we hope, and when shall the fruit come, and the time of the harvest?</p>

<p class="v">36. And the archangel Jeremiel answered them in these words: This shall come to pass when the number of the seeds that are to be sown in you is fulfilled; for the Lord has weighed the age in the balance.</p>

<p class="v">37. He has measured the times, he has numbered them; and the order of them shall not be disturbed, until the measure that has been foretold is fulfilled.</p>

<p class="v">38. And I said: Lord, sovereign ruler, we too have committed iniquity.</p>

<p class="v">39. Perhaps the number of the righteous will not be fulfilled because of the sins of those who are upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">40. And he answered me: Go ask the woman who is pregnant, whether after nine months of pregnancy she can retain in her womb the fruit she carries there:</p>

<p class="v">41. I answered him: Lord, that cannot be. And he said to me: The underground places that serve as retreats for souls are like the womb of a woman.</p>

<p class="v">42. And just as she who is giving birth hastens to be delivered of the pains of childbirth, so too hell hastens to render up the souls that have been entrusted to it.</p>

<p class="v">43. I will reveal to thee from the beginning the things thou wishest to know.</p>

<p class="v">44. And I said to him: If I have found favor in your eyes, if it is possible, and you judge me worthy of it,</p>

<p class="v">45. Tell me whether the time that is to follow will be longer than that which has preceded, or whether more of it has already elapsed than there is yet to come.</p>

<p class="v">46. I know what has happened; but I do not know the things that are to come.</p>

<p class="v">47. And he said to me: Stand at my right hand, and I will show thee, under similitudes, what thou askest me.</p>

<p class="v">48. And having risen, I was attentive to what was about to happen; at once a burning furnace passed before me; and when the flame had dispersed, I looked, and I saw the smoke rising.</p>

<p class="v">49. After that I saw a cloud full of water;</p>

<p class="v">50. And he said to me: Consider and reason; just as the rain is more abundant than the drops of water, and the fire than the smoke, so more time has already elapsed than there will yet be to come: for the drops of water and the smoke appeared only after the rain and the fire.</p>

<p class="v">51. I begged him to tell me whether I would live until those times, and what would happen then.</p>

<p class="v">52. And he answered me: As for the things thou desirest to know, I can reveal a part of them to thee; but as for the length of thy life, I am not sent to instruct thee about it, and I do not know it.</p>

### Chapter 5 <span class="chap-roman">(V)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. As for the signs which shall precede the last days, a time shall come when the inhabitants of the earth shall perish in great numbers. Truth shall no longer show itself there, and faith shall be banished from it.</p>

<p class="v">2. Injustice shall be greater there than thou seest it now, and such as it has never been.</p>

<p class="v">3. The land that had dominion over the others shall be destroyed, and trodden underfoot.</p>

<p class="v">4. If the Lord prolongs thy days until that time, thou shalt hear the sound of the third trumpet, and suddenly thou shalt see the sun shed its light in the middle of the night; the moon shall appear three times in the same day;</p>

<p class="v">5. Blood shall drip from wood, the stone shall make its voice heard, and the peoples shall be stirred.</p>

<p class="v">6. Then shall appear, in his reign, he in whom the nations had not placed their hope. The birds shall leave one land to pass into another;</p>

<p class="v">7. The sea of Sodom shall cast up fish from its bosom, it shall make a strange cry heard in the middle of the night, and all ears shall be struck by it.</p>

<p class="v">8. The earth shall open in several places, and frequent whirlwinds of fire shall come out of it; the wild beasts shall go seek new retreats, and pregnant women shall give birth to monsters,</p>

<p class="v">9. Fresh waters shall become salty; those who were united by the bonds of friendship shall rise up against one another; reason shall no longer show itself, and understanding shall shut itself up within itself;</p>

<p class="v">10. Many shall seek it and shall not find it; injustice and unrestraint shall multiply upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">11. One region shall question another, it shall say to it: Has justice, which justifies, passed through your midst? And it shall answer that it has not seen it.</p>

<p class="v">12. In that time men shall be filled with hope and shall obtain nothing; they shall labor, and their ways shall not prosper.</p>

<p class="v">13. These are the signs that I was permitted to reveal to thee; but if thou prayest again, if thou groanest still, and fastest for seven days, thou shalt learn things far more marvelous than those thou hast just heard.</p>

<p class="v">14. Then, having awakened, I was troubled in every part of my body, and my soul was so cast down as to fall into faintness;</p>

<p class="v">15. But the angel who was speaking to me sustained me, strengthened me, and set me firmly upon my feet.</p>

<p class="v">16. Now on the second night, Salathiel, the leader of the people, came to me and said: Where have you come from? And what can be the cause of the sadness that appears on your face?</p>

<p class="v">17. Have you forgotten that Israel has been entrusted to your care in the place of its captivity?</p>

<p class="v">18. Rise, then, take some food, and do not abandon us, like a neglectful shepherd, to the cruelty of the wolves.</p>

<p class="v">19. Then I said to him: Withdraw from me, and do not approach me; and having heard what I said to him, he left me.</p>

<p class="v">20. I fasted, then, seven days in cries and in tears, as the angel Uriel had commanded me.</p>

<p class="v">21. When that time had passed, I felt the same agitations as before.</p>

<p class="v">22. And still feeling within myself as keen a longing to penetrate these mysteries, I addressed myself again to the Most High,</p>

<p class="v">23. And I said to him: Lord, sovereign ruler, among all the forests and among all the trees, you have chosen a single vine;</p>

<p class="v">24. In all the extent of the earth a single pit, and among all the flowers the lily alone;</p>

<p class="v">25. Of all the abysses of the sea you have filled only a single stream; of all the cities you have made a covenant only with that of Zion;</p>

<p class="v">26. Of all the animals you have reserved for yourself only the dove; and among all the flocks the sheep alone has pleased you;</p>

<p class="v">27. Of all the peoples who are spread over the earth, you have acquired only one, you have loved it, and you have given it a law worthy of the praises of all men.</p>

<p class="v">28. And now, Lord, why have you delivered this one people to so many nations? Why have you raised up several others upon a single stem? Why, finally, have you divided this one inheritance?</p>

<p class="v">29. It has been trodden underfoot by those who have denied the truth of your promises, and have rejected your covenant.</p>

<p class="v">30. If this people has become the object of all your hatred, it is for you to punish it with your own hands.</p>

<p class="v">31. When I had ceased speaking, the same angel who had appeared to me the previous night was sent to me a second time,</p>

<p class="v">32. And he said to me: Listen to me, I will instruct thee, and be attentive to the new things I am about to reveal to thee.</p>

<p class="v">33. I answered him: Speak, my Lord. And he said to me: Thou hast been extremely troubled for Israel; dost thou think, then, that it is dearer to thee than to him who made it?</p>

<p class="v">34. And I said to him: No, Lord; it is sorrow that made me speak thus, and I am ceaselessly agitated by the desire I have to discover the paths of the Most High, and to know a part of the designs he has for his people.</p>

<p class="v">35. He said to me: Thou canst not. And I said to him: Why, Lord? Would to God that I had never seen the light of day, and that my mother's womb had served me as a tomb, so that I might not have been a witness of the misfortunes of Jacob and the desolation of Israel!</p>

<p class="v">36. And he said to me: Announce to me the things that have not yet happened, gather together the scattered drops, revive the withered flowers;</p>

<p class="v">37. Open those underground caverns, bring forth from them the winds that are shut up within, paint for me the image of the voice, and I will reveal to thee the things thou seekest with such ardor and anxiety.</p>

<p class="v">38. And I answered him: Lord, sovereign ruler, who can do all these things, except him who has no dealings with men?</p>

<p class="v">39. As for me, a feeble creature, whose portion is ignorance, how could I satisfy you as to what you ask of me?</p>

<p class="v">40. And he said to me: Since thou canst do none of the things I have proposed to thee, do not hope that it will be easier for thee to know either the day of my judgment, or the grace which I have resolved to grant my people at the end of the ages.</p>

<p class="v">41. I said to him: But Lord, all times are unveiled before your eyes; what then shall become of those who were before us? What shall become of us ourselves, and of those who shall come after us?</p>

<p class="v">42. And he said to me: My judgment shall be like a circle, all of whose parts are at an equal distance from the center, and move with an equal speed; so no interval shall be noticed in the judgment I shall exercise upon all men.</p>

<p class="v">43. I said to him: Could you not have brought into being at the same time those who have been, those who are, and those who shall be hereafter, so as to judge them more speedily?</p>

<p class="v">44. And he said to me: The creature cannot anticipate the Creator in his workings, and the earth could not have contained at the same time all the men who are to inhabit it in their turn.</p>

<p class="v">45. I said to him: As you have taught your servant that, after producing your creatures all together, you had given them life, and the earth had borne their weight, could it not still bear it in the same way?</p>

<p class="v">46. And he said to me: Ask the pregnant woman, ask her why she gives birth only successively; tell her to have ten children at once.</p>

<p class="v">47. And I said: She could not do it except after several intervals of time.</p>

<p class="v">48. Then he answered me: It is thus that, having cast various seeds into the bosom of the earth, I know how to bring them forth according to the times I have appointed.</p>

<p class="v">49. And just as children do not think as old men do, so it is that I govern the world I have created.</p>

<p class="v">50. But I questioned him and said to him: Since you have permitted me, I will continue to speak to you, for our mother, whom you have represented to me as young, is nevertheless approaching old age.</p>

<p class="v">51. And he said to me: Ask her who gives birth, and she will answer thee;</p>

<p class="v">52. Say to her: Why are the children you have just brought into the world not like those who were born before us? And why are yours smaller?</p>

<p class="v">53. And she will answer thee herself, that there is indeed a great difference between those who are the fruit of a strong and vigorous youth and those who are born in the weakened old age of their mother.</p>

<p class="v">54. Consider, then, that all you who now live are much smaller than those who preceded you</p>

<p class="v">55. And those who come after you shall be smaller still, because the creatures have arrived at their old age, and no longer have in them the strength and vigor of the first age.</p>

<p class="v">56. And I said: My Lord, if I have found favor before you, make known, I pray you, to your servant, him whom you will use to exercise your judgment upon your creatures.</p>
### Chapter 6 <span class="chap-roman">(VI)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. The angel said to me: At the beginning of the earthly globe, before the Creator had set bounds to the world, and before the winds had spread their impetuous breath through the air;</p>

<p class="v">2. Before the voice of thunder had shaken the earth, before bright lightnings had announced its approach, and before paradise had been laid upon its foundations;</p>

<p class="v">3. Before the earth had been adorned with flowers, before the shaken powers had been made firm, and before those innumerable armies of heavenly spirits had been gathered together;</p>

<p class="v">4. Before those vast expanses of air had been stretched out above the earth, before the firmament had received all its dimensions, before the walls of Zion had been raised;</p>

<p class="v">5. Before the present days had been laid open to the scrutiny of judgment, before sinners had been cast off in their iniquity, and before a seal had been set upon those who, by the ardor of their faith, have laid up for themselves a treasure of good works:</p>

<p class="v">6. Already I was occupied with these things. They were made by me alone, and they shall be destroyed by my power alone.</p>

<p class="v">7. I said to him: What shall be the division of the times, and when shall come the end of the first, and the beginning of the second?</p>

<p class="v">8. And he answered me: When, after Abraham, from Isaac were born Jacob and Esau, Jacob held Esau's heel with his hand.</p>

<p class="v">9. Esau is as the end of this first time; and Jacob, the beginning of the second.</p>

<p class="v">10. The hand of man is placed between the heel and the hand; and thou, Esdras, question me no further.</p>

<p class="v">11. And I said: Lord, sovereign ruler, if I have found favor before you,</p>

<p class="v">12. Finish making known to your servant the signs, part of which you revealed to me the previous night.</p>

<p class="v">13. And he said to me: Rise up, and be attentive to a very mighty voice.</p>

<p class="v">14. A kind of trembling shall arise over all the earth, and yet the place where you stand shall not be shaken.</p>

<p class="v">15. When the voice makes itself heard, fear not; for it will speak of the end of the times, and it will explain what the foundations of the earth are.</p>

<p class="v">16. It shall be moved and troubled at the telling of these things; for it knows that at the end of the times it must be changed.</p>

<p class="v">17. When he had ceased speaking, I rose up, and suddenly I heard a voice whose sound was like that made by the falling of many waters.</p>

<p class="v">18. And it said: Behold the times when I will enter into judgment with the inhabitants of the earth,</p>

<p class="v">19. When I will come to demand an account from those who, by their injustices, have tormented the rest of mankind; when Zion shall have filled up the measure of the ills she was to suffer,</p>

<p class="v">20. And when the end of all things shall have come, then I will give these signs. The books shall open in the midst of heaven, and all men shall be able to read them at the same time.</p>

<p class="v">21. Children a year old shall utter words, women with child shall bring forth after three or four months of pregnancy, and these untimely fruits shall revive, full of life.</p>

<p class="v">22. The fields that had been sown shall suddenly be laid waste, and the granaries that were full shall be found empty.</p>

<p class="v">23. The trumpet shall give forth a resounding sound, and men, hearing it, shall be seized with sudden terror.</p>

<p class="v">24. At that time friends, forgetting the claims of friendship, shall rise up against their friends. The earth shall be terrified at all these things. The springs of the fountains shall stop, and shall cease to flow for the space of three hours.</p>

<p class="v">25. Whoever escapes the evils I have just announced to you shall be saved: he shall see with his own eyes the author of his salvation, and the end of the present age.</p>

<p class="v">26. Those who have been kept in reserve, and who since their birth have not been under the dominion of death, shall also be witnesses of it. The heart of those who dwell on the earth shall be changed, and their feelings shall no longer be the same.</p>

<p class="v">27. For evil shall be destroyed, fraud shall reign no more.</p>

<p class="v">28. Faith shall flourish, corruption shall be overcome, and truth, which had for so long been barren and fruitless, shall become fruitful.</p>

<p class="v">29. While the voice was speaking thus, I gradually raised my eyes toward him before whom I stood.</p>

<p class="v">30. And he said to me: I have come to reveal when the time of this desolation shall come.</p>

<p class="v">31. If therefore you pray again and fast seven more days, I will tell you yet more wonderful things than those you have just heard;</p>

<p class="v">32. For your prayer has been heard by the Most High; the Almighty has seen the uprightness of your heart, and he has known the purity you have kept from your earliest childhood.</p>

<p class="v">33. Therefore he has sent me to reveal all these things to you and to explain them to you. Be therefore full of confidence, and fear not.</p>

<p class="v">34. Give not yourself over to the vanity of your thoughts, and take care lest, dwelling with too much curiosity on the former times, you remain in ignorance concerning the times to come.</p>

<p class="v">35. When he had finished speaking, I gave myself again to weeping, and I fasted seven days, to complete the number of three weeks that had been appointed to me.</p>

<p class="v">36. And on the night of the eighth day, finding myself still in trouble and agitation, I addressed myself to the Lord;</p>

<p class="v">37. For I was as if consumed by a secret fire, and my distress could not be expressed.</p>

<p class="v">38. Then I said: Lord, you made your voice heard at the beginning of the times, and from the first day you said: Let heaven and earth come forth out of nothing; and at once your word was fulfilled.</p>

<p class="v">39. The wind was then blowing; darkness enveloped that formless mass, a dreadful silence reigned; you had not yet made the voice of man.</p>

<p class="v">40. Then you drew forth from your treasuries a radiant light, to spread brightness over your work.</p>

<p class="v">41. On the second day, you created the firmament, and you commanded it to divide the waters from the waters, so that one part should rise above the firmament, and the other part should settle below.</p>

<p class="v">42. On the third day, you commanded the waters to gather together in the seventh part of the earth; you dried up the six other parts, and you set apart some of them to be cultivated by your own hands.</p>

<p class="v">43. For your word made itself heard, and the effect followed at once.</p>

<p class="v">44. The earth, opening her bosom all at once, brought forth from it a multitude of pleasant fruits of differing taste, flowers that were not to wither, and from which exquisite scents breathed forth: this was the work of the third day.</p>

<p class="v">45. On the fourth day, you commanded the sun and the moon to spread their light, and the stars to arrange themselves in the sky,</p>

<p class="v">46. and to serve the use of man who was about to come forth from your hands.</p>

<p class="v">47. On the fifth day, you told the seventh part in which the waters had gathered together to bring forth land animals, fish, and birds, and it was done so.</p>

<p class="v">48. And the water, which was mute and lifeless, brought forth animals as you had commanded, so that the nations of the earth might have therein a continual occasion to proclaim your wonders.</p>

<p class="v">49. You then created two animals; you gave to one the name of Behemoth, and to the other that of Leviathan.</p>

<p class="v">50. And you placed each of them in a different place; for the seventh part in which the waters had gathered together could not contain them both together.</p>

<p class="v">51. You put Behemoth in one of the parts that had been dried up on the third day, that he might remain there in the midst of the thousand mountains that are there.</p>

<p class="v">52. But you put Leviathan in the seventh part where the waters had gathered together, and you appointed him, at the times marked out, to swallow up those whom you had resolved to destroy.</p>

<p class="v">53. On the sixth day, you commanded the earth to bring forth animals, beasts, and reptiles.</p>

<p class="v">54. Then you formed Adam, and gave him dominion over all that you had just created; and it is from him that we, who are the chosen people, have drawn our origin.</p>

<p class="v">55. Lord, I have held this discourse in your presence, because it is for us that you formed the world.</p>

<p class="v">56. As for the other nations, who, like us, came forth from Adam, you have said that they were before you as nothing, and that all their glory was like spittle, or like water that flows out of a vessel.</p>

<p class="v">57. And yet, Lord, these nations, so vile in your eyes, are beginning to dominate over us, and are on the point of devouring us.</p>

<p class="v">58. And we, who are this people whom you called your firstborn, your only son, the dearest object of your tenderness, we are delivered into their hands.</p>

<p class="v">59. If it is true, then, that this world was created for us, why do we not possess in it the portion of our inheritance, and how long shall these things last?</p>

### Chapter 7 <span class="chap-roman">(VII)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. When I had ceased speaking, the angel who had been sent to me the previous night was sent to me again.</p>

<p class="v">2. And he said to me: Esdras, rise up and be attentive to what I am about to say to you.</p>

<p class="v">3. I said to him: Speak, my Lord. He answered me: The sea has been enclosed within vast spaces, so that its vastness might equal its depth.</p>

<p class="v">4. Now, suppose at present that its mouth is narrow, and that it has no more width than the ordinary bed of a river;</p>

<p class="v">5. Who is he who, driven by the desire to sail the sea and bring it under his power, could reach the midst of that vast domain, if beforehand he had not entered it through that narrow passage?</p>

<p class="v">6. Suppose further that there is a city built and situated in an open countryside, and that it is filled with every kind of good thing;</p>

<p class="v">7. That its entrance is narrow and slippery, that on the right there is fire, on the left a very deep water;</p>

<p class="v">8. And that finally these two chasms are separated only by a small path on which scarcely one man could walk;</p>

<p class="v">9. He who is to have that city for his inheritance — shall he take possession of it without having first passed through those terrible obstacles?</p>

<p class="v">10. I said: Lord, it is as you say. He added: Such is the lot of Israel.</p>

<p class="v">11. For it is for this people that I created the world, and as soon as Adam had violated my precepts, judgment was pronounced against the world.</p>

<p class="v">12. Its entrances became narrow, toilsome, grievous, few in number, evil, full of danger and affliction.</p>

<p class="v">13. But as for the entrances of the age to come, they are spacious, tranquil, and adorned with immortal fruits.</p>

<p class="v">14. Thus those who live in this age shall not be able to obtain those goods reserved for their efforts, unless they first pass through those narrow and grievous paths.</p>

<p class="v">15. Now then: Why should you be troubled, since you are subject to corruption? Why should you be anxious, since you are mortal?</p>

<p class="v">16. And why, finally, do you not aspire to know the things to come rather than the things present?</p>

<p class="v">17. Then I answered: Lord ruler, you have promised in your law that the righteous would have these goods for their inheritance, but that the wicked would perish.</p>

<p class="v">18. That the righteous would pass through tribulations before entering into those vast dwellings, but that the wicked, though tried by a thousand pains, would be excluded from them.</p>

<p class="v">19. And he said to me: There is no judge more just than God, and none penetrates hearts as the Most High does.</p>

<p class="v">20. Many perish in this life only because they have despised the law that he had prescribed to them.</p>

<p class="v">21. For God, in placing them on the earth, expressly marked out for them what they were to observe in order to live, and what they were to avoid in order not to be punished.</p>

<p class="v">22. But they did not listen to these salutary warnings; they contradicted them, and followed the vanity of their thoughts.</p>

<p class="v">23. And after having given themselves over to shameful and criminal deeds, they carried their pride so far as to deny that there was a God; they refused to walk in his ways.</p>

<p class="v">24. They despised his law, they renounced his promises, they were not faithful in keeping his ordinances, and did not perform his works.</p>

<p class="v">25. Therefore, Esdras, vanity shall be the portion of those who followed it, and truth shall fill the heart of those who sought it.</p>

<p class="v">26. Behold the times when the signs I have foretold to you shall be seen. The bride shall appear, and she who is now hidden in the bosom of the earth shall come forth from it in splendor:</p>

<p class="v">27. And he who shall have been delivered from all the evils I have foretold to you shall witness the wonders that I will then perform.</p>

<p class="v">28. For my Son Jesus shall appear in his glory with those who are his, and the men who shall then be found on the earth shall live there filled with joy for the space of four hundred years.</p>

<p class="v">29. At the end of that time, the Christ my Son shall die, and all those who shall then be on the earth shall die also.</p>

<p class="v">30. The world shall fall back into its first chaos; it shall remain in that state for seven days, until there are no more men on the earth.</p>

<p class="v">31. And when that time has passed, the age shall awaken from its slumber; and that which is corrupt shall die:</p>

<p class="v">32. The tombs shall open, the dead shall leave the dust, and the earth shall give back all those it held in its bosom.</p>

<p class="v">33. Then the Most High shall appear upon his tribunal to enter into judgment; evils shall cease, and patience shall no longer be put to any trial.</p>

<p class="v">34. Justice and truth alone shall reign, and faith shall grow ever stronger.</p>

<p class="v">35. Its works shall be seen, and the reward shall follow close upon them: justice shall rule everywhere, and injustice shall be banished.</p>

<p class="v">36. Then I said to him: Abraham once prayed for the inhabitants of Sodom. Moses prayed for our fathers after they had sinned in the desert.</p>

<p class="v">37. And those who came after him prayed for Israel in the days of Ahaz and of Samuel.</p>

<p class="v">38. David prayed to obtain victory over his enemies, and Solomon prayed for those who attended the dedication of his temple.</p>

<p class="v">39. Elijah prayed to bring down rain upon the earth, and to draw a dead man from the tomb.</p>

<p class="v">40. Hezekiah prayed to protect the people from the fury of Sennacherib; and many, in short, have prayed for their brethren.</p>

<p class="v">41. If, then, now that corruption has increased and injustice has multiplied, the righteous pray for the wicked, why should they not be heard?</p>

<p class="v">42. And he answered me: The present age is not the limit of the duration of the times; there are always on the earth a great number of righteous whose virtue shines forth in the eyes of God, and it is they who pray for the weak.</p>

<p class="v">43. But the day of judgment shall be its end and the beginning of an immortal life; then there shall be no more corruption.</p>

<p class="v">44. Intemperance and unbelief shall be banished; justice and truth alone shall reign.</p>

<p class="v">45. And then no one shall be able either to deliver him who has fallen into perdition, or to overthrow him who has remained victorious. And I answered:</p>

<p class="v">46. I have said it, and I shall not cease to say it: that it would have been more profitable for us that Adam had never been created on the earth; or that, having placed him there, he should have been kept from falling into transgression.</p>

<p class="v">47. For what advantage is it to man to spend his days in sorrow and misery, and after his death to expect nothing but torments and torture?</p>

<p class="v">48. And you, Adam, see what the enormity of your crime has been! For in sinning you destroyed yourself, and you drew down in your fall all the men of whom you were the father.</p>

<p class="v">49. And what good does it do us that immortality is promised to us, if we have done deeds worthy of death:</p>

<p class="v">50. That we live in expectation of eternity, if we are given over to corruption and vanity:</p>

<p class="v">51. That we aspire to rest and peace, if we have led a criminal life:</p>

<p class="v">52. That the glory of the Most High shall one day be the adornment of those who have lived in patience, if we have followed the ways of ungodliness:</p>

<p class="v">53. That paradise be opened, and that it be a place of delights whose fruits are incorruptible, the abode of health and of rest,</p>

<p class="v">54. If, after having spent our days on a wretched earth, we are still excluded from it.</p>

<p class="v">55. And what good does it do us, finally, that those who have been temperate shall one day be more brilliant than the stars, if we become blacker than darkness itself?</p>

<p class="v">56. For during our life we never thought that, in committing iniquity, we would be punished for it after death.</p>

<p class="v">57. And he said to me: This is a just notion of the struggle to which man is exposed as soon as he begins to see the light of day.</p>

<p class="v">58. So that, if he is defeated in it, he shall suffer what you say; and if, on the contrary, he comes out victorious, he shall receive the reward of which I have spoken to you:</p>

<p class="v">59. For it is of this immortal life that Moses once spoke to the people, when he said to them: Choose life, that you may live.</p>

<p class="v">60. But they believed neither Moses nor the prophets who came after him. And they did not believe even me myself, when I assured them,</p>

<p class="v">61. That the dire condition to which they were reduced would end less in the loss than in the happiness of those who had lived in hope of salvation.</p>

<p class="v">62. And I said: Lord, I know that the Most High is truly a God of goodness, in that he has made it shine upon those who have not yet come to these last times;</p>

<p class="v">63. And that he has pity on those who turn to him.</p>

<p class="v">64. I know that he is a patient God, since he waits with patience for those who in all their actions have committed ungodliness;</p>

<p class="v">65. That he is magnificent and generous, since he lavishes his gifts according to the various needs of his creatures;</p>

<p class="v">66. And that his mercy is infinite, since he pours it out so abundantly upon men who are, who have been, and who shall be in the course of the ages.</p>

<p class="v">67. For if he did not multiply his mercy, those of this age could not subsist, nor could those who are to inhabit it receive life.</p>

<p class="v">68. If, by his goodness, he did not forgive the iniquities committed against him, out of ten thousand men there would not be a single one saved.</p>

<p class="v">69. And if he himself who is to judge them did not forgive them after having purified them by his word, and did not forget the number of their crimes, out of that innumerable multitude of men scarcely a few would be saved.</p>

### Chapter 8 <span class="chap-roman">(VIII)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Then the angel answered me and said: The Most High created the present age to be the dwelling place of a multitude of creatures, but the age to come shall be only for a very small number of them.</p>

<p class="v">2. Esdras, I will make you understand these things by a comparison. If you ask the earth, it will answer you that it can furnish much matter fit for making earthen vessels, but very little of that from which gold is formed.</p>

<p class="v">3. Such is the state of the present age: many have received being in it, but very few of them shall be saved.</p>

<p class="v">4. And addressing my own spirit, I said to it: Meditate on these words, and discover their hidden meanings;</p>

<p class="v">5. For you have come here only to be instructed with docility, and you presume to prophesy as though your knowledge extended beyond earthly things.</p>

<p class="v">6. I said then: Lord, if you do not allow your servant to present his prayers to you, if you do not cast into our hearts that divine seed, that it may bear fruit there, and if you yourself do not enlighten our understanding, how shall corrupt man be able to subsist before you, and who shall be able to serve as his support?</p>

<p class="v">7. For you alone have power over all things, and man is the work of your hands, as you yourself have said:</p>

<p class="v">8. Now the body is created in the womb of the woman, you have formed all its members, and it is preserved there by the mingling of water and fire, and the woman carries for nine months the fruit with which you have made her fruitful.</p>

<p class="v">9. You preserve both the one and the other, and when the time has come, the mother lets come forth from her womb the child she carried there.</p>

<p class="v">10. You have further willed that she should carry in her breasts the milk she needs to nourish it.</p>

<p class="v">11. So that, having received this first nourishment for a while, it might afterward become the object of your mercies.</p>

<p class="v">12. You justify it in your eyes, you instruct it in your law, and your wisdom rules and guides all its steps:</p>

<p class="v">13. You finally deliver it to death as one of your creatures, and you will restore it to life as being your work.</p>

<p class="v">14. If, then, you allow to perish him whom you formed only with such care and attention, would it not have been easy for you, after having created him, to prevent him from being lost?</p>

<p class="v">15. And now, Lord, I will not pray to you for all men in general — you know what you have resolved to do with them — but I will speak to you on behalf of your people, for whom I am in affliction:</p>

<p class="v">16. For your inheritance, which is the continual subject of my tears — of Israel and of Jacob — for whom I feel the keenest pain and the most dreadful sorrow.</p>

<p class="v">17. Therefore I will begin to offer you my prayers, both for them and for myself, considering the sins we commit every day on the earth;</p>

<p class="v">18. So as to forestall the unforeseen day on which he who is to judge us must come to surprise us.</p>

<p class="v">19. Thus, Lord, deign to hear my prayers, and give attention to the groanings I am about to pour out in your presence.</p>

<p class="v">20. The beginning of the words that Esdras spoke before he was taken up from the earth: I said then: Lord, you who govern the universe, and who lay bare what is highest in the heavens:</p>

<p class="v">21. You whose throne is beyond price and whose glory is incomprehensible, before whom that innumerable host of angels is always in fear and in deep abasement:</p>

<p class="v">22. That host of spirits who dwell in the midst of the winds and the fire, and who are often clothed with them. You whose word is true, whose promises are certain,</p>

<p class="v">23. Whose purposes are effectual and whose acts are terrible. You whose glances dry up the depths, and whose wrath uproots the mountains, as has happened many times,</p>

<p class="v">24. Hear the prayer of your servant, and let yourself be moved by the groanings of your creature.</p>

<p class="v">25. For as long as I breathe, I will make my voice heard, and as long as I retain understanding I will answer you:</p>

<p class="v">26. Have no regard for those among us who have offended you, but for those who are faithful in practicing your law.</p>

<p class="v">27. Consider not those who have imitated the disorders of the nations, but those whom contradictions have not been able to turn away from the path of your commandments.</p>

<p class="v">28. Remember not those who have done evil in your sight, but those who, filled with fear of you, have respected your ordinances.</p>

<p class="v">29. Punish us not because of those who have made themselves like beasts; but pardon us for the sake of those who, fearing no man, have generously instructed them in your law.</p>

<p class="v">30. Let not your indignation be kindled because of those who are placed below the very brutes; but save us for the sake of those who have relied upon the justice and truth of your promises.</p>

<p class="v">31. For, like our fathers, we languish under all these infirmities, and you will make your mercy shine forth by pouring it out upon us who are sinners.</p>

<p class="v">32. If, then, you deign to have pity on us, you will truly be the God of mercy, since we have done no work of righteousness;</p>

<p class="v">33. But as for the righteous, who have laid up for themselves a treasure of good works, they shall receive the reward for them.</p>

<p class="v">34. What then is man, that he should be able to arouse your indignation? And what is this corrupt race, that you should arm against it all your fury?</p>

<p class="v">35. Certainly, all men have committed ungodliness, and even among your own people there is not one who has not offended you;</p>

<p class="v">36. But, Lord, it is in this very thing that your justice and your goodness shall shine forth, when you show mercy to those who have done nothing to deserve it.</p>

<p class="v">37. And he said to me: Some of your words have been in accord with the truth, and things shall come to pass as you have said.</p>

<p class="v">38. I will not examine the deeds of sinners before death, judgment, and the day of perdition.</p>

<p class="v">39. All my joy shall be to consider the works of the righteous, and I will forget neither their exile, nor their good works, nor the reward that is due to their labors.</p>

<p class="v">40. All that I have told you is according to the truth.</p>

<p class="v">41. As the seeds that the farmer entrusts to the earth do not all fulfill his expectation at harvest time, and as the plants he cultivates do not all take root alike, so of this multitude of men who have been created on the earth, not all shall be saved.</p>

<p class="v">42. And I said to him: If I have found favor in your eyes, allow me to speak.</p>

<p class="v">43. Just as the farmer's seed is lost if it does not come up out of the earth, and does not receive the rains according to the seasons, and rots if the water falls in too great abundance:</p>

<p class="v">44. So perishes man, whom you formed with your own hands, of whom you are the model and the pattern, and for whom you created all things; and yet you treat him as the farmer's seed.</p>

<p class="v">45. Be not angry with us; but forgive your people, have pity on your only inheritance, and let your creature find mercy with you.</p>

<p class="v">46. And he answered me: The things present concern those who are now present on the earth; but the things to come shall be for those who shall live at the end of the times:</p>

<p class="v">47. For you are far from loving my creature with a love equal to that which I feel for it; I have often communicated myself to it and to you, and never to the ungodly.</p>

<p class="v">48. And you are great in the eyes of the Most High</p>

<p class="v">49. Only because you have humbled yourself in his presence as you ought, and because you have not judged yourself worthy to be placed among the ranks of the righteous.</p>

<p class="v">50. But as for those who shall live at the end of the times, they shall experience every kind of misery and calamity, because they shall walk in great pride.</p>

<p class="v">51. Meditate then within yourself on all these mysteries, and understand what shall be the glory of those who are the imitators of your righteousness.</p>

<p class="v">52. For it is for you that paradise is opened, that the tree of life is planted, that the age to come shall exist, that abundance shall flow, that the holy city is built, and that rest, goodness, and wisdom shall reign there in a perfect state.</p>

<p class="v">53. You shall no longer bear within you the root of evil; sickness and infirmity shall no longer make war upon you, and corruption shall withdraw into hell to be forgotten there forever.</p>

<p class="v">54. The days of sorrow are past, and already the treasure of immortality begins to appear.</p>

<p class="v">55. Trouble yourself no longer, then, about the great number of those who must perish.</p>

<p class="v">56. For, finding themselves perfectly free, they rejected the Most High, they despised his holy law, and turned away from his paths.</p>

<p class="v">57. They have trampled underfoot the children of the Most High;</p>

<p class="v">58. And they said in their heart that there was no God, although they knew that they were mortal.</p>

<p class="v">59. And while you shall all enjoy the happiness I announce to you, as for them, they shall have for their portion the thirst and the torments prepared for them. God, however, has not desired the ruin of man.</p>

<p class="v">60. But men formed by his hands have defiled the holiness of his name, and have only ingratitude for the author of their being.</p>

<p class="v">61. Therefore I prepare to enter into judgment with them.</p>

<p class="v">62. I have revealed these mysteries only to you and to a small number of righteous men who resemble you. Then I said:</p>

<p class="v">63. It is true, Lord, that you have made known to me the great number of wonders you are to perform at the end of the ages; but you have hidden from me the time at which they shall come to pass.</p>

### Chapter 9 <span class="chap-roman">(IX)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. The Lord answered me and said: Measure the time exactly, traverse its spans, and when you have seen the fulfillment of a part of the signs I have foretold to you,</p>

<p class="v">2. Understand then that the Most High is about to enter into judgment with the age he has created.</p>

<p class="v">3. When the earth shall tremble in various places, and the peoples shall rise up one against another,</p>

<p class="v">4. Then you shall know that the Most High had foretold these things from the beginning, even before you were born.</p>

<p class="v">5. For just as all the things that have been created on the earth had a beginning, and it is no less certain that they must one day cease to be;</p>

<p class="v">6. So it is with the times of the Most High: they had beginnings marked by wonders, and their end shall be preceded by striking signs.</p>

<p class="v">7. Then all those who are among the elect, and who shall be able to escape by favor of their works and of a faith like that of the righteous,</p>

<p class="v">8. Those, I say, shall come forth victorious from the perils and obstacles I have foretold to you, and they shall enjoy under my reign and in my dominion the salvation I had prepared for them, for I had chosen them from the beginning.</p>

<p class="v">9. But as for those who have corrupted my ways, they shall be overwhelmed with miseries, and those who have rejected them with scorn shall have for their portion only endless torments.</p>

<p class="v">10. For I had loaded them with blessings during their life, and they did not know me.</p>

<p class="v">11. They had only distaste for my law, when they were still fully free to follow it.</p>

<p class="v">12. And having still time to do penance, they did not take advantage of it, and closed their eyes to it; it is therefore just that, given over at last to death, they should be instructed by torments and tortures.</p>

<p class="v">13. Seek then no longer to know in what manner the ungodly shall be tormented; strive rather to discover what shall be the happiness of the righteous, who are those who shall make up the age to come, and when it shall begin to appear.</p>

<p class="v">14. Then I answered and said:</p>

<p class="v">15. I have said it before, I say it again, and I shall not cease to say it: those who fall into perdition are more numerous than those who shall be saved,</p>

<p class="v">16. As the wave of the sea is greater than one of the drops of which it is formed. And he said to me:</p>

<p class="v">17. Such is the field, such are the seeds; such are the flowers, such are the colors; such is the workman, such is his work; such is the farmer, such is his labor: for such was the order that reigned in the universe.</p>

<p class="v">18. When I was preparing the world that was to be the dwelling of the men who inhabit it at present, no one then opposed my will,</p>

<p class="v">19. And each one obeyed; but since it has existed, the corruption of morals has multiplied through an unhappy fruitfulness and through a hidden law.</p>

<p class="v">20. I therefore considered this age, and I saw the misfortunes that its criminal desires were going to bring upon it.</p>

<p class="v">21. I nevertheless spared it, and I reserved for myself a grape from the cluster and a plant from a numerous stock.</p>

<p class="v">22. Let this ungrateful and barren multitude perish then forever, and let there remain of it only this grape and this plant that I have cultivated with such great care.</p>

<p class="v">23. As for you, Esdras, let seven more days pass, during which you shall not fast.</p>

<p class="v">24. But you shall go into a field full of flowers, in which there is no house; you shall feed only on the flowers that grow there, you shall eat no meat, and you shall drink no wine.</p>

<p class="v">25. Offer your prayers there without ceasing; I will come there and speak with you.</p>

<p class="v">26. I went therefore, as the Lord had told me, into a field called Ardath; I sat down there among the flowers, and I ate of the plants growing there until I was satisfied.</p>

<p class="v">27. At the end of the seven days, while I was still lying upon the grass of that field, I felt my heart stirred as before.</p>

<p class="v">28. And then, opening my mouth, I began to speak to the Most High, and I said to him:</p>

<p class="v">29. Lord, before showing yourself to us, you made yourself seen by our fathers in the desert, that barren and uninhabited place, and when they came out of Egypt, you said to them:</p>

<p class="v">30. Israel, hear me; and you, house of Jacob, be attentive to my words.</p>

<p class="v">31. For I will put my law into your hearts like a seed; it shall bear fruit there and shall make you forever glorious upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">32. But your fathers, after having received my law, did not keep it; they violated my covenant, the law bore no fruit in them, nor could it; for it was from you that the fruit was to come forth.</p>

<p class="v">33. And thus those to whom it had been given were rejected, because they did not keep the seed that had been in their hearts.</p>

<p class="v">34. It ordinarily happens that when the earth has received the seed, when a vessel has been put out to sea, when a vessel has been filled with some food, if the things in which all this was placed come to be destroyed,</p>

<p class="v">35. What was sown or placed in them, or what was received in them, is destroyed at the same time and no longer exists then among us; but it is not the same with regard to us.</p>

<p class="v">36. For we were rejected after having violated the law we had received, and our heart, where it had been cast like a seed, met the same fate.</p>

<p class="v">37. But the law was not annihilated, and it has kept all its force.</p>

<p class="v">38. As I was saying these things within myself, and was attentive, I saw on my right a woman who was weeping and uttering loud cries; she seemed greatly cast down with grief; her garments were torn, and she covered her head with dust.</p>

<p class="v">39. Then, interrupting all my reflections, I turned toward her, and said to her:</p>

<p class="v">40. Why do you weep, and what is the cause of your sorrow? She answered me:</p>

<p class="v">41. My lord, allow, allow me to weep and to give myself over more and more to my sorrow, for I am in great bitterness of heart, and nothing equals my affliction.</p>

<p class="v">42. Having then earnestly pressed her to tell me what had happened to her, she answered me:</p>

<p class="v">43. Your servant had lived in shameful barrenness, and I had not given birth, although I had been with my husband for the space of thirty years;</p>

<p class="v">44. And during all that time I did not cease, neither by day nor by night, to offer my prayers to the Most High.</p>

<p class="v">45. At last, at the end of thirty years, the Lord heard your servant, he saw my affliction, he was moved by my sufferings, and gave me a son who was all my joy, my husband's joy, and the hope of the whole city; and we gave thanks for it to Almighty God.</p>

<p class="v">46. I raised him with great difficulty.</p>

<p class="v">47. And when he was grown and of an age to marry, I celebrated the day of his wedding.</p>

### Chapter 10 <span class="chap-roman">(X)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. My son, having entered his bedchamber, fell down and died.</p>

<p class="v">2. We at once put out all the lights; all my fellow citizens came running in crowds to console me, and I remained with them until the night of the following day.</p>

<p class="v">3. But when they had all withdrawn, to leave me at rest, I rose up in the middle of the night, and taking flight, I came into the fields where you still see me.</p>

<p class="v">4. And now my purpose is not to enter the city, but to remain here without taking any food, to weep without ceasing, and to fast until I die.</p>

<p class="v">5. Then, changing my tone, I answered her with anger and said to her:</p>

<p class="v">6. O most senseless of all women! Do you not know then what our affliction is, and what evils overwhelm us?</p>

<p class="v">7. Zion, our mother, is in a dreadful sorrow, her humiliation is extreme, and her tears do not cease to flow.</p>

<p class="v">8. What! While we are all in mourning and affliction because of the evils we suffer, must the death of one child wring from you so many tears and regrets?</p>

<p class="v">9. Ask the earth, and it will tell you that it belongs to it to weep for the loss of so many things that come forth from its bosom.</p>

<p class="v">10. For all those who have been born, or who shall be born hereafter, come from the earth; yet almost all of them run to their ruin, and the greater number of them is destined to perish.</p>

<p class="v">11. She, then, who loses so great a number of children, has she not more right to give herself over to grief than you, who have lost but one? But you will say to me:</p>

<p class="v">12. The cause of my affliction is very different; for I have lost the fruit of my womb, that fruit which I carried in travail, which I brought forth in pain.</p>

<p class="v">13. But as for the earth, the multitude it now contains shall one day return into its bosom in the same manner it was drawn from it. Here is what I will answer you:</p>

<p class="v">14. Just as you brought forth in pain, so the earth, from the beginning, gives its fruit to the man who cultivates it.</p>

<p class="v">15. Now, therefore, restrain the excess of your grief, and bear with courage the misfortunes that overwhelm you.</p>

<p class="v">16. For if you acknowledge how just God is in all that he does, you will submit to the purposes he has resolved to carry out at the appointed times, and this submission shall be your true glory.</p>

<p class="v">17. Return then into the city, and go back to your husband. Then she said to me:</p>

<p class="v">18. I will not do it, and I shall die here.</p>

<p class="v">19. I spoke to her again, and said to her:</p>

<p class="v">20. Do not act thus, but yield to my counsel; consider into what misfortunes Zion has fallen, and learn, from the evils Jerusalem suffers, to bear your own.</p>

<p class="v">21. For, as you see, our sanctuary is abandoned, our altar is overthrown, and our temple is destroyed.</p>

<p class="v">22. Our instruments of music are silent, our holy songs are no longer heard, the days of feasts and rejoicing are forbidden us, the light of our lampstand is put out, the ark of our covenant has been plundered. The most holy things have been defiled, the name of our God has come close to being profaned, our children have fallen into disgrace, our priests have been burned, our Levites have been led into captivity, our virgins have been dishonored, our wives ravished, the good have been carried off, our children are no more, our young men are captives, the brave men of Israel have lost their strength.</p>

<p class="v">23. And what crowns our misfortunes, Zion, the famous Zion, has seen all her glory brought to nothing, and she herself has been delivered up to her enemies.</p>

<p class="v">24. Come forth, then, from the deep sorrow in which you are, and moderate the excess of your grief, so that the Most High may restore his mercies to you, and, after having put an end to your ills, may re-establish you in perfect rest.</p>

<p class="v">25. While I was speaking to her, her face suddenly became radiant, her eyes shone like fire; I was seized with fright at it, and as I was wondering what this could be,</p>

<p class="v">26. She uttered a terrible voice, and the whole earth was shaken by it; I looked at that same instant,</p>

<p class="v">27. And I no longer saw that woman; but from the place where I had seen her there rose up a city whose walls seemed very spacious. I was seized with fear, and raising my voice, I said:</p>

<p class="v">28. Where is the angel Uriel, who was sent to me at the beginning of this vision? For it is he who has given rise in my thoughts to the trouble and agitation in which I find myself; my hopes have been vain, and my prayer shall return to my shame.</p>

<p class="v">29. As I was speaking thus, he came to me and looked at me.</p>

<p class="v">30. I bore upon my face the image of death, and I had lost consciousness; then he took me by the right hand and filled me with strength, and having raised me up on my feet, he said to me:</p>

<p class="v">31. What has happened to you, and why are your spirit and your heart thus in trouble and agitation? And I answered him:</p>

<p class="v">32. Because you have abandoned me; yet I came into this field, as you had commanded me: I have seen there, and I still see there, things that I cannot relate. And he said to me:</p>

<p class="v">33. Take up your strength again, and I will tell you what you must do. I answered him:</p>

<p class="v">34. Speak, my Lord, and do not abandon me, lest I die without help.</p>

<p class="v">35. For I have seen things altogether new, and I hear of things I have never heard spoken of.</p>

<p class="v">36. Are my senses deceived, or is this the effect of some dream?</p>

<p class="v">37. And now I beseech you to explain these wonders to your servant. Then he said to me:</p>

<p class="v">38. Listen to me, I will instruct you and speak to you of the things that have cast you into fright; for the Most High has already revealed to you several mysteries.</p>

<p class="v">39. He has seen the uprightness of your heart. He knows that you have not ceased to grieve for your people, and that your tears have not been interrupted on account of Zion.</p>

<p class="v">40. Here, then, is the meaning of the vision you have just had:</p>

<p class="v">41. You first saw a woman in tears, and you approached her to console her.</p>

<p class="v">42. All at once, you ceased to see her, and in her place there appeared a city that was being built.</p>

<p class="v">43. She then spoke to you of the death of her son: here is the meaning of this vision.</p>

<p class="v">44. This woman is the figure of Zion, whom you now see as a built city.</p>

<p class="v">45. As for her telling you that she had been barren for the space of thirty years, it is that a like number of years had passed without any oblation yet having been made in that city.</p>

<p class="v">46. But at the end of thirty years, Solomon, having finished building it, offered sacrifices there, and it was then that she who was barren brought forth a son.</p>

<p class="v">47. What this woman told you of the pains she had taken to raise her son signifies what Jerusalem cost in care and labor to build.</p>

<p class="v">48. And finally, the tragic death of her son signifies what was the ruin of that city.</p>

<p class="v">49. You saw her herself under the figure of that woman; and as she wept for the death of her son, you had begun to console her. This is what you were to know of all that has happened before your eyes.</p>

<p class="v">50. And now the Most High, having seen the deep sorrow and sincere grief into which the misfortunes of Zion have cast you, has shown you the splendor and glory with which she is one day to be clothed.</p>

<p class="v">51. It is for this that I commanded you to go into a field where there was no house.</p>

<p class="v">52. For I knew that the Most High was going to reveal these wonders to you there.</p>

<p class="v">53. I therefore told you to go into a field where the foundations of no house had ever been laid.</p>

<p class="v">54. For a place where the city of the Most High was to appear could not have borne any building erected by the hand of man.</p>

<p class="v">55. Take courage, then, and fear not; but enter into this city, and as far as your feeble sight can bear it, contemplate the splendor and magnificence of its buildings.</p>

<p class="v">56. And afterward you shall lend your ear to what shall be said, as much as you are able.</p>

<p class="v">57. For you are more fortunate than a multitude of others, and the Most High has admitted you into the small number of his elect.</p>

<p class="v">58. Spend here also the following night.</p>

<p class="v">59. And he will show you what shall happen in the last times to the men who shall then be on the earth.</p>

<p class="v">60. I fell asleep, therefore, that night and the following night, as the angel had commanded me.</p>
### Chapter 11 <span class="chap-roman">(XI)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. While I was sleeping, I had a vision in which I saw an eagle rising from the bosom of the sea, and it had twelve wings and three heads.</p>

<p class="v">2. And as I watched it, it spread its wings over the whole earth, and the winds, joined together, armed all their fury against it.</p>

<p class="v">3. From its feathers I saw others spring forth, quite contrary to the first, and they formed only small wings.</p>

<p class="v">4. Its heads were asleep, but the middle one was larger than the other two, and it too was asleep.</p>

<p class="v">5. And all at once the eagle rose into the air, and it reigned over the earth and over those who dwell in it.</p>

<p class="v">6. Everything under heaven was subject to it, and none of the creatures that are on the earth dared withdraw from its dominion.</p>

<p class="v">7. And having raised itself upon its talons, it made its voice heard to its wings and said to them:</p>

<p class="v">8. Do not all keep watch at the same time, but sleep and keep watch one after another.</p>

<p class="v">9. And as for the heads, let them be given over to sleep until the end of time.</p>

<p class="v">10. I looked, and I perceived that the voice came not from the heads of the eagle, but issued from the middle of its body.</p>

<p class="v">11. I counted its wings, set opposite one another, and they numbered eight.</p>

<p class="v">12. One of them, having risen on the right side, reigned over all the earth.</p>

<p class="v">13. And while it reigned, it suddenly vanished, so that one could not even recognize the place where it had been before; then the nearest one, rising, took its place and reigned a long time.</p>

<p class="v">14. But the end drew near, and it vanished like the first.</p>

<p class="v">15. For a voice was heard, and said to it:</p>

<p class="v">16. Listen, you who have held the empire of the earth so long; here is what I announce to you before you are destroyed.</p>

<p class="v">17. None of the wings shall reign after you as long as your empire lasted, nor even half that time.</p>

<p class="v">18. The third having risen, it reigned as the first ones had, and vanished as they did too.</p>

<p class="v">19. All the others exercised dominion in turn, and they too vanished.</p>

<p class="v">20. I was attentive to what was happening, and I saw the other feathers rising from time to time toward the right to gain dominion; and some of them, having obtained it, vanished at that very instant.</p>

<p class="v">21. For they rose up, but they did not reign at all.</p>

<p class="v">22. After that, neither the twelve great wings nor the two small ones were seen any more.</p>

<p class="v">23. And of the whole body of the eagle there appeared nothing more but two sleeping heads and six wings.</p>

<p class="v">24. I was considering it attentively; suddenly two of these wings separated from the others and remained attached to the head that was on the right side, and the four others kept their place.</p>

<p class="v">23. Then the small wings thought of rising to empire.</p>

<p class="v">26. One of them rose up, but it vanished instantly.</p>

<p class="v">27. And at last all of them vanished more swiftly than the first ones had.</p>

<p class="v">28. I was attentive to what was happening, and all at once the two others that remained thought within themselves of usurping dominion.</p>

<p class="v">29. But at the moment they were occupied with this thought, the middle head awoke; it was the largest of the three.</p>

<p class="v">30. And they all held together.</p>

<p class="v">31. And this head, having turned itself with the others, devoured the two small wings underneath, which were thinking of reigning.</p>

<p class="v">32. It spread consternation over the whole earth, exercising a cruel dominion over those who dwell in it, and its reign was longer than that of the wings had been.</p>

<p class="v">33. I was considering attentively, and all at once, the middle head having vanished like the wings,</p>

<p class="v">34. There remained only the two others, which reigned over the earth and over those who dwell in it,</p>

<p class="v">35. Then the head that was on the right devoured the one that was on the left.</p>

<p class="v">36. And I heard a voice that said to me: Look before you, and consider what presents itself to your eyes.</p>

<p class="v">37. And as I was attentive, I saw a furious, roaring lion come out of a forest; its voice was like that of a man, and it said to the eagle:</p>

<p class="v">38. Listen, I will speak to you. Here is what the Most High says:</p>

<p class="v">39. Are you not the only one left of the four beasts that I made reign over the earth? For I allowed them to destroy one another in turn.</p>

<p class="v">40. Then rising up, you overcame the three others, and they ceased to be. You have exercised over the earth a cruel and tyrannical dominion, and throughout all the time it lasted, fraud was never banished from it.</p>

<p class="v">41. You have never made truth reign in your judgments.</p>

<p class="v">42. You have tormented good people, you have outraged those who loved peace; liars have shared in your friendship. You have ravaged the dwellings of those who prospered in their ways, and those who had never offended you were not exempt from your violence even within their own walls.</p>

<p class="v">43. These excesses have risen to the throne of the Most High, and your pride has been known to him who is almighty.</p>

<p class="v">44. He has considered these proud reigns, he has stopped their course, and the measure of your crimes is at last full.</p>

<p class="v">45. Therefore vanish, and let your horrible wings, your baleful feathers, your heads full of malice, your cruel talons, and all the vanity and falsehood you contain within yourself never be seen again,</p>

<p class="v">46. So that the whole earth may breathe again, and, freed from your cruel power, may hope from the author of its being for justice and mercy.</p>

### Chapter 12 <span class="chap-roman">(XII)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. While the lion was saying these things to the eagle, I was attentive.</p>

<p class="v">2. And all at once, this last head vanished with the four wings that had gone over to its side and had aspired to empire, and their reign was short and full of troubles.</p>

<p class="v">3. All these things having vanished, the body of the eagle appeared all in flames, and the whole earth was terrified by it; and after I came out of this state of fear and agitation into which I had fallen, I addressed my spirit, and said to it:</p>

<p class="v">4. It is you who have cast me into all these torments, by wanting to search out the ways of the Most High.</p>

<p class="v">5. My heart and my spirit are equally cast down, and the terrors that struck me this night have not left in me the slightest strength.</p>

<p class="v">6. Now I will pray the Lord to sustain me to the end.</p>

<p class="v">7. And I said to him: Lord, sovereign ruler, if I have found favor in your presence, if I am more righteous in your eyes than many others, and if my prayer is worthy to rise up to you,</p>

<p class="v">8. Sustain my weakness, and make known to me clearly the meaning of this terrible vision, so that my soul may receive perfect consolation from it.</p>

<p class="v">9. For you have judged me worthy to know what must happen at the end of time. And he said to me:</p>

<p class="v">10. Here is the meaning of this vision.</p>

<p class="v">11. The eagle that you saw coming up out of the midst of the sea is the empire that was shown to your brother Daniel in a vision.</p>

<p class="v">12. But he did not receive the understanding of it; therefore I will interpret it for you.</p>

<p class="v">13. Behold, the times are approaching, and there will arise on the earth an empire more terrible than all those that preceded it.</p>

<p class="v">14. Twelve kings shall govern it, one after another.</p>

<p class="v">15. But the second, after attaining it, shall hold it longer than any of the others.</p>

<p class="v">16. This is what the twelve wings that you saw signify.</p>

<p class="v">17. As for the voice that you heard, which came not from the head of the eagle, but from its body,</p>

<p class="v">18. Here is the explanation: When the end of this kingdom comes, dreadful troubles will arise in it; it will see itself on the brink of its ruin, and yet it will not yet be the time of its destruction, but it will rise again such as it was at its birth.</p>

<p class="v">19. As for the eight small wings underneath that you saw joining the great wings,</p>

<p class="v">20. Here is the explanation. Eight kings shall arise in this kingdom; the time of this reign shall be short, their years shall pass swiftly, and two of these kings shall perish.</p>

<p class="v">21. And when half the time this empire must last has elapsed, four of these kings shall reign for the time appointed to them, and the two others shall be reserved for the end.</p>

<p class="v">22. As for the three heads that were asleep,</p>

<p class="v">23. Here is what they signify. The Most High shall raise up three empires after this one; he shall raise up several others besides, which shall be joined to them, and they shall dominate the earth,</p>

<p class="v">24. And over those who dwell in it; they shall treat them with more rigor and cruelty than all the other empires that preceded them, and that is why they are marked by the heads of the eagle.</p>

<p class="v">25. For it is they who shall search out the number of its impieties, and who shall destroy it themselves.</p>

<p class="v">26. As for the largest head that vanished, this signifies that one of these kings shall perish by a violent death, although in his bed.</p>

<p class="v">27. The two others who shall reign after him shall perish by the sword.</p>

<p class="v">28. For one of them shall kill the other with his sword, and shall himself at last perish by the sword.</p>

<p class="v">29. As for the two small wings that went to join the right head of the eagle,</p>

<p class="v">30. Here is the explanation. These are those whom the Most High has reserved for the last day, and who are to form this weak and troubled kingdom.</p>
