<p class="v">31. As for the lion that you saw rushing forth roaring from the depths of the forest, and which spoke to the eagle to reproach it for its injustices,</p>

<p class="v">32. This is the tempest that the Most High shall arm against them and against their impieties at the end of time; for then he shall overwhelm them with reproaches, he shall lay before their eyes all the violence they have committed.</p>

<p class="v">33. He shall make them appear full of life at his judgment, and after having convicted them, he shall deliver them to torments.</p>

<p class="v">34. He shall deliver the remnant of my people from affliction;</p>

<p class="v">35. those who have been saved within my dominion shall be filled with joy until the end of time, on the day of judgment of which I have already spoken.</p>

<p class="v">36. You alone have been judged worthy to know these mysteries of the Most High.</p>

<p class="v">37. Write, therefore, a book of all the things you have seen, and then put it in a hidden place.</p>

<p class="v">38. Reveal them to those of your people who are wise, and whom you know capable of understanding them and keeping them in the secret of their heart.</p>

<p class="v">39. As for you, remain here still seven days, and you shall see all that it shall please the Most High to reveal to you.</p>

<p class="v">40. Then the angel left me, and the people, seeing that the seven days had already passed without my returning to the city, all gathered together, from the least to the greatest, and having come to find me, they said to me:</p>

<p class="v">41. What injury have you received from us, and what have we done that could oblige you to abandon us and stay here far from us?</p>

<p class="v">42. For of all the people, you are the only one who has been left to us, to be to us like the cluster of grapes in a vineyard, like light in a dark place, like a favorable harbor, and like a ship escaped from shipwreck.</p>

<p class="v">43. Was it not enough, the evils we suffer?</p>

<p class="v">44. And since you thus abandon us, would it not have been more advantageous for us to perish with Zion in the flames that consumed her?</p>

<p class="v">45. For we are no more innocent than those who perished with that holy city. And they wept with loud cries, and I said to them:</p>

<p class="v">46. Israel, be full of confidence, and you, house of Jacob, do not let yourself be cast down by sorrow.</p>

<p class="v">47. For the Most High will remember you, and the Almighty has not forgotten you in the evils you suffer.</p>

<p class="v">48. As for me, I have not abandoned you, and I have not withdrawn from you forever, but I came to this place to pray the Lord to halt the course of your misfortunes, and to restore the splendor and majesty of his sanctuary.</p>

<p class="v">49. And now let each one withdraw to his house, for in a few days I will return to you.</p>

<p class="v">50. Then the people returned to the city as I had told them.</p>

<p class="v">51. And I remained seven more days in the fields, as the angel had commanded me, and during all that time I fed only on the flowers and herbs that grew in that place.</p>

### Chapter 13 <span class="chap-roman">(XIII)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. After the seven days had expired, I had a vision during the night.</p>

<p class="v">2. All at once a wind arose from the sea that stirred up the waves.</p>

<p class="v">3. And as I was attentive, considering what was happening, I saw a man come out of it, who was followed by an infinite number of heavenly spirits, and wherever he cast his gaze, he spread fear and terror there.</p>

<p class="v">4. The voice that came out of his mouth, like a fire that ravages the countryside, burned all who heard it.</p>

<p class="v">5. I then saw an innumerable multitude of men gathering from the four corners of heaven to fight against him who had come up out of the sea.</p>

<p class="v">6. But he had carved out for himself, with his own hands, a very high mountain, and had flown up to it.</p>

<p class="v">7. And I sought the place from which this mountain had been taken, and I could not discover it.</p>

<p class="v">8. Then all those who had gathered to fight this man seemed to me seized with great fear, and yet they dared to expose themselves to battle.</p>

<p class="v">9. But when this man saw all this multitude coming to fall upon him, he did not raise his hand, nor arm it with his sword, nor with any other instrument of war.</p>

<p class="v">10. He did but let go from his mouth a breath of fire, and from his lips a burning wind; from his tongue he stirred up all these darts, sparks and tempests, and gathering all these darts together,</p>

<p class="v">11. He hurled them with fury upon this multitude prepared for battle, and consumed them all, so that there remained of them only ashes from which came a smell of smoke; and at the sight of these wonders, I was seized with fear.</p>

<p class="v">12. This man, having then come down from the mountain, called to himself another multitude of peaceable and tranquil men.</p>

<p class="v">13. And of all those who advanced toward him, some appeared joyful, others sad; some were bound, and others still were laden with things that are customarily offered to the Lord. And in the excess of my terror, I fell faint, I awoke, and I said:</p>

<p class="v">14. Lord, you have revealed these wonders to me from the beginning, and my prayer has seemed to you worthy to be heard.</p>

<p class="v">15. Now therefore, Lord, grant me the explanation of this new vision.</p>

<p class="v">16. For, as far as I can foresee, woe to those who shall be on the earth in those days, and still more unhappy those whom death shall already have carried off.</p>

<p class="v">17. And those who were no longer among the living appeared very sad.</p>

<p class="v">18. I see, then, at this present time, the things that shall happen at the end of time, and the evils that must fall upon those who have vanished from off the earth, and upon those who shall be there then.</p>

<p class="v">19. That is why they found themselves in great calamities and extreme perils, as these dreams indicated.</p>

<p class="v">20. Yet it would be easier for them to escape all these almost insurmountable dangers than for us to rise up out of this age, like a cloud, and discover what must happen at the end of time. And he answered me:</p>

<p class="v">21. I will explain the vision to you and reveal to you the things you have spoken of.</p>

<p class="v">22. As for those who shall then be found upon the earth, here is what shall happen to them.</p>

<p class="v">23. He who in that time shall have been able to guard himself from these perils shall find himself in safety; but as for the others who shall fall into them, these are those who have faith and who do the will of the Almighty.</p>

<p class="v">24. Understand, then, that the men who shall then live upon the earth shall be far happier than those who shall have been taken from it.</p>

<p class="v">25. As for the man whom you saw coming up out of the bosom of the sea, here is what he signifies:</p>

<p class="v">26. This is he whom the Most High reserves for the end of time; he shall deliver all his creatures by himself, and he shall take care of those who shall then be upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">27. And as there came out of his mouth a kind of breath mingled with fire and tempest,</p>

<p class="v">28. And that he had neither sword nor any other weapon of war; thus it is by his own strength that he overthrew this multitude that advanced to fight him. Here is the explanation of all these things.</p>

<p class="v">29. The days are approaching, and the Most High will come to deliver those who are on the earth.</p>

<p class="v">30. And when he appears, terror shall seize their minds.</p>

<p class="v">31. They shall be occupied in making war upon one another; city shall be seen rising against city, land against land, nation against nation, kingdom against kingdom.</p>

<p class="v">32. And when the time has come, and the signs that I first showed you begin to appear, then shall the revelation take place of my son, whom you saw under the figure of that man who came up out of the sea.</p>

<p class="v">33. Scarcely shall he have made his voice heard by all the nations of the earth, than they shall cease making war upon one another.</p>

<p class="v">34. And this innumerable multitude shall gather together as if with the design of fighting him.</p>

<p class="v">35. But as for him, he shall stand upon the top of Mount Zion.</p>

<p class="v">36. The city of Zion shall appear all at once in its glory, and all shall see it built and adorned, like the mountain that you saw form itself without anyone having touched it.</p>

<p class="v">37. Then my son shall judge the crimes and impieties of the nations, who, in the wandering of their thoughts, have cast themselves into the tempest and into the torments with which they shall then begin to be tormented.</p>

<p class="v">38. Flames shall serve his wrath, and he shall avenge himself by a law which, like a devouring fire, shall consume them without effort.</p>

<p class="v">39. As for that other multitude of peaceable men whom he has gathered around him,</p>

<p class="v">40. These are the ten tribes that Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, reduced to captivity under the reign of Hoshea, and whom he carried away beyond the river, into a foreign land.</p>

<p class="v">41. But as for them, they all resolved to abandon the multitude of the nations, and to advance further into the country, into a region that men had never inhabited before them.</p>

<p class="v">42. And to observe there the holy laws that they had violated in their own country.</p>

<p class="v">43. They finally entered it by the narrow passes of the Euphrates.</p>

<p class="v">44. The Lord then worked wonders in their favor, and stopped the course of the river until they had passed.</p>

<p class="v">45. For it was necessary to journey a year and a half to reach that region, and it was called Arsareth.</p>

<p class="v">46. They shall dwell there until the end of time, and when they prepare to return,</p>

<p class="v">47. The Most High shall again stop the currents of the river, so that they may have a free path, and that is why you saw that multitude in profound peace.</p>

<p class="v">48. It is in that place that he reigns over those of your people who have withdrawn there.</p>

<p class="v">49. And when he shall arm himself to destroy that innumerable assembly of all the nations, then he shall spare this people who have been kept in reserve.</p>

<p class="v">50. And he shall work several wonders in its favor.</p>

<p class="v">51. And I said to him: Lord, sovereign ruler, reveal to me what this man signifies, whom I saw coming up out of the midst of the sea. And he answered me:</p>

<p class="v">52. Just as you cannot fathom or know the things that are in that vast and deep abyss, so no living man shall be able to see my son, nor those who are with him, until the end of time has come.</p>

<p class="v">53. This is what the vision you have had signifies, and you are the only one who has received the understanding of it.</p>

<p class="v">54. For you have abandoned your own law to attach yourself to mine, and to meditate on it without ceasing.</p>

<p class="v">55. You have walked in the ways of wisdom, and you have loved understanding as your own mother.</p>

<p class="v">56. Therefore I have shown you the rewards that the Most High reserved for you; and when three more days have passed, I will reveal new mysteries to you, and I will teach you important and marvelous things.</p>

<p class="v">57. Then I set out on my way, and advanced into the countryside, glorifying and praising the Most High for the wonders he showed me from time to time,</p>

<p class="v">58. Because it is he who governs time, and all the things that are carried along in its course; and having stopped in a certain place, I remained sitting there for three days.</p>

### Chapter 14 <span class="chap-roman">(XIV)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. On the third day, having sat down under an oak,</p>

<p class="v">2. I suddenly heard a voice coming out of a bush, and it said to me: Ezra, Ezra; I rose at once, and I answered: Lord, here I am; then the voice said to me:</p>

<p class="v">3. I made myself known to Moses in the bush, and I spoke to him while my people were in bondage in Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">4. I sent him, and he brought my people out of that foreign land. I then made him go up onto Mount Sinai, and I kept him there beside me for many days.</p>

<p class="v">5. I told him of the great things I was to do. I revealed to him the secrets and the end of time, and I gave him this command:</p>

<p class="v">6. You shall tell these things to the people, and you shall hide these others from them.</p>

<p class="v">7. And now, Ezra, listen to what I am going to tell you.</p>

<p class="v">8. Keep in the secret of your heart the signs that I have shown you, the visions you have seen, and the interpretations you have received of them.</p>

<p class="v">9. For you shall vanish from off the earth, and you shall return at the end of time to serve my purposes with those who resemble you.</p>

<p class="v">10. The age has lost its strength and its youth, and the times are drawing near their last age.</p>

<p class="v">11. For it has been divided into twelve parts; ten of them have already elapsed, and half of the eleventh.</p>

<p class="v">12. And there shall be no more time than what remains until the end of the twelfth part.</p>

<p class="v">13. Now therefore, set your house in order, correct the disorders of your people, console those who are in affliction, and cease at last to walk in corrupt paths.</p>

<p class="v">14. Banish all base and mortal thoughts, unburden yourself of these crushing cares, strip yourself of a nature full of infirmities. And renouncing sad and grievous thoughts, hasten to go out of this age.</p>

<p class="v">15. For the evils with which you have seen it struck are nothing compared to those that shall come afterward.</p>

<p class="v">16. The more the age weakens as it approaches its end, the more evils shall multiply upon those who dwell in it.</p>

<p class="v">17. For truth shall withdraw day by day to make way for falsehood, and the vision you have had shall not be long in coming to pass.</p>

<p class="v">18. And I then said to you: O Lord,</p>

<p class="v">19. I am going to find the people as you command me, and I will admonish them; but who shall instruct those who come after us?</p>

<p class="v">20. For the age is plunged into dreadful darkness, and the light does not shine upon the steps of those who dwell in it</p>

<p class="v">21. The book of your law has been consumed by fire. Therefore there is no longer anyone found who is instructed in the great things you have done, and in those you are to do in time to come.</p>

<p class="v">22. If, then, I have found favor before you, fill me with your Holy Spirit, and I will write all that you have wrought in the world from the beginning, just as it was written in the book of the law, so that men may walk in your ways and live until the end of the ages, if they so wish.</p>

<p class="v">23. And the Lord answered me: Go, gather this people, and tell them not to seek you for forty days.</p>

<p class="v">24. Prepare several boxwood tablets, and take with you Sarea, Dabria, Selemia, Ecanus, and Asiel, who all write with great speed and skill.</p>

<p class="v">25. Then return here, and I will make the light of understanding shine in your heart, and it shall not go out until you have finished writing all the things I shall tell you.</p>

<p class="v">26. You shall reveal some of them to the perfect, and you shall tell others secretly to the wise; tomorrow, at this same hour, you shall begin to write them.</p>

<p class="v">27. I went away as he had commanded me, and having gathered the people, I spoke to them in these terms:</p>

<p class="v">28. Israel, listen to what I am about to tell you!</p>

<p class="v">29. Our fathers were once strangers in Egypt, and they at last came out of it.</p>

<p class="v">30. They received a law of life, but they did not keep it, and you yourselves have violated it after them.</p>

<p class="v">31. You divided the land of Zion by lot, but you and your fathers have committed iniquity, and you have not walked in the ways that the Most High had marked out for you.</p>

<p class="v">32. But since he is a just judge, he has taken away from you for a time what he had given you.</p>

<p class="v">33. Now here you are, all gathered together, and not one of the people is missing.</p>

<p class="v">34. If, then, you rise above your earthly and carnal thoughts, and fill your mind with understanding, you shall live, and after your death you shall obtain mercy.</p>

<p class="v">35. For we shall all be judged after death, when we shall live again; then the names of the righteous shall be made manifest, and the works of the wicked shall be exposed to the light of day.</p>

<p class="v">36. Let none of you come near me or seek me for forty days.</p>

<p class="v">37. I then took five persons with me, according to the order I had received, and all having arrived at the place from which I had come to find the people, we stopped there.</p>

<p class="v">38. The next day, the voice called me and said: Ezra, open your mouth, and drink what I offer you.</p>

<p class="v">39. I opened my mouth, therefore, and a vessel full of liquid was presented to me; it was like water, and it had the brightness of fire.</p>

<p class="v">40. I took the cup, and as soon as I had drunk it, I felt a multitude of thoughts spring up in my mind; wisdom grew in me, and my memory retraced various things for me.</p>

<p class="v">41. My mouth was opened, and it closed no more.</p>

<p class="v">42. The Most High also filled with understanding the five men I had chosen; and they wrote the wonders that were dictated to them in the silence of the night, but they did not understand them.</p>

<p class="v">43. They took some nourishment during the night, and as for me, I spoke by day, and I spoke by night.</p>

<p class="v">44. And in the space of these forty days, they filled two hundred and four books.</p>

<p class="v">45. And when that time had expired, the Most High made his voice heard and said to me: Publish those of these books that were written first, so that they may be read by those who are worthy of them and by those who are not.</p>

<p class="v">46. But you shall reserve the last seventy to give to the wise of your people.</p>

<p class="v">47. For in them is found a spring of understanding, a fountain of wisdom, and a river of knowledge. And I did as the voice had commanded me.</p>

### Chapter 15 <span class="chap-roman">(XV)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Go and announce to my people the preachings that I shall put in your mouth, says the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">2. Take care to write them in a book, because they are certain and true.</p>

<p class="v">3. Do not fear the designs they may form against you, and do not be troubled by the contradictions that their unbelief will oppose to your words.</p>

<p class="v">4. For every unbeliever shall die in his unbelief.</p>

<p class="v">5. Evils are going to spread over the earth, says the Lord; the sword, famine, death, and perdition shall be the ministers of my vengeance.</p>

<p class="v">6. For the whole earth is defiled with crimes, and those who dwell in it have reached the height of their malice.</p>

<p class="v">7. Therefore, says the Lord,</p>

<p class="v">8. I will avenge myself of the impieties they commit against me with such irreligion, and I will no longer bear with their injustices; innocent blood cries out to me, and the souls of the righteous do not cease demanding vengeance of me.</p>

<p class="v">9. I will avenge myself in a terrible manner, says the Lord, and I will demand an accounting from these wicked ones for the innocent blood they have shed.</p>

<p class="v">10. My people is led to death like a feeble flock. I will not suffer it to remain any longer in Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">11. But I will withdraw it with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. I will strike that land with new plagues, and I will ravage it throughout its whole extent.</p>

<p class="v">12. It shall be in affliction at the sight of the evils with which the Lord shall strike it, even to its foundations.</p>

<p class="v">13. The farmers shall weep, because blight, hail, and malignant influences shall ravage their seed.</p>

<p class="v">14. Woe to the age and to those who dwell in it!</p>

<p class="v">15. The sword is raised over their heads, and soon they shall be struck by it. The peoples shall make war upon one another, and the sword already gleams in their hands.</p>

<p class="v">16. Seditions shall break out everywhere amid these troubles; they shall no longer recognize their legitimate kings, and the princes shall make their own power the sole rule of their actions.</p>

<p class="v">17. He who wishes to enter the city shall not be able to.</p>

<p class="v">18. The cities shall be in confusion because of the pride of those who dwell in them; the houses shall vanish beneath their ruins, and men shall be seized with terror.</p>

<p class="v">19. They shall have no compassion for one another, and in the excess of their afflictions and their hunger, they shall go, sword in hand, to plunder houses and inheritances.</p>

<p class="v">20. Behold the time, says the Lord, when I shall gather all the kings of the East, of the South, of the North, and of Lebanon, to strike them with terror and repay them all the evils they have made Israel suffer.</p>

<p class="v">21. For I will treat them as they have treated my elect until this day: here is what the Lord says,</p>

<p class="v">22. My arm shall bear heavily upon sinners, and my sword shall not spare those who have defiled the earth with innocent blood.</p>

<p class="v">23. His wrath has spread like a fire; it has consumed the earth even to its foundations, and sinners have become like burnt straw.</p>

<p class="v">24. Woe to those who sin and who do not observe my commandments, says the Lord!</p>

<p class="v">25. I will not forgive them; and you who are my children, separate yourselves from the wicked, and do not profane the holiness of my name as they do.</p>

<p class="v">26. For the Lord knows those who offend him, and he shall deliver them to death and to slaughter.</p>

<p class="v">27. Evils have already spread over the earth; you shall all experience them, and the Lord shall not shield you from them, because you have offended him.</p>

<p class="v">28. In that time, dreadful things shall be seen, and they shall begin to appear from the direction of the East.</p>

<p class="v">29. There shall come from Arabia troops of dragons borne upon many chariots; they shall spread over the earth with as much speed as the wind, and at the noise of their arrival, fear and terror shall seize all minds.</p>

<p class="v">30. The peoples of Carmos, rousing themselves to anger, shall advance against them with impetuosity, like wild boars rushing out of the forest; they shall present themselves to fight them, and shall ravage part of Assyria.</p>

<p class="v">31. But the dragons, recalling at last the greatness of their origin, shall regain the upper hand and unite all their forces to pursue them.</p>

<p class="v">32. Then these peoples shall be troubled, and not daring to present themselves before such power, they shall seek safety in flight.</p>

<p class="v">33. A warrior shall attack them in Assyria, and the defeat of one of their own shall spread terror through their army, and shall set division among the chiefs.</p>

<p class="v">34. Clouds shall form from the east and the north as far as the south; they shall be dreadful, and shall carry everywhere the horror of the tempest.</p>

<p class="v">35. Clashing against one another, they shall cast down a great number of stars, and shall drag along with them also the fatal star that they carried in their midst. In the general slaughter that shall take place, then men shall be in blood up to the waist.</p>

<p class="v">36. And the corruption that shall come out of their bodies shall rise as high as the girths of the camels; the whole earth shall be in great consternation.</p>

<p class="v">37. Those who see that day of wrath shall be seized with horror, and fear shall take hold of their minds.</p>

<p class="v">38. Then many clouds shall come from the south and the north, and others shall appear from the west.</p>

<p class="v">39. But winds stirred up from the east shall disperse these last, as well as the cloud that bore the tempest, and the star that was to put to flight the winds of the East and the West shall be darkened.</p>

<p class="v">40. Then these great clouds, followed by the star, shall rise up with force and with fury; they shall cast terror over the whole earth and over those who dwell in it, and shall pour out over all high places that baleful star.</p>

<p class="v">41. And out of its midst shall come fire, hail, flying swords, torrents which, swelling the rivers, shall go and flood all the countryside.</p>

<p class="v">42. They shall overthrow the cities with their walls, they shall sweep along in their course the mountains, the hills, the forests, and all the fruits of the earth.</p>

<p class="v">43. They shall go without hindrance to carry terror as far as Babylon.</p>

<p class="v">44. And approaching its walls, they shall surround it, and shall pour out upon that city the star and all the fury and malice it contained; at once the sky shall grow dark with the dust and smoke that shall rise from its ruins; the neighboring peoples shall weep for its loss.</p>

<p class="v">45. And those who shall have remained within its walls shall pass under the dominion of the conquerors.</p>

<p class="v">46. And you, wretched Asia, who founded all your hopes upon Babylon, and who had made her the glory and foremost city of your empire,</p>

<p class="v">47. Woe to you, because you have imitated her, and have furnished your daughters with allurements for crime, so that they might please those who loved them, and glory in their number among those who have not ceased to burn for you with a criminal love!</p>

<p class="v">48. You have imitated that abominable city in all her works, in all her excesses; therefore, says the Lord,</p>

<p class="v">49. I will send all evils against you: widowhood, misery, famine, the sword, and pestilence, to lay waste your houses through dishonor, through death, and through the abasement of your power.</p>

<p class="v">50. Your glory shall wither like a flower, when the heat that must consume you appears.</p>

<p class="v">51. These great ones of the earth who had loved you with such passion shall no longer wish to have dealings with you, when they see you like one of those women whom misery exposes to contempt and insult.</p>

<p class="v">52. Would I have treated you thus in the full extent of my fury,</p>

<p class="v">53. If you had not cruelly slain my elect at all times, and if, after having become drunk with their blood, you had not still insulted those innocent victims?</p>

<p class="v">54. Gather, then, upon yourself all the allurements you can have,</p>

<p class="v">55. For you are near to receiving the reward of your shameful excesses.</p>

<p class="v">56. As you have treated my elect, so will I treat you, says the Lord, and I will overwhelm you with evils.</p>

<p class="v">57. Your children shall perish by famine, and you by the sword; your cities shall be destroyed.</p>

<p class="v">58. Those of yours who shall be found in the countryside shall fall by the sword, and those who flee into the mountains shall die of hunger; and in the extremity to which hunger and thirst shall reduce them, they shall eat their own flesh and drink their own blood.</p>

<p class="v">59. In this dreadful plight, you shall seek refuge beyond the seas; but it shall only be to be delivered over to new misfortunes.</p>

<p class="v">60. Your enemies shall throw themselves upon you, they shall break you anew, they shall ravage your empire, they shall make part of your glory vanish, and shall return to Babylon.</p>

<p class="v">61. And when you have been demolished, you shall serve them to kindle their fire.</p>

<p class="v">62. They shall devour you, your cities, your provinces, your mountains, and they shall set fire to your forests and to all your fruit trees.</p>

<p class="v">63. They shall lead your children into captivity, they shall plunder your riches, and they shall efface the brightness of your beauty.</p>

### Chapter 16 <span class="chap-roman">(XVI)</span> {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Woe to you, Babylon and Asia; woe to you, Egypt and Syria!</p>

<p class="v">2. Clothe yourselves with sackcloth and hair shirts, give yourselves over to grief, and weep for the loss of your children, for you are about to be destroyed.</p>

<p class="v">3. The sword has been sent against you; who shall escape it?</p>

<p class="v">4. Fire has been kindled against you; who shall put it out?</p>

<p class="v">5. All evils at last are going to fall upon you; who shall be able to guard against them?</p>

<p class="v">6. Who could defend himself in the forest against a lion driven by hunger, and who could put out the fire that begins to catch in the straw?</p>

<p class="v">7. Who, in short, could turn back an arrow shot by a strong and mighty arm?</p>

<p class="v">8. It is the Lord almighty who shall send these evils; who shall be able to avoid them?</p>

<p class="v">9. Fire shall be kindled in his wrath; who shall be able to put it out?</p>

<p class="v">10. The lightnings furrow the air; who shall not tremble? He shall make the voice of his thunder heard; who shall not be terrified by it?</p>

<p class="v">11. He shall threaten; who shall not be broken by his fury?</p>

<p class="v">12. The earth has trembled even to its foundations, the sea has been troubled, and from the depths of the abysses the waves have risen up; the fish it contains could not endure the gaze of the Lord, nor his fearsome power.</p>

<p class="v">13. For the right hand of him who has bent his bow is strong; the arrows he shoots are sharp, and they shall not lose their force once he has begun to pour them out upon the earth.</p>

<p class="v">14. Evils are going to flood it, and they shall not cease to afflict it.</p>

<p class="v">15. Fire has been kindled, and it shall not go out until it has consumed it even to its foundations.</p>

<p class="v">16. And the evils that shall lay it waste shall be like an arrow shot with force, which does not return to him who shot it.</p>

<p class="v">17. Woe is me, woe is me; who shall be my support in these days of calamity?</p>

<p class="v">18. This shall be the beginning of sorrows, and of the most dreadful groanings, of famine and a general death. Wars shall begin, and the powers shall be troubled by them; calamities shall follow in their train, and terror shall be universal.</p>

<p class="v">19. What shall become of me then, in the midst of all these evils?</p>

<p class="v">20. Famine, slaughter, oppressions, calamities were so many scourges meant to bring men back to their duty.</p>

<p class="v">21. But all these blows shall strike in vain, and nothing shall be able to tear them away from iniquity.</p>

<p class="v">22. In that time, everything shall sell at so low a price that they shall imagine themselves in a profound peace; but it shall be then that the sword, famine, disorder, and all the other evils shall rise up against them.</p>

<p class="v">23. The earth shall see a great number of its inhabitants perish by famine, and those who escape that kind of death shall fall beneath the edge of the sword.</p>

<p class="v">24. The dead bodies shall be thrown out as one throws out dung, and no one shall render them the last rites; the earth shall be a desert, the cities shall be buried beneath their ruins.</p>

<p class="v">25. And there shall remain no man to till the earth and cast seed upon it,</p>

<p class="v">26. The trees shall bear their fruit, and no one shall gather it.</p>

<p class="v">27. The grape shall come to its ripeness, and it shall not be trodden in the vat, because there shall be few people left on the earth.</p>

<p class="v">28. A man shall wish to see another man, or to hear his voice.</p>

<p class="v">29. There shall remain only ten men in a city, and only two in a field; and even that only after they have hidden themselves in dense forests and in the hollows of rocks.</p>

<p class="v">30. And just as only three or four olives remain on an olive tree,</p>

<p class="v">31. And as one scarcely finds a few clusters in a vineyard after a thorough harvest,</p>

<p class="v">32. So, in those unhappy days, scarcely three or four men shall escape the fury of those who shall come, weapons in hand, to plunder houses.</p>

<p class="v">33. The earth shall be changed into a wilderness, its fields shall become barren, all its paths and all its roads shall be covered with thorns and brambles, because no one shall pass through them any more.</p>

<p class="v">34. The virgins shall weep because they shall have no husbands; the women shall weep because they shall have no husbands, and the young girls shall give themselves over to groaning, because they shall remain without support.</p>

<p class="v">35. For their husbands shall perish in war, and famine shall consume their husbands.</p>

<p class="v">36. You who are the servants of the Lord, listen to these things and be instructed by them.</p>

<p class="v">37. Here is what the Lord says: listen to him, and do not put your faith in those gods of which he has told you:</p>

<p class="v">38. Behold, the evils are approaching, and they shall not delay.</p>

<p class="v">39. For just as a woman, in the ninth month of her pregnancy, two or three hours before giving birth, begins to feel the approach of her labor, and at the moment of childbirth is suddenly overwhelmed with the sharpest pains,</p>

<p class="v">40. So shall the evils hasten to spread over the earth; the age shall be in groaning, and evils shall overwhelm it from every side.</p>

<p class="v">41. You who are my people, listen to my words, prepare yourselves for battle, and conduct yourselves amid these calamities like a man who finds himself in a foreign land.</p>

<p class="v">42. Let him who sells do so as one soon to depart; let him who buys do so as one about to lose.</p>

<p class="v">43. Let him who trades do so as one who shall draw no profit from it; let him who builds a house do so as one who shall not dwell in it.</p>

<p class="v">44. Let him who sows do so as one who shall not reap; let him who tends his vineyard do so as one who shall not gather its harvest.</p>

<p class="v">45. Let him who marries do so as one who shall have no children, and let him who remains unmarried be as one who has become a widower.</p>

<p class="v">46. For those who labor shall then see the vanity of their labors.</p>

<p class="v">47. Strangers shall reap the grain they have sown, they shall carry off all they possess, and after having overthrown their houses, they shall lead their children away into captivity; because these unhappy fathers brought them into the world only at a time when they were to see them perish by famine or by captivity.</p>

<p class="v">48. As for those who enrich themselves by plunder, the more they labor at the embellishment of their cities, their houses, their lands, and their own persons,</p>

<p class="v">49. The more I will stir up my anger to avenge myself of their crimes, says the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">50. Just as a harlot burns with jealousy against a chaste and lawfully wedded woman,</p>

<p class="v">51. so shall justice rise up against injustice, which adorns itself with a false splendor, and shall reproach it to its face for its disorders, when he who must destroy the author of all sin upon the earth shall have come.</p>

<p class="v">52. Therefore do not make yourselves like him, and do not imitate his works.</p>

<p class="v">53. For a little more time shall pass, and then iniquity shall be banished from the earth, and justice shall reign over you.</p>

<p class="v">54. Let not the sinner say that he has not sinned; for coals of fire shall be kindled upon the head of him who says: I have not sinned against the Lord, nor against the holiness of his name.</p>

<p class="v">55. The Lord knows all the actions of men, their desires, their thoughts, and the deepest recesses of their heart.</p>

<p class="v">56. For it is he who said: Let the earth be made, and it was made; let the heavens be made, and they were made.</p>

<p class="v">57. The stars were created by his word, and he knows their number.</p>

<p class="v">58. He fathoms the depths, even to their most hidden places; he has measured the sea, and all the space it contains.</p>

<p class="v">59. He has placed the sea in the midst of the waters, and by his word he has surrounded the earth with that element.</p>

<p class="v">60. He has stretched out the heavens like a vault, he has raised it above the waters.</p>

<p class="v">61. He has made springs flow in the desert, he has formed reservoirs on the tops of the mountains, so that rivers might fall from the highest rocks to water the earth with their waters.</p>

<p class="v">62. He has made man, he has set the heart in the midst of the body, he has given him motion, life, understanding, and the breath of God almighty.</p>

<p class="v">63. He has created all things, and he uncovers what is most hidden in the caverns of the earth.</p>

<p class="v">64. He knows the movements and the thoughts of your hearts, even at the very time when you think you are hiding from his eyes in order to commit iniquity.</p>

<p class="v">65. The Lord has made an exact examination of all your works; he shall uncover the whole enormity of them,</p>

<p class="v">66. And you shall be covered with confusion on the last day, when your crimes shall be unveiled before the face of the whole earth, and your sins shall rise up against you and become your accusers.</p>

<p class="v">67. What will you do then, and how will you hide them from the eyes of God and of his angels?</p>

<p class="v">68. It is God himself who shall judge you: be seized with fear; cease to offend him, and renounce at last the corruption of your ways; then God shall be your refuge, and he shall deliver you from all these tribulations.</p>

<p class="v">69. A great multitude shall throw itself upon you with fury; they shall seize some of you, and after having slaughtered them, they shall present their flesh to their idols.</p>

<p class="v">70. They shall insult those who</p>

<p class="v">comply with their desires, and after having made them the object of their mockery, they shall rise up against those who fear the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">71. For in every place and in every city they shall rise up against those who fear the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">72. And in the excess of their fury, they shall spare none of them, but throwing themselves upon them to plunder and outrage them,</p>

<p class="v">73. They shall seize all the riches they find in their houses, and drive out the masters of them.</p>

<p class="v">74. Then my elect shall be tested as gold is tested by fire.</p>

<p class="v">75. You who are my beloved, listen to me, says the Lord: these days of tribulation are near, but I will deliver you from them.</p>

<p class="v">76. Give yourselves over neither to fear nor to uncertainty about what shall happen to you, because God shall put himself at your head.</p>

<p class="v">77. And he shall protect those who keep his commandments. Do not let yourselves be overwhelmed by the weight of your sins, lest it crush you.</p>

<p class="v">78. Woe to those who are bound with the chains of their crimes, and who are clothed with their iniquities; for, like a field covered with a dense forest, and like a path full of thorns through which no one passes any more, they shall be torn up and cast into the fire.</p>
# Part Four <SEP> Psalm 151 & the Prayer of Manasseh

<p class="part-sub">Two short texts of the Ethiopian canon — translations collected by J.-P. Migne (1856)</p>

The Ethiopian psalter, like the Greek psalter, closes with a psalm "outside the number" in which David
tells of his election; its Hebrew original has since been recovered at Qumran. The Prayer of Manasseh,
for its part, at last gives the words of the penitent king whose prayer 2 Chronicles 33:18-19 mentions
without quoting it; Ethiopia reads it together with Paralipomenon.

### Psalm 151 {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">David against Goliath — a psalm preserved by the Greek and Ethiopian psalters</p>

<p class="v">1. I was small among my brothers, and the youngest in my father's house; I kept his sheep.</p>

<p class="v">2. My hands made an instrument, and my fingers tuned a psaltery.</p>

<p class="v">3. And whoever invokes the Lord, the Lord himself does not fail to hear him.</p>

<p class="v">4. He himself sent his angel; he drew me from my father's flocks and anointed me with the oil of his anointing.</p>

<p class="v">5. My brothers were handsome and tall; and the Lord took no pleasure in them.</p>

<p class="v">6. I went forth to meet the stranger; he cursed me by his idols.</p>

<p class="v">7. But I, having wrested his sword from him, cut off his head, and took away the reproach from the children of Israel.</p>

### Prayer of Manasseh {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">Prayer of Manasseh, king of Judah, at the time when he was a captive in Babylon</p>

<p class="v">1. Lord Almighty, God of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and of their holy race!</p>

<p class="v">2. You who created heaven and earth, and all that they contain!</p>

<p class="v">3. You who by your word set bounds to the sea, who closed up the abyss and sealed it with your terrible and adorable name!</p>

<p class="v">4. You before whom all creatures tremble, and whose power they dread, because they cannot endure either the splendor of your glory or the wrath with which you threaten sinners!</p>

<p class="v">5. Lord! the mercy you have promised us is infinite and beyond all that can be conceived.</p>

<p class="v">6. For you are the Lord, the Most High, good, patient, merciful, and ever ready to relent of the evils with which you have afflicted us.</p>

<p class="v">7. You have promised to receive sinners unto repentance, and to save them in your infinite mercy.</p>

<p class="v">8. You, then, Lord! God of the righteous! it is neither to Abraham, nor to Isaac, nor to Jacob that you have commanded repentance; they did not offend you.</p>

<p class="v">9. But to me, who am a sinner, since the number of my crimes equals that of the sands of the sea.</p>

<p class="v">10. Lord! my iniquities have multiplied, they have increased, and I am not worthy to lift my eyes toward heaven.</p>

<p class="v">11. I am so bowed beneath the weight of my chains that it is impossible for me to raise my head, and there is no breath left in me.</p>

<p class="v">12. Because I have provoked your wrath and have done evil in your presence:</p>

<p class="v">13. I have been rebellious against your will and have not kept your commandments:</p>

<p class="v">14. I have brought shameful abominations into Israel, and my crimes have multiplied.</p>

<p class="v">15. But now I bend my knees in the bitterness of my heart and implore your goodness.</p>

<p class="v">16. I have sinned, Lord, and I acknowledge my iniquities. Therefore, Lord, I beseech you with the most fervent prayers to forgive them me, and not to destroy me by punishing them.</p>

<p class="v">17. Do not reserve me for eternal torments, and do not banish me to the depths of the earth, for you are the God of penitent sinners.</p>

<p class="v">18. You will make all your goodness shine forth upon me, saving me by your infinite mercy, unworthy as I am of it.</p>

<p class="v">19. And I will praise you all the days of my life, since all the powers of heaven make your praises resound, and glory belongs to you unto all ages of ages. So be it.</p>

# Part Five <SEP> The Deuterocanonical Books

<p class="part-sub">Books shared with the Catholic and Orthodox Bibles — translation by Canon A. Crampon (1923)</p>

The following books are fully part of the Ethiopian canon, as they are of the Catholic canon; they are,
however, absent from the 66-book Protestant Bibles. They are given here in the classic French translation
by Canon Augustin Crampon (1923 edition), made from the original texts. For Esther, only the Greek
additions (chapters 10 to 16 of the Vulgate) are reproduced; for Daniel, the three Greek additions are
given in their traditional place: the Song of the Three Young Men (Daniel 3:24-90), the Story of Susanna
(Daniel 13), and Bel and the Dragon (Daniel 14).

<p class="footer-note">A specialist's nuance: for Tobit and Judith, Crampon translates the Latin Vulgate, whereas
the Ethiopian Bible follows the Greek text; the narrative is the same, though the letter sometimes differs.</p>

## Tobit {: .book}

<p class="chap-sub">The story of the righteous exile who became blind, of his son Tobit guided by the angel Raphael, of Sarah delivered from the demon, and of the fish whose gall restores sight. One of the most beautiful accounts of Jewish family piety.</p>

### Chapter 1 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Tobit, of the tribe and a city of Naphtali, which is in Upper Galilee, above Naasson, behind the road that goes toward the west, having on its left the city of Sephet, 2. was carried away captive in the time of Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians; and, even in his captivity, he did not abandon the way of truth. 3. Every day he distributed to his brethren, those of his nation, captives like himself, all that he had at his disposal.</p>

<p class="v">4. And even though he was the youngest of those of the tribe of Naphtali, there was nothing youthful in his conduct. 5. So, while everyone else went to worship the golden calves that Jeroboam, king of Israel, had made, he alone fled the company of all, 6. and he would go to Jerusalem, to the temple of the Lord, where he worshiped the Lord, God of Israel, faithfully offering the firstfruits and the tithes of his goods. 7. Every third year, he distributed his whole tithe to proselytes and strangers. 8. He observed these and similar things, according to the law of God, from his youth. 9. Having come to manhood, he married a woman of his tribe, named Anna; and he had by her a son, to whom he gave his own name, 10. and whom he taught from childhood to fear God and to abstain from all sin.</p>

<p class="v">11. So when he arrived as a captive, with his wife and his son, in the city of Nineveh, where his whole tribe was, 12. although all the others ate of the food of the pagans, he kept his soul pure, and never defiled himself with their meats. 13. And because he faithfully remembered the Lord, God won for him the favor of King Shalmaneser, 14. who gave him leave to go wherever he wished, with freedom to do as he pleased. 15. He would therefore go and visit all who were captive, and give them wholesome counsel.</p>

<p class="v">16. Having once gone to Rages, a city of the Medes, with ten talents, from the bounty with which the king had enriched him, 17. he saw, among the great number of his countrymen, a man of his tribe, named Gabael, who was in need, and he gave him this sum of money against a receipt.</p>

<p class="v">18. Long afterward, King Shalmaneser having died, Sennacherib, his son, reigned in his place. As this prince held a great hatred for the children of Israel, 19. Tobit would go every day to visit all his kinsfolk; he comforted them and distributed, to each according to his means, of his own goods; 20. he gave food to those who were hungry, procured clothing for those who were naked, and took great pains to give burial to those who had died or been slain. 21. When King Sennacherib, having returned from Judea in flight after the defeat with which God had struck him for his blasphemies, was in his fury putting to death a great number of the children of Israel, Tobit buried the bodies. 22. Word of this having been brought to the king, he ordered him put to death and took away all his goods. 23. But Tobit fled with his son and his wife, and, stripped of everything, he managed to hide, because he had many friends. 24. Forty-five days later, the king was killed by his own sons. 25. Then Tobit returned to his house, and all his goods were restored to him.</p>

### Chapter 2 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. After this, a feast of the Lord having come, and a great meal having been prepared in Tobit's house, 2. he said to his son: "Go and bring some men of our tribe, who fear God, that they may eat with us." 3. His son went out; on his return, he told him that one of the children of Israel, who had been murdered, lay in the street. At once Tobit rose from the table and, leaving the meal without having eaten anything, went to the body, 4. took it up and carried it secretly to his house, so as to bury it with care after sunset. 5. When he had hidden it, he took his meal with tears and trembling, 6. remembering this word which the Lord had spoken through the prophet Amos: "Your feast days shall be turned into mourning and lamentation." 7. Then, when the sun had set, he went out and laid the body in the earth. 8. All his neighbors blamed him, saying: "You have already been ordered put to death for this very thing, and scarcely have you escaped that sentence of death, than you begin again to bury the dead!" 9. But Tobit, fearing God more than the king, would take away the bodies of those who had been slain, hide them in his house, and bury them at night.</p>

<p class="v">10. One day, having worn himself out giving burial to the dead, he returned to his house, threw himself down at the foot of the wall, and fell asleep. 11. While he slept, warm droppings fell upon his eyes from a swallow's nest, and he became blind. 12. God allowed this trial to befall him, so that his patience, like that of the holy man Job, might be given as an example to posterity. 13. For, having always feared God from his childhood and kept his commandments, he did not grow bitter against God because the misfortune of blindness had come upon him. 14. But he remained unshaken in the fear of God, giving him thanks all the days of his life.</p>

<p class="v">15. Just as the tribal chiefs insulted blessed Job, so the relatives and friends of Tobit mocked his conduct, saying: 16. "What has become of your hope, for which you gave alms and buried the dead?" 17. Tobit rebuked them, saying: "Do not speak so; 18. for we are children of the saints, and we await that life which God is to give to those who never withdraw their faithfulness from him."</p>

<p class="v">19. Anna, his wife, went every day to weave cloth and, by the work of her hands, brought home, for their support, whatever she could earn. 20. It happened that, having received a young goat, she brought it home. 21. Her husband, having heard the goat bleating, said: "See whether this goat has not been stolen, and give it back to its owner, for we are not permitted to eat anything that comes from theft, nor even to touch it." 22. Then his wife answered angrily: "It is plain that your hope has come to nothing; this is what your almsgiving has brought you!" 23. It was with these words, and others like them, that she reviled him.</p>

### Chapter 3 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Then Tobit, having heaved a sigh, began to pray with tears, 2. saying: "You are righteous, Lord; righteous are all your judgments, and all your ways are mercy, truth, and justice. 3. And now, Lord, remember me; do not take vengeance for my sins, and do not call to mind my offenses, or those of my forefathers. 4. For we have not obeyed your precepts; that is why we have been given over to plunder, to captivity, to death, to mockery, and to reproach among all the nations among whom you have scattered us. 5. And now, Lord, your chastisements are great, because we have not acted according to your precepts and have not walked sincerely before you. 6. And now, Lord, deal with me according to your will, and command that my spirit be received in peace, for it is better for me to die than to live."</p>

<p class="v">7. It happened on that same day, at Ecbatana, city of the Medes, that Sarah, daughter of Raguel, likewise heard the taunts of one of her father's maidservants. 8. For she had been given in marriage, one after another, to seven husbands, and a demon, named Asmodeus, had killed them as soon as they came near her. 9. As she was rebuking this servant for some fault, the servant answered her, saying: "May we never see on earth son or daughter of yours, murderess of your husbands! 10. Do you want to put me to death too, as you have already caused the death of seven husbands?" At these words, Sarah went up to the upper chamber of her house and stayed there three days and three nights, without eating or drinking. 11. But, persevering in prayer, she besought God with tears to deliver her from this reproach.</p>

<p class="v">12. On the third day, she finished her prayer and blessed the Lord, 13. saying: "Blessed be your name, O God of our fathers, who, even when you are angered, show mercy, and who, in the time of tribulation, forgive the sins of those who call upon you. 14. Toward you, Lord, I turn my face; toward you I lift up my eyes. 15. I ask you, Lord, to deliver me from the bonds of this reproach; or else, to take me from this earth. 16. You know, Lord, that I have never desired a husband, and that I have kept my soul pure of all lust. 17. Never have I frequented frivolous amusements, nor had dealings with men of light conduct. 18. It was in your fear, and not to follow my own passion, that I consented to take a husband. 19. Either I was not worthy of them, or perhaps they were not worthy of me, for it may be that you have kept me for another husband. 20. It is not within man's power to penetrate your designs. 21. But whoever honors you may be assured that his life, if it has been in trial, will be crowned; that if he has been in tribulation, he will be delivered; and that if chastisement has come upon him, he may obtain your mercy. 22. For you take no pleasure in our ruin, but after the storm you bring back the calm, and after weeping and tears you pour out joy. 23. May your name, God of Israel, be blessed throughout all ages!"</p>

<p class="v">24. These two supplications were heard at the same time before the glory of the sovereign God; 25. and the holy angel of the Lord, Raphael, was sent to heal Tobit and Sarah, whose prayers had been uttered at the same time in the presence of the Lord.</p>

### Chapter 4 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Tobit, believing that his prayer had been heard and that he was going to die, called to him Tobit, his son, 2. and said to him: "Listen, my son, to the words of my mouth, and lay them as a firm foundation in your heart. 3. When God has received my soul, lay my body in the earth. You shall honor your mother all the days of her life; 4. for you must remember what she suffered and the great dangers she ran for your sake, when she carried you in her womb. 5. And when she too has completed the span of her life, you shall bury her beside me. 6. All the days of your life, keep God present in your thoughts, and take care never to consent to sin or to transgress the precepts of the Lord your God. 7. Give alms from your goods, and never turn your face away from any poor man; for it will then come to pass that the face of God will not turn away from you. 8. In whatever way you are able, be merciful. 9. If you have much, give generously; if you have little, take care to share even that little with a good heart. 10. Thus you will lay up for yourself a great treasure for the day of need. 11. For almsgiving delivers from all sin and from death, and it will not let the soul go down into darkness. 12. Almsgiving will be, for all who have practiced it, a great ground of confidence before the sovereign God. 13. Keep yourself, my son, from all impurity, and apart from your own wife let your conscience never reproach you with a criminal act. 14. Never let pride rule in your heart or in your words, for it is from pride that all evils have taken their beginning. 15. When a man has done work for you, pay him his wages at once, and do not let the hired man's wages remain with you even an instant. 16. Whatever you would be angry to have done to you, take care never to do to another. 17. Eat your bread with those who are hungry and with the needy, and clothe the naked with your garments. 18. Let your bread and your wine be used to honor the burial of the righteous, but do not eat or drink it with sinners. 19. Always seek counsel from a wise man. 20. Bless God at all times; ask him to direct your ways, and that all your plans may succeed through him. 21. I also inform you, my son, that when you were still a small child, I gave ten talents of silver to Gabael of Rages, a city of the Medes, and that I have his receipt in my hands. 22. Therefore make haste to go and find him and recover this sum of money, and you will return to him his bond. 23. Have no fear, my son. It is true that we lead a poor life, but we shall have great wealth if we fear God, if we avoid all sin, and if we do good works.</p>

### Chapter 5 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Then Tobit answered his father, saying: "All that you have commanded me, I will do, my father. 2. But I do not know how I shall be able to recover this money. This man does not know me, and he is likewise unknown to me; what token shall I give him? I do not even know the road that leads to that country." 3. His father answered him, saying: "I have his bond in my hands; as soon as you have shown it to him, he will repay you. 4. But go now and find a trustworthy man to go with you, for a wage, so that you may come into possession of this money while I am still living."</p>

<p class="v">5. Tobit, having gone out, found a handsome young man, standing girded, as if ready to set out on a journey. 6. Not knowing that this was an angel of God, he greeted him and said: "Where are you from, good young man?" 7. The angel answered: "I am one of the children of Israel." And Tobit said to him: "Do you know the road that leads to the country of the Medes?" 8. He answered him: "I know it; I have often traveled all these roads, and I have lodged with Gabael, our brother, who lives at Rages, a city of the Medes, which is situated in the mountains of Ecbatana." 9. Tobit said to him: "Wait for me, I beg you, until I have told this to my father."</p>

<p class="v">10. Then Tobit, having gone back in, told his father everything. At this the father, filled with wonder, asked that the young man be brought in. 11. He came in and greeted them, saying: "May joy be with you always!" — 12. "What joy can I have," answered Tobit, "I who sit in darkness and do not see the light of heaven?" 13. The young man said to him: "Take courage! It is easy for God to heal you." 14. Then Tobit said to him: "Could you indeed lead my son to Gabael, at Rages, city of the Medes? On your return, I will give you your wage." — 15. "I will lead him," answered the angel, "and I will bring him back to you." 16. Tobit said to him: "Tell me, I beg you, of what family and of what tribe you are?" 17. The angel Raphael answered him: "Is it the family of the hired man you seek, or the hired man himself, who is to accompany your son? 18. But so as not to leave you uneasy, I am Azarias, son of the great Ananias." 19. "You are of a noble race," Tobit said to him. "But do not be angry, I beg you, that I desired to know your family." 20. And the angel said to him: "I will lead your son safe and sound, and I will bring him back to you safe and sound." 21. Tobit added: "Have a happy journey! May God be on your road, and may his angel accompany you!"</p>

<p class="v">22. When everything they were to take on the journey had been prepared, Tobit bade farewell to his father and his mother, and set out on the road with the angel.</p>

<p class="v">23. When they had gone, the mother began to weep, saying: "You have taken from us the staff of our old age, and you have sent it away from us. 24. Would to God that this money, for which you sent him, had never existed! 25. For our poverty was enough for us, and it was riches to us to see our son." 26. Tobit answered her: "Do not weep; our son will arrive safe and sound, and he will return to us safe and sound, and your eyes will see him again. 27. For I believe that a good angel of God accompanies him, and orders happily all that befalls him, so that he will come back to us with joy." 28. At these words, his mother ceased weeping and was silent.</p>

### Chapter 6 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Tobit set out, followed by the dog, and made his first halt near the river Tigris. 2. As he went down to the bank to wash his feet, behold, an enormous fish leapt up to devour him. 3. Frightened, Tobit gave a great cry, saying: "Lord, it is throwing itself upon me!" 4. The angel said to him: "Take it by the gills and draw it to yourself." Having done this, he drew it onto the dry land, and the fish thrashed about at his feet. 5. The angel said to him: "Gut this fish, and keep its heart, its gall, and its liver, for they are used as useful remedies." 6. He obeyed; then he roasted part of the flesh, which they took with them for the journey; they salted the rest, which was to suffice them until they arrived at Rages, city of the Medes. 7. And Tobit questioned the angel, saying: "I beg you, Azarias my brother, to tell me what curative power the parts of this fish possess, which you commanded me to keep." 8. The angel answered him: "If you place a small part of the heart on coals, the smoke that rises from it drives away every kind of demon, whether from a man or a woman, so that they can no longer come near. 9. And the gall serves to anoint eyes covered with a cataract, and it heals them."</p>

<p class="v">10. Tobit said to him: "Where do you want us to take our rest?" 11. The angel answered him: "There is here a man called Raguel, of your tribe and your family; he has a daughter named Sarah, but besides her he has no other child, son or daughter. 12. All his goods are to come to you, and you must take her for a wife. 13. Ask her, then, of her father, and he will give her to you as wife." 14. Then Tobit answered: "I have heard it said that she has already had seven husbands, and that they are all dead, and I have also been told that a demon killed them. 15. I fear, therefore, that the same thing may happen to me also, and that, being my parents' only son, I might bring their old age down to the grave in sorrow." 16. And the angel Raphael said to him: "Listen to me, and I will teach you who those are over whom the demon has power. 17. They are those who enter into marriage banishing God from their heart and their thoughts, to give themselves up to their passion, like the horse and the mule that have no reason: over these the demon has power. 18. But you, when you have married her, having entered the chamber, live with her in continence for three days, and think of nothing else but praying to God with her. 19. On the first night, give the fish's liver to the fire, and the demon will flee. 20. On the second night, you will be admitted into the fellowship of the holy patriarchs. 21. On the third night, you will receive the blessing promised to their posterity, so that vigorous children may be born of you. 22. When the third night is past, you shall take the young woman in the fear of the Lord, guided far more by the desire to have children than by passion, so that you may obtain in your children the blessing promised to the race of Abraham."</p>

### Chapter 7 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. They entered the house of Raguel, who received them with joy. 2. At the sight of Tobit, Raguel said to Anna, his wife: "How this young man resembles my cousin!" 3. Having spoken thus, he said to the travelers: "Where are you from, young men, our brothers?" They answered: "We are of the tribe of Naphtali, among the captives of Nineveh." 4. Raguel said to them: "Do you know Tobit, my brother?" — "We know him," they answered. 5. And as Raguel was speaking very highly of Tobit, the angel said to him: "Tobit, of whom you speak to us, is the father of this young man." 6. At once Raguel ran to him and embraced him with tears, weeping upon his neck. 7. "Blessed be you, my son," he said, "for you are the son of a good man, of the best of men!" 8. And Anna, his wife, and Sarah, their daughter, wept.</p>

<p class="v">9. After they had thus spoken together, Raguel had a ram killed and a feast prepared; and, as he was pressing them to sit down to the meal, 10. Tobit said: "I will neither eat nor drink here today, unless you first grant my request, and promise to give me Sarah, your daughter." 11. On hearing these words, Raguel was seized with fear, knowing what had happened to the seven husbands who had approached her, and he began to fear that a like misfortune might again befall this one. While he was in this uncertainty and gave no answer to Tobit's request, 12. the angel said to him: "Do not be afraid to give your daughter to this young man; for it is to him, who fears God, that she is to belong as wife; that is why no other has been able to possess her." 13. Then Raguel said: "I do not doubt that God has admitted my prayers and my tears into his presence. 14. And I believe that he has brought you to me, that my daughter might marry her kinsman, according to the law of Moses. Have no more doubt, then, that I give her to you." 15. And taking his daughter's right hand, he placed it in Tobit's right hand, saying: "May the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob be with you; may he himself unite you, and pour out upon you his full blessing!" 16. Then, having taken paper, they drew up the marriage contract. 17. After which they took part in the feast, blessing God.</p>

<p class="v">18. Raguel called Anna, his wife, and ordered her to prepare another room. 19. She led Sarah, her daughter, there, who began to weep. 20. And she said to her: "Take courage, my daughter. May the Lord of heaven give you joy in place of the sorrow you have felt!"</p>

### Chapter 8 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. The meal ended, they led the young man to Sarah. 2. Tobit, remembering the angel's words, drew from his bag a part of the liver and laid it on burning coals. 3. Then the angel Raphael seized the demon and bound him in the desert of Upper Egypt.</p>

<p class="v">4. And Tobit exhorted the young woman, saying to her: "Sarah, arise, and let us pray to God today, tomorrow, and the day after; during these three nights we shall be united to God, and, after the third night, we shall live in our marriage. 5. For we are children of the saints, and we cannot unite as the nations do who do not know God." 6. Having therefore risen together, they both prayed earnestly to God to grant them health. 7. Tobit said: "Lord, God of our fathers, may heaven and earth, may the sea, the springs and the rivers, with all your creatures that they contain, bless you! 8. You made Adam from the slime of the earth, and you gave him Eve as a companion. 9. And now, Lord, you know that it is not to satisfy my passion that I take my sister for a wife, but from the sole desire to leave children who will bless your name throughout all ages." 10. Sarah also said: "Have pity on us, Lord, have pity on us, and may we both together come to old age in perfect health!"</p>

<p class="v">11. At the hour of cockcrow, Raguel ordered his servants to be brought, and they went with him to dig a grave. 12. For he said: "The same thing may well have happened to him as to the seven other husbands who went in to her." 13. When they had prepared the grave, Raguel went back to his wife and said to her: 14. "Send one of your maidservants to see whether he is dead, so that I may bury him before it is day." 15. Anna sent one of her maidservants. She, having entered the room, found them both safe and sound, likewise asleep. 16. Having returned, she announced this good news; and Raguel and Anna, his wife, blessed the Lord, 17. saying: "We bless you, Lord, God of Israel, for the misfortune we dreaded has not happened. 18. You have dealt with us in mercy, and you have driven away from us the enemy who was persecuting us. 19. You have had pity on two only children. Grant, Lord, that they may bless you more and more, and that they may offer you a sacrifice of praise for their preservation, so that all the nations may know that you alone are God over all the earth."</p>

<p class="v">20. At once Raguel ordered his servants to fill in, before daylight, the grave they had made. 21. And he told his wife to prepare a feast and to arrange everything travelers would need for their sustenance. 22. He also had two fatted cows and four rams killed, to prepare a meal for all his neighbors and all his friends. 23. And Raguel urged Tobit to remain with him for two weeks. 24. Raguel gave Tobit half of all he possessed, and he drew up a document so that the half remaining should become Tobit's property after their death.</p>

### Chapter 9 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Then Tobit called the angel to him, whom he believed to be a man, and said to him: "Azarias, my brother, I beg you to listen to my words. 2. Even were I to give myself to you as a slave, I would still not sufficiently acknowledge all your care. 3. Nevertheless I address this further request to you: Take with you beasts of burden and servants, and go find Gabael, at Rages, city of the Medes; you shall give him back his bond, you shall receive the money from him, and you shall ask him to come to my wedding. 4. For you know yourself that my father counts the days, and that, if I delay a single day more, his soul will be in sorrow. 5. You also see in what manner Raguel has urged me to stay here, and that I cannot resist his pressing entreaties."</p>

<p class="v">6. Then Raphael, taking four of Raguel's servants and two camels, went to Rages, city of the Medes. Having found Gabael, he gave him back his note and received from him all the money; 7. and, after telling him all that had happened to Tobit, son of Tobit, he brought him along with him to the wedding. 8. When Gabael entered the house of Raguel, he found Tobit at table; the latter rose at once; they kissed one another, and Gabael wept and blessed God, 9. saying: "May the God of Israel bless you, for you are the son of an excellent man, righteous and God-fearing, and giving much alms! 10. May the blessing also be poured out upon your wife and upon your kindred! 11. May you see your sons and the sons of your sons, to the third and fourth generation! May your posterity be blessed by the God of Israel, who reigns forever and ever!" 12. All having said: Amen! they sat down to table, and it was in the fear of God that they held the wedding feast.</p>

### Chapter 10 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. While Tobit was delaying his departure because of his wedding, his father Tobit was filled with worry: "What," he said to himself, "can be the cause of my son's delay? What reason can be keeping him in that country? 2. Could Gabael be dead, and is there no longer anyone to repay him this money?" 3. He therefore began to grieve greatly, he and Anna, his wife, and together they fell to weeping because their son had not returned to them on the appointed day. 4. His mother especially poured out unceasing tears: "Alas! alas! my son," she said, "why did we send you so far away, you who were the light of our eyes, the staff of our old age, the comfort of our life and the hope of our posterity? 5. We who had everything in you alone, we ought never to have sent you away from us." 6. Tobit would say to her: "Cease your complaints and do not be troubled; our son is well, and the man with whom we sent him is very trustworthy." 7. But nothing could console her; going out of her house every day, she looked in every direction, and went along every road by which there was hope that he might return, so as, if possible, to catch sight of him from afar.</p>

<p class="v">8. Meanwhile Raguel was saying to his son-in-law: "Stay here, and I will send news of your well-being to Tobit, your father." 9. Tobit answered him: "I know that my father and my mother count the days, and that their spirit is tormented within them." 10. After urging Tobit further at great length, without his being willing to hear any of his reasons, Raguel gave him Sarah, along with half of all he possessed, in menservants and maidservants, in flocks, in camels, in cattle, in money, of which he had much, and let him go, full of health and joy, 11. saying: "May the holy angel of the Lord be on your road, may he lead you home safe and sound; may you find everything prosperous with your parents, and may my eyes see your children before I die!" 12. And the father and the mother, taking their daughter, embraced her and let her go, 13. after charging her to honor her parents-in-law, to love her husband, to guide her household well, to govern her house, and to keep herself blameless.</p>

### Chapter 11 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. As they were returning, they arrived on the eleventh day at Charan, a city situated halfway to Nineveh. 2. And the angel said: "Tobit, my brother, you know in what condition you left your father. 3. If, then, you think it good, let us go on ahead, and let your servants follow by easy stages, with your wife and your flocks." 4. Tobit having approved this plan, Raphael said to him: "Take with you some of the fish's gall, for you will need it." Tobit took some of this gall, and they set out.</p>

<p class="v">5. Anna meanwhile went every day to sit by the road, on top of a hill, from where she could see far off. 6. And as she was watching from there for her son's arrival, she caught sight of him in the distance, returning, and, having recognized him, she ran to tell her husband, saying: "Here is your son coming."</p>

<p class="v">7. At the same time, Raphael said to Tobit: "When you have entered your house, worship the Lord your God at once, and give him thanks; then, going up to your father, you shall kiss him, 8. and you shall spread at once upon his eyes some of this fish's gall which you carry with you; for know that his eyes will open at once, and that your father will see the light of heaven, and that the sight of you will fill him with joy."</p>

<p class="v">9. Then the dog which had accompanied them on the journey ran ahead of them, as if to bring the news, wagging its tail and full of joy. 10. And the blind father rose and began to run, and, as he stumbled with his feet, he gave his hand to a servant to go to meet his son. 11. Taking him in his arms, he kissed him, as did his wife also, and both of them shed tears of joy.</p>

<p class="v">12. After they had worshiped God and given him thanks, they sat down. 13. At once Tobit, taking some of the fish's gall, spread it upon his father's eyes. 14. After about half an hour of waiting, a white film, like the skin of an egg, began to come out of his eyes. 15. Tobit seized it and pulled it away from his father's eyes, and at once the latter recovered his sight. 16. And they gave glory to God, he and his wife and all who knew him. 17. Tobit said: "I bless you, Lord, God of Israel, because you have chastised me and have healed me; and behold, I see my son Tobit!"</p>

<p class="v">18. Seven days later Sarah also arrived, his son's wife, with all her servants in good health, with the flocks and the camels, and all the money of her marriage settlement and that which Gabael had returned. 19. And Tobit told his parents all the benefits with which God had filled him through the man who had led him. 20. Achior and Nabath, kinsmen of Tobit, came to find him, full of joy, and congratulated him on all the good things God had done for him. 21. And for seven days, eating together, they gave themselves over to great rejoicing.</p>

### Chapter 12 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Then Tobit called his son to him and said to him: "What shall we give to this holy man who accompanied you on your journey?" 2. Tobit answered his father: "My father, what reward can we offer him? Is there anything commensurate with his services? 3. He led me and brought me back safe and sound; he himself went to receive the money from Gabael; he obtained for me a wife, from whom he drove away the demon, and he filled her parents with joy; he saved me myself from the fish that was about to devour me; he made you see the light of heaven, and through him we have been filled with every kind of good thing. What can we give him equal to what he has done for us? 4. But I beg you, my father, to ask him whether he would deign to accept half of all the goods we have brought back." 5. Having therefore called him, Tobit and his son took him aside, and asked him to be so good as to accept half of all they had brought back.</p>

<p class="v">6. Then the angel, alone with them, said to them: "Bless the God of heaven and give him glory before every living being, because he has shown you his mercy. 7. It is good to keep the king's secret hidden, but it is honorable to reveal and publish the works of God. 8. Prayer is good with fasting, and almsgiving is worth more than gold and treasures. 9. For almsgiving delivers from death, and it is what blots out sins and obtains mercy and eternal life. 10. But those who commit sin and iniquity are their own enemies. 11. I will therefore reveal the truth to you, and I do not wish to hide anything from you. 12. When you prayed with tears and gave burial to the dead; when, leaving your meal, you hid the dead in your house during the day and laid them in the earth during the night, I presented your prayer to the Lord. 13. And because you were pleasing to God, it was necessary that trial should test you. 14. Now the Lord has sent me to heal you, and to deliver Sarah, your son's wife, from the demon. 15. I am the angel Raphael, one of the seven who stand in the presence of the Lord."</p>

<p class="v">16. On hearing these words, they were beside themselves, and, trembling all over, fell with their faces to the ground. 17. And the angel said to them: "Peace be with you! Do not be afraid. 18. For when I was with you, I was there by the will of God; bless him, then, and sing his praises. 19. It seemed to you that I ate and drank with you; but I was nourished with invisible food and a drink that the eye of man cannot perceive. 20. It is time, then, for me to return to him who sent me; but you, bless God and publish all his wonders."</p>

<p class="v">21. After thus speaking, he was taken away from their sight, and they could see him no more. 22. Then, having prostrated themselves for three hours with their faces to the ground, they blessed God, and, having risen, they recounted all his wonders.</p>
### Chapter 13 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Old Tobit, opening his mouth, blessed the Lord, saying:</p>

<p class="v">"You are great, Lord, forever,<br/>and your reign extends through all ages.<br/>2. For you chastise and you save,<br/>you lead down to the grave and bring back again,<br/>and there is no one who can escape your hand.</p>

<p class="v">3. Praise the Lord, children of Israel,<br/>and glorify him before the nations.<br/>4.
