For he has scattered you among the nations that do not know him, that you may tell of his wonders, and make known to them<br/>that there is no other almighty God but him alone.<br/><br/>5. He has chastised us because of our iniquities,<br/>and he will save us because of his mercy.<br/>6. Consider how he has dealt with us,<br/>and bless him with fear and trembling,<br/>and glorify by your works the King of the ages.<br/><br/>7. As for me, I will bless him in this land where I am a captive,<br/>because he has displayed his glory upon a sinful nation.<br/>8. Be converted, then, sinners, and do justice before God,<br/>trusting that he will show you mercy!<br/>9. As for me, I will rejoice in him with all my soul.<br/><br/>10. Bless the Lord, all you who are his chosen people;<br/>keep days of joy and sing his praises!<br/><br/>11. Jerusalem, city of God, the Lord has chastised you for the works of your hands.<br/>12. Glorify the Lord by your good works, and bless the God of the ages,<br/>that he may rebuild in you his sanctuary,<br/>that he may call back to you all your captives,<br/>and that you may rejoice throughout all ages of ages.<br/><br/>13. You will shine with a dazzling light,<br/>and all the peoples of the earth will bow down before you.<br/>14. The nations will come to you from distant lands,<br/>bringing gifts; they will worship the Lord within your walls,<br/>and will regard your land as a sanctuary;<br/>15. for they will call upon the great Name in your midst.<br/><br/>16. Cursed will be those who despise you,<br/>condemned those who blaspheme you,<br/>blessed those who build you up.<br/>17. And you, you will rejoice in your children,<br/>because they will all be blessed and will gather together to the Lord.<br/>18. Happy are all who love you and who rejoice in your peace!<br/><br/>19. My soul, bless the Lord,<br/>because he has delivered Jerusalem, his city,<br/>from all her tribulations, he, the Lord, our God!<br/>20. Happy shall I be, if there remain any offspring of my race<br/>to see the splendor of Jerusalem!<br/><br/>21. The gates of Jerusalem will be built of sapphires and emeralds,<br/>and the whole circuit of her walls of precious stones.<br/>22. Stones of immaculate whiteness will form the pavement of her squares,<br/>and in her streets they will sing: Alleluia!<br/>23. Blessed be the Lord who has given this glory to Jerusalem,<br/>and may he reign over her forever and ever! Amen!"</p>

### Chapter 14 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Thus ended the words of Tobit. After he had recovered his sight, Tobit lived forty-two more years, and he saw the children of his grandchildren. 2. He lived in all a hundred and two years, and he was honorably buried at Nineveh. 3. For he was fifty-six years old when he lost his sight, and he recovered it at sixty. 4. All the rest of his life passed in joy, and the more he advanced in the fear of God, the more peace he tasted.</p>

<p class="v">5. At the hour of his death, he called to him Tobit, his son, and the latter's seven young sons, his grandsons, and he said to them:</p>

<p class="v">6. "The ruin of Nineveh is near, for the word of God must have its fulfillment; and our brothers who are scattered there, far from the land of Israel, will return to it. 7. All the land of Israel, after having been a wilderness, will be repopulated, and the house of God, after having been burned, will be rebuilt, and all who fear God will return there. 8. The nations will abandon their idols; they will come to Jerusalem and dwell there; 9. and all the kings of the earth will rejoice there, worshiping the King of Israel.</p>

<p class="v">10. "Listen, then, my children, to your father; serve the Lord in truth, and strive to do what is pleasing to him. 11. Charge your children to practice justice and to give alms, to remember God and to bless him at all times in truth and with all their strength.</p>

<p class="v">12. "Listen to me now, then, my children, and do not remain in this city; but on the very day you have buried your mother beside me in the same tomb, set out to leave this place; 13. for I see that the iniquity of Nineveh will bring about its ruin."</p>

<p class="v">14. After his mother's death, the young Tobit left Nineveh with his wife, his children, and his children's children, and he returned to his parents-in-law. 15. He found them in good health, in a happy old age; he took care of them and closed their eyes; he received the entire inheritance of the house of Raguel, and he saw the children of his children to the fifth generation. 16. After he had lived ninety-nine years in the fear of the Lord, his children buried him with joy. 17. All his kindred and all his descendants persevered in a good life and holy conduct, so that they were loved by God and by men, and by all who dwelt in the land.</p>

## Judith {: .book}

<p class="chap-sub">The widow of Bethulia who, by her faith and courage, cuts off the head of Holofernes and saves Israel. "You are the glory of Jerusalem, you are the joy of Israel" (Jdt 15:10).</p>

### Chapter 1 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Arphaxad, king of the Medes, after having subjected many nations to his empire, built of squared, hewn stones a very strong city, which he called Ecbatana. 2. He surrounded it with walls seventy cubits high and thirty cubits wide, and he built there towers a hundred cubits high, 3. square in shape, each side being twenty feet wide, and he made the gates in proportion to the height of the towers. 4. He gloried in being invincible through the power of his army and the multitude of his chariots.</p>

<p class="v">5. Now in the twelfth year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Assyrians, who reigned at Nineveh, the great city, made war on Arphaxad and defeated him 6. in the great plain called Ragau, with the help of those who dwell near the Euphrates, the Tigris, and the Jadason, in the plain of Erioch, king of the Elicians.</p>

<p class="v">7. Then the dominion of Nebuchadnezzar was enlarged, and his heart was lifted up, and he sent messengers to all who dwelt in Cilicia, at Damascus, and on Mount Lebanon, 8. to the peoples of Carmel and of Kedar, to the inhabitants of Galilee, in the great plain of Esdrelon, 9. to all who were in Samaria, beyond the river Jordan, as far as Jerusalem, and in all the land of Goshen as far as the borders of Ethiopia: 10. to all these peoples Nebuchadnezzar, king of Assyria, sent messengers. 11. And all of them, with one accord, refused; they sent them away without gifts and had nothing but contempt for them. 12. Then King Nebuchadnezzar was enraged against all these lands, and swore by his throne and by his kingdom to take vengeance on all these regions.</p>

### Chapter 2 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. In the thirteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, on the twenty-second day of the first month, it was decided in the house of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Assyria, that he would take vengeance. 2. And he summoned all the elders, all his chiefs and his warriors, and held a secret council with them. 3. He told them that his design was to subject the whole earth to his empire. 4. This speech having been approved by all, King Nebuchadnezzar summoned Holofernes, commander-in-chief of his army, 5. and said to him: "Set out against all the kingdoms of the West, and especially against those who have despised my command. 6. Your eye shall spare no kingdom, and you shall subject to me all the fortified cities.</p>

<p class="v">7. Then Holofernes, having called together the chiefs and officers of the army of the Assyrians, enrolled men for the expedition, according to the king's order, to the number of a hundred and twenty thousand foot soldiers and twelve thousand mounted archers. 8. He had his army preceded by an innumerable multitude of camels, with abundant provisions for his soldiers, and innumerable herds of oxen and sheep. 9. He had wheat gathered from all Syria along his route. 10. He took from the king's house immense sums of gold and silver. 11. And he set out, he and the whole army, with the chariots, the horsemen and the archers, who covered the face of the earth like locusts. 12. Having crossed the border of Assyria, he came to the great mountains of Ange, which are north of Cilicia, and he penetrated all their fortresses and seized all their strongholds. 13. He took by storm the famous city of Melitene, and plundered all the inhabitants of Tarsus, as well as the children of Ishmael who dwelt facing the desert and south of the land of Cellon.</p>

<p class="v">14. Crossing the Euphrates, he went into Mesopotamia, and forced all the strongholds of the region, from the torrent of Chaboras to the sea.</p>

<p class="v">15. Then he seized all the lands bordering the Euphrates from Cilicia to the territory of Japheth, which extends toward the south. 16. He carried off captive all the sons of Midian, plundered all their riches, and put to the sword all who resisted him. 17. He then went down into the plains of Damascus, at the time of the harvest, burned all the crops, and had all the trees and all the vines cut down. 18. And the terror of his arms seized all the inhabitants of the earth.</p>

### Chapter 3 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Then the kings and princes of all the cities and all the lands — namely of Mesopotamian Syria, of the Syria of Soba, of Libya, and of Cilicia — sent their ambassadors, who went to Holofernes and said to him: 2. "Calm your anger against us; it is better, with our lives spared, to serve Nebuchadnezzar, the great king, and to submit ourselves to you, than to die, after having suffered, perishing in the evils of servitude. 3. All our cities, all that we possess, all our mountains, our hills, our fields, our herds of oxen, sheep, goats, horses, camels, all our goods and our families are before you. 4. Let all that we have be under your dependence. 5. We and our children are your servants. 6. Come to us as a peaceful master, and make use of our services as it shall please you."</p>

<p class="v">7. Holofernes then came down from the mountains with his horsemen, in great force, and made himself master of all the cities and all the inhabitants of the land. 8. From every city he took, to make auxiliaries of them, valiant men chosen for war. 9. Now such was the fear that weighed upon these provinces that the inhabitants of every city, the magistrates and the most honorable persons, as well as the common people, came out at his approach to meet him, 10. and received him with crowns and torches, dancing to the sound of drums and flutes. 11. Nevertheless, even by this conduct, they could not soften the ferocity of his heart. 12. He destroyed their cities and cut down their sacred groves. 13. For Nebuchadnezzar had ordered him to exterminate all the gods of the earth, so that he alone might be called God by all the nations that the power of Holofernes might subdue.</p>

<p class="v">14. After having traveled through Syria and Soba, all of Apamea and all of Mesopotamia, he came to the Idumeans in the land of Gabaa; 15. and, having taken their cities, he stopped there thirty days, during which he had all the troops of his army gathered together.</p>

### Chapter 4 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. The children of Israel who dwelt in the land of Judah, having learned these things, were seized with fear at the approach of Holofernes. 2. They felt a sense of dread and horror at the thought that he might treat Jerusalem and the temple of the Lord as he had treated the other cities and their temples. 3. They sent messengers throughout Samaria and the surrounding country as far as Jericho, and occupied beforehand all the mountain summits. 4. They surrounded their towns with walls and laid in stores of wheat to prepare themselves to withstand the struggle. 5. The high priest Eliakim also wrote to all who dwelt facing Esdrelon, opposite the great plain that is near Dothan, and to all in whose territory the mountain passes lay, 6. urging them to occupy the mountain slopes by which one could go to Jerusalem, and to guard the defiles that might offer a way between the mountains. 7. The children of Israel carried out the orders of Eliakim, priest of the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">8. And all the people called upon the Lord with great insistence, and they humbled their souls in fasting and prayer, they and their wives. 9. The priests put on sackcloth, and the children prostrated themselves before the temple of the Lord, and the altar of the Lord was covered with sackcloth. 10. And with one heart they cried out to the Lord, God of Israel, that he would not allow their children to become the prey of a conqueror and their wives spoil to be divided, that their cities be given over to destruction and their sanctuary profaned, and that they themselves become an object of reproach among the nations.</p>

<p class="v">11. Then Eliakim, the high priest of the Lord, traveled through all the land of Israel, and addressed the people, 12. saying: "Know that the Lord will hear your supplications, if you persevere in fasting and prayer in his presence. 13. Remember Moses, servant of the Lord: Amalek trusted in his strength and in his power, in his army, in his shields, in his chariots and in his horsemen; Moses conquered him, not by fighting with the sword, but by addressing holy prayers to God. 14. So it will be with all the enemies of Israel, if you persevere in the work you have begun." 15. Following this exhortation, they entreated the Lord, remaining in his presence: 16. so that even those who offered burnt offerings offered them to the Lord clothed in sackcloth and with ashes on their heads. 17. And all prayed to God with all their heart, that he would visit his people Israel.</p>

### Chapter 5 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. It was announced to Holofernes, chief of the army of the Assyrians, that the children of Israel were preparing to resist and that they had closed the mountain passes. 2. Carried away with fury and burning with anger, he called all the princes of Moab and the chiefs of Ammon, 3. and said to them: "Tell me what people this is that occupies the mountains; what are their cities, what is their strength and importance; what is their military power, what is their number, and what chief commands them. 4. Why are they the only ones, among all the peoples of the West, who have despised us and have not come out to meet us to receive us in peace?"</p>

<p class="v">5. Then Achior, chief of all the sons of Ammon, answered him: "If you deign to listen to me, my lord, I will tell before you the truth about this people who dwell in the mountains, and no false word shall come out of my mouth. 6. This people is of the race of the Chaldeans. 7. They first came to dwell in Mesopotamia, because they did not wish to follow the gods of their fathers, who were in the land of the Chaldeans. 8. Having thus abandoned the rites of their ancestors, who paid honor to a multitude of gods, 9. they worshiped the one God of heaven, who had commanded them to leave their country and go to dwell in Canaan. Famine having invaded the whole earth, they went down into Egypt, and there they multiplied so greatly over four hundred years that they became an innumerable multitude. 10. Treated harshly by the king of Egypt and forced to build his cities with mortar and brick, they called upon the Lord their God, who struck all the land of Egypt with various plagues. 11. The Egyptians drove them out of their homes, and the plague ceased to strike them; but they wanted to take them again and make them their slaves once more. 12. Then the Israelites fled, and God opened the sea before them, so that the waters became solid like a wall on each side, and they were able to pass through, walking on dry ground at the bottom of the sea. 13. The innumerable army of the Egyptians having pursued them there, it was buried beneath the waters, to the point that not a single one remained to hand down to posterity the account of this event. 14. When the Israelites had come out of the Red Sea, they occupied the deserts of Mount Sinai, in which no man could ever dwell, nor any son of man fix his abode. 15. There the bitter springs were turned into sweet waters to quench their thirst, and for forty years they received their food from heaven. 16. Wherever they advanced without bow and without arrow, without shield and without sword, their God fought for them and won the victory. 17. And no one has ever triumphed over this people, except when it turned away from the service of the Lord, its God. 18. But every time they worshiped a god other than him, they were given over to plunder, to the sword, and to disgrace. 19. And every time they repented of having abandoned the service of their God, the God of heaven gave them the strength to resist their enemies. 20. At last they conquered the kings of the Canaanites, the Jebusites, the Perizzites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Amorites, and all the mighty ones of Heshbon, and they took possession of their lands and their cities. 21. As long as they did not sin in the presence of their God, happiness was with them; for their God hates iniquity. 22. Indeed, even in these last years, having strayed from the way in which God had commanded them to walk, they were cut to pieces in battle by several nations, and many of them were led captive into a foreign land. 23. But recently, having returned to the Lord their God, they have gathered together again after this dispersion, they have occupied all these mountains, and they possess Jerusalem once more, where their sanctuary is. 24. Now therefore, my lord, make inquiry: if they are guilty of some iniquity before their God, let us go up against them, for their God will surely deliver them to you, and they will be subjected to the yoke of your power. 25. But if this people has not offended its God, we shall not be able to stand before them, for their God will defend them, and we shall become an object of mockery to the whole earth."</p>

<p class="v">26. When Achior had finished speaking, all the great men of Holofernes, seized with anger, thought of killing him, saying to one another: 27. "Who is this man who dares to say that the children of Israel can resist King Nebuchadnezzar and his armies, they, people without weapons, without strength, strangers to the art of war? 28. Therefore, to show Achior that he deceives us, let us climb these mountains, and when the strongest among them are in our hands, we will put him to the sword along with them: 29. so that all the nations may know that Nebuchadnezzar is the god of the earth, and that there is no other besides him."</p>

### Chapter 6 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. When they had finished speaking, Holofernes, carried away with fury, said to Achior: 2. "Since, setting yourself up as a prophet, you announce to us that the people of Israel will be defended by their God, I want to show you that there is no God but Nebuchadnezzar. 3. When we have struck them all down as one man, you yourself will perish by the sword of the Assyrians, and all Israel will be annihilated with you. 4. You will thus know that Nebuchadnezzar is the master of the whole earth. And then the sword of my soldiers will pierce your sides, you will fall pierced among the wounded of Israel, and you will breathe no more, until you are exterminated with them. 5. If you believe your prophecy to be true, let your face cease to be downcast; and let the paleness that covers it depart from you, if you imagine that my words cannot be fulfilled. 6. But so that you may know well that you will perish with them, from this moment you shall be joined to this people, so that, when my sword inflicts on them the punishment they deserve, you may fall with them under my vengeance."</p>

<p class="v">7. Then Holofernes gave orders to his servants to seize Achior, to bring him to Bethulia, and to hand him over to the children of Israel. 8. The servants of Holofernes, having seized him, crossed the plain; but when they were near the mountain, the slingers came out against them. 9. The Assyrians turned aside, skirting the mountain, bound Achior to a tree by his hands and feet, and, having left him there, returned to their master.</p>

<p class="v">10. Then the children of Israel, coming down from Bethulia, came to him and, having untied him, led him to Bethulia; then they brought him into the midst of the people, and asked him why the Assyrians had abandoned him thus bound. 11. — In those days, Ozias, son of Micah, of the tribe of Simeon, and Charmi, also called Gothoniel, were the chiefs who commanded in the city. — 12. Achior then related, in the midst of the elders and in the presence of all the people, all that he had answered to the questions of Holofernes, how the men of Holofernes had wanted to kill him because of what he had said, 13. and how Holofernes himself had ordered, in his anger, that he be handed over for this reason into the hands of the Israelites, so that after his victory over the children of Israel, he might also put Achior to death by various tortures, because he had said that the God of heaven was their defender.</p>

<p class="v">14. When Achior had finished his account, all the people fell face down on the ground, worshiping the Lord, and, mingling their groans and their tears, poured out with one heart their prayers before the Lord, 15. saying: "Lord, God of heaven and earth, behold their pride and consider our lowliness; turn your gaze upon the face of your saints, and show that you do not abandon those who place their trust in you, and that you humble those who presume upon themselves and grow proud of their power."</p>

<p class="v">16. When the people had finished weeping and had spent the whole day in prayer, they consoled Achior, 17. saying: "The God of our fathers, whose power you have proclaimed, will grant you in return to see their ruin instead. 18. And when the Lord our God has granted this deliverance to his servants, may God be with you still in our midst, so that, as it shall please you, you may live with us, you and all who are yours." 19. When the assembly had dispersed, Ozias received Achior into his house and gave him a great feast. 20. He invited the elders to it, and, the fast being over, they ate together.</p>

<p class="v">21. Then all the people gathered together again and prayed all night in the place where they were assembled, imploring the help of the God of Israel.</p>

### Chapter 7 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. The next day, Holofernes gave the order to his troops to march up against Bethulia. 2. His army was made up of a hundred and twenty thousand foot soldiers and twenty-two thousand horsemen, not counting the men fit for war whom he had taken prisoner and the young men he had brought from the provinces and cities. 3. All together they prepared for battle against the children of Israel and, marching along the mountain as far as the summit overlooking Dothan, they camped from the place called Belma to Chelmon, which is opposite Esdrelon. 4. When the children of Israel saw this multitude, they fell face down on the ground and, covering their heads with ashes, they all prayed together to the God of Israel to display his mercy upon his people. 5. Then, having taken up their weapons of war, they occupied the places where small paths allowed passage between the mountains, and they kept watch there day and night.</p>

<p class="v">6. While going about the surrounding area, Holofernes discovered a spring outside the city, on the south side, which carried its waters there by an aqueduct, and he had this aqueduct cut off. 7. However, there were, not far from the walls, other springs where the besieged came to draw a little water by stealth, more, it seems, to relieve their thirst than to quench it. 8. But the sons of Ammon and of Moab came to Holofernes, saying: "The children of Israel trust neither in their spears nor in their arrows; but these mountains defend them, and these hills suspended over precipices are their strength. 9. Therefore, so that you may triumph over them without giving battle, place guards near the springs to prevent them from drawing water there; you will thus make them perish without striking a blow, or else, worn out by thirst, they will surrender their city, which they regard as impregnable because it is set upon the mountains." 10. The advice pleased Holofernes and his officers, and he had a post of a hundred men placed around each spring.</p>

<p class="v">11. This watch having been kept for twenty days, all the cisterns and reservoirs of water were dry for all the inhabitants of Bethulia, so that there remained in the city nothing to satisfy their thirst even for a single day, for the water was distributed to the people each day by measure. 12. Then all the men and women, the young people and the children, gathered around Ozias, and with one common voice 13. they all said to him: "Let God be judge between you and us, for you have acted to our misfortune in refusing to make proposals of peace to the Assyrians; and it is for this that God has delivered us into their hands. 14. That is why there is no one to come to our aid, while thirst and great misery make us collapse before their eyes. 15. Now therefore, assemble all who are in the city, so that we may all surrender willingly to the men of Holofernes. 16. For it is better for us to have our lives spared and to bless God in captivity, than to die and be a reproach to all men, after having seen our wives and our children perish before our eyes. 17. Taking heaven and earth to witness today, and the God of our fathers, who chastises us according to our sins, we implore you to hand over the city without delay into the hands of the soldiers of Holofernes, so that we may find a swift death by the edge of the sword, instead of a slow death in the torments of thirst." 18. When they had spoken thus, there arose lamentations and great cries throughout the whole assembly, and all with one voice, for many hours, cried out to God, saying: 19. "We have sinned with our fathers, we have been unfaithful, we have committed iniquity. 20. You, who are merciful, have pity on us; or else take vengeance for our crimes by chastising us yourself, and do not deliver those who glorify you to a people who do not know you, 21. lest it be said among the nations: Where is their God?"</p>

<p class="v">22. Having worn themselves out with crying and weeping, they fell silent. 23. Then Ozias rose, bathed in tears, and said: "Take courage, my brothers, and let us wait five days for the mercy of the Lord. 24. For perhaps he will put an end to his anger and give glory to his name. 25. When these five days have passed, if help has not come, we will do what you have proposed to us."</p>

### Chapter 8 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. These words were reported to Judith, a widow, daughter of Merari, son of Idox, son of Joseph, son of Ozias, son of Elai, son of Jamnor, son of Gideon, son of Raphaim, son of Achitob, son of Melchias, son of Enan, son of Nathanias, son of Salathiel, son of Simeon, son of Israel. 2. Her husband, named Manasseh, had died at the time of the barley harvest. 3. As he was overseeing the reapers, who were binding the sheaves in the fields, the heat of the sun struck him on the head, and he died in Bethulia, his city, and was buried there with his fathers. 4. Judith had already remained a widow for three years and six months. 5. She had built for herself, on the roof of her house, a secluded chamber, where she remained shut up with her maidservants. 6. With her loins covered with sackcloth, she fasted every day of her life, except the sabbaths and the new moons and the feasts of the house of Israel.</p>

<p class="v">7. She was very beautiful in appearance, and her husband had left her great riches, many servants, and estates full of herds of oxen and sheep. 8. She was held in great esteem by all, because she greatly feared the Lord, and there was no one who spoke a word of blame against her.</p>

<p class="v">9. Having learned, then, that Ozias had promised to surrender the city after the fifth day, she sent for Chabri and Charmi, elders of the people. 10. They came to her, and she said to them:</p>

<p class="v">"How could Ozias say that he would surrender the city to the Assyrians, if within five days help does not come to you? 11. And who are you, to put the Lord to the test in this way? 12. That is not a word that draws down mercy, but rather one that stirs up anger and kindles fury. 13. You have set for the Lord a deadline within which he must exercise his mercy, and you have appointed him a day according to your own good pleasure! 14. But because the Lord is patient, let us do penance for this fault, and implore his pardon with tears. 15. For God does not threaten as man does, and he does not burn with anger as a son of man does. 16. Let us therefore humble our souls before him, and put within us a spirit of humility, as befits his servants. 17. Let us pray to the Lord with tears that he make us feel, in whatever way shall please him, the effects of his mercy, so that, just as the pride of our enemies has cast trouble into our heart, so our humility may become for us a source of glory. 18. For we have not imitated the sins of our fathers, who abandoned their God and worshiped foreign gods. 19. It was because of this crime that they were given over to the sword, to pillage, and to the mockery of their enemies; but we know no other God but him. 20. Let us humbly wait for his consolation, and he will avenge our blood upon our enemies who afflict us; he will humble all the nations that rise up against us, and he will cover them with confusion, he, the Lord our God. 21. And now, my brothers, since you are the elders of the people of God, and their life depends on you, lift up their hearts by your words, so that they may remember that our fathers were tested, that it might be known whether they truly served their God. 22. They must remember how Abraham, our father, was tempted, and how, tried by many tribulations, he became the friend of God. 23. So too Isaac, so too Jacob, so too Moses, and all who pleased God, passed through many afflictions while remaining faithful. 24. But those who did not accept these trials with the fear of the Lord, and who gave way to their impatience and to injurious murmurings against the Lord, 25. those the destroyer struck with death, and the serpents caused to perish. 26. Let us not, then, give way to impatience because of the evils we suffer. 27. But let us consider that these torments, lesser than our sins, are the rods with which the Lord chastises us, as his servants, to amend us, and let us believe that they have not been sent to us for our ruin."</p>

<p class="v">28. Ozias and the elders answered her: "All that you have said is true, and there is nothing to find fault with in your words. 29. Now therefore, pray to God for us, for you are a holy woman and one who fears God."</p>

<p class="v">30. And Judith said to them: "Since you acknowledge that what I have said is from God, 31. test whether what I have resolved to do is also from him, and pray that God may give me the strength to carry out my plan. 32. You will keep watch tonight at the gate, and I will go out, with my companion; and pray that within five days, as you have said, the Lord may look upon his people Israel. 33. But I do not want you to try to find out what I am undertaking; until I return to bring you news of it, let nothing else be done but to pray for me to the Lord our God." 34. Ozias, the prince of Judah, said to her: "Go in peace, and may the Lord be with you to take vengeance on our enemies!"</p>

### Chapter 9 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. When they had gone, Judith entered her oratory, and, clothed in sackcloth, her head covered with ashes, she prostrated herself before the Lord and called upon him, saying:</p>

<p class="v">2. "Lord, God of my father Simeon, who gave him a sword to avenge himself on the strangers who, carried away by passion, had violated a virgin and had outraged her to her shame; 3. you who delivered their wives to the ravishers, their daughters to slavery, and all their spoils to be divided among your servants burning with zeal for your cause, assist me, I beg you, Lord my God, help a widow. 4. It is you who worked the wonders of ancient times, and who formed the design of those that followed, and they were accomplished because you willed it. 5. All your ways are marked out in advance, and you have arranged your judgments through your foreknowledge. 6. Look now upon the camp of the Assyrians, as you once deigned to look upon that of the Egyptians, when they pursued your servants, weapons in hand, trusting in their chariots, in their horsemen, and in the multitude of their fighters. 7. But you looked upon their camp, and darkness took away their strength. 8. The deep held their feet fast, and the waters swallowed them up. 9. May it be the same, Lord, with these men, who trust in their multitude, in their chariots, in their javelins, in their shields and in their arrows, and who are proud of their spears. 10. They do not know that you are our God, you who from the beginning struck down armies and whose name is Lord. 11. Raise your arm, as in ages past; break their power by your power; let their strength fall before your wrath, they who intend to violate your sanctuary, to profane the tabernacle of your name, and to strike down with their sword the horns of your altar. 12. Grant, Lord, that the pride of this man be brought down by his own sword. 13. Let him be caught in the snare of his own gaze upon me, and strike him by the sweet words of my lips. 14. Put into my heart enough firmness to despise him, enough strength to destroy him. 15. It will be a memorable glory for your name that he be brought down by the hand of a woman. 16. For your power, Lord, does not lie in numbers, and your will does not depend on the strength of horses; and from the beginning the proud have not pleased you, but you have always been pleased with the prayer of the humble and the meek. 17. God of heaven, Creator of the waters and Lord of all creation, hear me, a wretched woman, who beseeches you and who places my trust in your mercy. 18. Remember, Lord, your covenant, give the word to my mouth, strength to the design that is in my heart, so that your house may keep the holiness with which you have clothed it, 19. and that all nations may acknowledge that you are God, and that there is no other besides you."</p>

### Chapter 10 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. When she had finished her prayer to the Lord, Judith rose from the place where she had lain prostrate on the ground before the Lord. 2. She called her maidservant and, having gone down into her house, she took off her sackcloth and laid aside the garments of her widowhood. 3. She washed her body, anointed herself with the finest myrrh, arranged her hair, put the turban on her head, put on her festal garments, fastened sandals on her feet, took her bracelets, her necklace, her earrings, and her rings — in a word, adorned herself with all her ornaments. 4. The Lord further heightened her splendor, because all this adornment had its source not in sensual pleasure but in virtue; therefore the Lord increased her beauty in such a way that she shone before the eyes of all with incomparable brilliance. 5. Then she had her maidservant carry a skin of wine, a vessel of oil, roasted grain, dried fruit, bread, and cheese, and she set out.</p>

<p class="v">6. Having arrived, she and her maidservant, at the gate of the city, she found Ozias and the elders waiting for her. 7. On seeing her, they were struck with admiration for her beauty. 8. However, they asked her no questions, and let her pass, saying: "May the God of our fathers grant you his grace; may he strengthen by his power all the designs that are in your heart, so that Jerusalem may be glorified because of you, and that your name may be numbered among those of the saints and the just." 9. Those present all answered with one voice: "So be it! So be it!" 10. And Judith passed through the gates, she and her maidservant, praying to the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">11. As she was going down the mountain, at daybreak, the advance posts of the Assyrians met her and stopped her, saying: "Where do you come from, and where are you going?" 12. She answered: "I am a daughter of the Hebrews, and I have fled from among them, having recognized that they will be given over to you as prey, because they have despised you and have not wanted to surrender to you willingly, to find favor before you. 13. Therefore I said to myself: I will present myself before the prince Holofernes, to reveal to him their secrets and to show him a way by which he may take them without losing a single man of his army." 14. When these men had heard her words, they gazed upon her face, and surprise was in their eyes, so greatly did they admire her great beauty: 15. "You have saved your life," they said to her, "by taking this resolution to come down to our lord. 16. You may be assured that, when you appear before him, he will treat you well and that you will be very pleasing to his heart." Then, having led her to the tent of Holofernes, they announced her.</p>

<p class="v">17. As soon as she had entered his presence, Holofernes was immediately captivated by her eyes. 18. His officers said to him: "Who then could despise the people of the Hebrews, who have such beautiful women? Do they not well deserve that, to possess them, we should wage war on them?" 19. Judith saw Holofernes seated beneath his canopy, whose fabric of purple and gold was adorned with emeralds and precious stones.</p>

<p class="v">20. Having fixed her eyes upon his face, she did him homage, prostrating herself to the ground. At once, at the order of their master, the servants of Holofernes raised her up.</p>

### Chapter 11 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Then Holofernes said to her: "Take heart and banish fear from your heart, for I have never done harm to anyone who was willing to serve King Nebuchadnezzar. 2. If your people had not despised me, I would not have raised my spear against them. 3. Now, tell me why you have withdrawn from them and have chosen to come to us?"</p>

<p class="v">4. Judith answered him: "Receive the words of your servant, for if you follow the words of your servant, the Lord will fully carry out his designs concerning you, 5. as surely as Nebuchadnezzar, king of the earth, lives, and his power lives, that power of which you are the custodian for the punishment of all who go astray; for not only are men led by you to serve him, but even the animals of the field obey him. 6. Indeed, the wisdom of your mind is renowned among all nations; everyone knows that in his whole kingdom you alone are good and mighty, and your rule is praised in every province. 7. It is also known what Achior said, and it is not unknown how you ordered him to be treated. 8. For it is certain that our God is so offended by the sins of his people that he has caused it to be announced by his prophets that he was going to deliver them to their enemies because of their unfaithfulness. 9. And because the children of Israel know that they have offended their God, they tremble with fear before you. 10. Moreover, famine presses upon them, and, their reservoirs of water being dried up, they are already to be counted among the dead. 11. They have even resolved to kill their livestock and drink its blood. 12. They have even resolved to put to their own use the very things consecrated to the Lord their God, which God has forbidden them to touch — the grain, the wine, and the oil of the tithes and the first fruits — daring to feed on things which it is not even lawful for them to touch with their hands. Since they are acting thus, it is certain that they will be given over to ruin. 13. This is what I know, I, your servant, and I have fled far from them, and the Lord has sent me to inform you of it. 14. For I, your servant, serve God, even now while I am with you; and your servant will go out of the camp to pray to God. 15. And he will let me know when he is to punish them for their sin, and I will come to announce it to you. I will then lead you through Judea as far as Jerusalem, and you will find all the people of Israel like sheep that have no shepherd anymore, and there will not even be a dog to bark at you. 16. It is the foreknowledge of God that has revealed these things to me; 17. and since he is angry with them, I have received the mission to announce them to you."</p>

<p class="v">18. All this speech pleased Holofernes and his servants. They admired the wisdom of Judith and said to one another: 19. "There does not exist on earth a woman like this one for bearing, for beauty, and for the wisdom of her words." Holofernes said to her: 20. "God has done well to send you ahead of this people, to deliver them into our hands. 21. Since your proposal is good, if your God does this for me, he will also be my God, and you, you will be great in the house of Nebuchadnezzar, and your name will become famous throughout the whole earth."</p>
### Chapter 12 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Then Holofernes ordered that Judith be brought into the tent where his treasures were kept, that she might remain there, and he arranged what should be given her from his table. 2. Judith answered him, "I cannot now eat of the things you command to be given me, lest I make myself guilty of a sin; I will eat of what I have brought for myself." 3. Holofernes said to her, "When the provisions you have brought are exhausted, what shall we do for you?" 4. "My lord," answered Judith, "I swear by your life that your servant will not have consumed all these provisions before God has accomplished by my hand the design I have formed." And his servants brought her into the tent he had appointed. 5. On entering it, she asked that she be granted leave to go out, at night and before daybreak, to pray and call upon the Lord. 6. And Holofernes ordered his servants to let her go out and come in at her pleasure, for three days, to worship her God. 7. So she went out every night into the valley of Bethulia, and washed herself at a spring. 8. When she had come up again, she prayed the Lord, the God of Israel, to direct her way for the deliverance of his people. 9. Then, returning to her tent, she remained there pure until she took her food toward evening.</p>

<p class="v">10. On the fourth day, Holofernes gave a feast for his servants, and said to Vagao, his eunuch, "Go, and persuade this Jewess to consent willingly to dwell with me. 11. It would be a shame for a man, among the Assyrians, that a woman should mock him and leave him without having yielded to his desires."</p>

<p class="v">12. Then Vagao went in to Judith and said to her, "Let the good girl not be afraid to come to my lord, to be honored in his presence, to eat with him and drink wine with joy." 13. "Who am I," answered Judith, "to resist my lord? 14. Whatever is good and excellent in his eyes, I will do; and whatever he prefers shall be the best for me, all the days of my life." 15. And she rose, and having adorned herself with her ornaments, she went in and presented herself before Holofernes. 16. Holofernes' heart was stirred, for he burned with desire for her. Holofernes said to her: 17. "Drink then, and eat with joy, for you have found favor before me." 18. Judith answered, "I will drink, my lord, for my soul is more honored this day than it has been all the days of my life." 19. And taking what her maidservant had prepared for her, she ate and drank before him. 20. Holofernes was transported with joy because of her, and he drank wine to excess, more than he had ever drunk in his life.</p>

### Chapter 13 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. When evening had come, Holofernes' servants hastened to return to their tents; and Vagao, having closed the doors of the chamber, went away. 2. All were heavy with wine, 3. and Judith remained alone in the chamber. 4. Holofernes was lying on his bed, sunk in the stupor of complete drunkenness. 5. Judith had told her maidservant to stand outside before the chamber, and to keep watch.</p>

<p class="v">6. Standing before the bed, Judith prayed for some time with tears, moving her lips in silence: 7. "Lord, God of Israel," she said, "strengthen me, and cast at this moment a favorable glance upon the work of my hands, that, according to your promise, you may raise up your city of Jerusalem, and that I may accomplish what I have believed possible by your help." 8. Having said these words, she approached the post that was at the head of Holofernes' bed, took down his sword that hung there, and, 9. having drawn it from its sheath, she seized Holofernes by the hair, saying, "Lord God, strengthen me at this hour!" 10. And with two blows to the neck, she cut off his head. Then she took down the curtain from the posts and rolled the beheaded body onto the ground; 11. and, going out without delay, she gave Holofernes' head to her maidservant, ordering her to put it in her bag.</p>

<p class="v">12. The two of them then set out, according to their custom, as if to go and pray, and, having crossed the camp and gone around the valley, they arrived at the gate of the city. 13. Judith cried from afar to the keepers of the walls, "Open the gate, for God is with us, and he has shown forth his power in favor of Israel."</p>

<p class="v">14. Having heard her words, the guards called the elders of the city. 15. At once all the inhabitants ran to her, from the least to the greatest, for they had begun to despair of her return. 16. Lighting torches, they all gathered around her. Judith, going up to a high place, commanded that silence be kept; and when all had grown quiet, 17. she said to them, "Praise the Lord our God, who has not abandoned those who hoped in him. 18. Through me, his servant, he has fulfilled his promises of mercy in favor of the house of Israel, and he has this night slain, by my hand, the enemy of his people." 19. Then, drawing Holofernes' head out of the bag, she showed it to them, saying, "Here is the head of Holofernes, chief of the army of the Assyrians, and here is the curtain under which he lay in his drunkenness, when the Lord our God struck him by the hand of a woman. 20. As surely as the Lord lives, his angel kept me at my departure, during my stay among them, and at my return, and the Lord did not allow his servant to be defiled; but he has restored me to you without any stain of sin, full of joy for his victory, for my preservation, and for your deliverance. 21. All of you, sing his praises, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever!"</p>

<p class="v">22. All of them, worshiping the Lord, said to her, "The Lord has blessed you with his strength, for through you he has brought all our enemies to nothing." 23. Ozias, the prince of the people of Israel, said to her, "My daughter, you are blessed by the Lord, the Most High God, above all the women who are on the earth. 24. Blessed be the Lord, creator of heaven and earth, who has guided your hand to cut off the head of the greatest of our enemies! 25. He has made your name so glorious this day, that your praise will not depart from the mouths of men, who will remember forever the power of the Lord; for, on their behalf, you did not spare your life when you saw the sufferings and distress of your people, but you have saved us from ruin by walking in uprightness before our God." 26. And all the people answered, "So be it! So be it!"</p>

<p class="v">27. Then Achior was brought in, and Judith said to him, "The God of Israel, to whom you bore this testimony, that he takes vengeance on his enemies, has himself this night cut off, by my hand, the head of the chief of all the unbelievers. 28. And to convince you that it is so, here is the head of Holofernes, who, in the insolence of his pride, despised the God of Israel and threatened you with death, saying: When the people of Israel are conquered, I will put you to the edge of the sword." 29. At the sight of Holofernes' head, Achior shuddered with horror; he fell face down on the ground, and fainted. 30. When he had recovered his senses and come to himself, he threw himself at Judith's feet and said to her:</p>

<p class="v">31. "Be proclaimed blessed by your God in all the tents of Jacob! Among all the peoples who hear your name, the God of Israel will be glorified because of you."</p>

### Chapter 14 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Then Judith said to all the people, "Listen to me, my brothers, hang this head on the top of our walls. 2. And, when the sun has risen, let each one take up his weapons; then go out impetuously, not merely to go down into the valley, but as if to make a general attack. 3. The outposts will then have to flee to their general, to wake him for battle. 4. And when their leaders have run to Holofernes' tent and find him beheaded, bathed in his blood, terror will seize them. 5. And when you see them flee, pursue them boldly, for the Lord will crush them before your eyes."</p>

<p class="v">6. Then Achior, seeing the power that the God of Israel exercised, abandoned the worship of the nations; he believed in God, was circumcised, and was incorporated into the people of Israel, together with all his descendants, to the present time.</p>

<p class="v">7. As soon as day appeared, the inhabitants of Bethulia hung Holofernes' head on the walls, and, every man having taken up his weapons, they went out of the city with great tumult and loud shouts. 8. The outposts, having noticed this, ran to Holofernes' tent. 9. Those who were in the tent came and made noise at the door of the bedchamber to wake him, deliberately increasing the tumult, so that Holofernes might be roused from his sleep by all this noise, without any of them needing to wake him. 10. For no one dared, whether by knocking or by entering, to open the door of the bedchamber of the greatest of the Assyrians. 11. But his generals, his commanders, and all the officers of the army of the king of the Assyrians, having come, said to the chamberlains: 12. "Go in and wake him, for these rats have come out of their holes and have dared to challenge us to battle." 13. Then Vagao, having entered the chamber, stopped before the curtain, and clapped his hands, for he imagined that his master was sleeping with Judith. 14. But when, listening closely, he heard none of the movements of a man who might have been lying there, he approached the curtain and, having lifted it, saw Holofernes' corpse stretched out on the ground, headless, and bathed in his blood. At once he let out a great cry, weeping, and tore his garments. 15. And, having entered Judith's tent, he did not find her. He rushed out in great haste to the people, 16. and said, "One single Jewish woman has brought confusion into the house of King Nebuchadnezzar; behold, Holofernes lies on the ground, and his head is no longer with his body!" 17. On hearing these words, all the princes of the army of the Assyrians tore their garments; extreme fear and terror seized them, their minds were thrown into confusion, 18. and an indescribable clamor rang out in the midst of their camp.</p>

### Chapter 15 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. When the whole army had learned that Holofernes had had his head cut off, they lost all sense and all prudence, and, heeding only fear and terror, they sought their safety in flight. 2. Without saying a word to one another, heads bowed and leaving everything behind, eager to escape the Hebrews whom they heard coming upon them weapons in hand, they fled across the fields and along the mountain paths. 3. The children of Israel, seeing them flee, set out in pursuit of them; they went down sounding the trumpet and raising loud shouts behind them. 4. And as the Assyrians fled scattered, and in great haste, the children of Israel, who pursued them gathered as a single body, cut to pieces all those they could reach.</p>

<p class="v">5. At the same time Ozias sent messages to all the cities and all the countryside of Israel. 6. So every village and every town, having armed the flower of their young men, sent them after the Assyrians, and they pursued them at the point of the sword to their farthest border. 7. Those who had remained at Bethulia entered the camp of the Assyrians, carried off the spoil the Assyrians had abandoned in their flight, and returned laden with it. 8. On the other hand, those who, after the victory, returned to Bethulia brought with them everything that had belonged to the Assyrians — countless cattle, draft animals, and all their baggage — so that all, from the least to the greatest, grew rich from their spoils.</p>

<p class="v">9. Joakim, the high priest, came from Jerusalem to Bethulia, with all his elders, to see Judith. 10. When she went out to meet him, all blessed her with one voice, saying, "You are the glory of Jerusalem; you are the joy of Israel; you are the honor of our people! 11. For you have shown a manly soul, and your heart has been full of valor. Because you loved chastity, and, after losing your husband, would not know another, the hand of the Lord has clothed you with strength, and you shall be blessed forever." 12. All the people answered, "So be it! So be it!"</p>

<p class="v">13. Thirty days were scarcely enough for the people of Israel to gather the spoils of the Assyrians. 14. Everything recognized as having belonged to Holofernes — the gold and silver, the garments, the precious stones, and all the various objects — was given to Judith, and all of it was made over to her by the people. 15. And all the people rejoiced, with the women, the young girls, and the young men, to the sound of harps and citherns.</p>

### Chapter 16 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Then Judith sang this canticle to the Lord, saying:</p>

<p class="v">2. "Praise the Lord with the sound of timbrels,<br/>sing to the Lord with cymbals,<br/>tune to him a new canticle,<br/>exalt and acclaim his name.<br/>3. The Lord puts an end to wars;<br/>the Lord is his name!<br/>4. He has pitched his camp in the midst of his people,<br/>to deliver us from the hands of all our enemies.</p>

<p class="v">5. Assur came from the mountains,<br/>from the side of the north, with the myriads of his warriors;<br/>their multitude stopped up the torrents,<br/>and their horses covered the valleys.<br/><br/>6. He promised himself to ravage my territory with fire,<br/>to slay my young men with the sword,<br/>to make my children a spoil,<br/>and my virgins captives.<br/><br/>7. But the almighty Lord covered him with disgrace;<br/>he delivered him into the hands of a woman, and she triumphed over him.<br/>8. Their hero did not fall beneath the blows of young men;<br/>the sons of the mighty did not strike him;<br/>the giants of lofty stature did not measure themselves against him.<br/><br/>It was Judith, the daughter of Merari,<br/>who laid him low by the beauty of her face.<br/>9. She stripped off the garments of her widowhood,<br/>she adorned herself with her festal garments,<br/>for the triumph of the children of Israel;<br/>10. she anointed her face with perfumed oil,<br/>she arranged the locks of her hair beneath her turban.<br/><br/>She put on a new robe to seduce him.<br/>11. The brightness of her sandal dazzled his eyes,<br/>her beauty took his soul captive,<br/>and she cut off his head with the sword.<br/><br/>12. The Persians trembled at her courage, the Medes at her boldness;<br/>13. the camp of the Assyrians rang with howls,<br/>when my people appeared, worn out and parched with thirst.<br/><br/>14. Sons of young women pierced them through<br/>and killed them like children who flee:<br/>they perished in the battle, before the face of the Lord my God.<br/><br/>15. Let us sing a canticle to the Lord,<br/>let us sing to the Lord a new canticle:<br/>16. Sovereign Master, Lord, you are great,<br/>and magnificent in your power,<br/>and none can surpass you.<br/><br/>17. Let all your creatures serve you,<br/>for you spoke, and all was made;<br/>you sent forth your spirit, and all was created,<br/>and none can resist your voice.<br/><br/>18. The mountains, as well as the waters, are shaken on their foundations,<br/>the rocks melt like wax before your face;<br/>19. but those who fear you<br/>are great before you in all things.<br/><br/>20. Woe to the nation that rises up against my people!<br/>For the Lord, the Almighty, will take vengeance on it,<br/>he will visit it on the day of judgment,<br/>21. he will deliver their flesh to fire and to worms,<br/>that they may burn and suffer this torment forever."</p>

<p class="v">22. After this victory, all the people went to Jerusalem to worship the Lord, and, as soon as they were purified, they all offered burnt offerings and fulfilled their vows and their promises. 23. Judith offered up all the weapons of Holofernes, which the people had given her, and the curtain she had herself taken from the bed, as a votive offering of forgetting. 24. All the people were full of joy before the sanctuary, and the joy of this victory was celebrated with Judith for three months.</p>

<p class="v">25. When these days of feasting had passed, each one returned to his home; Judith was honored in Bethulia, and she enjoyed great renown throughout the land of Israel. 26. Joining chastity to courage, she knew no man for the rest of her life, from the death of Manasseh, her husband. 27. On feast days, she appeared magnificently adorned. 28. After having dwelt a hundred and five years in her husband's house, and having given her maidservant her freedom, she died and was buried at Bethulia with her husband; 29. and all the people mourned her for seven days. 30. Throughout the whole course of her life and after her death, there was no one, for many years, who troubled the peace of Israel.</p>

<p class="v">31. The feast day instituted in memory of this victory is counted by the Hebrews among the number of holy days, and it has been kept by the Jews from that time until this day.</p>

## Wisdom {: .book}

<p class="chap-sub">Written in Greek at Alexandria, the Wisdom of Solomon meditates on justice and immortality ("God created man for incorruptibility," Wis 2:23), and reinterprets the Exodus as the triumph of divine Wisdom.</p>

### Chapter 1 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Love justice, you who are judges of the earth;<br/>let your thoughts of the Lord be in uprightness,<br/>and seek him with a sincere heart;<br/>2. for he lets himself be found by those who do not put him to the test,<br/>and he manifests himself to those who trust in him.<br/><br/>3. For perverse thoughts separate from God,<br/>and his power, when it is put to the test, convicts fools.<br/>4. Wisdom does not enter a soul that plots evil,<br/>nor dwell in a body enslaved to sin.<br/>5. The Holy Spirit, instructor of men,<br/>flees deceit; he withdraws from thoughts devoid of understanding,<br/>and departs when iniquity draws near.<br/><br/>6. For Wisdom is a spirit that loves mankind,<br/>and he will not leave the blasphemer unpunished for his words,<br/>for God is witness of his inmost being,<br/>the true observer of his heart,<br/>and he hears his words.<br/>7. For the Spirit of the Lord fills the universe,<br/>and he who contains all things knows everything that is said.<br/>8. So he who utters impious speech cannot remain hidden,<br/>and avenging justice does not forget him.<br/>9. For there will be an inquiry into the designs of the wicked,<br/>and the report of his words will reach the Lord,<br/>for the punishment of his iniquities.<br/>10. A jealous ear hears everything,<br/>and the sound of murmurings does not escape it.<br/>11. Beware, then, of useless murmurings,<br/>and keep your tongue from blasphemy; for the most secret word does not go forth unpunished,<br/>and the mouth that lies brings death to the soul.</p>

<p class="v">12. Do not court death by the wanderings of your life;<br/>and do not draw ruin upon yourselves by the works of your hands.<br/>13. For God did not make death,<br/>and he takes no joy in the destruction of the living.<br/>14. He created all things for life;<br/>the creatures of the world are wholesome;<br/>there is in them no destructive principle<br/>, and death has no dominion on the earth.<br/>15. For justice is immortal.</p>

<p class="v">16. But the wicked summon death with gesture and voice;<br/>looking upon her as a friend, they long for her,<br/>they make a covenant with her, and indeed they are worthy to belong to her.</p>

### Chapter 2 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. They said among themselves, reasoning wrongly:<br/>"Short and sorrowful is the time of our life,<br/>and, when a man's end comes, there is no remedy;<br/>no one is known who delivers from the abode of the dead.<br/>2. Chance brought us into existence,<br/>and, after this life, we shall be as though we had never been;<br/>the breath in our nostrils is a smoke,<br/>and thought, a spark that leaps at the beating of our heart.<br/>3. Let it go out, our body will fall to ashes,<br/>and the spirit will dissipate like the light air.<br/>4. Our name will fall into oblivion with time,<br/>and no one will remember our works.<br/>Our life will pass like a trace of cloud;<br/>it will dissipate like a mist,<br/>which the sun's rays chase away,<br/>and which the heat condenses into rain.<br/>5. Our life is the passing of a shadow;<br/>its end is without return<br/>, the seal is set and none comes back.<br/><br/>6. "Come, then, let us enjoy the good things now present;<br/>let us use the creatures with the ardor of youth,<br/>7. let us drink our fill of precious wine and perfumes,<br/>and let us not let the flower of spring pass by.<br/>8. Let us crown ourselves with rosebuds before they wither.<br/>9. Let none of us fail to join our revels; let us leave everywhere the marks of our merrymaking;<br/>for this is our portion, this is our destiny.<br/><br/>10. "Let us oppress the just man who is poor;<br/>let us not spare the widow,<br/>nor have any regard for the white hairs of the old man weighed down with years.<br/>11. Let our strength be the law of justice;<br/>for what is weak is judged good for nothing.</p>

<p class="v">12. Let us hunt down the just man, then, since he annoys us,<br/>since he is contrary to our way of acting,<br/>since he reproaches us with breaking the law, and accuses us of denying our upbringing.<br/>13. He claims to possess the knowledge of God,<br/>and calls himself a son of the Lord.<br/>14. He is for us the condemnation of our thoughts;<br/>the mere sight of him is unbearable to us;<br/>15. for his life is unlike that of others,<br/>and his ways are strange.<br/>16. In his reckoning, we are impure dross;<br/>he avoids our way of living as a defilement;<br/>he proclaims the final lot of the just to be happy,<br/>and boasts of having God for his father.<br/>17. Let us see, then, whether what he says is true, and let us examine what will happen to him when he departs this life.<br/>18. For if the just man is a son of God, God will take up his defense,<br/>and deliver him from the hand of his adversaries.<br/>19. Let us subject him to outrage and torment,<br/>that we may know his forbearance,<br/>and judge his patience.<br/>20. Let us condemn him to a shameful death,<br/>for, according to what he says, God will take care of him."<br/><br/>21. Such are their thoughts, but they are deceived;<br/>their malice has blinded them.<br/>22. Ignorant of the secret designs of God,<br/>they do not hope for a reward for holiness,<br/>and they do not believe in the recompense of pure souls.<br/>23. For God created man for immortality,<br/>and made him in the image of his own nature.<br/>24. It was through the envy of the devil that death entered the world;<br/>25. those who belong to him will experience it.</p>

### Chapter 3 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. The souls of the just are in the hand of God,<br/>and torment will not touch them.<br/>2. In the eyes of fools, they seem to be dead,<br/>and their departure from this world seems a disaster,<br/>3. and their leaving from among us an annihilation;<br/>but they are at peace.<br/><br/>4. Even though, in the sight of men, they suffered punishments,<br/>their hope is full of immortality.<br/>5. After a brief chastisement, they will receive a great reward;<br/>for God tested them,<br/>and found them worthy of himself.<br/>6. He tried them as gold in the furnace,<br/>and accepted them as a perfect burnt offering.</p>

<p class="v">7. In the time of their recompense, they will shine;<br/>like sparks, they will run through the stubble.<br/>8. They will judge the nations and rule over the peoples,<br/>and the Lord will reign over them forever.<br/>9. Those who put their trust in him will understand the truth;<br/>his faithful ones will dwell with him in love;<br/>for grace and mercy are for his elect.<br/><br/>10. But the wicked will have the punishment<br/>deserved by their perverse thoughts,<br/>they who despised the just man,<br/>and turned away from the Lord.<br/>11. For whoever rejects wisdom and correction is doomed to misfortune;<br/>their hope is vain, their labors fruitless,<br/>and their works of no profit.<br/>12. Their wives are foolish,<br/>their children full of malice,<br/>and their offspring accursed.</p>

<p class="v">13. Therefore happy is the barren woman who is undefiled,<br/>whose bed has not known transgression!<br/>She shall have fruit when souls are visited.<br/>14. Happy too is the eunuch who with his hand has done no iniquity<br/>and has conceived no wicked thoughts against the Lord!<br/>He shall receive a choice reward for his faithfulness,<br/>and a most delightful lot in the temple of the Lord.<br/>15. For the fruit of good labors is glorious,<br/>and the root of prudence does not perish.<br/><br/>16. But the children of adulterers will not come to their fullness,<br/>and the offspring of an unlawful bed will disappear.<br/>17. Even if their life is long, they will be counted as nothing,<br/>and their old age will in the end be without honor.<br/>18. If they die quickly, they will have no hope,<br/>nor any consolation on the day of judgment.<br/>19. For the unjust race always has a dreadful end.</p>

### Chapter 4 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Better is barrenness with virtue;<br/>its memory is immortal, for it is known both to God and to men.<br/>2. When it is present, it is imitated;<br/>when it is gone, it is missed;<br/>crowned in eternity, it triumphs,<br/>having won the victory in undefiled contests.</p>

<p class="v">3. But the numerous offspring of the wicked are of no use;<br/>sprung from bastard shoots, they will not put down deep roots,<br/>and will not establish themselves on a sure foundation.<br/>4. Even though they cover themselves for a time with green branches,<br/>fixed in the ground without firmness, they will be shaken by the wind,<br/>and uprooted by the violence of the storm.<br/>5. Their branches will be broken while still tender,<br/>their fruits are useless, too unripe to be eaten,<br/>and fit for nothing.<br/>6. For children born of unlawful unions<br/>are, when questioned, witnesses to the crime against their parents.</p>

<p class="v">7. But the just man, even if he dies before his time,<br/>finds rest.<br/>8. Honorable old age is not that which is given by long life;<br/>nor is it measured by the number of years.<br/>9. But understanding takes the place of gray hairs for man;<br/>and an unblemished life is the true measure of old age.<br/>10. Being pleasing to God, he was loved by him,<br/>and, as he was living among sinners, he was translated.<br/>11. He was taken away lest malice should alter his understanding,<br/>or deceit pervert his soul.<br/>12. For the bewitchment of vice obscures the good,<br/>and the whirl of passion perverts a mind without malice.<br/>13. Having reached perfection in a short time,<br/>he fulfilled a long career.<br/>14. For his soul was pleasing to the Lord;<br/>therefore the Lord made haste to take him out of the midst of iniquity.<br/>15. The peoples see this and understand nothing of it,<br/>not laying it to heart<br/>that the grace of God and his mercy are with his elect,<br/>and that he watches over his holy ones.<br/>16. But the just man who dies condemns<br/>the wicked who survive,<br/>and youth so quickly brought to perfection condemns<br/>the long old age of the unjust man.<br/>17. They will see the end of the wise man,<br/>but without understanding God's designs concerning him,<br/>nor why the Lord placed him in safety.<br/>18. They will see, and mock,<br/>but the Lord will laugh at them;<br/>19. and after that they will be a corpse without honor,<br/>they will be among the dead in reproach forever.<br/>The Lord will shatter them, and, reduced to silence, cast them down;<br/>he will shake them from their foundations,<br/>and they will be utterly destroyed;<br/>they will be in anguish,<br/>and their memory will perish.</p>

<p class="v">20. They will come full of dread at the thought of their sins,<br/>and their crimes, rising up before them, will accuse them.</p>

### Chapter 5 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Then the just man will stand with great confidence,<br/>before the face of those who persecuted him,<br/>and who despised his labors.<br/>2. At this sight, they will be shaken with horrible dread,<br/>they will be stupefied at the revelation of salvation.<br/>3. They will say, full of regret,<br/>and groaning in the anguish of their heart:<br/><br/>"This, then, is he who was once the object of our mockery,<br/>and the target of our insults!<br/>4. Fools that we were, we regarded his life as madness,<br/>and his end as a disgrace.<br/>5. How is he counted among the children of God,<br/>and his lot among the saints?<br/>6. We have therefore strayed from the way of truth;<br/>the light of justice has not shone upon us,<br/>and the sun has not risen for us.<br/>7. We have taken our fill in the way of iniquity and ruin,<br/>we have walked through pathless deserts,<br/>and we have not known the way of the Lord.<br/>8. What good has pride done us,<br/>and what has wealth with boasting brought us?<br/>9. All these things have passed away like a shadow,<br/>like a rumor that flees;<br/>10. like a ship that cleaves the stirred wave,<br/>of whose passage no trace can be found,<br/>nor the mark of its keel amid the waves;<br/>11. or like a bird crossing the air,<br/>of whose path no vestige is found;<br/>but it beats the light air with the strokes of its wings,<br/>tears through it with a powerful thrust,<br/>makes itself a path by beating its wings;<br/>then, no sign of its passage is seen;<br/>12. or as, when an arrow has been shot toward its mark,<br/>the air it has cleft closes again at once upon itself,<br/>and one no longer knows by what way it passed:<br/>13. So we ourselves were born and ceased to be,<br/>and we have no trace of virtue to show;<br/>and in our iniquity we have been cut off."<br/><br/>14. For the hope of the wicked is like down that the wind carries off,<br/>like the light frost that a storm scatters,<br/>like smoke that a breath disperses,<br/>like the memory of a guest of a day that vanishes.<br/><br/>15. But the just live forever;<br/>their reward is with the Lord,<br/>and the Almighty cares for them.<br/>16. Therefore they will receive from the hand of the Lord<br/>the magnificent kingdom and the splendid diadem;<br/>for he will protect them with his right hand, with his arm,<br/>he will cover them as with a shield.<br/><br/>17. He will take up his zeal as armor,<br/>and will arm creation to avenge itself on his enemies.</p>

<p class="v">18. He will put on justice as a breastplate,<br/>and take sincere judgment for a helmet.<br/>19. He will take holiness as an impregnable shield.<br/>20. Of his inexorable wrath he will make a sharp sword,<br/>and the universe will fight with him against the foolish.<br/>21. Well-aimed shafts of lightning will go forth,<br/>and, from the midst of the clouds, as from a well-bent bow,<br/>will fly to the appointed mark.<br/>22. His wrath, like a catapult, will hurl a mass of hail;<br/>the water of the sea will rise up against them,<br/>and the rivers will rush upon them in fury.<br/>23. The breath of the divine power will rise up against them,<br/>and scatter them like a whirlwind:<br/>and thus iniquity will make a desert of the whole earth,<br/>and malice will overturn the thrones of the mighty.</p>

### Chapter 6 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Listen, then, O kings, and understand;<br/>hear this instruction, you who judge the ends of the earth.<br/>2. Give ear, you who rule over multitudes,<br/>who are proud of commanding throngs of peoples.<br/>3. Know that your strength was given you by the Lord,<br/>and your power by the Most High,<br/>who will examine your works and search out your thoughts.<br/><br/>4. Because, being ministers of his kingship,<br/>you did not judge with uprightness,<br/>nor observe the law, nor walk according to the will of God;<br/>5. terrible and swift, he will fall upon you,<br/>for a severe judgment awaits those who command.<br/>6. To the lowly, pardon is granted out of pity;<br/>but the mighty will be mightily chastised.<br/>7. The sovereign of all will draw back before no one,<br/>he will not be checked by respect for any greatness;<br/>for he made both great and small,<br/>and he takes care of both alike.<br/>8. But the mighty will be subjected to a more rigorous trial.<br/><br/>9. It is to you, then, O kings, that my words are addressed,<br/>that you may learn wisdom and not fall.<br/>10. Those who keep the holy laws in holiness will be sanctified,<br/>and those who have learned them will have an answer ready.<br/>11. Set your delight, then, in my words,<br/>desire them, and you will receive instruction.</p>

<p class="v">12. Wisdom is radiant, and her brightness does not fade;<br/>she is easily seen by those who love her,<br/>easily found by those who seek her.<br/>13. She anticipates those who desire her,<br/>and shows herself to them first.<br/>14. He who rises early to seek her will have no trouble:<br/>he will find her sitting at his gate.<br/>15. For to think upon her is the perfection of prudence,<br/>and whoever keeps watch for her sake will soon be free of care;<br/>16. she herself goes about seeking those who are worthy of her,<br/>she shows herself to them kindly in their paths,<br/>and assists them in all their designs.<br/><br/>17. For her surest beginning is the desire for instruction.<br/>18. And the care of instruction leads to love,<br/>love brings about obedience to her laws,<br/>obedience to her laws secures immortality,<br/>19. and immortality brings us near to God.<br/>20. Thus the desire for wisdom leads to kingship.<br/>21. If, then, O kings of the peoples,<br/>you set your delight in thrones and scepters,<br/>honor wisdom, that you may reign forever.</p>

<p class="v">22. But what wisdom is, and her origin, I shall set forth,<br/>without hiding from you the mysteries of God.<br/>I shall trace her back to the beginning of creation,<br/>I shall bring to light what concerns her,<br/>and I shall not depart from the truth.<br/>23. Far be it from me to keep company with consuming envy!<br/>It has nothing in common with wisdom.<br/>24. A multitude of the wise is the salvation of the earth,<br/>and a wise king the prosperity of his people.<br/>25. Receive, then, instruction from my words,<br/>and you will profit by it.</p>

### Chapter 7 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. I myself am a mortal, like all men,<br/>and a descendant of the first man who was formed of earth.<br/>2. I was fashioned as to the flesh in my mother's womb,<br/>taking shape for ten months in blood, from the seed of man, during the repose of sleep.<br/>3. I too, at my birth, breathed the air common to all,<br/>I fell upon the same earth,<br/>and, like everyone's, my first cry was a wail.<br/>4. I was reared in swaddling clothes and with unceasing care.<br/>5. No king has had any other beginning of existence.<br/>6. There is for all but one single way<br/>of entering life and of leaving it.<br/><br/>7. Therefore I prayed, and prudence was given me;<br/>I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.<br/>8. I preferred her to scepters and thrones,<br/>and I reckoned riches as nothing beside her.</p>

<p class="v">9. I did not think the most precious stones her equal,<br/>for all the gold of the world is, beside her, but a little sand,<br/>and silver, next to her, must be reckoned as mud.<br/>10. I loved her more than health and beauty;<br/>I chose to possess her rather than the light,<br/>for her radiance never goes out.<br/>11. With her came to me all good things,<br/>and countless riches are in her hands.<br/>12. And I rejoiced in all these good things,<br/>for wisdom brings them with her;<br/>yet I did not know that she was their mother.<br/>13. I learned her without dissembling,<br/>I share her without envy, and I do not hide her treasures.<br/>14. For she is an inexhaustible treasure to men;<br/>those who make use of her share in the friendship of God,<br/>commended to him by the gifts they have gained through instruction.</p>

<p class="v">15. May God grant me to speak of her as I would wish,<br/>and to conceive thoughts worthy of the gifts I have received!<br/>For it is he who guides wisdom,<br/>and who directs the wise.<br/>16. We are in his hand, we and our words,<br/>and all prudence and skill.<br/>17. It is he who gave me true knowledge of the things that are,<br/>to make known to me the structure of the universe<br/>and the properties of the elements,<br/>18. the beginning, the end, and the midst of times,<br/>the alternating cycles of the sun, the vicissitudes of the seasons,<br/>19. the cycles of the years and the position of the stars,<br/>20. the nature of animals and the instincts of beasts,<br/>the power of spirits and the reasonings of men,<br/>the different kinds of plants and the virtues of roots.<br/>21. All that is hidden and all that is manifest, I have learned;<br/>22. for wisdom, the artisan of all things, taught it to me.<br/><br/>In her, indeed, there is a spirit that is intelligent, holy,<br/>unique, manifold, immaterial,<br/>active, penetrating, undefiled,<br/>unerring, unharmed, loving the good, keen,<br/>knowing no obstacle, beneficent,<br/>23. kind to men, steadfast, sure, untroubled,<br/>all-powerful, overseeing all things,<br/>penetrating all spirits,<br/>the intelligent, the pure, and the subtlest.</p>

<p class="v">24. For wisdom is more agile than any motion;<br/>she penetrates and pervades all things, because of her purity.<br/><br/>25. She is a breath of the power of God,<br/>a pure emanation of the glory of the Almighty;<br/>so nothing defiled can fall upon her.<br/>26. She is the brightness of eternal light,<br/>the spotless mirror of the working of God,<br/>and the image of his goodness.<br/><br/>27. Being one, she can do all things;<br/>remaining the same, she renews all things;<br/>passing down through the ages into holy souls,<br/>she makes of them friends of God and prophets.<br/>28. For God loves none but him who dwells with wisdom.<br/><br/>29. For she is more beautiful than the sun,<br/>and than the harmonious arrangement of the stars.<br/>Compared with light, she takes precedence over it;<br/>30. for light gives way to night,<br/>but evil does not prevail against wisdom.</p>

### Chapter 8 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Wisdom reaches mightily from one end of the world to the other,<br/>and orders all things sweetly.</p>

<p class="v">2. I loved her and sought her from my youth;<br/>I sought to take her for my bride,<br/>and I was enamored of her beauty.<br/>3.
