She displays the glory of her origin<br/>in that she dwells with God,<br/>and the master of all things loves her.<br/><br/>4. For it is she who initiates men into the knowledge of God,<br/>and who chooses among his works.<br/>5. If riches are a desirable good in this life,<br/>what is richer than wisdom, who works all things?<br/>6. If prudence presides over labor,<br/>who more than wisdom is the artisan of all that exists?<br/>7. Does one love justice?<br/>The labors of wisdom produce the virtues;<br/>she teaches temperance and prudence,<br/>justice and fortitude,<br/>which are the most useful things to men in life.<br/>8. Does one desire wide knowledge?<br/>She knows the past and conjectures the future;<br/>she grasps subtle discourses and resolves riddles;<br/>she knows beforehand signs and wonders;<br/>she knows the outcomes of times and seasons.<br/><br/>9. Therefore I resolved to take her as the companion of my life,<br/>knowing that she would be for me a counselor of all good,<br/>and a comfort in my cares and sorrows.</p>

<p class="v">10. Through her, I told myself, I shall have glory among the assemblies,<br/>and, though still young, honor among the elders.<br/>11. My keenness will be recognized in judgments,<br/>and before me the great will stand in admiration.<br/>12. If I am silent, they will wait for me to speak;<br/>if I speak, they will keep their eyes fixed on me,<br/>and if I go on speaking, they will lay their hand upon their mouth.<br/>13. Through her, I shall obtain immortality,<br/>and I shall leave to posterity an everlasting memory.<br/>14. I shall govern peoples,<br/>and foreign nations will be subject to me.<br/>15. On hearing of me, redoubtable kings will fear me;<br/>I shall show myself good among the people, and valiant in war.<br/>16. On returning to my house, I shall rest beside her;<br/>for her company causes no bitterness,<br/>nor her converse any weariness,<br/>but contentment and joy.<br/><br/>17. Pondering these thoughts within myself,<br/>and reflecting in my heart<br/>that immortality is the fruit of union with wisdom,<br/>18. that there is a noble delight in her friendship,<br/>and inexhaustible riches in the works of her hands,<br/>that one gains prudence by constant intercourse with her,<br/>and glory by sharing in her conversation:<br/>I went about on every side, seeking the means to have her with me.</p>

<p class="v">19. I was a child of good natural gifts,<br/>and I had received a good soul as my portion;<br/>20. or rather, being good, I came into a body undefiled.<br/>21. But, knowing that I could not obtain wisdom unless God gave it to me,<br/>— and it was already a mark of prudence to know from whom this gift comes, —<br/>I turned to the Lord, and called upon him,<br/>and said to him from the depths of my heart:</p>
### Chapter 9 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. "God of the fathers, Lord of mercy,<br/>who made the universe by your word,<br/>2. and who, by your wisdom, established man<br/>to have dominion over all the creatures you have made,<br/>3. to govern the world in holiness and justice,<br/>and to exercise dominion in uprightness of heart,<br/>4. give me the Wisdom that sits beside your throne,<br/>and do not reject me from the number of your children.<br/><br/>5. For I am your servant and the son of your handmaid,<br/>a weak man, of short life,<br/>and little able to understand judgment and the laws.<br/>6. Should anyone be perfect among the children of men,<br/>if he lacks the wisdom that comes from you, he will be counted as nothing.</p>

<p class="v">7. You chose me to reign over your people,<br/>and to judge your sons and your daughters.<br/>8. And you told me to build a temple on your holy mountain,<br/>and an altar in the city where you dwell,<br/>after the pattern of the holy tabernacle that you prepared from the beginning.<br/><br/>9. With you is Wisdom, who knows your works,<br/>who was there when you made the universe,<br/>and who knows what is pleasing in your eyes,<br/>and what is right according to your commandments.<br/>10. Send her from your most holy heavens, send her from the throne of your glory,<br/>that she may assist me in my labors,<br/>and that I may know what is pleasing to you.<br/>11. For she knows and understands all things,<br/>and she will guide me prudently in my works,<br/>and will guard me by her glory.<br/>12. And so my works will be pleasing to you,<br/>I will govern your people with justice,<br/>and I will be worthy of my father's throne.<br/><br/>13. For what man can know the counsel of God,<br/>or who can grasp what the Lord wills?<br/>14. The thoughts of men are uncertain,<br/>and our opinions are but chance.<br/>15. For the body, subject to corruption, weighs down the soul,<br/>and its earthly dwelling burdens the mind full of many thoughts.<br/>16. We can scarcely guess at what is on earth,<br/>and we find with difficulty what is at hand:<br/>who then has grasped what is in heaven?<br/>17. Who has known your will, unless you gave him Wisdom,<br/>and sent your Holy Spirit from on high?<br/>18. Thus were made straight the paths of those on earth,<br/>and men learned what is pleasing to you,<br/>and were saved by Wisdom."</p>

### Chapter 10 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. It was Wisdom who kept watch over the first man formed by God,<br/>to be the father of mankind, the only one created;<br/>2. she brought him out of his sin,<br/>and gave him the power to govern all creatures.</p>

<p class="v">3. Having withdrawn from her in his anger,<br/>the unjust one perished by his fratricidal fury.<br/><br/>4. When, because of him, the earth was flooded, Wisdom saved it,<br/>guiding the just man upon a worthless piece of wood.<br/><br/>5. When the nations were confounded in their common iniquity,<br/>Wisdom recognized the just man and kept him blameless before God,<br/>and preserved him unshaken against his tenderness for his son.<br/><br/>6. It was she who, amid the ruin of the wicked, saved the just man,<br/>who fled far from the fire that fell upon the five cities.<br/>7. In witness of their wickedness,<br/>that desolate land continues to smoke,<br/>the trees bear their fruit out of season;<br/>a monument to an unbelieving soul, a pillar of salt stands there still.<br/>8. Having disregarded Wisdom,<br/>they were not only deprived of the knowledge of good,<br/>but they left to the living a monument of their folly,<br/>so that their crimes could not fall into oblivion.<br/>9. But Wisdom delivered her faithful ones from misfortune.<br/><br/>10. It was she who guided by straight paths<br/>the just man fleeing his brother's wrath,<br/>who showed him the kingdom of God,<br/>and gave him knowledge of holy things;<br/>she enriched him in his hard labors,<br/>and made his toil fruitful.<br/>11. She assisted him against greedy oppressors,<br/>and caused him to gain riches.<br/>12. She guarded him against his enemies,<br/>and protected him from those who laid snares for him;<br/>she gave him victory in a hard struggle,<br/>to teach him that piety is more powerful than all things.<br/><br/>13. She did not abandon the just man when he was sold,<br/>but preserved him from sin;<br/>14. she went down with him into the pit,<br/>and did not leave him in chains,<br/>until she had procured for him the royal scepter,<br/>and power over his oppressors;<br/>she convicted of falsehood those who had accused him,<br/>and gave him eternal glory.</p>

<p class="v">15. She delivered from the nations that oppressed them<br/>the holy people and the blameless race.<br/>16. She entered into the soul of the servant of God,<br/>and, by signs and wonders,<br/>she stood up to fearsome kings.<br/>17. She rendered to the saints the wages of their labors,<br/>she led them by a road strewn with wonders,<br/>and was for them a shade by day,<br/>and as the light of the stars by night.</p>

<p class="v">18. She made them cross the Red Sea,<br/>and led them through the great waters.<br/>19. She engulfed their enemies,<br/>then cast them up again from the depths of the abyss.<br/>20. Therefore the just took the spoils of the wicked,<br/>and sang your holy name, Lord,<br/>and praised together your hand that fought for them.<br/>21. For Wisdom opened the mouths of the mute<br/>and made the tongues of infants eloquent.</p>

### Chapter 11 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. She made their works prosper by the hand of a holy prophet.<br/>2. They journeyed through an uninhabited wilderness,<br/>and pitched their tents in trackless regions.<br/>3. They withstood their enemies,<br/>and took vengeance on their adversaries.<br/>4. They suffered thirst and called upon you,<br/>and water was given them from a steep rock,<br/>and from a stone, the quenching of their thirst.</p>

<p class="v">5. What had been the punishment of their enemies<br/>became for them a blessing in their distress.<br/>6. For indeed, while the waters of an unfailing river<br/>were fouled with impure blood,<br/>7. in punishment for the decree that put the children to death,<br/>you gave your faithful ones, against all hope, abundant water,<br/>8. showing them thereby, by the thirst they then felt,<br/>with what punishment you struck your adversaries.<br/>9. After this trial, though chastened with mercy,<br/>they learned how the wicked were tormented when judged in wrath.<br/>10. You tested the one as a father who warns,<br/>and you chastised the others as a stern king who condemns.<br/>11. Whether absent or present, they were equally tormented.<br/>12. A twofold grief seized them, and they groaned at the memory of what had happened.<br/>13. For when they learned that their own torments<br/>turned to the advantage of the fugitives, they recognized the hand of the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">14. He whom they had once exposed and rejected with scorn,<br/>they admired at the end of events,<br/>when they had suffered a thirst quite different from that of the just.<br/><br/>15. In punishment for the extravagant thoughts of their perversity,<br/>which led them astray and made them worship<br/>irrational reptiles and vile animals,<br/>you sent against them, as chastisement, a multitude of senseless beasts:<br/>16. to teach them that one is punished by the very things by which one sins.<br/>17. It was not difficult for your almighty hand,<br/>which made the world out of formless matter,<br/>to send against them a multitude of bears or fierce lions,<br/>18. or newly created beasts, unknown and full of fury,<br/>breathing fiery vapor, exhaling foul smoke,<br/>or flashing terrible lightning from their eyes,<br/>19. able, not only to kill by a wound,<br/>but to strike dead with fear by their mere appearance.<br/>20. And even without that, they could have perished by a mere breath,<br/>pursued by justice,<br/>and scattered by the breath of your power.<br/><br/>But you have ordered all things by measure,<br/>by number and by weight.<br/>21. For sovereign power is always at your command,<br/>and who then could resist the strength of your arm?<br/>22. The whole world is before you as the grain that tips the scale,<br/>as a drop of morning dew that falls upon the earth.<br/>23. But because you can do all things, you have mercy on all,<br/>and you close your eyes to the sins of men so that they may repent.<br/>24. For you love all created things,<br/>and you hate nothing that you have made;<br/>if you had hated a thing, you would not have made it.<br/>25. And how could a thing subsist, if you did not will it,<br/>or be preserved, if you had not called it into being?<br/>26. But you spare all things, because all things are yours,<br/>Lord, lover of souls.</p>

### Chapter 12 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. For your incorruptible spirit is in all things.<br/>2. Therefore you chastise with moderation those who fall,<br/>and, when they sin, you warn them and rebuke them,<br/>so that, forsaking their malice, they may believe in you, Lord.</p>

<p class="v">3. You held in hatred the ancient inhabitants of your holy land,<br/>4. because they gave themselves over to detestable works of magic,<br/>to impious rites,<br/>5. and to the cruel murder of children,<br/>devouring human flesh and drinking blood.<br/>These initiates of abominable mysteries,<br/>6. these parents who murdered defenseless beings,<br/>you willed to destroy by the hand of our fathers,</p>

<p class="v">7. so that this land which you honor above all others<br/>might receive a worthy colony of the children of God.<br/>8. Nevertheless, since they were men, you showed clemency,<br/>and you sent, as forerunners of your army,<br/>hornets to make them perish little by little.<br/><br/>9. Not that it was impossible for you to bring down these impious ones,<br/>in pitched battle, under the hand of the just,<br/>or to exterminate them at a single stroke by fierce beasts,<br/>or by a stern decree;<br/>10. but, by executing your judgments by degrees,<br/>you gave them room to repent,<br/>though you knew well that they were a perverse race,<br/>that their malice was innate, and that their thoughts would never change;<br/>11. for they were a race accursed from the beginning.<br/><br/>Nor was it out of fear of anyone<br/>that you showed yourself indulgent toward their sins.<br/>12. For who could say to you: "What have you done?"<br/>Who could oppose your judgment?<br/>Who would accuse you of destroying the nations you have made?<br/>Who would come to plead against you the cause of impious men?<br/>13. For there is no other God besides you,<br/>who takes care of all things,<br/>to show that you do not judge unjustly.<br/>14. There is neither king nor tyrant who can rise up against you,<br/>in defense of those whom you have chastised.<br/>15. But, being just, you order all things with justice,<br/>and you regard it as contrary to your power<br/>to condemn one who does not deserve punishment.<br/><br/>16. For your power is the foundation of justice,<br/>and it is because you are the Lord of all<br/>that you deal indulgently with all.<br/>17. It is to those who do not believe in your almighty power<br/>that you show your strength,<br/>and you confound the boldness of those who do know it.<br/>18. Master of your strength, you judge with gentleness,<br/>and you govern us with great indulgence,<br/>for power is with you whenever you will it.<br/><br/>19. By acting thus, you have taught your people<br/>that the just man must be humane,<br/>and you have inspired in your children the joyful hope<br/>that, if they sin, you grant them time to repent.<br/>20. If indeed you have punished, with such restraint and indulgence,<br/>the enemies of your servants, though they deserved death,<br/>giving them time and opportunity to turn from their malice,<br/>21. with what circumspection do you judge your own children,<br/>whose fathers received from you oaths and covenants,<br/>joined to magnificent promises!<br/>22. When you correct us, you scourge our enemies a thousand times more severely,<br/>to teach us, when we judge, to think of your goodness,<br/>and, when we are judged, to hope in your mercy.<br/><br/>23. That is why you tormented, by their own abominations,<br/>the unjust who spent their lives in folly.</p>

<p class="v">24. For they had sunk so deep into the ways of error,<br/>that they regarded as gods the vilest of animals,<br/>having let themselves be deceived like senseless children.<br/>25. So, as to senseless children,<br/>you sent them first a derisory punishment.<br/>26. But those whom a derisory correction did not amend will suffer a punishment worthy of God.<br/>27. Chastised by the very things they took for gods,<br/>they were exasperated by their sufferings,<br/>and, seeing Him whom they had once refused to know,<br/>they acknowledged him as the true God; that is why the supreme condemnation fell upon them.</p>

### Chapter 13 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Senseless by nature are all the men who have not known God,<br/>and who, from the visible good things, were not able to see Him who is,<br/>nor, by considering his works, to recognize the Maker.<br/>2. But they have looked upon fire, wind, the moving air,<br/>the circle of the stars, the raging water, the torches of heaven,<br/>as gods governing the universe.<br/><br/>3. If, charmed by their beauty, they took these creatures for gods,<br/>let them know how much the Master surpasses them;<br/>for it is the very Author of beauty who made them.<br/>4. And if they admired their power and their effects,<br/>let them conclude from this how much more powerful is he who made them.<br/>5. For the greatness and beauty of created things<br/>make known, by analogy, Him who is their Creator.<br/><br/>6. These, however, incur a lesser reproach;<br/>for perhaps they go astray<br/>while seeking God and wishing to find him.<br/>7. Occupied with his works, they make them the object of their inquiries,<br/>and are guided by appearances, so beautiful is what they see!<br/>8. On the other hand, they are not excusable either;<br/>9. for, if they acquired enough knowledge<br/>to come to know the world,<br/>how did they not more readily come to know its Master?</p>

<p class="v">10. But they are truly wretched,<br/>and they place their hope in lifeless objects,<br/>those who have called gods the works of men's hands,<br/>gold and silver wrought with art,<br/>figures of animals or a useless stone,</p>

<p class="v">the work of an ancient hand.<br/>11. Behold, a craftsman has cut down a tree easy to work;<br/>he skillfully strips off all its bark,<br/>and, fashioning it with skill,<br/>makes of it a useful piece of furniture for the service of life.<br/>12. His work finished, he uses what remains<br/>to cook his food, and satisfies his hunger.<br/>13. As for the last scraps, which are no longer of any use,<br/>the crooked wood full of knots,<br/>he takes it, carves it to occupy his leisure,<br/>and, by skillful work, gives it a shape:<br/>he makes it resemble a man.<br/>14. Or else he makes of it the image of some vile animal,<br/>paints it with vermilion, covers its surface with a red color,<br/>and hides every blemish under a coat of paint.<br/>15. Then, having prepared a fitting dwelling for it,<br/>he sets it against the wall and fastens it with iron.<br/>16. He takes great care that it not fall,<br/>knowing that the god cannot help itself,<br/>for it is only a statue that needs support.<br/><br/>17. Yet he prays to it concerning his possessions,<br/>his marriages, and his children,<br/>and he is not ashamed to speak to that which has no soul.<br/>He asks health from that which has no strength,<br/>18. life from that which is dead,<br/>help from that which can render no service,<br/>a safe journey from that which cannot use its own feet.<br/>19. To secure his profits, his undertakings, the success of his work,<br/>he asks energy from that which has the feeblest hands of all.</p>

### Chapter 14 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Here is another who thinks of putting to sea,<br/>and prepares to travel upon the raging waves:<br/>he invokes a wood more fragile still than the vessel that carries him;<br/>2. for this vessel was invented by the passion for gain,<br/>and it was the skill of the craftsman that built it.<br/>3. But, O Father, it is your providence that steers it,<br/>you who have even opened a path in the sea,<br/>and a safe road amid the waves,<br/>4. showing thereby that you can deliver from every peril,<br/>so that, even without skill in navigation, one may put out to sea.<br/>You do not want the works of your wisdom to remain useless;<br/>that is why men, entrusting their lives to fragile wood,<br/>5. cross the waves on a raft, and escape death.<br/>6. And in ancient times, when the proud giants were perishing,<br/>the hope of the world escaped upon a boat,<br/>and, steered by your hand, left to the world the seed of a posterity.<br/>7. For blessed is the wood that serves a righteous use.<br/><br/>8. But the idol, work of men's hands,<br/>is accursed, both it and its maker:<br/>the latter because he made it,<br/>the former because, being perishable, it is called a god;<br/>9. for God hates equally the impious man and his impiety,<br/>10. and the work and the worker will be alike punished.</p>

<p class="v">11. Therefore the idols of the nations will be visited with punishment,<br/>because, being creatures of God, they have become an abomination,<br/>a stumbling block for the souls of men,<br/>a snare for the feet of fools.</p>

<p class="v">12. The idea of making idols was the beginning of fornication,<br/>and their invention brought about the ruin of life.<br/>13. There were none at the beginning, and there will not always be any.<br/>14. It was the vanity of men that introduced them into the world;<br/>thus their swift end is decreed in the divine mind.<br/><br/>15. A father overwhelmed by a premature grief<br/>fashioned the image of a son too soon taken from him;<br/>and that child who was dead, he began to honor as a god,<br/>and he instituted among the people of his household<br/>pious rites and ceremonies.<br/>16. Then this impious custom, growing firm with time,<br/>was observed as a law,<br/>and, by order of princes, statues were worshiped.<br/><br/>17. When men could not honor them face to face,<br/>because they dwelt too far away,<br/>they pictured their distant likeness,<br/>and fashioned a visible image of the venerated king,<br/>so as to render to the absent one homage<br/>as eager as if he had been present.<br/>18. And, for the success of this superstition, those who did not know him<br/>were drawn to it by the ambition of the artist.<br/>19. He indeed, desirous of pleasing the powerful master,<br/>spent all his art in embellishing the portrait.<br/>20. And the crowd of men, seduced by the elegance of the work,<br/>looked upon as a god him who had lately been honored as a man.</p>

<p class="v">21. It was a snare for the living that men,<br/>under the influence of misfortune or tyranny,<br/>should have given to stone or wood the incommunicable name.<br/>22. Soon it was not enough for them to err in the notion of God;<br/>living in a state of violent strife, as a result of their ignorance,<br/>they called such evils by the name of peace.<br/><br/>23. Celebrating murderous rites of their children<br/>or clandestine mysteries,<br/>and giving themselves over to the unbridled debaucheries of strange rites,<br/>24. they have kept no modesty either in their life or in their marriages.<br/>One kills another by treachery, or wrongs him by adultery.<br/>25. Everywhere it is a mingling of blood and murder, of theft and deceit,</p>

<p class="v">of corruption and unfaithfulness, of revolt and perjury,<br/>26. of persecution of good people, of forgetfulness of benefits received,<br/>of defilement of souls, of crimes against nature,<br/>of instability in unions, of adultery and shamelessness.<br/>27. For the worship of nameless idols<br/>is the beginning, the cause, and the end of every evil.<br/>28. Their amusements are mad revelries,<br/>and their oracles, lies;<br/>they live in injustice and perjure themselves without scruple.<br/>29. Since they place their trust in lifeless idols, they expect no harm from their false oaths.<br/><br/>30. But a just punishment will strike them for this twofold crime:<br/>because, clinging to idols,<br/>they held perverse thoughts about God,<br/>and because they made deceitful oaths against justice,<br/>in contempt of the most holy laws.<br/>31. It is not the power of the idols by which they swore,<br/>it is the punishment due to sinners<br/>that always overtakes the transgression of the impious.</p>

### Chapter 15 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. But you, O our God, are good, faithful, and patient,<br/>and you govern all things with mercy.<br/>2. Even when we sin, we are yours,<br/>knowing your power;<br/>but we do not wish to sin,<br/>for we know that we are counted among your own.<br/>3. To know you is perfect righteousness,<br/>and to know your power is the root of immortality.<br/>4. We have not been led astray by the invention of a baneful art,<br/>nor by a figure daubed with various colors,<br/>the vain work of a painter:<br/>5. objects whose appearance excites the passion of the fool,<br/>who falls in love with the lifeless shape of an image without life.<br/>6. Loving evil, they are worthy of such hopes,<br/>both those who make them and those who love or worship them.</p>

<p class="v">7. Indeed, here is a potter who laboriously kneads the soft clay;<br/>he shapes each vessel for our use,<br/>and from the same clay he makes<br/>vessels intended for noble uses,<br/>and others for wholly contrary uses,<br/>without in any way distinguishing for what use each of them will serve:<br/>it is the potter who is the judge of that.<br/>8. Then, by an impious labor, from the same clay,<br/>he fashions a vain divinity,<br/>he who, though lately made of clay himself,<br/>will soon return to the place from which he was taken,<br/>when his soul, which had been lent to him, is demanded back.</p>

<p class="v">9. Yet he is not troubled that his strength is wearing out,<br/>nor that his life is short;<br/>but he vies with those who work gold and silver,<br/>he imitates those who work bronze,<br/>and takes pride in producing deceptive figures.<br/>10. His heart is like ashes,<br/>his hope is viler than earth,<br/>and his life is of less worth than clay.<br/>11. For he fails to know him who made him,<br/>who breathed into him an active soul,<br/>and put in him a breath of life.<br/>12. He looks upon our existence as a pastime,<br/>life as a market where people gather for gain;<br/>for, they say, "one must acquire by every means, even by crime."<br/>13. For that man well knows that he is more guilty than all others,<br/>who, from the same clay, fashions fragile vessels and idols.</p>

<p class="v">14. But they are all utterly senseless,<br/>and more wretched than the soul of a child,<br/>the enemies of your people who hold it in oppression!<br/><br/>15. For they have regarded as gods all the idols of the nations,<br/>which can use neither their eyes to see,<br/>nor their nostrils to breathe the air,<br/>nor their ears to hear,<br/>nor the fingers of their hands to touch,<br/>and whose feet are unable to walk.<br/>16. It was a man who made them,<br/>and it is one to whom breath was lent who fashioned them.<br/>There is no man who can make a god like himself,<br/>17. for, being mortal, he makes with his impious hands only a dead work;<br/>he is worth more than the objects he worships,<br/>for at least he has life, and they never had it.<br/><br/>18. They render worship to the most hateful animals,<br/>which, judged by their stupidity, are worse than the rest.<br/>19. There is nothing good in them to awaken affection,<br/>as at the sight of other animals;<br/>they escape the praise of God and his blessing.</p>

### Chapter 16 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Therefore they were justly chastised by like creatures,<br/>and tormented by a multitude of beasts.</p>

<p class="v">2. In place of these plagues, you granted benefits to your people,<br/>and, to satisfy their ardent desire, you prepared for them a marvelous food,<br/>quails for their nourishment:<br/>3. so that the ones, despite their desire to eat,<br/>at the repugnant sight of the insects sent against them,<br/>came to loathe even their natural appetite,<br/>while the others, after a brief deprivation,<br/>tasted a new food.<br/><br/>4. For it was fitting that an inescapable want<br/>should afflict the former, the oppressors,<br/>and that it should only be shown to the others<br/>how their enemies were being tormented.<br/>5. For indeed, when these were suffering from the fury of cruel beasts,<br/>and were perishing under the bite of writhing serpents,<br/>your wrath did not last to the end;<br/>6. they were troubled for a moment, for their correction,<br/>and they had a sign of salvation,<br/>to remind them of the precepts of your law.<br/>7. For he who turned toward it was healed,<br/>not by the object he had before his eyes,<br/>but by you, who are the savior of all.<br/><br/>8. But by this you also taught our enemies<br/>that it is you who deliver from every evil.<br/>9. Indeed, the bite of locusts and gnats destroyed them,<br/>and no means was found to save their lives,<br/>because they deserved to be punished in this way.<br/>10. Your children were not overcome by the fangs of venomous serpents,<br/>for your mercy came to their aid and healed them.<br/>11. It was so that your words might come back to their memory<br/>that they were wounded, and promptly healed,<br/>lest, coming to forget them entirely,<br/>they be excluded from your benefits.<br/>12. It was neither an herb nor a medicine that healed them,<br/>but your word, Lord, which heals all things.<br/>13. For you have power over life and death;<br/>you lead down to the gates of the abode of the dead and bring back up again.<br/>14. Man, in his wickedness, can indeed cause death,<br/>but cannot bring back the spirit once it has departed,<br/>nor free the soul that Sheol has received.</p>

<p class="v">15. But it is impossible to escape your hand.<br/><br/>16. The impious who claimed not to know you<br/>have been scourged by the strength of your arm;<br/>extraordinary waters, hail,<br/>and relentless rains tormented them,<br/>and fire consumed them.<br/>17. What was most strange was that, in the water which quenches all things,<br/>the fire burned only the more fiercely,<br/>for the universe fights for the just.</p>

<p class="v">18. At times the flame grew gentle,<br/>so that the animals sent against the impious would not be consumed,<br/>and that these, at this sight, might recognize<br/>that a judgment of God was pursuing them.<br/>19. At other times it burned in the very midst of the water,<br/>with greater force than the nature of fire allows,<br/>so as to destroy all the produce of an impious nation.<br/><br/>20. Instead, you fed your people with the food of angels,<br/>and gave them from heaven, without labor, bread all prepared,<br/>affording every pleasure and suited to every taste.<br/>21. This substance, sent by you, showed the tenderness<br/>you have toward your children,<br/>and this bread, adapting itself to the desire of the one who ate it,<br/>changed into whatever he wished.<br/>22. Snow and ice withstood the violence of the fire without melting,<br/>so that they might know that the fire, which burned in the hail<br/>and flashed in the rain,<br/>was destroying the harvests of their enemies,<br/>23. and that it then forgot its own power,<br/>for the sustenance of the just.<br/>24. For creation, subject to you, its Creator,<br/>musters its energy to torment the wicked,<br/>and relaxes to procure the good of those who trust in you.<br/>25. That is why, bending then to all these changes,<br/>it was at the command of your grace, which nourishes all things,<br/>according to the will of those who were in need;<br/>26. so that your children, whom you love, Lord, might learn<br/>that it is not the different kinds of produce that nourish men,<br/>but that it is your word that preserves those who believe in you.<br/>27. For what resisted the destructive action of fire<br/>melted easily, warmed by the slightest ray of sun:<br/>28. to teach everyone that one must rise before the sun to give you thanks,<br/>and worship you at the break of day.<br/>29. As for the ungrateful, his hope will melt like winter ice,<br/>and will flow away like useless water.</p>

### Chapter 17 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. For your judgments are great and hard to explain;<br/>and so uninstructed souls have gone astray.<br/><br/>2. While the wicked had persuaded themselves<br/>that they could oppress the holy nation,<br/>bound by darkness and prisoners of a long night,<br/>shut in under their own roofs, they lay there,<br/>themselves fleeing your unceasing providence.<br/>3. While they imagined they remained hidden with their secret sins,<br/>beneath the thick veil of forgetfulness,<br/>they were scattered, seized with horrible dread,<br/>and terrified by phantoms.</p>

<p class="v">4. The recesses in which they shut themselves up did not preserve them from fear:<br/>frightful sounds echoed around them,<br/>and specters appeared to them with gloomy faces.<br/>5. There was no fire capable of giving light,<br/>and the bright flames of the stars<br/>could not illumine that horrible night.<br/>6. At times only there appeared to them<br/>a mass of fire, self-kindled and terrifying,<br/>and, terrified by this vision whose cause they could not see,<br/>they judged these apparitions to be more dreadful still.<br/>7. The mocking art of the magicians was exhausted,<br/>and their pretension to wisdom shamefully convicted of falsehood.<br/>8. They who boasted of driving away<br/>terror and confusion from sick souls,<br/>were themselves sick with a ridiculous fear.<br/>9. For, though there was nothing dreadful to frighten them,<br/>the passing of animals and the hissing of serpents terrified them;<br/>10. and they died of fright,<br/>refusing even to look upon that air from which no one can escape.<br/><br/>11. — For wickedness is cowardly,<br/>condemned as it is by its own testimony;<br/>hard pressed by conscience,<br/>it always exaggerates the evil.<br/>12. Fear, indeed, is nothing other<br/>than the abandonment of the help that reflection would bring.<br/>13. Hope being feebler within the heart,<br/>one is all the more terrified at not knowing the cause of one's torments. —<br/><br/>14. They, during that night of powerlessness,<br/>which came forth from the depths of powerless Sheol,<br/>sunk in the same sleep,<br/>15. were now shaken by terrifying specters,<br/>now overwhelmed by the failing of their souls;<br/>for a sudden and unexpected dread had spread over them.<br/>16. Likewise all the others, whoever they were, falling there without strength,<br/>were held as if shut up in a prison without bolts.<br/>17. The farmer, the shepherd,<br/>the workman busy at the hard labors of the field,<br/>surprised by the plague, were subjected to the same inescapable necessity;<br/>18. for all were bound by the same chain of darkness.<br/>The whistling wind,<br/>the melodious song of birds among the thick branches, the sound of waters rushing in their course,<br/>19. the crash of rolling stones,<br/>the unseen coursing of leaping animals,<br/>the howling of fierce beasts,<br/>the echo resounding in the hollows of the mountains,<br/>everything made them faint with terror.<br/><br/>20. For while the whole universe was lit with a brilliant light,<br/>and went about its labors without hindrance,<br/>21. over them alone stretched a heavy night,<br/>an image of the darkness that was to receive them;<br/>but they were an even heavier burden to themselves than the darkness.</p>

### Chapter 18 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Meanwhile a great light shone for your saints;<br/>the Egyptians heard their voice without seeing their faces,<br/>and, despite their own past sufferings, called them blessed.<br/>2. And because, after having been ill-treated,<br/>they did not take revenge, they thanked them,<br/>and asked their pardon for having treated them as enemies.<br/>3. In place of that darkness, you gave your saints<br/>a pillar of fire, a guide on an unknown road,<br/>a harmless sun for their glorious pilgrimage.<br/>4. Well did they deserve to be deprived of light,<br/>and to be imprisoned in darkness,<br/>those who held your children shut up,<br/>through whom the incorruptible light of your law<br/>was to be given to the world.</p>

<p class="v">5. They had resolved to destroy the children of the saints,<br/>and, one of these having been exposed and delivered,<br/>you took from them, as their punishment, the multitude of their own sons,<br/>and engulfed them all together in the raging waters.<br/><br/>6. That night had been made known beforehand to our fathers,<br/>so that, knowing well what promises they had believed,<br/>they might take better courage.<br/>7. And thus your people awaited<br/>the deliverance of the just and the destruction of its enemies.<br/>8. Just as you chastised our adversaries,<br/>so by the same stroke you glorified us by calling us to yourself.<br/>9. For indeed, the devout children of the saints offered their sacrifice in secret,<br/>and made together this divine compact:<br/>that the saints would share alike<br/>in the same blessings and the same dangers; —<br/>already singing beforehand the hymns of their fathers.<br/>10. In answer, there resounded the discordant cries of the enemies,<br/>and lamentations were heard for the children who were mourned.<br/>11. The slave and the master were punished with the same penalty,<br/>and the common man suffered the same thing as the king.<br/>12. They all alike had, in a single kind of death,<br/>dead beyond number,<br/>and the living did not suffice for the burials, for their noblest offspring had been destroyed in an instant.</p>

<p class="v">13. They had refused to believe, because of their sorceries;<br/>when the destruction of the firstborn came,<br/>they acknowledged that this people was a son of God.<br/><br/>14. While a profound silence enveloped the whole land,<br/>and night had reached the midpoint of its swift course,<br/>15. your all-powerful Word leapt down from heaven,<br/>from your royal throne, like a pitiless warrior,<br/>into the midst of a land doomed to destruction,<br/>16. bearing your irrevocable decree like a sharp sword;<br/>it stood there, filling all things with death;<br/>it touched heaven and stood upon the earth.<br/>17. At once visions of frightful dreams troubled them,<br/>and unexpected terrors fell upon them.<br/>18. Thrown to the ground here and there, half dead,<br/>they revealed the cause for which they were dying.<br/>19. For the dreams that troubled them had revealed it to them,<br/>so that they would not die without knowing<br/>why they were so harshly struck down.<br/><br/>20. The trial of death touched the just as well,<br/>and there was in the wilderness a destruction of the multitude;<br/>but your wrath did not last long.<br/>21. For a blameless man hastened to fight on behalf of the guilty;<br/>taking up the weapons of his ministry,<br/>prayer and expiatory incense,<br/>he withstood the divine wrath and put an end to the plague,<br/>showing that he was your servant.<br/>22. He overcame this uprising, not by bodily strength,<br/>nor by the power of arms;<br/>but he subdued by his word the one who was chastising them,<br/>by recalling the oaths made to the fathers and the covenants.<br/>23. When the dead had already fallen in heaps upon one another,<br/>stepping between them, he stayed the wrath,<br/>and closed to the Destroyer the path of the survivors.<br/>24. For upon the robe that fell to the ground was the whole universe;<br/>the glorious names of the fathers were engraved upon the four rows of precious stones,<br/>and your majesty upon the diadem of his head.<br/>25. Before these symbols the Destroyer withdrew, terrified;<br/>for the mere experience of your wrath was enough.</p>

### Chapter 19 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. But a merciless wrath<br/>pursues the impious to the end.</p>

<p class="v">For God knew beforehand what their conduct would be:<br/>2. That after having allowed the just to depart,<br/>and urged their departure with great insistence,<br/>they would regret it and set out in pursuit of them.<br/>3. Indeed, they had not yet finished their mourning,<br/>and were still lamenting at the tombs of their dead,<br/>when they embarked upon another mad scheme,<br/>and pursued as fugitives<br/>those whom they had implored to depart.<br/>4. A just necessity was driving them to this end,<br/>and made them forget what had just happened to them,<br/>so that they might undergo, in full measure, the punishment<br/>still lacking to their previous torments,<br/>5. and that, while your people benefited from a glorious passage,<br/>they might meet a strange death.<br/><br/>6. For all creation was transformed in its nature,<br/>obeying the particular commands given to it,<br/>so that your children might be kept safe from all harm.<br/>7. Thus a cloud was seen covering the camp with its shadow;<br/>where before there had been water, dry land appeared;<br/>the Red Sea opened a free passage,<br/>and the raging waves turned into a field of green.<br/>8. Through it they passed, — a whole nation, — protected by your hand,<br/>having before their eyes marvelous wonders.<br/>9. Like horses at pasture,<br/>like leaping lambs,<br/>they glorified you, Lord, their deliverer.<br/>10. For they still remembered what had happened<br/>during their sojourn in the foreign land:<br/>how, instead of other animals,<br/>the earth had produced gnats,<br/>and the river, instead of fish, a multitude of frogs.<br/><br/>11. Later, they saw yet another strange production of birds,<br/>when, driven by craving,<br/>they asked for delicate food:<br/>12. to satisfy them, quails came up from the direction of the sea.<br/><br/>13. But punishment fell upon the sinners,<br/>not without being announced beforehand by violent flashes of lightning.<br/>They suffered justly for their crimes,<br/>14. for they had shown the most odious hatred toward the stranger.<br/>Others had not wished to receive people<br/>whom they did not know;<br/>the former had enslaved strangers who had done them good.</p>

<p class="v">15. There is more, — for here is another consideration in favor of the former: —<br/>It was as enemies that they received these strangers;<br/>16. the latter, on the contrary, welcomed your people with festivities;<br/>and, after having admitted them to the enjoyment of their rights,<br/>overwhelmed them with cruel sufferings.<br/>17. Therefore they were struck with blindness,<br/>like those who besieged the door of the just man,<br/>when, wrapped in profound darkness,<br/>each of them sought the entrance of the door.</p>

<p class="v">18. For the elements exchanged their properties,<br/>just as in a psaltery the notes change their rhythm,<br/>while still keeping the same pitch.<br/>This can be clearly seen<br/>from the events that took place.<br/>19. Land animals became aquatic;<br/>and those that swim moved over onto the land.<br/>20. Fire, in the water, exceeded its natural power,<br/>and water forgot its property of quenching.<br/>21. On the other hand, the flame did not touch the flesh<br/>of the frail creatures scattered all about,<br/>nor did it melt that heavenly food,<br/>like frost in appearance and as meltable.<br/><br/>22. In all things, Lord, you glorified your people,<br/>you honored them and did not despise them;<br/>at all times and in every place you assisted them.</p>
## Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) {: .book}

<p class="chap-sub">The great book of wisdom of Ben Sira of Jerusalem (c. 180 BCE): the fear of the Lord, friendship, speech, work, the praise of the Fathers — fifty-one chapters for living well.</p>

### Chapter 1 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. All wisdom comes from the Lord,<br/>and is with him forever.<br/>2. Who can count the sand of the sea,<br/>the drops of rain, and the days of old?<br/>3. Who can attain the height of heaven, the breadth of the earth,<br/>the depth of the abyss, and wisdom?<br/><br/>4. Wisdom was created before all things,<br/>and the light of understanding from eternity.<br/><br/>5. [The source of wisdom is the word of God in the highest heavens,<br/>her ways are the everlasting commandments.]<br/>6. To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed,<br/>and who has known her deep designs?<br/><br/>7. [To whom has the knowledge of wisdom been revealed and made manifest,<br/>and who understands the richness of her ways?]<br/>8. There is but one who is greatly to be feared in wisdom,<br/>seated upon his throne: it is the Lord.<br/>9. It is he who created her;<br/>he saw her and made her known.<br/>10. He poured her out upon all his works,<br/>and upon all flesh according to the measure of his gift,<br/>he has given her freely to those who love him.</p>

<p class="v">11. The fear of the Lord is glory and honor,<br/>and joy, and a crown of gladness.<br/>12. The fear of the Lord rejoices the heart;<br/>it gives cheerfulness, joy, and long life.</p>

<p class="v">13. He who fears the Lord will find it well with him at the last,<br/>and he shall find favor in the day of his death.<br/><br/>[The love of God is a glorious wisdom;<br/>to those to whom he shows himself, God imparts wisdom,<br/>that they may be able to behold him.]<br/><br/>14. The beginning of wisdom is to fear God;<br/>she is formed with the faithful in their mother's womb.<br/>15. She has prepared for herself an everlasting dwelling among men;<br/>she will remain faithfully with their race.<br/>16. The fullness of wisdom is to fear the Lord;<br/>she satisfies with her fruits those who possess her.<br/>17. She fills all her house with things to be desired,<br/>and her storehouses with her produce.<br/>18. The crown of wisdom is the fear of the Lord;<br/>she makes peace and the fruits of salvation flourish.<br/>19. The Lord saw her and made her manifest;<br/>[and both are gifts of God.]<br/>He rains down knowledge and the light of understanding in floods,<br/>he exalts the glory of those who possess her.<br/>20. The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord,<br/>and her branches are long life.<br/><br/>21. [The fear of the Lord banishes sin,<br/>and he who cleaves to it turns away wrath.]<br/>22. The unjust and hot-tempered man cannot be justified,<br/>for the vehemence of his anger brings about his ruin.<br/>23. The patient man waits until the appointed time,<br/>and afterward joy is restored to him.<br/>24. He hides his words until the appointed time,<br/>and the lips of the faithful will tell of his prudence.<br/>25. The treasures of wisdom contain maxims of prudence,<br/>but godliness is an abomination to the sinner.<br/><br/>26. Do you desire wisdom? Keep the commandments,<br/>and the Lord will grant her to you.<br/>27. For wisdom and instruction are the fear of the Lord,<br/>and what pleases him is fidelity and meekness.<br/>28. Do not refuse the fear of the Lord,<br/>and do not approach him with a double heart.<br/>29. Do not be a hypocrite before men,<br/>and take heed to your lips.</p>

<p class="v">30. Do not exalt yourself, lest you fall,<br/>and bring confusion upon yourself.<br/><br/>For the Lord will reveal what you hide,<br/>and will cast you down in the midst of the assembly,<br/>because you have not devoted yourself to the fear of the Lord,<br/>and your heart is full of deceit.</p>

### Chapter 2 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. My son, if you come to serve the Lord,<br/>prepare your soul for trial.<br/>2. Make your heart right and be steadfast,<br/>and do not be hasty in time of trouble.<br/>3. Cling to God and do not depart from him,<br/>that you may grow to your last end.<br/>4. Whatever befalls you, accept it,<br/>and in the changes of your humiliation, be patient.<br/>5. For gold is tested in the fire,<br/>and men acceptable to God in the furnace of humiliation.<br/>6. Have faith in God, and he will lift you up;<br/>make your ways straight, and hope in him.</p>

<p class="v">7. You who fear the Lord, wait for his mercy,<br/>and do not turn aside, lest you fall.<br/>8. You who fear the Lord, have faith in him,<br/>and your reward will not be lost.<br/>9. You who fear the Lord, hope for good things,<br/>for everlasting joy and mercy.<br/><br/>10. Consider the generations of old, and see:<br/>who has ever hoped in the Lord and been confounded?<br/>Who has remained steadfast in his fear and been forsaken?<br/>Who has called upon him and received nothing but contempt from him?<br/>11. For the Lord is compassionate and merciful;<br/>he forgives sins and saves in the day of affliction.<br/><br/>12. Woe to timid hearts, and to slack hands,<br/>and to the sinner who walks two ways!<br/>13. Woe to the heart that is slack, for it has no faith in God!<br/>Therefore it will not be protected.<br/>14. Woe to you who have lost patience!<br/>What will you do in the day of the Lord's visitation?</p>

<p class="v">15. Those who fear the Lord are not unyielding to his words,<br/>and those who love him keep his ways faithfully.<br/>16. Those who fear the Lord seek his good pleasure,<br/>and those who love him are filled with his law.<br/>17. Those who fear the Lord prepare their hearts,<br/>and humble their souls in his sight,<br/>18. saying: We will fall into the hands of the Lord,<br/>and not into the hands of men;<br/>for as great as his power is, so great is his mercy.</p>

### Chapter 3 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. My children, listen to me, I who am your father,<br/>and act so that you may obtain salvation.<br/><br/>2. For the Lord wills that the father be honored by his children,<br/>and he has confirmed the mother's authority over her sons.<br/>3. He who honors his father atones for his sins,<br/>4. and to honor one's mother is to lay up a treasure.<br/>5. He who honors his father will be gladdened by his own children,<br/><br/>and will be heard in the day of his prayer.<br/>6. He who honors his father will have long life;<br/>he who obeys the Lord will give comfort to his mother.<br/><br/>7. [He who fears the Lord honors his parents;]<br/>and serves as masters those who gave him life.<br/>8. In deed and in word honor your father,<br/>that his blessing may come upon you;<br/>9. for a father's blessing establishes the houses of his children;<br/>but a mother's curse uproots their foundations.<br/><br/>10. Do not glory in your father's disgrace,<br/>for his confusion can bring you no honor;<br/>11. for a man's glory comes from the honor of his father,<br/>and a mother held in contempt is a reproach to her children.<br/><br/>12. My son, support your father in his old age,<br/>and do not grieve him during his life.<br/>13. Should his understanding fail, be indulgent with him,<br/>and do not despise him while you are in the fullness of your strength.<br/>14. For good done to a father will not be forgotten,<br/>and in place of your sins, your house will prosper.</p>

<p class="v">15. In the day of tribulation, the Lord will remember you;<br/>as ice melts away in fair weather,<br/>so your sins will be dissolved.<br/>16. He who abandons his father is like a blasphemer;<br/>he who provokes his mother is cursed of the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">17. My son, carry out your works with meekness,<br/>and you will be loved by the man who is acceptable to God.<br/>18. The greater you are, the more humble yourself,<br/>and you will find favor before the Lord;<br/>19. for the power of the Lord is great,<br/>and he is glorified by the humble.<br/><br/>20. Do not seek what is too difficult for you,<br/>and do not search into what is beyond your strength.<br/>21. What is commanded you, on that you must think,<br/>for you have no need of hidden things.<br/>22. Do not busy yourself with superfluous matters,<br/>for more has already been shown you than the human mind can grasp.<br/>23. Their own illusion has led many astray,<br/>and a guilty presumption has warped their thoughts.<br/><br/>24. He who loves danger will find his ruin in it,<br/>and the hard heart will fall at last into misfortune.<br/>25. The hard heart will be weighed down with afflictions,<br/>and the sinner heaps sin upon sin.<br/>26. The misfortune of the proud man is without remedy,<br/>for the plant of evil has cast its roots in him.<br/>27. The heart of the intelligent man meditates on the parable;<br/>to find an attentive ear is the desire of the wise man.</p>

<p class="v">28. Water extinguishes the most burning fire,<br/>and almsgiving atones for sins.<br/>29. He who repays kindness thinks of the future,<br/>and in the day of misfortune he will find support.</p>

### Chapter 4 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. My son, do not deprive the poor of his subsistence,<br/>and do not make the eyes of the needy wait.<br/>2. Do not afflict the soul of one who is hungry,<br/>and do not embitter a needy man in his distress.<br/>3. Do not further vex a heart already provoked,<br/>and do not delay giving to the needy.<br/>4. Do not turn away the suffering suppliant,<br/>and do not turn your face from the poor.<br/>5. Do not turn your gaze from the needy,<br/>and give him no occasion to curse you;<br/>6. for if he curses you in the bitterness of his soul,<br/>he who made him will hear his prayer.<br/><br/>7. Make yourself agreeable to the assembly,<br/>and bow your head before a great man.<br/>8. Incline your ear to the poor,<br/>and give him a gentle answer that will gladden him.<br/><br/>9. Deliver the oppressed from the hands of the oppressor,<br/>and do not be fainthearted when you render justice.<br/>10. Be as a father to orphans,<br/>and as a husband to their mother;<br/>and you will be like a son of the Most High,<br/>who will love you more than your mother does.</p>

<p class="v">11. Wisdom exalts her children,<br/>and takes care of those who seek her.<br/>12. He who loves her loves life,<br/>and those who seek her earnestly are filled with joy.<br/>13. He who lays hold of her will have glory as his portion,<br/>and wherever he enters, the Lord will bless him.<br/>14. Those who serve her, serve the Holy One,<br/>and those who love her are loved by the Lord.<br/>15. He who listens to her will judge the nations,<br/>and he who comes to her will dwell in security.<br/><br/>16. He who puts his trust in her will have her as his portion,<br/>and his descendants will keep possession of her.<br/>17. For at first she walks with him in a difficult way;<br/>she brings upon him fear and dread;<br/>she torments him with her hard discipline,<br/>until she can trust him,<br/>and has tested him by her precepts.</p>

<p class="v">18. But then she returns to him by the straight path;<br/>she gladdens him and reveals her secrets to him.<br/>19. If he strays, she abandons him,<br/>and gives him up to his ruin.</p>

<p class="v">20. Observe the time, and keep yourself from evil,<br/>and do not have cause to blush at yourself.<br/>21. There is a shame that brings sin,<br/>and there is a shame that brings glory and grace.<br/><br/>22. Have no regard for anyone to the harm of your own soul,<br/>and do not blush at your own ruin.<br/><br/>23. Do not withhold a word in the time it is needed,[and do not hide your wisdom out of vainglory];<br/>24. for it is by speech that wisdom is known,<br/>and by the words of the tongue that knowledge is shown.<br/><br/>25. Do not contradict the truth,<br/>but blush at your own lack of instruction.<br/><br/>26. Do not be ashamed to confess your sins,<br/>and do not strive against the current of a river.<br/><br/>27. Do not submit yourself to a foolish man,<br/>and do not show partiality to a powerful man.<br/><br/>28. Fight to the death for the truth,<br/>and the Lord God will fight for you.<br/><br/>29. Do not be harsh in your speech,<br/>slothful and slack in your deeds.<br/><br/>30. Do not be like a lion in your house,<br/>nor capricious among your servants.<br/><br/>31. Let not your hand be stretched out to receive,<br/>and drawn back when it is time to give.</p>

### Chapter 5 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Do not rely on your riches,<br/>and do not say, "I have enough to live on!"<br/>2. Do not follow your own lust and strength,<br/>to satisfy the desires of your heart;<br/>3. and do not say, "Who will be my master?"<br/>For the Lord will surely punish you.</p>

<p class="v">4. Do not say, "I have sinned, and what has happened to me?"<br/>For the Lord is patient.<br/>5. Do not be without fear concerning atonement,<br/>so as to add sin to sin.<br/>6. Do not say, "The mercy of God is great,<br/>he will pardon the multitude of my sins."<br/>For in him are found both pity and wrath,<br/>and his anger falls upon sinners.<br/>7. Do not delay to turn to the Lord,<br/>and do not put it off from day to day;<br/>for the wrath of the Lord will burst forth suddenly,<br/>and in the day of vengeance you will perish.<br/><br/>8. Do not rely on unjust riches,<br/>for they will be of no use to you in the day of misfortune.</p>

<p class="v">9. Do not winnow before every wind,<br/>and do not walk in every path;<br/>so does the sinner with the double tongue.<br/>10. Be steadfast in your understanding,<br/>and let your speech be one.<br/><br/>11. Be swift to hear,<br/>and slow to give an answer.<br/>12. If you have understanding, answer your neighbor;<br/>if not, put your hand upon your mouth.<br/>13. Glory and shame are in speech,<br/>and a man's tongue is his downfall.<br/><br/>14. Do not earn for yourself the name of slanderer,<br/>and do not lay snares with your tongue;<br/>for confusion falls upon the thief,<br/>and a severe condemnation befalls the double tongue.<br/>15. Do not be at fault in either much or little,</p>

### Chapter 6 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. nor from a friend become an enemy;<br/>for the wicked man will have as his portion ill repute,<br/>shame, and reproach:<br/>such is the sinner with the double tongue.</p>

<p class="v">2. Do not exalt yourself in the will of your own soul,<br/>lest your soul be torn to pieces as by a bull.<br/>3. You will devour your own leaves,<br/>you will destroy your own fruit,<br/>and you will leave yourself nothing but a withered tree.</p>

<p class="v">4. A perverse soul destroys him who possesses it;<br/>it makes him the laughingstock of his enemies.</p>

<p class="v">5. A pleasant word makes many friends,<br/>and an agreeable tongue is rich in kindnesses.<br/>6. Let those who live at peace with you be many,<br/>but take counsel from one in a thousand.<br/>7. If you would gain a friend, gain him by testing him,<br/>and do not trust him lightly.<br/><br/>8. For there is a friend for a season,<br/>who will not remain so in the day of your affliction;<br/>9. there is a friend who will become an enemy,<br/>and who will reveal your quarrel to your confusion;<br/>10. there is a friend who sits at your table,<br/>who will not remain so in the day of your misfortune.<br/>11. In your prosperity, he will be as another self to you,<br/>and will speak freely with the people of your household.<br/>12. If you fall into humiliation, he will turn against you,<br/>and will hide himself from you.<br/>13. Keep away from your enemies,<br/>and be on your guard with your friends.<br/><br/>14. A faithful friend is a strong protection;<br/>he who finds one has found a treasure.<br/>15. Nothing can equal a faithful friend;<br/>no weight of gold or silver can measure his worth.<br/>16. A faithful friend is a medicine of life;<br/>those who fear the Lord find him.<br/>17. He who fears the Lord has true friendship,<br/>for his friend is like himself.</p>

<p class="v">18. My son, devote yourself to instruction from your youth,<br/>and even to your gray hairs you will find wisdom.<br/>19. Approach her as one who plows and sows,<br/>and wait for her good fruits.<br/>For a little while you will labor to cultivate her,<br/>and soon you will eat of her fruits.<br/>20. How rugged she is to the ignorant!<br/>The fool will not remain attached to her.</p>

<p class="v">21. Like a heavy testing-stone, she weighs upon him,<br/>and he does not delay to cast her off.<br/>22. For wisdom lives up to her name:<br/>she does not reveal herself to the multitude.<br/><br/>23. Listen, my son, and receive my thought,<br/>and do not reject my counsel.<br/>24. Put your foot into her fetters,<br/>and your neck into her collar.<br/>25. Bend your shoulder and carry her,<br/>and do not be irritated by her bonds.<br/>26. Come to her with all your soul,<br/>and keep her ways with all your strength.<br/>27. Follow her tracks and seek her, and she will make herself known to you,<br/>and once you have grasped her, do not let her go.<br/><br/>28. For at last you will find her rest,<br/>and she will be changed for you into a source of joy.<br/>29. Her fetters will become for you a strong protection,<br/>and her collar a robe of glory.<br/>30. For upon her head is an ornament of gold,<br/>and her bands are a fabric of hyacinth.<br/>31. You will clothe yourself with her as with a robe of glory,<br/>and you will set her upon your head as a crown of joy.<br/><br/>32. My son, if you wish it, you will acquire instruction,<br/>and if you apply your soul, you will become skillful.<br/>33. If you love to listen, you will learn;<br/>if you incline your ear, you will become wise.<br/>34. Keep company with the elders;<br/>is someone wise? Attach yourself to him.<br/>35. Listen gladly to every discourse about God,<br/>and let not maxims of wisdom escape you.<br/>36. If you see a man of understanding, be near him from early morning,<br/>and let your foot wear away the threshold of his door.<br/>37. Meditate on the commandments of the Lord,<br/>and reflect constantly on his precepts;<br/>he himself will strengthen your heart,<br/>and the wisdom you desire will be given to you.</p>

### Chapter 7 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Do not do evil, and evil will not seize you;<br/>2. keep away from what is unjust, and the unjust will keep away from you.<br/>3. My son, do not sow in the furrows of injustice,<br/>lest you reap seven times as much.<br/><br/>4. Do not ask the Lord for power,<br/>nor the king for a seat of honor.</p>

<p class="v">5. Do not try to appear righteous before the Lord,<br/>and do not seek to appear wise before the king.<br/><br/>6. Do not seek to become a judge,<br/>lest you lack the strength to root out injustice,<br/>lest you be intimidated in the presence of a powerful man,<br/>and put your integrity in peril.<br/><br/>7. Do not offend the whole population of a city,<br/>and do not throw yourself into the midst of the crowd.<br/><br/>8. Do not bind sin twice over,<br/>for not even for one sin will you go unpunished.<br/>9. Do not say, "God will consider the multitude of my gifts,<br/>and when I offer them to the Most High God, he will accept them."<br/><br/>10. Do not be fainthearted in your prayer,<br/>and do not neglect to give alms.<br/><br/>11. Do not mock the man whose heart is afflicted,<br/>for there is One who humbles and who exalts.<br/><br/>12. Do not forge a lie against your brother;<br/>do not do the same against your friend.<br/>13. Guard yourself from telling any lie,<br/>for the habit of lying never turns out well.<br/><br/>14. Do not chatter in the company of the elders,<br/>and do not repeat the words of your prayer.<br/><br/>15. Do not hate hard labor,<br/>nor the work of the fields instituted by the Most High.<br/><br/>16. Do not place yourself among the great number of sinners;<br/>remember that vengeance will not delay.<br/>17. Humble your soul deeply,<br/>for fire and the worm are the punishment of the ungodly.</p>

<p class="v">18. Do not exchange a friend for money,<br/>nor a brother for the gold of Ophir.<br/><br/>19. Do not turn away from an intelligent and good wife;<br/>for her charm is worth more than gold.</p>

<p class="v">20. Do not mistreat the slave who works faithfully,<br/>nor the hired servant who devotes himself to your service.<br/>21. Love the intelligent slave;<br/>do not deprive him of his freedom.<br/><br/>22. Do you have flocks? Take care of them,<br/>and if they are useful to you, keep them with you.<br/><br/>23. Do you have sons? Instruct them,<br/>and bend them to the yoke from their childhood.<br/><br/>24. Do you have daughters? Watch over their chastity,<br/>and do not show them too cheerful a face.<br/>25. Marry off your daughter, and you will have finished a great task;<br/>and give her to an intelligent man.<br/><br/>26. Do you have a wife after your own heart? Do not divorce her;<br/>[but do not give yourself to a woman who is hateful to you].<br/><br/>27. Honor your father with all your heart,<br/>and do not forget the pains of your mother.<br/>28. Remember that it is through them that you came into the world:<br/>and how will you repay them for what they have given you?</p>

<p class="v">29. Fear the Lord with all your soul,<br/>and hold his priests in great honor.<br/>30. Love with all your strength Him who made you,<br/>and do not forsake his ministers.<br/>31. Fear the Lord and honor the priest;<br/>give him his portion, as was prescribed from the beginning:<br/>the victim for guilt with the gift of the shoulders,<br/>the holy oblation and the firstfruits.<br/><br/>32. Stretch out your hand also to the poor,<br/>that your blessing may be complete.<br/>33. Give graciously to every living thing,<br/>and do not withhold your kindness from the dead.<br/>34. Do not fail those who weep,<br/>and mourn with those who mourn.<br/>35. Do not neglect to care for the sick;<br/>for such acts of charity you will be loved by God.<br/>36. In all your actions remember your last end,<br/>and you will never sin.</p>

### Chapter 8 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Do not quarrel with a powerful man,<br/>lest you fall into his hands.</p>

<p class="v">2. Do not quarrel with a rich man,<br/>lest he oppose you with the weight of his gold;<br/>for gold has ruined many people,<br/>it has even turned aside the hearts of kings.<br/><br/>3. Do not dispute with a great talker,<br/>and do not heap wood on his fire.<br/><br/>4. Do not jest with an ill-bred man,<br/>lest your ancestors be dishonored.<br/><br/>5. Do not mock a man who turns away from sin;<br/>remember that we are all deserving of punishment.<br/><br/>6. Do not despise a man in his old age,<br/>for some of us also grow old.<br/><br/>7. Do not rejoice when a man dies;<br/>remember that we shall all die.<br/><br/>8. Do not neglect the discourse of the wise,<br/>and occupy yourself with their maxims;<br/>for from them you will learn instruction,<br/>and the art of serving the great.<br/><br/>9. Do not let the discourse of the elders escape you,<br/>for they themselves learned from their fathers.<br/>From them you will learn wisdom,<br/>and how to give a good answer when it is needed.<br/><br/>10. Do not kindle the coals of the sinner,<br/>lest you be consumed by the heat of his flame.<br/>11. Do not stand up to the insolent man who insults you,<br/>lest he lie in ambush to spy upon your words.<br/><br/>12. Do not lend to one more powerful than yourself,<br/>and if you have lent him something, consider it lost.<br/>13. Do not go surety beyond your means,<br/>and if you have gone surety, be as concerned as if you had to pay.<br/><br/>14. Do not go to law with a judge,<br/>for they will decide in his favor according to his standing.<br/><br/>15. Do not travel with a reckless man,<br/>lest he become a burden to you;<br/>for he does everything according to his own fancy,<br/>and through his folly you will perish with him.<br/><br/>16. Do not quarrel with an irascible man,<br/>and do not cross the desert with him;<br/>for blood is as nothing in his eyes,<br/>and where there is no help at hand, he will strike you down.</p>

<p class="v">17. Do not take counsel with a fool,<br/>for he will be unable to keep anything secret.<br/><br/>18. Before a stranger do nothing that must remain hidden,<br/>for you do not know what he may do.<br/><br/>19. Do not open your heart to every man,<br/>lest you be ill repaid for it.</p>

### Chapter 9 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Do not be jealous of the wife who rests upon your breast,<br/>and do not put into her mind, to your own harm, an evil thought.<br/>2. Do not give yourself over to your wife,<br/>so that she rises up against your authority.<br/><br/>3. Do not go to meet a woman who is a harlot,<br/>lest you fall into her snares.<br/><br/>4. Do not linger long with a singing woman,<br/>lest you be caught by her art.<br/><br/>5. Do not fix your gaze on a young girl,<br/>lest you suffer punishment on her account.<br/><br/>6. Do not give yourself over to harlots,<br/>lest you lose your inheritance.<br/>7. Do not let your eyes wander through the streets of the city,<br/>and do not roam about in its solitary places.<br/><br/>8. Turn your eyes away from an elegant woman,<br/>and do not gaze curiously at a strange beauty.<br/>Many have been seduced by the beauty of a woman,<br/>and passion is kindled by it like a fire.<br/><br/>9. Never sit down beside a married woman,<br/>[do not recline at table with her],<br/>and do not drink wine with her at banquets,<br/>lest your soul turn toward her,<br/>and passion draw you down to your ruin.</p>

<p class="v">10. Do not abandon an old friend,<br/>for the new one will not equal him.</p>

<p class="v">A new wine, a new friend;<br/>let it age, and you will drink it with pleasure.<br/><br/>11. Do not envy the glory of the sinner,<br/>for you do not know what his ruin will be.<br/>12. Do not take pleasure in the pleasure of the ungodly;<br/>remember that they will not go unpunished until Sheol.<br/><br/>13. Keep far from the man who has the power to put to death,<br/>and you will not have the fear of death.<br/>And if you approach him, guard against every fault,<br/>lest he take your life.<br/>Know that you walk in the midst of snares,<br/>and that you are walking upon the battlements of the city.<br/><br/>14. Observe your neighbor as much as you can,<br/>and take counsel from the wise.<br/>15. Converse with intelligent men,<br/>and let all your conversation be about the law of the Most High.<br/>16. Let righteous men be your table companions,<br/>and put your glory in the fear of God.<br/><br/>17. It is the hand of the craftsman that earns a work its praise,<br/>it is his speech that makes the leader of the people appear wise.<br/><br/>18. The great talker is feared in his city,<br/>and the reckless man draws hatred upon himself by his speech.</p>

### Chapter 10 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. The wise ruler keeps his people in discipline,<br/>and the government of the sensible man is well ordered.<br/>2. As is the leader of the people, so are his ministers;<br/>and as is the government of the city, so are all its inhabitants.<br/>3. An ignorant king ruins his people,<br/>but a city prospers by the intelligence of its rulers.<br/>4. The sovereignty of the land is in the hand of the Lord,<br/>and in due time he raises up over it the capable ruler.<br/>5. A man's success is in the hand of the Lord;<br/>it is he who sets his authority upon the ruler's brow.</p>

<p class="v">6. Bear no grudge against your neighbor for any wrong,<br/>and do nothing in the midst of acts of violence.<br/><br/>7. Pride is hateful to God and to men;<br/>and to both, injustice is iniquity.<br/>8. Dominion passes from one people to another,<br/>because of injustice, insults, and the coveting of riches.</p>

<p class="v">9. Why does that which is earth and dust grow proud?<br/>For even during its life I bring trouble upon its members;<br/>10. the sickness lingers; the physician laughs;<br/>and the king of today will die tomorrow!<br/><br/>11. And when a man is dead,<br/>he has for his portion maggots, beasts, and worms.<br/><br/>12. Pride begins when a man separates himself from the Lord,<br/>and when his heart turns away from Him who made him.<br/>13. For the beginning of pride is sin,<br/>and he who clings to it pours forth abomination like rain.<br/><br/>Therefore the Lord sends forth extraordinary punishments,<br/>and strikes down the wicked with complete ruin.<br/>14. The Lord overturns the throne of princes,<br/>and seats the meek in their place.<br/>15. The Lord uproots the nations,<br/>and plants the humble in their place.<br/>16. The Lord overthrows the lands of the nations,<br/>and pursues their destruction to the foundations of the earth.<br/>17. He withers many of them and exterminates their inhabitants;<br/>he blots out their memory from the earth.<br/><br/>18. Pride was not made for man,<br/>nor insolent wrath for those born of woman.</p>

<p class="v">19. What race is honored? The race of man.<br/>What race is honored? Those who fear the Lord.<br/>What race is despised? The race of man.<br/>What race is despised? Those who transgress the commandments.<br/><br/>20. Among his brothers, their leader is held in honor;<br/>those who fear the Lord are likewise honored in his sight.<br/>21. Rich, noble, and poor,<br/>their glory is the fear of the Lord.<br/>22. It is not right to despise an intelligent poor man;<br/>it is not fitting to honor a sinner.<br/>23. The great man, the judge, and the powerful man are held in honor,<br/>but none of them is greater than he who fears the Lord.<br/>24. Free men are the servants of the prudent slave,<br/>and the intelligent man will not complain.</p>

<p class="v">25. Do not reason overmuch about doing your work,<br/>and do not boast in the time of your distress.<br/>26. Better is the man who labors at everything,<br/>than he who walks about, boasts, and lacks bread.<br/>27. My son, honor your soul in gentleness,<br/>and give it the respect it deserves.<br/>28. The man who sins against his own soul, who will regard him as righteous?<br/>Who will honor him who dishonors his own life?<br/><br/>29. The poor man is honored for his knowledge,<br/>and the rich man is honored for his riches.<br/>30. But he who is honored in poverty,<br/>how much more would he be honored in riches?<br/>And he who is without honor in riches,<br/>how much more would he be without honor in poverty?</p>

### Chapter 11 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. The wisdom of the humble man will lift up his head,<br/>and will seat him among the great.</p>

<p class="v">2. Do not praise a man for his beauty,<br/>and do not hold a man in disgust for his appearance.<br/>3. The bee is small among winged creatures,<br/>and its product ranks first among sweet things.<br/>4. Do not glory in the clothes that cover you,<br/>and do not exalt yourself on a day of glory.<br/><br/>For the works of the Lord are wondrous,<br/>and his action among men is hidden.<br/>5. Many princes have sat upon the ground,<br/>and one no one thought of has worn the crown.<br/>6. Many powerful men have been overwhelmed with disgrace,<br/>and illustrious men delivered into the hands of others.<br/><br/>7. Before you inquire, do not cast blame;<br/>examine first, and then you may reprove.</p>

<p class="v">8. Do not answer anything before you have listened,<br/>and do not thrust your words into the midst of others' speech.<br/>9. Do not contend over a thing that is not yours,<br/>and do not sit down with sinners to judge.</p>

<p class="v">10. My son, do not apply your energy to a multitude of things:<br/>if you take on too much, you will not be free of fault.<br/>If you pursue too many things, you will not attain them,<br/>and you will not escape by fleeing.</p>

<p class="v">11. One man labors, wears himself out, and hurries,<br/>and only becomes the poorer for it.<br/>12. Another is without energy, calling for help,<br/>poor in strength and rich in need;<br/>but the eyes of the Lord look upon him favorably,<br/>he lifts him out of his lowly condition,<br/>13. he raises up his head,<br/>and many marvel at him.</p>

<p class="v">14. Good things and evil, death and life,<br/>poverty and riches, come from the Lord.<br/>15. The gifts of God remain with the righteous,<br/>and his favor assures them prosperity forever.<br/><br/>16. One man is rich through care and thrift,<br/>and here is the portion that falls to him as reward:<br/>17. He may say, "I have found rest,<br/>and now I will eat of my goods."<br/>But he does not know how much time will pass;<br/>he will leave his goods to others and die.<br/>18. Be faithful to your covenant with God, and live by that thought,<br/>and grow old in your work.<br/><br/>19. Do not be amazed at the affairs of the sinner;<br/>trust in the Lord and persevere in your labor.<br/>For it is an easy thing in the sight of the Lord<br/>to enrich the poor man promptly and all at once.<br/>20. The blessing of the Lord is the reward of the godly man;<br/>in a swift hour, he makes his blessing flourish.<br/><br/>21. Do not say, "What do I need,<br/>and what happiness can be mine from now on?"<br/>22. Nor say, "I have what I need,<br/>and what evil could I have to suffer?"<br/>23. In the day of happiness, misfortune is forgotten,<br/>and in the day of misfortune, happiness is remembered no more.<br/><br/>24. For it is an easy thing before the Lord,<br/>in the day of death, to repay a man according to his ways.<br/>25. A moment of affliction makes one forget past well-being,<br/>and at a man's end, his works will be laid bare.<br/>26. Call no one happy before his death:<br/>it is by his children that a man is known.</p>

<p class="v">27. Do not bring everyone into your house,<br/>for the snares of the deceitful man are many.<br/>28. Like the decoy partridge in its cage,<br/>so is the heart of the proud man;<br/>and, like a spy, he watches for ruin.<br/>29. Turning good into evil, he sets traps,<br/>and he stains what is purest.<br/>30. A single spark produces much charcoal;<br/>so the sinner insidiously seeks to shed blood.<br/>31. Beware of the wicked man — for he plots evil —<br/>lest he brand you with an indelible stain.<br/>32. Give the stranger entry into your house,<br/>and he will overturn you by stirring up trouble,<br/>and will estrange from you the people of your household.</p>

### Chapter 12 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. If you do good, know to whom you do it,<br/>and you will be thanked for your kindness.<br/>2. Do good to the godly man, and you will find your reward,<br/>if not from him, then from the Lord.<br/>3. Kindness is not for him who persists in evil,<br/>nor for him who does not practice beneficence.<br/>4. Give to the godly man, and do not help the sinner.<br/>5. Do good to him who is humbled, and give nothing to the ungodly;<br/>withhold bread from him, and do not give it to him,<br/>lest by it he become stronger than you;<br/>for you will reap a double harm<br/>from all the good you have done him.<br/>6. The Most High also hates sinners,<br/>and he will take vengeance on the ungodly.<br/>7. Give to the virtuous man, and do not help the sinner.</p>

<p class="v">8. It is not in prosperity that a friend earns punishment,<br/>nor in adversity that an enemy hides himself.<br/>9. When a man is prosperous, his enemies are grieved;<br/>when he is in misfortune, even his friend separates himself from him.</p>

<p class="v">10. Never trust your enemy,<br/>for his malice is like bronze covered over with rust;<br/>11. even when he shows himself humble and walks bent low,<br/>watch yourself and be on guard against him;<br/>and you will be to him like one who polishes a mirror,<br/>and you will know that it has no rust, right to the end.<br/><br/>12. Do not set him beside you,<br/>lest he overthrow you and take your place.<br/>Do not seat him at your right hand,<br/>lest he seek to occupy your seat,<br/>and lest at last, recognizing the truth of my words,<br/>you grieve at the remembrance of what I have said.<br/><br/>13. Who will have pity on the enchanter bitten by a serpent,<br/>and on all those who go near wild beasts?<br/>14. So it is with him who joins company with a sinner,<br/>and mingles in his sins.<br/>15. He stays with you for an hour;<br/>but if you turn aside, he will not remain any longer.<br/><br/>16. The enemy has sweetness on his lips,<br/>and in his heart he plots how to throw you into the pit.<br/>The enemy has tears in his eyes,<br/>and if he finds the occasion, he will be insatiable for your blood.<br/>17. If misfortune reaches you, you will find him there before you,<br/>and, under pretense of helping you, he will trip you up.<br/>18. Then he will shake his head, he will clap his hands,<br/>he will not stop whispering, and he will put on another face.</p>

### Chapter 13 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. He who touches pitch is defiled by it,<br/>and he who joins with the proud man becomes like him.<br/>2.
