Do not put a heavy burden on your shoulders,<br/>and do not join with a man stronger and richer than yourself.<br/>What partnership can there be between the clay pot and the cauldron?<br/>The cauldron will strike the pot, and it will be shattered.<br/>3. The rich man commits an injustice, and he trembles with indignation;<br/>the poor man is mistreated, and he must beg pardon.<br/>4. As long as you can be useful to him, he will make use of you,<br/>and when you have nothing left, he will abandon you.<br/>5. If you have goods, he will live with you,<br/>he will strip you bare, and feel no concern at all.</p>

<p class="v">6. Are you of use to him? He will cajole you,<br/>he will smile at you and give you hopes,<br/>he will speak fine words to you and say, "What do you need?"<br/>7. He will confuse you with his feasting,<br/>until he has stripped you two or three times over,<br/>and, in the end, he will laugh at you;<br/>after that, he will see you and abandon you,<br/>and shake his head at you.<br/>8. Beware of letting yourself be seduced,<br/>and, in the midst of prosperity, of falling into humiliation.<br/><br/>9. If a powerful man calls you, draw back;<br/>he will only invite you all the more insistently.<br/>10. Do not fall upon him unexpectedly, lest you be repulsed,<br/>and do not keep yourself too far from him, lest you be forgotten.<br/>11. Do not imagine that you can converse with him as an equal,<br/>and do not trust in his many words.<br/>12. For by his flow of words he will test you,<br/>and he will question you as though smiling.<br/>A man without pity, he will not keep your words to himself,<br/>and he will spare you neither blows nor chains.<br/>13. Take heed and pay close attention,<br/>for you walk together with your own ruin.<br/><br/>14. Every living creature loves its like,<br/>and every man his neighbor.<br/>15. All flesh unites according to its kind,<br/>and every man associates with his like.<br/>16. What union can there be between the wolf and the lamb?<br/>It is the same between the sinner and the godly man.<br/>17. What peace can the hyena have with the dog?<br/>What peace the rich man with the poor?<br/>18. Wild donkeys are the prey of lions in the desert;<br/>so the poor are the prey of the rich.<br/>19. The proud man holds humility in horror:<br/>so the rich man holds the poor man in horror.<br/><br/>20. Does the rich man begin to totter? His friends support him;<br/>but when the humble man falls, he is pushed down further by his friends.<br/>21. When the rich man has a fall, many come to his aid;<br/>he speaks foolish words, and they are approved.<br/>When the humble man has a fall, he is met with reproaches besides.<br/>22. The rich man speaks, and everyone falls silent;<br/>and his speech is exalted to the clouds.<br/>The poor man speaks, and they say, "Who is that?"<br/>and, if he stumbles, they push him down further.</p>

<p class="v">23. Riches are good when they are not joined to sin,<br/>and poverty is evil in the mouth of the ungodly.<br/><br/>24. The heart of a man changes his countenance,<br/>whether for good or for evil.<br/>25. The sign of a contented heart is a joyful face;<br/>to find wise maxims requires the labor of reflection.</p>
### Chapter 14 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Happy the man who has not sinned by the words of his mouth,<br/>and who has not been wounded by the remorse of sin!<br/>2. Happy he whom his own soul does not condemn,<br/>and who has not lost his hope in the Lord!<br/><br/>3. To the sordid man riches are of no use;<br/>and what good are treasures to the envious man?<br/>4. He who gathers by depriving himself gathers for others;<br/>with his goods others will live in delights.<br/>5. He who is evil to himself, to whom will he be good?<br/>He will not enjoy his own treasures.<br/>6. There is nothing worse than one who denies himself everything,<br/>and that is the just wages of his malice.<br/>7. If he does any good, it is by forgetfulness,<br/>and in the end he lets his malice be seen.<br/>8. He is wicked who looks with an envious eye,<br/>who turns away his face and despises souls.<br/>9. The eye of the covetous man is not satisfied with one portion,<br/>and a fatal greed withers the soul.<br/>10. The evil eye denies itself bread,<br/>and it goes hungry at its own table.<br/><br/>11. My son, according to what you possess, do good to yourself,<br/>and bring the Lord worthy offerings.<br/>12. Remember that death does not delay,<br/>and that the covenant of Sheol has not been revealed to you.<br/>13. Before you die, do good to your friend;<br/>and, according to your means, reach out your hand and give to him.<br/>14. Do not deprive yourself of a festive day,<br/>and let no part of a good desire slip away.<br/>15. Will you not leave to others the fruit of your labor,<br/>and the fruit of your toil to the decision of chance?<br/>16. Give and take, and gladden your soul,<br/>for there is no seeking of delights in Sheol.<br/>17. All flesh grows old like a garment,<br/>for it is a law laid down from the beginning; you shall surely die.</p>

<p class="v">18. Like the leaves growing green on a leafy tree—<br/>it lets some fall, and makes others grow—<br/>so it is with the generations of flesh and blood:<br/>some die, others come to life.<br/>19. Every corruptible work ends by perishing,<br/>and its maker will go away with it.</p>

<p class="v">20. Happy the man who meditates on wisdom,<br/>and who speaks with good sense;<br/>21. who reflects in his heart on her ways,<br/>and who studies her secrets;<br/>22. who pursues her, like a hunter,<br/>and watches at her entrances.<br/>23. He stoops to look through her windows,<br/>and he listens at her door.<br/>24. He settles close to her dwelling,<br/>and fixes his stakes in her walls.<br/>25. He pitches his tent beside her,<br/>and he dwells in the house where happiness is found.<br/>26. He places his children under her protection,<br/>and shelters under her branches.<br/>27. In her shade he shall be shielded from the heat,<br/>and he shall rest in her glory.</p>

### Chapter 15 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. This is what he who fears the Lord does,<br/>and he who holds fast to the law shall obtain wisdom.<br/>2. She will come to meet him like a mother,<br/>and will welcome him like a virgin bride.<br/>3. She will feed him with the bread of understanding,<br/>and give him the water of wisdom to drink.<br/>4. He shall lean on her and not waver,<br/>he shall cling to her and not be put to shame.<br/>5. She will exalt him above his companions,<br/>and open his mouth in the midst of the assembly.<br/>6. Joy, a crown of gladness,<br/>and an everlasting name shall be his portion.<br/><br/>7. Fools shall not possess her,<br/>and sinners shall not even see her.<br/>8. She keeps far from men of pride,<br/>and men of falsehood do not think of her.</p>

<p class="v">9. Praise of God is not pleasing in the mouth of the sinner,<br/>because it is not sent by the Lord.<br/>10. For it is by wisdom that praise is dictated,<br/>and the Lord will find it pleasing.</p>

<p class="v">11. Do not say: "It is the Lord's doing that I went astray,"<br/>for what he hates, you must not do.<br/>12. Do not say: "It is he who led me astray;"<br/>for he has no need of the sinner.<br/>13. The Lord hates every abomination,<br/>and it must not be loved by those who fear him.<br/><br/>14. In the beginning he created man,<br/>and he left him in the hand of his own counsel:<br/>15. "If you will, you shall keep the commandments;<br/>faithfulness depends on your own good pleasure.<br/>16. He has set before you fire and water;<br/>toward whichever you wish, you may stretch out your hand."<br/>17. Before men are life and death;<br/>whichever he shall have chosen shall be given him.<br/><br/>18. For the wisdom of the Lord is great;<br/>he is strong and mighty, and he sees all things.<br/>19. His eyes are on those who fear him,<br/>and he himself knows every work of man.<br/>20. He has commanded no one to be ungodly,<br/>and to no one has he given permission to sin.</p>

### Chapter 16 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Do not desire a great number of worthless children,<br/>and do not set your joy in ungodly sons.<br/>2. Though they multiply, do not rejoice in them,<br/>if the fear of the Lord is not with them.<br/>3. Do not hope for them a long life,<br/>and place no reliance on their prosperity.<br/>One is worth more than a thousand;<br/>and it is better to die childless than to have ungodly sons.<br/>4. For a single man of understanding will people a country,<br/>but the race of the wicked shall be destroyed.</p>

<p class="v">5. I have seen many examples with my own eyes,<br/>and my ears have heard of graver ones still.<br/>6. Fire is kindled against the assembly of sinners,<br/>and the wrath of God blazes against a rebellious people.<br/>7. The Lord did not forgive the ancient giants,<br/>who, trusting in their strength, had rebelled.<br/>8. He did not spare those who dwelt with Lot,<br/>he held them in horror because of their insolent pride.<br/>9. He had no pity on the people doomed to destruction,<br/>who were exterminated together with their sins.<br/>10. Likewise he exterminated six hundred thousand footmen,<br/>who had gathered together in the hardness of their hearts.<br/><br/>11. Should but one man stiffen his neck,<br/>it would be a wonder if he went unpunished.<br/>For from the Lord come mercy and wrath;<br/>mighty in forgiveness, he also pours out his wrath.<br/>12. As great as his mercy, so great also are his punishments;<br/>he will judge man according to his works.<br/>13. The sinner will not escape with his plunder,<br/>and he will not put off the expectation of the godly man.<br/>14. He will give free course to the whole of his mercy,<br/>and each one will receive according to his works.</p>

<p class="v">15. Do not say: "I will hide myself from the sight of the Lord,<br/>and from on high who then will think of me?<br/>In the midst of the crowd I shall be forgotten,<br/>and what am I amid the vastness of creation?"<br/>16. Behold: the heaven and the heaven of heavens of God,<br/>the abyss and the earth are shaken when he visits them;<br/>17. together the mountains and the foundations of the earth<br/>are seized with trembling when he looks upon them.<br/>18. But the heart of man does not reflect on this,<br/>and who is he that studies his own ways?<br/>19. The storm escapes the eye of man,<br/>and most of the works of God are hidden.<br/>20. "Who will tell us the works of his justice, and who will wait for them?<br/>The covenant of punishment is so far off!"<br/>21. So thinks the man without understanding;<br/>the fool who goes astray imagines nothing but follies.</p>

<p class="v">22. Listen to me, my son, and learn wisdom;<br/>and make your heart attentive to my words.<br/>23. I will disclose to you a doctrine weighed in the balance,<br/>and I will make known to you an exact science.<br/>24. The works of the Lord have subsisted from the beginning as he arranged them,<br/>and from their creation he separated out their parts.<br/><br/>25. He has adorned his works forever,<br/>and the fairest of them to shine from age to age.<br/>They know neither hunger nor weariness,<br/>and they do not interrupt their task.<br/>26. None of them jostles its neighbor,<br/>and forever they obey the divine command.<br/><br/>27. After this, the Lord looked upon the earth,<br/>and he filled it with his good things.<br/>28. With animals of every kind he covered its surface,<br/>and it is to its bosom that they must return.</p>

### Chapter 17 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. The Lord formed man out of earth,<br/>and he makes him return into the earth.<br/>2. He assigned him a number of days and a set time,<br/>and he gave him power over everything that is on the earth.<br/><br/>3. According to his nature, he clothed him with strength,<br/>and he made him in his own image.<br/>4. He instilled the fear of him into all flesh,<br/>and gave him dominion over the beasts and the birds.</p>

<p class="v">5. He gave him discernment, a tongue, eyes,<br/>ears, and a heart to think with.<br/>6. He filled him with knowledge and understanding,<br/>and made known to him good and evil.<br/>7. He set his eye upon their hearts,<br/>to show them the greatness of his works.<br/>8. And so they will praise his holy name,<br/>proclaiming the wonders of his works.<br/><br/>9. He gave them knowledge besides,<br/>and put them in possession of the law of life.<br/>10. He made with them an everlasting covenant,<br/>and revealed to them his commandments.<br/>11. Their eyes beheld the splendors of his majesty,<br/>and their ears heard the magnificent tones of his voice.<br/>12. And he said to them: "Keep yourselves from all iniquity!"<br/>and he gave each of them commands concerning his neighbor.<br/><br/>13. Their ways are constantly before him;<br/>nothing can be hidden from his sight.<br/>14. Over every people he sets a ruler,<br/>but Israel is the Lord's own portion.<br/>15. All their works are before him, as the sun,<br/>and his eyes are ever turned upon their ways.<br/>16. Their injustices are not hidden from him,<br/>and all their sins are before the Lord.<br/>17. A man's charitable work is to him like a seal,<br/>and he keeps a man's good deed as the apple of his eye.<br/><br/>18. Afterward he will rise and repay them according to their deeds,<br/>and will bring down upon their heads what is owed them.<br/>19. Yet to those who repent he grants return,<br/>and he comforts those who have lost hope.<br/>20. Turn to the Lord and forsake your sins;<br/>pray before his face and lessen your offenses.<br/>21. Return to the Most High, turn away from injustice,<br/>and greatly detest what is abominable.<br/><br/>22. Who will praise the Most High in Sheol,<br/>in place of the living and those who render him their homage?<br/>23. For the dead man, as though he were nothing anymore, praise is impossible;<br/>he who has life and health praises the Lord.<br/>24. How great is the mercy of the Lord,<br/>and his compassion toward those who turn back to him!</p>

<p class="v">25. For not everything can be found in men,<br/>since the son of man is not immortal.<br/>26. What is brighter than the sun? And yet it is darkened:<br/>so the wicked man is mindful of flesh and blood.<br/>27. The sun visits the host of the stars in the heights of the heavens,<br/>but all men are earth and ashes.</p>

### Chapter 18 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. He who lives forever created all things without exception;<br/>2. the Lord alone is just.<br/>3. He has given no one the power to recount his works;<br/>and who shall discover his greatness?<br/>4. Who shall express the almighty power of his majesty,<br/>and who again shall tell of his mercies?<br/>5. Nothing to take away, nothing to add;<br/>it is impossible to penetrate the wonders of the Lord.<br/>6. When man has finished searching, he is only at the beginning,<br/>and when he stops, he does not know what to think.<br/><br/>7. What is man, and what good is he?<br/>What is his happiness and what is his misfortune?<br/>8. The number of a man's days is at most a hundred years.<br/>9. Like a drop of water taken from the sea and like a grain of sand,<br/>so are his few years compared to the day of eternity.<br/>10. This is why the Lord is patient toward men<br/>and pours out his mercy upon them.<br/>11. He sees and knows that their end is pitiable;<br/>this is why he is generous in forgiving.<br/><br/>12. The mercy of man is shown toward his neighbor,<br/>but the mercy of God extends to all flesh.<br/><br/>He reproves, he corrects, he instructs,<br/>and brings back to the fold, as the shepherd his flock.<br/>13. He has pity on those who accept correction,<br/>and on those who are eager to fulfill his precepts.</p>

<p class="v">14. My son, do not add insult to your kindnesses,<br/>nor words that provoke sorrow to all your gifts.<br/>15. Does not the dew refresh the heat of the wind?<br/>So a word is worth more than a gift.<br/>16. Do you not see that a word is better than a gift?<br/>The gracious man joins the two together.<br/>17. The fool makes bitter reproaches,<br/>and the gift of the envious man dries up the eyes.</p>

<p class="v">18. Before speaking, instruct yourself;<br/>before sickness, take care of yourself.<br/>19. Before judgment, examine yourself,<br/>and at the hour of inquiry, you will find favor.</p>

<p class="v">20. Before you are sick, humble yourself,<br/>and when you are in sin, return to God.</p>

<p class="v">21. Let nothing keep you from fulfilling your vow at the appointed time,<br/>and do not wait until death to discharge it.<br/>22. Before making a vow, prepare yourself,<br/>and do not be like a man who puts the Lord to the test.<br/>23. Think of the wrath of the last day,<br/>of the time of vengeance, when God will turn away his face.</p>

<p class="v">24. In the time of abundance, think of the time of hunger;<br/>in the days of wealth, think of poverty and want.<br/>25. From morning to evening the season changes:<br/>so every change is swift before the Lord.<br/>26. The wise man is on his guard in everything;<br/>in days of sin, he keeps himself from fault.<br/>27. Every sensible man knows wisdom,<br/>and pays homage to him who has found her.<br/>28. Those who grasp the sayings of the wise are themselves wise,<br/>and they pour forth perfect maxims.</p>

<p class="v">29. Do not give yourself over to your cravings,<br/>and guard yourself against your desires.<br/>30. If you grant your soul the satisfaction of its cravings,<br/>it will make you the laughingstock of your enemies.<br/><br/>31. Do not set your joy in an abundance of good fare,<br/>and do not join in fellowship with it.<br/>32. Do not impoverish yourself by giving banquets with borrowed money,<br/>and when you have nothing in your purse.</p>

### Chapter 19 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. The workman given to wine will not grow rich;<br/>he who does not take care of the little he has will soon fall into ruin.<br/><br/>2. Wine and women lead intelligent men astray,<br/>and he who attaches himself to courtesans is reckless.<br/>3. Maggots and worms will make him their prey,<br/>and the criminal soul will be cut off.</p>

<p class="v">4. He who believes too quickly is light-hearted,<br/>and he who falls into this fault sins against his own soul.</p>

<p class="v">5. He who takes pleasure in foolish talk will be condemned,<br/>6. and he who hates gossip keeps himself from evil.<br/><br/>7. Never repeat a word,<br/>and you will incur no harm.<br/>8. Do not repeat it to friend or to foe,<br/>and unless it be a fault for you to keep silent, do not reveal it.<br/>9. For if he hears you, he will be on his guard against you,<br/>and when the moment comes, he will show himself your enemy.<br/><br/>10. Have you heard some grave matter? Let it die with you!<br/>Have no fear, it will not make you burst.<br/>11. For a word he must keep, the fool is in anguish,<br/>like a woman in labor with child.<br/>12. Like an arrow lodged in the flesh of the thigh,<br/>so is a word in the heart of a fool.</p>

<p class="v">13. Question your friend; perhaps he has not done the thing;<br/>and if he has done it, that he may not do it again.<br/>14. Question your friend; perhaps he has not said the thing;<br/>and if he has said it, that he may not repeat it.<br/>15. Question your friend, for often there is slander,<br/>and do not believe everything that is said.<br/>16. There are those who fail, but without their heart being in it;<br/>and who has not sinned with his tongue?<br/>17. Question your friend before resorting to threats,<br/>and be careful to observe the law of the Most High.</p>

<p class="v">18. All wisdom consists in the fear of the Lord,<br/>and in all wisdom is the fulfillment of the law.<br/><br/>19. Wisdom is not skill in doing evil,<br/>and prudence is not found in the counsel of sinners.<br/>20. There is a cleverness that is execrable,<br/>and there is a folly that is nothing but a lack of wisdom.<br/>21. Better is he who has little understanding and fears God,<br/>than the man who has great sense and transgresses the law.<br/>22. There is a true cleverness, but one that violates justice,<br/>and there is one who twists a case to obtain the sentence he desires.<br/><br/>23. There is a wicked man who walks bowed down with grief,<br/>and his heart is full of deceit.<br/>24. He hangs his head, he is deaf on one side,<br/>and as soon as he is unnoticed, he gets ahead of you.</p>

<p class="v">25. And if, through weakness, he is kept from sinning,<br/>he will do evil when he finds the occasion.<br/><br/>26. By his bearing a man is known,<br/>and by the face he presents the wise man is known.<br/>27. A man's clothing, the laughter of his lips,<br/>and a man's gait reveal what he is.</p>

### Chapter 20 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. There is a rebuke that is not timely,<br/>and there is one who keeps silent who shows prudence.<br/>2. Better to reprove than to burn with suppressed anger;<br/>and he who confesses will be spared harm.<br/>3. Like the eunuch who desires to deflower a young girl,<br/>so is he who administers justice with violence.<br/>[How fine it is, when one is reproved, to show repentance!<br/>Thus you will escape willful sin.]<br/><br/>4. There is one who by keeping silent shows himself wise,<br/>and there is one who makes himself hateful by intemperance of speech.<br/>5. There is one who keeps silent because he has nothing to answer;<br/>another keeps silent because he knows the right time.<br/>6. The wise man keeps silent until the favorable moment,<br/>but the braggart and the rash man overstep it.<br/>7. He who multiplies words will be detested,<br/>and he who gives himself full license will make himself hateful.</p>

<p class="v">8. There is a man who finds in misfortune something fortunate,<br/>and there is unhoped-for good fortune that turns to his loss.<br/>9. There is a gift that brings you nothing,<br/>and there is a gift that is repaid twofold.<br/>10. From a brilliant position harm often results,<br/>and there is one who lifts up his head again after humiliation.<br/>11. There is one who buys many things at a vile price,<br/>who pays for them seven times their value.<br/>12. He who is wise in his speech makes himself loved,<br/>but the pleasant words of the fool are wholly wasted.</p>

<p class="v">13. The gift of the fool will be of no use to you;<br/>for his eyes, instead of one, are many.<br/>14. He gives little, and reproaches much,<br/>and he opens his mouth like a town crier.<br/><br/>He lends today, and will ask it back tomorrow:<br/>such a man is odious.<br/>15. The fool says: "I have no friend,<br/>and no one is grateful to me for my kindnesses;<br/>those who eat my bread have perverse tongues."—<br/>16. How many times, and by how many people, will he not be mocked?</p>

<p class="v">17. Better a fall on the pavement than a fall of the tongue;<br/>it is thus that the ruin of the wicked comes swiftly.<br/>18. An unpleasant man is like a tale told out of season;<br/>the ill-bred man has it constantly on his lips.<br/>19. A maxim is not accepted from the lips of a fool;<br/>for he does not utter it at the time that suits it.</p>

<p class="v">20. There is one who cannot sin, because of his poverty;<br/>and in his rest, he has no remorse.<br/><br/>21. There is one who ruins himself through false shame,<br/>and falls into ruin because of the look of a fool.<br/><br/>22. There is one who through false shame promises much to his friend,<br/>and thereby makes an enemy of him for nothing.<br/><br/>23. Falsehood in a man is a shameful stain;<br/>it is always on the lips of the ill-bred.<br/>24. Better a thief than the man who makes a trade of lying:<br/>both shall have ruin as their portion.<br/>25. The habit of the liar is dishonorable,<br/>and the shame of the liar is constantly with him.<br/><br/>26. He who is wise in his speech rises in esteem,<br/>and the prudent man is pleasing to the great.<br/><br/>27. He who tills his land will raise up his heap of grain,<br/>and he who pleases the great obtains pardon for his injustices.<br/><br/>28. Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise,<br/>and, like a muzzle on the mouth of an animal, they stop reproof.<br/><br/>29. Hidden wisdom, invisible treasure:<br/>what use is either the one or the other?<br/>30. Better the man who hides his folly than he who hides his wisdom.</p>

### Chapter 21 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. My son, have you sinned? Do it no more,<br/>but pray for your past faults.<br/>2. Flee from sin as from a serpent;<br/>for if you go near it, it will bite you.<br/>Its teeth are the teeth of a lion;<br/>they bring death to men.<br/>3. Every transgression is like a two-edged sword;<br/>the wound it makes is incurable.</p>

<p class="v">4. Threats and insults destroy wealth;<br/>it is thus that the house of the proud man is destroyed.</p>

<p class="v">5. The prayer of the poor man rises from his lips to the ear of the rich man;<br/>but upon the proud man his judgment will soon come.<br/>6. He who hates reproof walks in the footsteps of the sinner,<br/>but he who fears God turns to him with a sincere heart.<br/>7. The man mighty in speech makes himself known from afar;<br/>but the man of sense knows when he fails.<br/>8. The man who builds his house with money that is not his own<br/>is like one who gathers his stones for winter.</p>

<p class="v">9. The company of the wicked is a heap of tow;<br/>it will end by being the prey of fire.<br/>10. The way of sinners is paved with stones,<br/>but at its end is the pit of Sheol.</p>

<p class="v">11. He who observes the law masters his own thoughts,<br/>and the final result of the fear of the Lord is wisdom.<br/>12. He who lacks skill will not be instructed;<br/>but there is a skill that produces much bitterness.<br/>13. The knowledge of the wise man abounds like overflowing water,<br/>and his counsel is a fountain of life.<br/>14. The inward part of the fool is like a cracked vessel;<br/>it will hold no knowledge.<br/>15. Let the intelligent man hear a wise saying,<br/>he praises it and adds something to it.<br/>Let the voluptuous man hear it, it displeases him,<br/>and he casts it behind him.<br/><br/>16. The talk of the fool is like a burden on a journey,<br/>but on the lips of the intelligent man is found grace.<br/>17. The mouth of the prudent man is sought out in the assembly,<br/>and his words are pondered in the heart.<br/>18. Wisdom is for the fool like a house in ruins,<br/>and the knowledge of the fool is nothing but incoherent words.<br/>19. Instruction is for fools like chains on the feet,<br/>and manacles on the right hand.<br/>20. The fool, when he laughs, lets his voice burst out,<br/>but the clever man barely smiles, and softly.<br/>21. Instruction is for the sensible man like an ornament of gold,<br/>and like a bracelet on the right arm.<br/><br/>22. The fool enters the house with a quick step,<br/>but the man of experience halts timidly at the entrance.<br/>23. The fool bends down at the door to see into the house,<br/>but the well-bred man stands outside.<br/>24. It is a coarseness for a man to listen at the door;<br/>the sensible man is indignant at so shameful an act.<br/>25. The lips of fools utter nothing but foolishness,<br/>but the words of prudent men are weighed in the balance.<br/>26. In the mouth of fools is their heart,<br/>but the heart of the wise is their mouth.</p>

<p class="v">27. When the wicked man curses his adversary,<br/>it is himself that he curses.<br/>28. The talebearer defiles himself,<br/>and he is detested by all who come near him.</p>

### Chapter 22 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. The lazy man is like a stone covered with filth,<br/>and everyone hisses at his disgrace.<br/>2. The lazy man is like a lump of dung:<br/>whoever picks it up shakes his hand.</p>

<p class="v">3. An ill-bred son is the shame of the father who gave him life;<br/>a daughter of the same kind has come into the world to his detriment.<br/>4. A prudent daughter will find her husband,<br/>but one who brings shame is the grief of her father.<br/>5. The shameless girl brings shame on her father and her husband;<br/>both will despise her.<br/>6. Like music at a time of mourning, like a discourse out of season;<br/>but the rod and correction are wisdom at every time.</p>

<p class="v">7. To instruct a fool is to glue back together a broken pot;<br/>[to tell a thing to one who does not listen],<br/>it is to wake a man sunk in a deep sleep.<br/>8. It is like speaking to a man asleep to converse with a fool;<br/>at the end of your discourse, he will say: "What is it?"<br/><br/>9. Weep for the dead, for he is deprived of light;<br/>weep for the fool, for he is deprived of good sense.<br/>Weep gently for the dead, for he has found rest,<br/>but the life of the fool is worse than death.<br/>10. Mourning for the dead lasts seven days;<br/>for the fool and for the ungodly, it lasts all the days of their life.<br/><br/>11. With the fool do not have long conversations,<br/>and do not go about with the man devoid of sense.<br/>Beware of him, if you do not want trouble,<br/>and you will not be defiled by his contact.<br/>Turn away from him and you will find rest,<br/>and you will not have to grieve at the sight of his folly.<br/>12. What is heavier than lead,<br/>and what other name can be given it than fool?<br/>13. Sand, salt, a mass of iron<br/>are easier to carry than a man without understanding.</p>

<p class="v">14. A well-braced timber frame for a building<br/>will not be shaken loose by an earthquake:<br/>so a heart fixed on a maturely considered purpose<br/>will be without fear at the critical moment.<br/>15. The heart that rests on a thought of wisdom<br/>is like plaster mixed with sand on a polished wall.<br/>16. A fence on a height does not hold against the wind:<br/>so a timid heart with its foolish resolves will not withstand fear.</p>

<p class="v">17. He who bruises an eye causes tears to flow;<br/>he who bruises a heart stirs up a feeling of pain.<br/>18. He who throws a stone at birds puts them to flight,<br/>and he who reproaches a friend for a kindness dissolves the friendship.<br/>19. Have you drawn the sword against your friend?<br/>Do not despair; a return is possible.<br/>20. Have you opened your mouth against your friend?<br/>Be without fear; reconciliation is possible.<br/>But the reproach of a kindness, arrogance,<br/>the revealing of a secret, a treacherous stroke of the tongue:<br/>these put all friends to flight.<br/><br/>21. Remain faithful to your neighbor in his poverty,<br/>so that you may share with him in his prosperity.<br/>Remain with him in the days of his trial,<br/>so that you may have a part in the good things that come to him.<br/>22. Before the fire rise the vapor of the furnace and the smoke;<br/>likewise before the shedding of blood, insults resound.<br/>23. I will not be ashamed to defend my friend,<br/>and I will not hide myself from him;<br/>24. and if some harm comes to me through his doing,<br/>whoever learns of it will be on guard against him.</p>

<p class="v">25. Who will set a guard on my mouth,<br/>and a prudent seal upon my lips,<br/>that I may not fall because of them,<br/>and that my tongue may not destroy me!</p>

### Chapter 23 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Lord, Father and sovereign Master of my life,<br/>do not abandon me to the counsel of my own lips,<br/>and do not allow me to find in it an occasion for falling.</p>

<p class="v">2. Who will make my thoughts feel the whip,<br/>and the discipline of wisdom my heart,<br/>so as not to spare me in my follies,<br/>and not to give free rein to my sins:<br/>3. lest my follies increase,<br/>lest my sins multiply,<br/>lest I fall in the presence of my adversaries,<br/>and lest my enemy rejoice over me?<br/><br/>4. Lord, Father and God of my life,<br/>do not give me license of the eyes,<br/>5. and turn away from me evil desires.<br/>6. Let not the desires of the flesh and sensuality seize hold of me,<br/>and do not hand me over to a shameless soul.</p>

<p class="v">7. My children, listen to the discipline of the mouth;<br/>he who observes it will not be caught.<br/>8. By his lips the sinner will be caught;<br/>the slanderer and the insolent will find in it an occasion for falling.<br/><br/>9. Do not accustom your mouth to making oaths,<br/>and do not make a habit of pronouncing the name of the Holy One.<br/>10. For as a slave often put to torture<br/>cannot be free of bruises,<br/>so he who swears oaths and continually pronounces the name of the Holy One<br/>will not be pure of sin.<br/>11. The man who multiplies oaths multiplies iniquity,<br/>and the scourge will not depart from his house.<br/>If he has become guilty, his sin is upon him;<br/>if he pays no heed to it, his sin is doubled.<br/>If he has made a false oath, he will not be absolved,<br/>for his house will be filled with punishments.<br/><br/>12. There are words that call down death:<br/>let them not be found in the heritage of Jacob!<br/>All this is far removed from godly men;<br/>they do not engage in these sins.<br/>13. Do not accustom your mouth to vile coarseness,<br/>for it gives rise to guilty words.<br/>14. Remember your father and your mother,<br/>when you sit among the great,<br/>lest, forgetting them in their presence,<br/>you fall into foolishness through mere habit,<br/>and come to wish you had never been born,<br/>and to curse the day of your birth.<br/>15. A man who accustoms himself to coarse language<br/>will never attain wisdom.</p>

<p class="v">16. Two kinds of men multiply sins,<br/>and a third draws down wrath.<br/>The man whom passion burns, like a blazing fire,<br/>will not be quenched until he is consumed.<br/>The man unchaste in his own flesh<br/>will not cease until the fire is kindled.<br/>17. To the voluptuous man all bread is sweet;<br/>he will not stop until he is dead.<br/>18. The man who forsakes the marriage bed<br/>says in his heart: "Who sees me?<br/>Darkness surrounds me, the walls hide me,<br/>and no one notices me: what should I fear?<br/>The Most High will not remember my sins."—<br/>19. The eyes of men are what he fears,<br/>and he does not know that the eyes of the Lord<br/>are a thousand times brighter than the sun;<br/>that they watch all the ways of man,<br/>and penetrate even into hidden places!<br/>20. Before they are created, all things are known to the Lord,<br/>and they are known to him still after their completion.<br/>21. The adulterer will be punished in the streets of the city,<br/>and where he did not expect it, he will be caught.<br/><br/>22. It is the same with the woman who has forsaken her husband,<br/>and given an heir from a union with a stranger.<br/>23. For first she has disobeyed the law of the Most High;<br/>secondly, she has sinned against her husband;<br/>and thirdly, she has committed adultery,<br/>and given children of alien blood.<br/>24. She will be brought before the assembly,<br/>and punishment will visit her children.<br/>25. Her children will strike no roots,<br/>and her branches will bear no fruit.<br/>26. She will leave behind a memory doomed to a curse,<br/>and her infamy will never be blotted out.<br/>27. And those who survive will know<br/>that there is nothing better than the fear of the Lord,<br/>nothing sweeter than to keep his commandments.<br/>[It is a great glory to follow the Lord;<br/>to cling to him is length of days].</p>

### Chapter 24 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Wisdom praises herself,<br/>and glories in the midst of her people.<br/>2. She opens her mouth in the assembly of the Most High,<br/>and glories in the presence of his Majesty:<br/><br/>3. I came forth from the mouth of the Most High,<br/>and, like a mist, I covered the earth.<br/>4. I dwelt in the heights,<br/>and my throne was upon a pillar of cloud.<br/>5. Alone, I made the circuit of the heavens,<br/>and I walked in the depths of the abyss.<br/>6. In the waves of the sea and over all the earth,<br/>in every people and every nation I held sway.<br/><br/>7. Among them all I sought a place of rest,<br/>and in what domain I was to dwell.<br/>8. Then the Creator of all things gave me his commands,<br/>and he who created me made my tent to rest;<br/>and he said to me: "Dwell in Jacob,<br/>have your inheritance in Israel."<br/>9. Before all ages, from the beginning he created me,<br/>and unto eternity I shall not cease to be.<br/>10. I exercised my ministry before him in the holy tabernacle,<br/>and thus I had a fixed dwelling in Zion.<br/>11. Likewise, he made me rest in the beloved city,<br/>and in Jerusalem is the seat of my dominion.<br/>12. I struck my roots in the glorified people,<br/>in the portion of the Lord, in his inheritance.</p>

<p class="v">13. I grew tall like the cedar on Lebanon,<br/>and like the cypress on Mount Hermon.<br/>14. I grew tall like the palm tree on the shores,<br/>and like the rose bushes at Jericho;<br/>like a fair olive tree in the plain,<br/>and I grew tall like the plane tree.<br/>15. I gave forth perfume like cinnamon and like fragrant balsam,<br/>and like choice myrrh I spread a sweet odor,<br/>like galbanum, onyx and stacte,<br/>and like the vapor of incense in the tabernacle.<br/>16. I spread out my branches like the terebinth,<br/>and my boughs are boughs of glory and grace.<br/>17. Like the vine, I brought forth charming shoots,<br/>and my flowers yielded fruits of glory and riches.<br/>[I am the mother of pure love, of the fear of God,<br/>of knowledge and of holy hope].<br/><br/>18. Come to me, all you who desire me,<br/>and take your fill of my fruits.<br/>19. For my memory is sweeter than honey,<br/>and my possession sweeter than the honeycomb.<br/>20. Those who eat me will hunger still,<br/>and those who drink me will thirst still.<br/>21. He who listens to me will never be put to shame,<br/>and those who act through me will not sin.<br/><br/>22. All this is the book of the covenant of the Most High God,<br/>it is the law that Moses gave,<br/>to be the heritage of the assemblies of Jacob.<br/>23. This law makes Wisdom overflow, like the Pishon,<br/>and like the Tigris at the time of new fruits.<br/>24. It pours forth understanding in floods, like the Euphrates,<br/>like the Jordan at the time of harvest.<br/>25. It makes knowledge gush forth, like the River,<br/>like the Gihon at the time of vintage.<br/>26. The first who studied it did not finish knowing it,<br/>and likewise, the last has not fathomed it.<br/>27. For her understanding is vaster than the sea,<br/>and her counsel deeper than the great abyss.</p>

<p class="v">28. And I flowed forth like a channel drawn from a river,<br/>like an aqueduct watering a garden of delight.<br/>29. I said: "I will water my garden,<br/>I will drench my flower bed."<br/>And behold, my channel became a river,<br/>and my river became a sea.<br/>30. I mean, then, to make instruction shine forth yet again like the dawn,<br/>to make its maxims known afar;<br/>31. I mean also to pour out doctrine like a prophecy,<br/>and to leave it as an inheritance to generations far off.<br/><br/>32. Know that I have not labored for myself alone,<br/>but for all who seek Wisdom.</p>

### Chapter 25 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Three things please me,<br/>and they are beautiful before the Lord and men:<br/>concord between brothers, friendship between neighbors,<br/>and good accord between husband and wife.<br/>2. But there are three kinds of people whom I hate,<br/>and whose life is utterly hateful to me:<br/>the proud poor man, the rich man who practices fraud,<br/>and the lustful old man devoid of sense.</p>

<p class="v">3. You have not gathered in your youth:<br/>how then would you possess in your old age?<br/>4. How fine it is for gray hairs to judge rightly,<br/>for old age to know good counsel!<br/>5. How well wisdom befits the aged,<br/>prudence and counsel those who are honored!<br/>6. The crown of the aged is rich experience;<br/>their glory is the fear of the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">7. There are nine things that in my heart I count happy,<br/>and a tenth that my tongue proclaims:<br/>the man who has joy in his children,<br/>and he who lives long enough to see the ruin of his enemies.<br/>8. Happy he who dwells with a sensible wife,<br/>and he who does not sin with his tongue!<br/>[Happy he who has found a faithful friend],<br/>and he who does not serve masters unworthy of him!<br/>9. Happy he who has found prudence,<br/>and he who teaches it to an attentive ear!<br/>10. How great is the man who has found wisdom!<br/>Yet he is not above him who fears the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">11. The fear of the Lord surpasses all things;<br/>he who possesses it, to whom shall he be compared?<br/>[The fear of the Lord is the beginning of his love,<br/>and faith is the beginning of attachment to God].</p>

<p class="v">12. All sufferings, but not suffering of the heart;<br/>all wickednesses, but not the wickedness of a woman.<br/>13. All evils, but not the evil caused by adversaries,<br/>all vengeances, but not the vengeance of enemies.<br/><br/>14. There is no venom worse than the venom of the serpent,<br/>and there is no anger greater than the anger of a woman.<br/>15. I would rather dwell with a lion and a dragon,<br/>than live with a wicked woman.<br/>16. The wickedness of a woman changes her countenance;<br/>it makes her face as black as sackcloth.<br/>17. Her husband goes to sit among his friends,<br/>and, hearing them, he sighs bitterly.<br/>18. All wickedness is light, compared to the wickedness of a woman:<br/>may the lot of sinners fall upon her!<br/><br/>19. Like a sandy climb for the feet of an old man,<br/>so is a talkative wife for a peaceable husband.<br/>20. Do not let yourself be seduced by a woman's beauty,<br/>and let no woman stir your desire.<br/>21. It is a cause for indignation, a reproach and a great shame,<br/>that a wife should provide her husband's keep.<br/>22. Dejection of heart, sadness of face, suffering of soul:<br/>this is what a wicked wife produces.<br/>Drooping hands, and knees that give way:<br/>this is what a wife who does not make her husband happy produces.<br/>23. It was through a woman that sin began;<br/>it is because of her that we all die.<br/><br/>24. Give water no outlet,<br/>nor a wicked wife any authority.<br/>25. If she does not walk as your hand guides her,<br/>cut her off from your flesh.</p>
### Chapter 26 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Happy is the husband of a virtuous wife,<br/>and the number of his days shall be doubled.<br/>2. A strong woman is the joy of her husband,</p>

<p class="v">and he spends his years in peace.<br/>3. A virtuous wife is a good portion;<br/>she shall be given as a share to those who fear the Lord.<br/>4. Rich or poor, her husband's heart is glad,<br/>and at all times his face is cheerful.<br/><br/>5. There are three things my heart dreads,<br/>and concerning a fourth, I pray before the Lord:<br/>the evil talk of a whole city,<br/>the gathering of a mob, and slander:<br/>all these things are more hateful to me than death;<br/>6. but grief of heart and affliction, this is a wife jealous of another,<br/>and the scourge of a tongue that tells its grievances to all.<br/>7. A wicked wife is like a pair of ill-matched oxen;<br/>he who holds her is like one who has caught hold of a scorpion.<br/><br/>8. A woman given to wine is a great occasion of wrath;<br/>she will not even hide her shame.<br/>9. By the boldness of her look, by the fluttering of her eyelids,<br/>the unchastity of a woman is known.<br/>10. Keep close watch over a headstrong daughter,<br/>lest, seeing your negligence, she give herself over to debauchery.<br/>11. Guard yourself from following a shameless eye;<br/>and do not be surprised, otherwise, if it leads you into sin.<br/>12. As a thirsty traveler opens his mouth,<br/>and drinks of any water he finds,<br/>so the shameless woman sits down before every post,<br/>and opens her quiver before every arrow.<br/><br/>13. The graciousness of a wife delights her husband,<br/>and her understanding fills his bones with vigor.<br/>14. A silent wife is a gift from God,<br/>and nothing is comparable to a well-trained woman.<br/>15. A modest woman is a grace above every grace,<br/>and no treasure is worth a chaste woman.<br/>16. The sun rises in the heights of the Lord:<br/>so the beauty of a good wife shines in her well-ordered house.<br/>17. As the lamp that shines upon the sacred lampstand,<br/>so is beauty of face on a noble stature.<br/>18. As pillars of gold upon bases of silver,<br/>so are shapely feet upon steadfast heels.</p>

<p class="v">19. Two things grieve my heart,<br/>and a third stirs up my indignation:<br/>a man of war who suffers want,<br/>men of understanding who are held in contempt;<br/>one who turns from righteousness to sin,<br/>the Lord prepares him for the sword.</p>

<p class="v">20. A merchant will scarcely avoid wrongdoing,<br/>and a wine-seller will not be free from sin.</p>

### Chapter 27 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Many sin for the sake of money,<br/>and he who seeks to grow rich turns away his eyes.<br/>2. A peg is driven in between the joints of stones:<br/>so sin thrusts itself in between selling and buying.<br/>3. If you do not hold fast to the fear of God,<br/>your house will soon be destroyed.</p>

<p class="v">4. When a sieve is shaken, the refuse remains behind:<br/>so the failings of a man appear in his speech.<br/>5. The furnace tests the vessels of the potter,<br/>and the trial of a man is in his conversation.<br/>6. The fruit of a tree shows the care given to it:<br/>so a word reveals the thoughts of a man's heart.<br/>7. Praise no one before he has spoken,<br/>for speech is the test of men.</p>

<p class="v">8. If you pursue righteousness, you will attain it,<br/>and you will clothe yourself with it as with a robe of honor.<br/>9. Birds gather together with their own kind:<br/>so truth returns to those who practice it.<br/>10. The lion lies in wait for its prey:<br/>so sin lies in wait for those who commit injustice.</p>

<p class="v">11. The speech of a godly man is always wisdom,<br/>but the fool changes like the moon.<br/>12. If you must go among fools, watch for the right time;<br/>but stay continually among men of reflection.<br/>13. The conversation of fools is detestable;<br/>their laughter breaks out in the delight of sin.<br/>14. The speech of one who swears many oaths makes the hair stand on end;<br/>when he quarrels, one stops one's ears.<br/>15. The quarrels of the proud draw blood,<br/>and their abuse is grievous to hear.</p>

<p class="v">16. He who reveals secrets loses trust,<br/>and he will never find a friend to his liking.<br/>17. Love your friend and be faithful to him;<br/>but if you disclose his secrets, do not run after him.<br/>18. For as a man puts his enemy to death,<br/>so you have killed the affection of your friend.</p>

<p class="v">19. And as when you have let a bird escape from your hand,<br/>so you have driven away your friend, and you will not catch him again.<br/>20. Do not pursue him, for he is far away;<br/>he has fled like a gazelle escaped from the net.<br/>21. A wound is bound up, and after an insult one is reconciled;<br/>but he who has revealed secrets has no more hope.</p>

<p class="v">22. He who winks with his eye devises iniquity,<br/>and no one can rid himself of him.<br/>23. In your presence, he will have nothing but sweetness on his lips,<br/>he will admire your words;<br/>but afterward he will change his speech,<br/>and give an unpleasant turn to your discourse.<br/>24. I hate many things, but nothing so much as him;<br/>the Lord also holds him in aversion.</p>

<p class="v">25. He who throws a stone into the air throws it upon his own head:<br/>so a treacherous blow wounds the treacherous man.<br/>26. Whoever digs a pit will fall into it,<br/>and whoever sets a snare will be caught in it.<br/>27. He who does evil will see it roll back upon him,<br/>and he will not know where it comes from.<br/>28. Mockery and insult are in the mouth of the proud,<br/>but vengeance lies in wait for them like a lion.<br/>29. They will be caught in a trap, those who rejoice at the misfortune of the godly,<br/>and grief will consume them before their death.</p>

<p class="v">30. Resentment and anger, they too are detestable,<br/>and the sinner possesses them.</p>

### Chapter 28 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. He who takes revenge will find vengeance from the Lord,<br/>who will keep careful account of his sins.<br/>2. Forgive your neighbor his wrongdoing,<br/>and then, when you pray, your sins shall be forgiven.<br/>3. A man nurses anger against another man,<br/>and yet seeks healing from God!...<br/>4. He has no pity on a man, his fellow,<br/>and yet pleads for his own faults!...<br/>5. He, who is but flesh, holds a grudge;<br/>who then will obtain forgiveness of his sins for him?<br/>6. Remember your end, and cease from hating;<br/>remember corruption and death, and keep the commandments.<br/>7. Remember the commandments, and bear no grudge against your neighbor;<br/>remember the covenant of the Most High, and overlook the offense.</p>

<p class="v">8. Keep yourself far from strife, and you will sin less;<br/>for a hot-tempered man inflames the quarrel,</p>

<p class="v">9. and the sinner brings trouble among friends,<br/>and casts slander among those who live in peace.<br/>10. Fire blazes up in proportion to the fuel that feeds it:<br/>so the anger of a man kindles in proportion to his power.<br/>According to his wealth, he lets his fury rise;<br/>it flares up according to the violence of the quarrel.<br/>11. A hasty quarrel kindles a fire,<br/>and a reckless dispute sheds blood.<br/>12. If you blow upon a spark, it blazes up;<br/>if you spit upon it, it goes out:<br/>both things come from your mouth.</p>

<p class="v">13. Curse the talebearer and the double-tongued man,<br/>for they have destroyed many who lived in peace.<br/>14. The slanderous tongue has brought many to ruin,<br/>and has driven them from one people to another;<br/>it has overthrown strong cities,<br/>and cast down the palaces of the great.<br/>15. The slanderous tongue has caused valiant women to be driven out,<br/>and has stripped them of the fruit of their labors.<br/><br/>16. Whoever lends it his ear will find no more rest,<br/>and he will have no more peace in his dwelling.<br/>17. The blow of a rod leaves bruises,<br/>the blow of a tongue breaks bones.<br/>18. Many have perished by the edge of the sword;<br/>but not as many as those who have perished by the tongue.<br/><br/>19. Happy is he who is sheltered from it,<br/>who is not given over to its fury,<br/>who has not dragged its yoke,<br/>and who has not been bound with its chains!<br/>20. For its yoke is a yoke of iron,<br/>and its chains are chains of bronze.<br/>21. The death it deals is a dreadful death,<br/>and Sheol is better than it.<br/><br/>22. It will have no power over the godly,<br/>and they will not be burned by its flame.<br/>23. Those who forsake the Lord will fall into it;<br/>and it will consume them without being quenched.<br/><br/>24. Behold, hedge your estate with a fence of thorns,<br/>bind up your gold and your silver in a bag;<br/>25. and make a balance and weights for your words,<br/>and make a door and a bolt for your mouth.<br/>26. Take care not to fail through the tongue,<br/>lest you fall before him who lies in wait for you.</p>

### Chapter 29 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. He who practices mercy lends to his neighbor,<br/>and he who supports him with his hand keeps the commandments.<br/>2. Lend to your neighbor when he is in need,<br/>and, in your turn, repay your neighbor, when the time comes, what he lent you.<br/>3. Keep your word, and deal loyally with him,<br/>and you will find at all times what is necessary for you.<br/><br/>4. Many regard what has been lent them as a windfall,<br/>and cause trouble to those who have come to their aid.<br/>5. Until they have received it, they kiss the neighbor's hand,<br/>with a humble voice they praise his wealth;<br/>but when the moment comes to repay, they take delays,<br/>they return nothing but words of complaint,<br/>and blame the hardness of the times.<br/>6. If he has means, the lender will scarcely receive half,<br/>and will think he has made a windfall.<br/>If he has none, he is defrauded of his money,<br/>and this man, without meaning to, makes an enemy of his debtor,<br/>who repays him with curses and insults,<br/>and who, instead of honor, gives him nothing but outrage.<br/>7. Many refuse to lend because of the malice of men;<br/>they fear being needlessly defrauded of their money.<br/><br/>8. Yet be lenient toward the unfortunate,<br/>and do not make him wait for your almsgiving.<br/>9. Assist the poor for the sake of the divine commandment,<br/>and, because of his distress, do not send him away empty-handed.<br/>10. Consent to lose your money for the sake of your brother and your friend,<br/>and do not let it rust profitlessly under a stone.<br/><br/>11. Use your treasure according to the precepts of the Most High,<br/>and it will profit you more than gold.<br/>12. Store your almsgiving in your chambers,<br/>and it will deliver you from every misfortune.<br/>13. Better than a strong shield, better than a mighty spear,<br/>it will fight for you in the face of the enemy.</p>

<p class="v">14. A good man goes surety for his neighbor,<br/>and only one who has lost all shame abandons him.<br/>15. Do not forget the kindness of him who stood surety,<br/>for he pledged himself for you.<br/>16. The sinner causes his surety to lose his goods,<br/>and the ungrateful man abandons his savior.<br/>17. A pledge of surety has brought many prosperous men to ruin,<br/>and has tossed them about like the waves of the sea;<br/>18. it has caused powerful men to be banished,<br/>and they have had to wander among foreign nations.</p>

<p class="v">19. The sinner is quick to become surety,<br/>and he who pursues gain will experience the rigor of judgments.<br/>20. Assist your neighbor according to your power,<br/>and take care lest you yourself fall into misfortune.</p>

<p class="v">21. The first thing for life is water and bread,<br/>clothing and a house to cover one's nakedness.<br/>22. Better the life of the poor man under a roof of planks,<br/>than sumptuous fare in a house not one's own.<br/>23. Whether you have little or much, be content,[and you will not hear yourself reproached for being a stranger.]<br/>24. It is a sorry life to go from house to house;<br/>where one is received as a stranger, one dares not open one's mouth.<br/>25. You will give your host food and drink without his being grateful for it,<br/>and you will hear, on top of it, bitter words:<br/>26. "Come, stranger, prepare the table,<br/>and if you have something, give me food.<br/>27. "Be gone, stranger, away from this splendor;<br/>I have my brother to receive, I need my house."<br/>28. It is hard for a man of sense<br/>to be reproached for his hospitality and insulted by his own debtor.</p>

### Chapter 30 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. He who loves his son often makes him feel the rod,<br/>so that afterward he may have joy of him.<br/>2. He who raises his son well will draw advantages from him,<br/>and will glory in him before his acquaintances.<br/>3. He who instructs his son will make his enemy jealous,<br/>and will rejoice in him before his friends.<br/>4. Does his father come to die? It is as if he had not died,<br/>for he leaves behind him one who resembles him.<br/>5. During his life, he sees him and rejoices,<br/>and at his death, he is not grieved.<br/>6. He leaves behind one who will avenge him on his enemies,<br/>and who will show gratitude to his friends.<br/><br/>7. He who spoils his son will bind up his wounds,<br/>and at his every cry his bowels will be moved.<br/>8. The unbroken horse becomes unmanageable: so a son left to himself becomes reckless.<br/>9. Pamper your child, and he will make you tremble;<br/>play with him, and he will bring you grief.</p>

<p class="v">10. Do not laugh with him, lest you have to grieve with him,<br/>and lest in the end you gnash your teeth.<br/>11. Do not give him full freedom in his youth,<br/>and do not close your eyes to his follies.<br/><br/>12. [Bend his neck while he is young,]<br/>and bruise his sides while he is a child,<br/>lest he become stubborn and no longer obey you,<br/>[and lest you have sorrow of heart.]<br/>13. Correct your son, and make him work,<br/>lest he stumble through your shameful weakness.</p>

<p class="v">14. Better a poor man, healthy and vigorous,<br/>than a rich man whose body is scourged by disease.<br/>15. Health and a good constitution are worth more than all gold,<br/>and a vigorous body is preferable to an immense fortune.<br/>16. There is no wealth preferable to bodily health,<br/>and there is no joy better than the joy of the heart.<br/>17. Better death than a life of bitterness,<br/>and eternal rest than continual suffering.<br/>18. Good things poured out on a closed mouth<br/>are like food offerings placed upon a tomb.<br/>19. What good is an offering to an idol?<br/>It will not eat it and will not smell its scent:<br/>20. so it is with the man whom God pursues with sickness:<br/>he sees with his eyes, and he sighs,<br/>as a eunuch sighs who holds a virgin in his arms.</p>

<p class="v">21. Do not give your soul over to sadness,<br/>and do not torment yourself with your thoughts.<br/>22. Joy of heart is the life of man,<br/>and gladness of man means length of days for him.<br/>23. Love your soul and console your heart,<br/>and drive sadness far from you;<br/>grief has killed many,<br/>and there is no profit in it.<br/>24. Rage and anger shorten the days,<br/>and worries bring old age before its time.<br/>25. A generous and good heart takes care<br/>of the food that forms its nourishment.</p>

### Chapter 31 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. The wakeful nights of the rich man waste away his flesh,<br/>and worries take away his sleep.<br/>2. Perpetual worry prevents sleep,<br/>as a grave illness banishes it.<br/><br/>3. The rich man labors to amass riches,<br/>and when he rests, he gluts himself with pleasures.<br/>4. The poor man labors, for want of enough to live on,<br/>and when he rests, he lacks everything.<br/><br/>5. He who loves gold will not be without sin,<br/>and he who pursues corruption will be glutted with it.<br/>6. Many have been given over to ruin because of gold,<br/>and their destruction was before them.<br/>7. Gold is a stumbling-block for those who sacrifice to it;<br/>every fool will be caught by it.<br/><br/>8. Happy the rich man who is found without blemish,<br/>and who has not gone after gold!<br/>9. Who is he, that we may proclaim him happy?<br/>For he has done a marvelous thing among his people.<br/><br/>10. Who is he that has been tested in this and found blameless?<br/>Let this trial be a matter of glory for him!<br/>Who could have broken the law and did not break it,<br/>could have done evil and did not do it?<br/>11. His prosperity will be made secure,<br/>and the assembly will proclaim his good deeds.</p>

<p class="v">12. Have you taken your place at a well-furnished table,<br/>do not open your mouth wide before it,<br/>and do not say: "There is plenty upon it."<br/>13. Remember that the envious eye is an evil thing;<br/>has anything more evil been created than the envious eye? So it weeps out of every face.<br/>14. Wherever it looks, do not reach out your hand,<br/>and do not collide with it in the dish.<br/><br/>15. Judge your neighbor's desires by your own,<br/>and act in all things with reflection.</p>

<p class="v">16. Eat, as befits a man, of what is before you,<br/>and do not chew noisily, lest you cause disgust.<br/>17. Be the first to stop, out of good breeding,<br/>and do not show yourself insatiable, lest you give offense.<br/>18. If you are seated in a large company,<br/>do not reach out your hand before the others.<br/><br/>19. How little suffices for a well-bred man!<br/>So, on his bed, he breathes freely.<br/>20. Healthy sleep belongs to the sober stomach;<br/>one rises early and has one's wits about one.<br/>The pains of sleeplessness, vomiting, and colic belong to the intemperate man.<br/>21. If you have been led to eat too much,<br/>get up, walk about freely, and you will be relieved.<br/>22. Listen to me, my son, and do not despise me,<br/>and in the end you will experience the truth of my words:<br/>in all your actions, be diligent,<br/>and no illness will befall you.<br/><br/>23. Lips bless him who is generous at his table,<br/>and the testimony given to his generosity is true.<br/>24. The city murmurs against him who is stingy at his table,<br/>and the testimony given to his stinginess is accurate.<br/><br/>25. Do not play the brave man with wine,<br/>for wine has destroyed many.<br/>26. The furnace tests steel when it is tempered;<br/>so wine tests hearts when the proud quarrel.<br/>27. Wine is like life for man,<br/>if you drink it in its proper measure.<br/>What life is there for one who lacks wine?<br/>And indeed wine was made to gladden men.<br/>28. Gladness of heart and joy of soul,<br/>such is wine taken at the right time, in proper measure.<br/>29. Bitterness of soul is wine drunk in excess,<br/>when one is excited and quarrels.<br/>30. Drunkenness inflames the fool's fury and brings him down;<br/>it diminishes his strength and brings on wounds.<br/><br/>31. At a banquet, do not reproach your neighbor,<br/>and do not treat him with contempt while he is rejoicing;<br/>do not address insulting words to him,<br/>and do not press him by demanding something back from him.</p>

### Chapter 32 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Have they made you master of the feast? Do not exalt yourself;<br/>be among the guests as one of them.<br/>Take care of them, and only then sit down.</p>

<p class="v">2. When you have fulfilled all your duties, take your place,<br/>so as to rejoice on their account,<br/>and, for the fair ordering of the banquet, receive the crown.<br/><br/>3. Speak, old man, for it is fitting for you,<br/>but with precision and sound teaching, and without hindering the music.<br/>4. When music is being listened to, do not pour out words,<br/>and do not display your wisdom out of season.<br/>5. A seal of carbuncle set in gold,<br/>such is a harmonious concert at a banquet.<br/>6. A seal of emerald in a setting of gold,<br/>such is a sweet melody with pleasant wine.<br/><br/>7. Speak, young man, if there is use in it for you;<br/>hardly twice, if you are questioned.<br/>8. Cut your speech short, much in few words;<br/>be like a man who has knowledge and knows how to be silent.<br/>9. Among the great, do not make yourself their equal,<br/>and where there are elders, be sparing of words.<br/>10. Before the thunder the lightning flashes:<br/>so before the modest young man goes favor.<br/>11. When the hour comes, rise from the table without delay;<br/>run to your house, and do not be careless.<br/>12. There amuse yourself, indulge your fancies,<br/>yet without sinning by insolent speech.<br/>13. And for all this, bless Him who created you,<br/>and who fills you to overflowing with all his good gifts.</p>

<p class="v">14. He who fears the Lord accepts instruction,<br/>and those who seek him eagerly will find his favor.<br/>15. He who seeks the law will find fullness in it;<br/>but for the hypocrite, it will be an occasion of stumbling.<br/>16. Those who fear the Lord will find the true judgment,<br/>and they will make just sentences shine forth like a torch.<br/><br/>17. The sinner declines correction,<br/>and finds excuses to his liking.</p>

<p class="v">18. The man of understanding despises no counsel,<br/>but the stranger and the proud man are held back by no fear,<br/>and, after having acted, they give it no further thought,<br/>[and so they are convicted of folly.]<br/><br/>19. Do nothing without reflection,<br/>and after the deed, you will have no cause to repent.<br/>20. Do not go on a broken road,<br/>and you will not stumble against the stones.<br/>21. Do not trust an even path,<br/>and be on your guard even with your own children.<br/><br/>22. In all that you do, have confidence in your own soul,<br/>for this too is the keeping of the commandments.<br/>23. He who trusts in the law heeds its precepts,<br/>and he who trusts in the Lord will suffer no harm.</p>

### Chapter 33 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Upon him who fears the Lord no misfortune will fall;<br/>but if he is tried, he will be delivered.<br/>2. The wise man does not hate the law,<br/>but he who is a hypocrite toward it is like a ship in a storm.<br/>3. The man of understanding trusts in the law,<br/>and for him the law is as trustworthy as the oracle of the Urim.</p>

<p class="v">4. Prepare your speech, and so you will be listened to;<br/>gather your knowledge, and answer.<br/>5. The inward part of the fool is like the wheel of a cart,<br/>and his thought like a turning axle.<br/>6. The stallion is the image of the mocking friend:<br/>he neighs under every rider.</p>

<p class="v">7. Why does one day surpass another day,<br/>since the light of all the days of the year comes from the sun?<br/>8. It is the wisdom of the Lord that has established distinctions between them,<br/>he has instituted different seasons and feasts.<br/>9. Among the days, there are some he has exalted and sanctified,<br/>and there are some he has counted among ordinary days.</p>

<p class="v">10. So all men come from dust,<br/>from the earth from which Adam was formed.<br/>11. But with great wisdom the Lord has distinguished them,<br/>and has made them walk in different ways.<br/>12. He has blessed some and exalted them;<br/>he has sanctified others and brought them near to himself.<br/>Others, he has cursed and brought low,<br/>and has cast them down from their places.<br/><br/>13. As clay is in the hand of the potter,<br/>and he disposes of it according to his good pleasure,<br/>so men are in the hand of Him who made them,<br/>and he deals with them according to his judgment.<br/>14. Opposite evil is good, opposite death, life:<br/>so opposite the righteous is the sinner.<br/>15. Consider likewise all the works of the Most High:<br/>they are two by two, the one set against the other.</p>

<p class="v">16. As for me, coming last, I have devoted my wakeful nights to wisdom,<br/>like one who gleans the grapes after the vintage;<br/>by the blessing of the Lord I got ahead of the others,<br/>and, like the grape-gatherer, I have filled the winepress.<br/>17. Acknowledge that I have not labored for myself alone,<br/>but for all those who seek wisdom.<br/>18. Hear me, then, leaders of the people;<br/>presiding officers of the assembly, lend me your ear.</p>

<p class="v">19. Neither to your son nor to your wife, neither to your brother nor to your friend,<br/>give power over yourself during your lifetime,<br/>and do not give your goods to another,<br/>lest, filled with regret, you should have to address entreaties to them.<br/>20. As long as you live and breath remains in you,<br/>do not enslave yourself to any flesh.<br/>21. For it is better that your children should ask of you,<br/>than that you yourself should have to look to the hands of your children.<br/>22. In all that you do, remain the master,<br/>and let no stain be set upon your reputation.<br/>23. When the end of the days of your life comes,<br/>and the moment of death, distribute your inheritance.</p>

<p class="v">24. For the donkey, fodder, the stick, and the load;<br/>for the slave, bread, correction, and work.<br/>25. Keep your slave at work, and you will be at rest;<br/>leave his hands idle, and he will seek freedom.<br/>26. The yoke and the strap bend the neck;<br/>for the wicked slave, torture and pain.<br/><br/>27. Send him to work, so that he does not remain idle,<br/>for idleness teaches much evil.<br/>28. Set him to labor, that is what suits him;<br/>and if he does not obey, tighten his fetters;<br/>but do not go beyond measure with anyone,<br/>and do nothing contrary to justice.<br/><br/>29. If you have a slave, let him be as yourself,<br/>for you have acquired him with blood.<br/>30. If you have a slave, treat him as yourself,<br/>and so you will bind him to your soul.<br/>31. If you mistreat him and he takes flight,<br/>on what road will you go to look for him?</p>

### Chapter 34 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. The fool gives himself over to vain and deceptive hopes,<br/>and dreams give wings to the foolish.<br/>2. It is like trying to grasp a shadow and catch the wind,<br/>to dwell upon dreams.<br/>3. One thing after another, that is what one sees in a dream;<br/>it is like the image of a face facing a face.<br/>4. From uncleanness, what pure thing can come?<br/>From falsehood, what true thing can come?<br/>5. Divination, omens, and dreams are vain things,<br/>like the fancies of the heart of a pregnant woman.<br/><br/>6. Unless they are sent by the Most High, in a visitation,<br/>do not give your heart over to them.<br/>7. For dreams have led many astray,<br/>and those who rested their hopes upon them have fallen.<br/>8. But the law is fulfilled without falsehood,<br/>as every wise word from a faithful mouth comes true.</p>

<p class="v">9. The educated man knows many things,<br/>and the man of great experience speaks wisely.</p>

<p class="v">10. He who has not been tested knows little,<br/>and he who has traveled possesses great prudence.<br/>11. I have seen many things in my travels,<br/>and my knowledge is greater than my words.<br/>12. Often I have been in danger of death,<br/>and I have been saved thanks to this experience.</p>

<p class="v">13. The spirit of those who fear the Lord shall live,<br/>for their hope is in him who saves them.<br/>14. He who fears the Lord is afraid of nothing;<br/>he does not tremble, for God is his hope.<br/>15. Happy the soul of him who fears the Lord!<br/>On whom does it lean, and who is its support?<br/>16. The eyes of the Lord are upon those who love him;<br/>he is a mighty protector, a support full of strength,<br/>a shelter from the east wind, a shelter from the heat of noonday,<br/>a guard against stumbling, a help against falling;<br/>17. he raises up the soul, he lightens the eyes,<br/>he gives health, life, and blessing.</p>

<p class="v">18. To sacrifice ill-gotten goods is to make a mockery of an offering;<br/>and the mockeries of sinners cannot be pleasing to God.<br/>19. The Most High does not accept the offerings of the wicked,<br/>and it is not for their many victims that he forgives sins.<br/><br/>20. He sacrifices a son before his father's eyes,<br/>he who offers a sacrifice taken from the substance of the poor.<br/>21. The bread of the wretched is the life of the poor;<br/>he who deprives them of it is a murderer.<br/>22. He gives death to his neighbor, he who takes away his livelihood;<br/>he sheds blood, he who deprives the hired laborer of his wages.<br/>23. One builds and another destroys:<br/>what do they gain from it, but toil?<br/>24. One prays and another curses:<br/>whose voice will the Master listen to?<br/><br/>25. He who washes after touching a corpse and touches it again,<br/>what does he gain by having washed?<br/>26. So it is with the man who fasts for his sins,<br/>if he goes and commits them again:<br/>who will hear his prayer,<br/>and what good will his humbling do him?</p>

### Chapter 35 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. He who observes the law makes many offerings;<br/>2. he who holds to the precepts offers a peace-offering.<br/>3. He who gives thanks makes an offering of fine flour;<br/>4. he who practices mercy offers a sacrifice of praise.<br/>5. What pleases the Lord is that one turn away from evil;<br/>what obtains his forgiveness is the flight from injustice.<br/><br/>6. Yet do not appear before the Lord empty-handed,<br/>7. for all these offerings must be made because of the precept.<br/>8. The offering of the righteous enriches the altar,<br/>and its sweet fragrance rises before the Lord.<br/>9. The sacrifice of the righteous man is pleasing,<br/>and his memory will not be forgotten.<br/><br/>10. Glorify the Lord with a generous heart,<br/>and hold back nothing from the firstfruits of your hands.<br/>11. In all your offerings, have a joyful face,<br/>and consecrate your tithe with gladness.<br/>12. Give to the Most High according to what he has given you,<br/>with a generous heart, according to what your hands have acquired.<br/>13. For the Lord repays,<br/>and he will give back to you seven times as much.<br/><br/>14. Do not seek to bribe him with gifts, for he would not accept them,<br/>15. and do not rely upon an unjust offering.<br/>For the Lord is a judge,<br/>and he has no regard for the rank of persons.<br/>16. He shows no partiality to the detriment of the poor,<br/>and he listens to the prayer of the oppressed.<br/>17. He does not disdain the orphan who pleads,<br/>nor the widow who pours out her complaint.<br/>18. Do not the tears of the widow flow down her cheeks,<br/>19. and does not her cry rise up against him who causes them to flow?<br/><br/>20. He who honors God in the way that pleases him will be well received,<br/>and his prayer rises up to the clouds.</p>

<p class="v">21. The prayer of the humble will pierce the clouds;<br/>he will not be consoled until it has reached God; he will not cease until the Most High has looked upon him,<br/>and the Lord will judge with equity and render justice.<br/>22. The Lord will not delay,<br/>he will have no more patience toward the oppressors;<br/>until he has broken the loins of these pitiless men,<br/>23. and has taken vengeance on the nations;<br/>until he has annihilated the multitude of blasphemers,<br/>and shattered the scepters of the wicked;<br/>24. until he has repaid man according to his deeds,<br/>and rewarded the works of men according to their thoughts;<br/>25. until he has taken up the cause of his people,<br/>and has gladdened it by his mercy.</p>

<p class="v">26. Mercy is beautiful in the time of Israel's oppression,<br/>like clouds heavy with rain in a time of drought.</p>

### Chapter 36 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Have pity on us, Master, God of the universe, and look upon us;<br/>2. and spread your terror over all the nations.<br/>3. Lift up your hand against the foreign peoples,<br/>and let them feel your power!<br/>4. As you have shown them your holiness by punishing us,<br/>so show your greatness before us by chastising them;<br/>5. and let them learn, as we ourselves have learned,<br/>that there is no other God but you, Lord!<br/><br/>6. Renew your wonders, and repeat your marvels;<br/>7. glorify your hand and your right arm.<br/>8. Rouse your wrath and pour out your anger;<br/>9. destroy the adversary and annihilate the enemy.<br/>10. Hasten the time and remember the oath;<br/>and let your mighty deeds be celebrated!<br/>11. Let him who has escaped be devoured by a burning fire,<br/>and let those who mistreat your people find their ruin.<br/>12. Shatter the heads of the chiefs of the enemies,<br/>who say: "There is none but us!"<br/><br/>13. Gather together all the tribes of Jacob,<br/>and restore to them their inheritance as at the beginning.<br/>14. Lord, have pity on your people, who are called by your name,<br/>and on Israel, whom you have made like a firstborn son.<br/>15. Have compassion on the city of your sanctuary,<br/>on Jerusalem, the place of your rest.<br/><br/>16. Fill Zion with your oracles,<br/>and your people with your glory.<br/>17. Bear witness to those who have been your creatures from the beginning, and fulfill the promises made in your name.<br/>18. Reward those who hope in you,<br/>and let your prophets be found truthful.<br/>Hear, Lord, the prayer of those who implore you,<br/>19. according to the blessing of Aaron upon your people;<br/>and let all the inhabitants of the earth acknowledge<br/>that you are the Lord, the God of the ages!</p>

<p class="v">20. The stomach receives every kind of food,<br/>but one food is better than another.</p>

<p class="v">21. The palate discerns wild game by its taste:<br/>so the sensible heart recognizes the lying word.<br/>22. The perverse heart causes grief,<br/>but the experienced man is on his guard against it.<br/>23. A woman will accept any kind of husband,<br/>but one girl is better than another.<br/>24. The beauty of a woman gladdens the face,<br/>and surpasses every desire of man.<br/>25. If kindness and gentleness are on her tongue,<br/>her husband is no longer a mere child among men.<br/>26. He who acquires a wife has the beginning of his fortune,<br/>a helper like himself and a supporting pillar.<br/>27. Where there is no hedge, the estate is plundered;<br/>where there is no wife, the wandering man groans.<br/>28. Who trusts the nimble robber,<br/>who runs from city to city?<br/>So it is with the man who has no home,<br/>and who takes his lodging wherever night overtakes him.</p>

### Chapter 37 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Every friend says: "I too am your friend;"<br/>but such a friend is one in name only.<br/>2. Is it not a grief unto death,<br/>when a companion and a friend turn into enemies?<br/>3. O perverse thought, from where have you come,<br/>to cover the earth with deceit?<br/>4. The companion of a friend rejoices in his joys,<br/>and, on the day of adversity, turns against him!<br/>5. A companion shares his friend's trouble for the sake of his own stomach,<br/>and, in the face of battle, takes up his shield!<br/>6. Do not forget your friend in your heart,<br/>and, in the midst of prosperity, do not lose his memory.</p>

<p class="v">7. Every counselor gives advice,<br/>but there are some who counsel in their own interest.<br/>8. Toward a counselor, be on your guard,<br/>and seek first to know what his interest is,<br/>— for it is for himself that he will counsel, —<br/>lest he cast the lot against you,<br/>9. and lest he say: "Your way is good";<br/>and then stand aside to see what will happen to you.</p>

<p class="v">10. Do not consult a man who looks at you askance,<br/>and hide your resolve from him who is jealous of you.<br/>11. Do not consult a woman about her rival,<br/>a coward about war,<br/>a merchant about an exchange,<br/>a buyer about a sale,<br/>an envious man about gratitude,<br/>a man without compassion about a charitable act,<br/>a lazy man about any kind of work,<br/>a hired hand of the house about the completion of a task,<br/>a lazy slave about heavy work:<br/>place no reliance on such people for any counsel.<br/>12. But be constant with a godly man,<br/>whom you know as a keeper of the commandments,<br/>whose heart is like your own,<br/>and who, if you fall, will suffer with you.<br/>13. Then hold fast to what your own heart advises you,<br/>for no one is more faithful to you than it.<br/>14. For the soul of a man sometimes announces more things<br/>than seven watchmen posted on a height to keep watch.<br/>15. And with all this, pray to the Most High,<br/>that he may surely direct your way.</p>

<p class="v">16. Before every work is the word:<br/>before every undertaking, reflection.<br/>17. As a trace of the change of heart four things appear:<br/>18. good and evil, life and death;<br/>and the tongue is always their mistress.<br/><br/>19. Such a man is prudent and the teacher of many,<br/>but he is useless to himself.<br/>20. He who affects wisdom in his words is odious;<br/>he will end by lacking all food.<br/>21. For the Lord has not given him his favor,<br/>because he is devoid of all wisdom.<br/><br/>22.
