Such a wise man is wise for himself,<br/>and the fruits of his knowledge are secure upon his lips.<br/>23. The wise man instructs his people,<br/>and the fruits of his knowledge are secure.<br/>24. The wise man is filled with blessings,<br/>and all who see him proclaim him happy.<br/>25. The life of man is of a limited number of days,<br/>but the days of Israel are without number.<br/>26. The wise man gains trust in the midst of his people,<br/>and his name will live forever.</p>

<p class="v">27. My son, for your manner of living, consult your own soul;<br/>see what is harmful to it and do not give it that.<br/>28. For not everything is good for everyone,<br/>and not everyone finds his well-being in everything.<br/>29. Do not be insatiable before every delicacy,<br/>and do not throw yourself greedily upon food;<br/>30. for excess of food brings discomforts,<br/>and intemperance leads even to colic.<br/>31. Because of intemperance many have died,<br/>but he who abstains prolongs his life.</p>

### Chapter 38 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Give the physician, for your needs, the honors due to him;<br/>for he too was created by the Lord.<br/>2. For it is from the Most High that healing comes,<br/>and from the king himself he receives gifts.<br/>3. The physician's knowledge lifts up his head,<br/>and he is admired in the presence of the great.<br/><br/>4. The Lord causes the earth to produce its medicines,<br/>and the sensible man does not despise them.<br/>5. Did not a piece of wood sweeten the bitter water,<br/>that its virtue might be known to all?<br/>6. He has given men knowledge,<br/>that he might be glorified by his marvelous gifts.<br/>7. By them man procures healing, and takes away pain.<br/>8. The pharmacist makes mixtures of them,<br/>and his work is scarcely finished<br/>before well-being spreads over the face of the earth through him.<br/><br/>9. My son, if you are ill, do not neglect my counsel,<br/>but pray to the Lord, and he will heal you.<br/>10. Put away transgression, set your hands right,<br/>and purify your heart from every sin.<br/>11. Offer incense and an oblation of fine flour,<br/>and sacrifice fat victims, as though it were your last act.<br/>12. Then give access to the physician, for he too was created by the Lord,<br/>and let him not go far from you, for you have need of him.<br/><br/>13. It happens that their hands have success,<br/>14. for they too will pray to the Lord,<br/>that he may grant them to procure rest<br/>and healing, to prolong the life of the sick man.<br/>15. Let him who sins before his Creator<br/>fall into the hands of the physician!</p>

<p class="v">16. My son, shed tears over the dead,<br/>and, as though you suffered cruelly, begin the lamentation.<br/>Then give his body the care that is due to it,<br/>and do not neglect his burial.<br/>17. Pour out bitter tears, breathe forth burning sighs,<br/>and mourn as is fitting,<br/>a day or two, to avoid ill-natured talk.<br/>Then console yourself, to drive away sadness;<br/>18. for from sadness death can come,<br/>and grief of heart brings down all vigor.<br/><br/>19. When a dead man is carried out, grief must pass away with him,<br/>as the life of the poor man is against his own heart.<br/>20. Do not give your heart over to sadness;<br/>drive it away, remembering your own end.<br/>21. Do not forget it: there is no return;<br/>you will be of no use to the dead man, and you will do harm to yourself.<br/>22. Remember that the sentence passed on him will be the same for you:<br/>"For me yesterday, for you today."<br/>23. When the dead man is at rest, let his memory rest too,<br/>and console yourself concerning him, at the departure of his spirit.</p>

<p class="v">24. The wisdom of the scribe is acquired through leisure,<br/>and he who does not have to busy himself with affairs will become wise.<br/><br/>25. How could he become wise, he who guides the plow,<br/>whose ambition is to wield the goad as though it were a spear;<br/>who drives his oxen and shares in their labors,<br/>and can talk of nothing but the young of bulls?<br/>26. He sets his whole heart on tracing furrows,<br/>and a watchful care on providing fodder for his heifers.<br/>27. So it is likewise with every carpenter and builder,<br/>who pursue their occupations night as well as day;<br/>with him who engraves the impressions of seals:<br/>his diligence is to vary the figures;<br/>he sets his heart on reproducing the design,<br/>a watchful care on perfecting his work.</p>

<p class="v">28. Such is the blacksmith seated near his anvil,<br/>and considering the iron still raw;<br/>the vapor of the fire melts his flesh,<br/>and he holds firm against the heat of the furnace;<br/>the noise of the hammer deafens his ear,<br/>and his eye is fixed on the model of the tool.<br/>He sets his heart on perfecting his work,<br/>a watchful care on polishing it to perfection.<br/>29. Such too is the potter seated at his work,<br/>turning the wheel with his feet:<br/>he is constantly anxious about his work,<br/>and all his efforts aim at producing a certain number of vessels.<br/>30. With his arm he shapes the clay,<br/>and before his feet he makes it pliable;<br/>he sets his heart on perfecting the glaze,<br/>a watchful care on cleaning his kiln.<br/><br/>31. These kinds of people expect everything from their hands,<br/>and each of them is skilled in his trade.<br/>32. Without them no city could be built,<br/>one could not go abroad, one could not travel.<br/>33. But they will not be sought after in the council of the people,<br/>and they will not distinguish themselves in the assembly;<br/>they will not have knowledge of the covenant of justice;<br/>they will not take their seat on the judge's bench;<br/>they will not interpret justice and law,<br/>and they will not be found to pronounce sentences.<br/>34. Yet they sustain the affairs of the age,<br/>and their prayer relates to the labors of their trade.</p>
### Chapter 39 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. It is otherwise with him who applies his mind,<br/>and meditates on the law of the Most High!<br/>He seeks out the wisdom of all the ancients,<br/>and devotes his leisure to prophecies.<br/>2. He keeps in his memory the accounts of famous men,<br/>and penetrates into the windings of maxims.<br/>3. He seeks the hidden meaning of proverbs,<br/>and busies himself with enigmatic sayings.<br/>4. He serves in the midst of the great,<br/>and appears before the prince.<br/><br/>He travels through the land of foreign peoples,<br/>for he desires to know good and evil among men.<br/>5. He sets his heart to rise early in the morning<br/>to seek the Lord who made him:<br/>he prays in the presence of the Most High,<br/>he opens his mouth in prayer<br/>and asks pardon for his sins.<br/><br/>6. If it be the will of the Lord, who is great,<br/>he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding;<br/>then he shall pour out in floods the words of wisdom,<br/>and, in his prayer, he shall give thanks to the Lord.<br/>7. He shall know how to guide his prudence and his knowledge,<br/>and he shall study the divine mysteries.<br/>8. He shall proclaim the doctrine of his teaching,<br/>and shall glory in the law of the covenant of the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">9. Many will praise his understanding,<br/>and he shall never be forgotten;<br/>his memory shall not pass away,<br/>and his name shall live from age to age.<br/>10. The peoples shall tell of his wisdom,<br/>and the assembly shall celebrate his praises.<br/>11. As long as he lives, his name remains more illustrious than a thousand others; and, when he rests, his glory shall grow still greater.</p>

<p class="v">12. I wish yet to make known the fruit of my reflections,<br/>for I am filled, as the moon at its full.<br/>13. Listen to me, pious children, and grow,<br/>like the rose planted by a flowing stream:<br/>14. give forth, like frankincense, your sweet fragrance;<br/>put forth your blossom, like the lily;<br/>send out your perfume and sing a canticle,<br/>bless the Lord for all his works.<br/>15. Give glory to his name,<br/>proclaim his praise,<br/>with the songs of your lips and on your harps,<br/>and, in celebrating him, you shall say:<br/><br/>16. All the works of the Lord are very good,<br/>and everything he has commanded shall be fulfilled in its time.<br/>17. One must not say: "What is this? What good is it?"<br/>for every thing shall be sought out in its time.<br/>At his word the waters gathered together as a heap,<br/>and, at a word of his mouth, there were reservoirs of water.<br/>18. By his command, whatever pleases him comes to pass,<br/>and none can stop the salvation he sends.<br/><br/>19. The works of all flesh are before him,<br/>and none can hide from his eyes.<br/>20. His gaze reaches from eternity to eternity,<br/>and nothing is astonishing before him.<br/>21. One must not say: "What is this? What good is it?"<br/>for every thing has been created for its use.<br/>22. The blessing of the Lord overflows like a river,<br/>and, like a flood, it waters the earth.<br/>23. So too he gives his wrath as a portion to the nations,<br/>as he turned a well-watered land into a region of salt.<br/>24. His ways are straight for holy men,<br/>and likewise they are, for the impious, occasions of stumbling.</p>

<p class="v">25. Good things were created for the good from the beginning,<br/>and, likewise, evil things for the wicked.<br/>26. What is of first necessity for the life of man<br/>is water, fire, iron and salt,<br/>flour of wheat, honey and milk,<br/>the blood of the grape, oil and clothing.<br/>27. All these things are good for pious men,<br/>but turn into evils for sinners.<br/><br/>28. There are winds that were created for vengeance,<br/>and, in their fury, they unleash their scourges.<br/>On the day of destruction, they shall deploy their power,<br/>and shall appease the wrath of Him who made them.<br/>29. Fire and hail, famine and pestilence,<br/>all these things have been created for punishment;<br/>30. as well as the teeth of fierce beasts, scorpions and vipers,<br/>and the destroying sword, fatal to the impious.<br/>31. These creatures rejoice at the command of the Lord,<br/>they hold themselves ready on the earth for need,<br/>and, at the appointed times, they do not disobey his orders.<br/><br/>32. Therefore I was, from the beginning, firm in my thoughts,<br/>and, after meditating, I set them down in writing:<br/>33. All the works of the Lord are good,<br/>and he provides for every need in its time.<br/>34. There is no cause to say: "This is worse than that,"<br/>for every thing in its time shall be found good.<br/>35. And now sing with all your heart and mouth,<br/>and bless the name of the Lord.</p>

### Chapter 40 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Upon every man has been laid a great misery,<br/>and a heavy yoke is upon the children of men,<br/>from the day they come forth from their mother's womb,<br/>until the day of their burial in the bosom of the common mother.<br/>2. What troubles their thoughts and makes their hearts fear<br/>is the thought of what they await, it is the fear of death.<br/><br/>3. From the man who sits enthroned in glory,<br/>to the wretch seated on the ground and in the ashes;<br/>4. from him who wears purple and the crown,<br/>to the poor man, covered with coarse cloth,<br/>5. anger, envy, trouble, agitation,<br/>fear of death, bitterness and quarrels are the lot of all;<br/>and, in the time when each one rests upon his couch,<br/>the sleep of night troubles his thoughts.<br/>6. He rests but a moment, scarcely anything at all,<br/>and at once dreams disturb him;<br/>it seems to him he is standing watch by day,<br/>he is frightened by the vision of his mind,<br/>like a man fleeing before battle.<br/>7. At the moment of deliverance he awakes,<br/>and marvels at his vain fright.</p>

<p class="v">8. So it is with all flesh, from man to beast,<br/>and for sinners, seven times more still.<br/>9. Pestilence, murder, discord, the sword,<br/>[calamities, famine, destruction, and the other scourges]:<br/>10. all these were created against sinners,<br/>as it was because of them that the flood came.</p>

<p class="v">11. All that comes from the earth returns to the earth,<br/>as what comes from the waters goes down to the sea.<br/>12. Every gift and every unjustly acquired good shall perish,<br/>but good faith shall endure forever.<br/>13. The riches of the unjust shall dry up like a torrent,<br/>and like a loud thunderclap that resounds during the storm.<br/>14. The man who knows how to open his hand shall rejoice,<br/>but transgressors shall suffer utter ruin.<br/>15. The offspring of the impious do not put forth many branches,<br/>and their impure roots are on a steep rock.<br/>16. The reed that grows near the waters and on a river's bank<br/>is torn up before any other plant.<br/>17. Kindness is like a blessed garden,<br/>and beneficence endures forever.</p>

<p class="v">18. Sweet is the life of the self-sufficient man and of the worker;<br/>more than both, the life of him who finds a treasure:<br/>19. Children and the founding of a city perpetuate a name:<br/>more than both, a blameless wife is esteemed.<br/>20. Wine and music gladden the heart:<br/>more than either, the love of wisdom.<br/>21. The flute and the harp make sweet sounds heard:<br/>more than both, a kindly tongue.<br/>22. Grace and beauty delight your eyes:<br/>more than both, the greenness of the fields.<br/>23. Friend and companion meet at certain hours:<br/>more than both, a wife with her husband.<br/>24. Brothers and helpers are for the time of affliction:<br/>more than both, beneficence delivers.<br/>25. Gold and silver make the feet firm:<br/>more than both, prudence is esteemed.<br/>26. Wealth and strength lift up the heart:<br/>more than both, the fear of the Lord.<br/>With the fear of the Lord, one lacks nothing;<br/>with it, there is no need to beg for help.<br/>27. The fear of the Lord is like a blessed garden,<br/>and the Lord clothes it with a glory beyond compare.</p>

<p class="v">28. My son, may you never lead a life of begging;<br/>better to die than to beg.<br/>29. When a man is reduced to looking toward another's table,<br/>his life can no longer be counted a life.<br/>For he defiles his soul with food not his own,<br/>a thing from which the instructed and well-bred man will keep himself.<br/>30. In the mouth of the shameless man begging is sweet;<br/>but, in his inward parts, it burns like a fire.</p>

### Chapter 41 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. O death, how bitter is the remembrance of you<br/>to the man who lives at peace amid his riches,<br/>to the man free of care and who prospers in all things,<br/>and who is still able to enjoy the pleasure of the table!<br/><br/>2. O death, your sentence is welcome<br/>to the needy man, to him whose strength is spent,<br/>to the old man weighed down with years and worn out with a thousand cares,<br/>to him who will not submit to his lot and who has lost hope.<br/><br/>3. Do not dread the sentence of death:<br/>remember those who went before you and those who will come after.<br/>4. This is the sentence passed by the Lord upon all flesh;<br/>and why rebel against the good pleasure of the Most High?<br/>Whether you have lived ten years, a hundred, a thousand:<br/>in Sheol one is no longer troubled about the length of life.</p>

<p class="v">5. Abominable children are the children of sinners,<br/>they who frequent the dwellings of the impious.<br/>6. The inheritance of the children of sinners goes to ruin,<br/>and reproach clings to their offspring.<br/>7. The children of an impious father cast reproach upon him,<br/>because it is on his account that they are in disgrace.<br/><br/>8. Woe to you, impious men,<br/>who have abandoned the law of God most high!<br/>9. If you are born, you are born for the curse,<br/>and if you die, the curse shall be your portion.<br/>10. All that is of the earth returns to the earth:<br/>so the impious go from the curse to ruin.<br/><br/>11. Men grieve over their bodies,<br/>but the hateful name of sinners shall be blotted out.<br/>12. Take care of your name, for it shall remain with you<br/>longer than a thousand great treasures of gold.<br/>13. The days of a good life are numbered,<br/>but a good name remains forever.</p>

<p class="v">14. My children, keep my instructions in peace:<br/><br/>Hidden wisdom and unseen treasure,<br/>of what use are either of them?<br/>15. Better the man who hides his folly,<br/>than the man who hides his wisdom.<br/><br/>16. Therefore be ashamed of the things I am about to tell you.<br/>For not all shame is good to keep,<br/>and not all things are judged by everyone according to the truth.<br/><br/>17. Be ashamed of fornication, before your father and your mother,<br/>and of lying, before the prince and the powerful;<br/>18. of an offense, before the judge and the magistrate,<br/>of transgression of the law, before the assembly and the people;<br/>of injustice, before your companion and your friend,<br/>19. of theft, before the people of the neighborhood.<br/>In the name of the truth of God and of his covenant,<br/>be ashamed of leaning your elbow on the bread;<br/>of drawing contempt upon yourself in taking and in giving,<br/>20. and of keeping silent before those who greet you;<br/>of looking upon a loose woman,<br/>21. and of turning away your face from a relative;<br/>of taking from him his share and his gift,<br/>and of watching a married woman;<br/>22. of being over-familiar with your servant girl,<br/>and do not linger near her bed;<br/>be ashamed of offensive words before your friends,<br/>and do not reproach after having given.</p>

### Chapter 42 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Be ashamed of repeating what you have heard,<br/>and of revealing secret things.<br/>Thus you will have true shame,<br/>and you will find favor before all men.<br/><br/>Do not blush at these things,<br/>and do not show partiality so as to commit sin:<br/>2. at the law of the Most High and his covenant,<br/>at the sentence that justifies the impious,<br/>3. at conversing with companions and travelers,<br/>at giving some good thing to your friends,<br/>4. at using just balances and just weights,<br/>at acquiring much or little,<br/>5. at not making a difference in selling and with merchants,<br/>at correcting your children severely,<br/>and at striking a wicked slave's back till it bleeds.<br/>6. With a wicked wife, a seal is good;<br/>and where there are many hands, keep things under lock.<br/>7. Whatever you hand over to your people, count it and weigh it,<br/>and put in writing what you give and what you receive.</p>

<p class="v">8. Do not blush to reprimand the fool and the senseless,<br/>and the old man who disputes with young men.<br/><br/>And so you will be truly instructed,<br/>and approved by everyone.</p>

<p class="v">9. A daughter is for her father a secret worry;<br/>the anxiety she causes him takes away his sleep:<br/>while young, she may pass the flower of her age;<br/>joined to a husband, she may become hateful to him;<br/>10. a virgin, she might let herself be seduced,<br/>and become pregnant in her father's house;<br/>with a husband, she may perhaps be unfaithful,<br/>and, living with him, she may perhaps remain barren.<br/>11. Over a headstrong daughter, keep strict watch,<br/>lest she make you the laughingstock of your enemies,<br/>the talk of the city and the subject of public gossip,<br/>and dishonor you before all the people.</p>

<p class="v">12. Do not look upon the beauty of any man,<br/>and do not sit among women;<br/>13. for from garments comes the moth,<br/>and from woman, feminine malice.<br/>14. A wicked man is better than a fawning woman,<br/>for the woman covers with reproach and shame.</p>

<p class="v">15. I will call to mind the works of the Lord,<br/>and make known what I have seen.<br/><br/>It is by the word of the Lord that his works were made.<br/>16. The sun that lights them beholds them all;<br/>a work of the Lord, it is full of his glory.</p>

<p class="v">17. The Lord has not made even his saints able<br/>to declare all his wonders,<br/>which the Lord Almighty has firmly established,<br/>so that the whole universe might be made steadfast by his glory.<br/><br/>18. He fathoms the depths of the ocean and the heart of men,<br/>and he knows their most subtle designs.<br/>For the Lord possesses all knowledge,<br/>and he sees the signs of the times.<br/>19. He declares things past and things to come,<br/>and he unveils the traces of hidden things.<br/>20. No thought escapes him,<br/>no word is hidden from him.<br/><br/>21. He has adorned the great works of his wisdom;<br/>he is before all ages, and he shall endure forever;<br/>nothing has been added to his being, and nothing has been taken from it;<br/>and he has needed no counselor.<br/>22. How beautiful are all his works!<br/>And what we behold of them is but a single spark.<br/>23. All things are alive and endure forever,<br/>for every use,<br/>and all things obey the Creator.<br/>24. All things go in pairs, one facing the other,<br/>and he has made nothing that tends to ruin.<br/>25. The one ensures the good of the other:<br/>who could ever have enough of beholding the glory of the Lord?</p>

### Chapter 43 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. The pride of the heights is the firmament in its pure splendor;<br/>and the sight of the sky is a vision of glory.<br/>2. The sun, when it appears, glorifies the Lord at its rising;<br/>it is a marvelous creature, the work of the Most High.<br/>3. At its noon it dries up the earth;<br/>who can withstand its heat?<br/>4. For his labors the craftsman keeps the furnace fire burning:<br/>three times more the sun heats the mountains.<br/>It sets ablaze the vapors of the air,<br/>and, when it makes its rays shine forth, it dazzles the eyes.<br/>5. Great is the Lord who made it,<br/>and, at his command, it hastens its course.<br/><br/>6. The moon too is always faithful, at the hour assigned to it;<br/>it marks the seasons of the year, and announces what is to come.<br/>7. From the moon comes the signal of the feasts;<br/>its light diminishes once it has come to its full.<br/>8. It is from it that the month takes its name;<br/>it grows wonderfully through its various phases.<br/>It is the tent of a camp in the heights of the heavens;<br/>it shines in the firmament of the sky.</p>

<p class="v">9. The beauty of the sky is the brightness of the stars,<br/>a resplendent ornament in the heights of the Lord.<br/>10. At the command of the Holy One, they stand in their appointed place,<br/>and do not grow weary in their watches.<br/><br/>11. Behold the rainbow and bless Him who made it;<br/>it is very beautiful in its splendor!<br/>12. It encircles the sky with its radiant circle;<br/>it is the hands of the Most High that stretch it out.<br/><br/>13. At his command the snow falls swiftly,<br/>and the lightnings hasten, executors of his judgments.<br/>14. Therefore his treasuries open,<br/>and the clouds fly like birds.<br/>15. By his power he gives strength to the clouds,<br/>and the hail falls like fragments of stone.<br/>16. The voice of his thunder makes the earth tremble,<br/>and, when he appears, the mountains quake.<br/>17. At his will the south wind blows,<br/>the north wind rages and the whirlwind storms.<br/>He scatters the snow like birds swooping down;<br/>it comes down like the locust settling to rest.<br/>18. The eye admires the beauty of its whiteness,<br/>and the heart is filled with wonder at its falling.<br/>19. He pours out hoarfrost on the earth like salt,<br/>and the frost hardens it into points like thorns.<br/><br/>20. The cold north wind begins to blow,<br/>and the water hardens into ice;<br/>this ice spreads motionless over every gathering of water,<br/>and clothes the water as with a breastplate.<br/>21. The Lord devours the mountains and sets the desert ablaze,<br/>he burns up the green growth like fire.<br/>22. For all these ills the remedy is a cloud that swiftly comes;<br/>a dew that follows gives relief from the burning heat.<br/>23. According to his design he has tamed the deep,<br/>and planted islands in it.<br/>24. Those who sail upon the sea tell of its perils,<br/>and, hearing their tales, we are astonished.<br/>25. There are strange and wondrous creatures,<br/>animals of every kind and the race of sea monsters.</p>

<p class="v">26. Through the Lord, everything moves happily to its end,<br/>and all things subsist by his word.<br/><br/>27. We could say much, and yet not attain it;<br/>the sum of our discourse: He is the all.<br/>28. Wishing to praise him, where would we find the strength?<br/>He is the Almighty, above all his works.<br/>29. The Lord is terrible and supremely great,<br/>and wonderful is his power.<br/>30. In praising the Lord, exalt him as much as you can,<br/>for he will always be higher still.<br/>To exalt him, gather all your strength;<br/>do not grow weary, for you will never attain him.<br/>31. Who has seen him and could speak of him?<br/>Who is able to praise him as he is?<br/>32. Many hidden wonders are greater still,<br/>for we see but a small number of his works.<br/>33. The Lord has made all things,<br/>and he gives wisdom to pious men.</p>

### Chapter 44 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Let us now praise illustrious men,<br/>and the fathers of our race.<br/>2. In them the Lord wrought glorious wonders,<br/>he manifested his greatness from the beginning.<br/><br/>3. They were sovereigns in their kingdoms,<br/>men renowned for their might,<br/>counselors full of wisdom,<br/>declaring the divine will through their prophecies,</p>

<p class="v">4. guides of the people by their counsel and prudence,<br/>teachers of the people, who instructed it by wise discourse;<br/>5. men cultivating the art of sacred melodies,<br/>and who set down poetic accounts in writing;<br/>6. rich men possessing goods in abundance,<br/>living in peace in their dwellings:<br/>all these men were honored by their contemporaries,<br/>7. all were the glory of their time.<br/><br/>8. There are some among them who left a name,<br/>so that their praises might be told.<br/>9. There are others of whom there is no more memory,<br/>they have perished as though they had never existed;<br/>they have become as though they had never been born,<br/>and, likewise, their children after them.<br/>10. The former were pious men,<br/>whose virtues have not been forgotten.<br/>11. Happiness remains attached to their race,<br/>and an inheritance is assured to their children.<br/>12. Their race remains faithful to the covenants,<br/>and their children for their sake.<br/>13. Their race endures forever,<br/>and their glory shall never be blotted out.<br/>14. Their bodies were buried in peace,<br/>and their name lives from age to age.<br/>15. The peoples celebrate their wisdom,<br/>and the assembly proclaims their praises.</p>

<p class="v">16. Enoch was pleasing to the Lord, and he was taken up,<br/>an example of repentance for the generations.<br/><br/>17. Noah was found perfect and just;<br/>in the time of wrath, he was the ransom of humanity.<br/>Therefore a remnant was left to the earth,<br/>when the flood came.<br/>18. An everlasting covenant was made with him,<br/>that all flesh should no more be destroyed by a flood.</p>

<p class="v">19. Abraham is the illustrious father of a multitude of nations,<br/>and none was found to equal him in glory.<br/>20. He kept the law of the Most High,<br/>and he entered into covenant with him.<br/>He established this covenant in his flesh,<br/>and, in trial, he showed himself faithful.</p>

<p class="v">21. So God assured him by oath<br/>that the nations would be blessed in his offspring;<br/>he promised to multiply him like the dust of the earth,<br/>to raise up his posterity like the stars,<br/>to give them for an inheritance from sea to sea,<br/>from the river to the ends of the earth.<br/><br/>22. In the same way he confirmed in Isaac,<br/>for the sake of his father Abraham,<br/>the blessing of all peoples and the covenant.<br/><br/>23. And he then caused it to rest upon the head of Jacob;<br/>he had regard for him in his blessings;<br/>he gave him the land for an inheritance;<br/>he divided it into various portions,<br/>and apportioned them among the twelve tribes.</p>

### Chapter 45 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. He brought forth from Jacob a pious man,<br/>who found favor with all flesh,<br/>a man beloved of God and of men, Moses:<br/>may his memory be blessed!<br/>2. He gave him a glory equal to that of the saints,<br/>he made him great by the terrors he inspired in the enemies.<br/>3. By his word, he put an end to wonders;<br/>he glorified him before kings;<br/>he gave him commandments for his people,<br/>and he let him see a ray of his glory.<br/>4. Because of his faith and his meekness, he consecrated him,<br/>he chose him from among all mortals.<br/>5. He let him hear his voice,<br/>and brought him into the cloud;<br/>he gave him commandments face to face,<br/>the law of life and knowledge,<br/>that he might teach Jacob his covenant,<br/>and his decrees to Israel.</p>

<p class="v">6. He raised up Aaron, a saint like unto him,<br/>his brother, of the tribe of Levi.<br/>7. He made with him an everlasting covenant,<br/>and gave him the priesthood of his people.<br/><br/>He adorned him with splendid apparel,<br/>and girded him with the robe of glory.</p>

<p class="v">8. He clothed him with sovereign magnificence,<br/>and assigned him garments of honor:<br/>the breeches, the long tunic and the ephod.<br/>9. He surrounded him with pomegranates,<br/>with many golden bells about him,<br/>which were to ring out as he walked,<br/>and make their sound heard in the temple;<br/>it was a memorial for the sons of his people.<br/>10. He clothed him with the sacred vestment,<br/>woven of gold, of violet<br/>and of purple, the work of the embroiderer;<br/>with the breastplate of judgment, with the Urim and the Thummim,<br/>made of scarlet thread, the work of a craftsman;<br/>11. with precious stones, engraved like seals,<br/>and set in gold, the work of a lapidary,<br/>to be a memorial, names being written,<br/>according to the number of the tribes of Israel.<br/>12. He set upon his turban the crown of gold,<br/>bearing these words engraved: Holy to the Lord,<br/>an emblem of honor, a perfect work,<br/>a delight to the eyes, a magnificent adornment.<br/>13. Nothing like it existed before him nor shall ever be;<br/>no stranger has ever put it on, but only his sons,<br/>and his descendants throughout the ages to come.<br/><br/>14. His whole burnt offerings shall be offered,<br/>twice each day, without interruption.<br/>15. Moses filled his hands,<br/>and anointed him with the holy oil.<br/>This was for him an everlasting covenant,<br/>and for his race, as long as the days of heaven shall last,<br/>to serve the Lord and fulfill the functions of the priesthood,<br/>and to bless his people in his name.<br/>16. The Lord chose him from among all the living,<br/>to present to him the offering,<br/>the incense and the sweet fragrance as a memorial,<br/>and to make atonement for the sins of his people.<br/>17. He gave him, among his commandments,<br/>authority over the holy ordinances,<br/>to teach Jacob his precepts,<br/>and to teach his law to Israel.<br/><br/>18. Strangers conspired against him,<br/>and were jealous of him in the wilderness:<br/>the men of the faction of Dathan and Abiram,<br/>and the band of Korah, fierce and furious.</p>

<p class="v">19. The Lord saw it and took no pleasure in it,<br/>and they were exterminated in the heat of his wrath;<br/><br/>he wrought wonders against them,<br/>and consumed them with the flame of his fire.<br/><br/>20. And he increased the glory of Aaron,<br/>and assigned him an inheritance:<br/>he gave him for a portion the firstfruits of the produce of the earth;<br/>before all else he prepared bread to satisfy them.<br/>21. They feed on the sacrifices of the Lord,<br/>which he gave to Aaron and to his descendants.<br/>22. Only he has no inheritance in the land of the people,<br/>and he has no portion within the nation,<br/>for, says the Lord, "I will be your portion and your inheritance."</p>

<p class="v">23. Phinehas, son of Eleazar, is third in glory,<br/>in that he showed zeal in the fear of the Lord,<br/>and that, in the defection of the people, he remained steadfast,<br/>in the noble courage of his soul,<br/>and made atonement for Israel.<br/>24. Therefore a covenant of peace was made with him,<br/>which made him chief of the priests and of his people,<br/>that to him and to his descendants might belong<br/>forever the august dignity of the priesthood.<br/>25. There was also a covenant with David, son of Jesse, of the tribe of Judah;<br/>the inheritance of the king passes only from son to son,<br/>whereas the inheritance of Aaron belongs to all his descendants.<br/>26. May the Lord grant you, O high priests, wisdom in your heart,<br/>to judge his people in justice,<br/>that their prosperity may not vanish,<br/>nor their glory in the ages to come!</p>

### Chapter 46 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Valiant in war was Joshua son of Nun,<br/>who succeeded Moses in the dignity of prophet,<br/>and who, living up to his name, showed himself<br/>great in delivering the chosen of the Lord,<br/>by punishing the enemies who rose up,<br/>so as to put Israel in possession of the land.<br/>2. With what glory he covered himself when he lifted up his hands,<br/>and stretched out his sword against the cities!</p>

<p class="v">3. Who ever before him fought so many battles,<br/>when the Lord himself led on the enemies?<br/>4. Did not the sun, at the gesture of his hand, turn back,<br/>and was not a single day equal to two days?<br/>5. He called upon the most high Sovereign<br/>while he pressed the enemies on every side;<br/><br/>and the Lord almighty heard him,<br/>with hailstones of great force.<br/>6. The Lord fell upon the hostile nation,<br/>and destroyed the adversaries in the pass,<br/>that the nations might know all the weapons of Joshua,<br/>and learn that the war he waged was before the Lord;<br/>for he followed the Almighty.<br/>7. Already, in the days of Moses, he had shown his piety,<br/>he and Caleb, son of Jephunneh,<br/>by standing firm against the enemy,<br/>by keeping the people from sinning,<br/>and by silencing the murmuring of the wicked.<br/>8. So these two men alone were preserved,<br/>out of six hundred thousand men on foot,<br/>to be brought into the inheritance,<br/>into the land flowing with milk and honey.<br/>9. And the Lord gave vigor to Caleb,<br/>— and it remained with him even to old age, —<br/>so that he was able to climb the heights of the region,<br/>and his posterity kept this inheritance:<br/>10. that all the children of Israel might know<br/>that it is good to follow the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">11. And the Judges, each according to his name,<br/>all those whose heart did not give itself to fornication,<br/>all those who did not turn away from the Lord,<br/>may their memory be blessed!<br/>12. May their bones flourish again from their graves,<br/>may their name be renewed<br/>in the children of these illustrious men!</p>

<p class="v">&lt;/poem&gt; 13. Samuel was beloved of the Lord his God; a prophet of the Lord, he established the kingship, and anointed princes to rule over his people. 14. He judged the assembly according to the law of the Lord, and the Lord looked down favorably upon Jacob. 15. By his truthfulness he showed himself a prophet; by his truthfulness he was recognized as a seer worthy of trust.</p>

<p class="v">16. He called upon the sovereign Lord,<br/>when his enemies pressed him on every side,<br/>and he offered a lamb still at the breast.<br/>17. And the Lord thundered from the height of heaven,<br/>and, with a great sound, made his voice heard;<br/>18. and he crushed the chiefs of the Tyrians,<br/>and all the princes of the Philistines.<br/>19. Before the time of the eternal sleep,<br/>Samuel took the Lord and his Anointed to witness:<br/>"From no one have I received<br/>any gift, not even sandals;"<br/>and no man rose up to accuse him.<br/>20. And when he had fallen asleep, he prophesied still,<br/>and he announced to the king his approaching end.<br/>From the bosom of the earth he raised his voice<br/>in prophecy, to blot out the iniquity of the people.</p>

### Chapter 47 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Then appeared Nathan,<br/>to prophesy in the days of David.<br/>2. As the fat is set apart from the thanksgiving victim,<br/>so David was set apart among the children of Israel.<br/>3. He played with lions as with young goats,<br/>with bears as with young lambs.<br/>4. In his youth, did he not slay the giant,<br/>and take away the reproach of the people,<br/>when he lifted his hand with the stone of his sling,<br/>and struck down the insolence of Goliath?<br/>5. For he called upon the Lord, the Most High,<br/>and the Lord gave strength to his right hand,<br/>to put to death the mighty warrior,<br/>to raise up the horn of his people.<br/>6. So they celebrated him for the ten thousands,<br/>they praised him for the blessings of the Lord,<br/>and they offered him the crown of glory.<br/>7. For he crushed the enemies on every side,<br/>he trampled underfoot the Philistines, the adversaries;<br/>he broke their power to this day.<br/>8. In all his undertakings he rendered homage,<br/>to the Holy One, to the Most High, in words of praise,<br/>with all his heart he sang hymns,<br/>and he loved Him who had made him.</p>

<p class="v">9. He appointed singers before the altar,<br/>and, by their voices, he made sweet melodies heard.<br/>10. He gave splendor to the feasts,<br/>and sovereign magnificence to the solemnities,<br/>while the singers celebrated the holy name of the Lord,<br/>and, from early morning, made the sanctuary resound.<br/>11. The Lord forgave him his faults,<br/>and exalted his power forever;<br/>he assured him a line of kings,<br/>and the throne of glory in Israel.</p>

<p class="v">12. After him rose up a son full of wisdom;<br/>because of his father, he lived in prosperity.<br/>13. Solomon reigned in days of peace,<br/>God having procured him rest on every side,<br/>that he might build a temple to his name,<br/>and prepare an everlasting sanctuary.<br/><br/>14. How wise you were in your youth,<br/>and overflowing with understanding, like a river!<br/>15. Your mind covered the earth,<br/>and you filled it with sayings of hidden meaning.<br/>16. Your name reached even to the far-off islands,<br/>and you were beloved in your peace.<br/>17. For your songs, your proverbs, your parables<br/>and your answers, the world admired you.<br/>18. In the name of the Lord God,<br/>who is called the God of Israel,<br/>you gathered gold as though it were tin,<br/>and heaped up silver as though it were lead.<br/><br/>19. You gave yourself over to women,<br/>and you gave them power over your body;<br/>20. you set a stain upon your glory,<br/>and you profaned your race,<br/>and so you drew down wrath upon your children.<br/>I feel a bitter grief for your folly;<br/>21. it was the cause that the empire was divided in two,<br/>and that from Ephraim arose the head of a rebellious kingdom.<br/>22. But the Lord will not abandon his mercy,<br/>and none of his works shall perish.<br/>He will not destroy the posterity of his chosen one,<br/>and he will not let the race of him who loved him disappear.<br/>He has left to Jacob a remnant,<br/>and to David an offshoot of his race.</p>

<p class="v">23. Solomon rested with his fathers,<br/>and left after him, of his race,<br/>a son, foolish in the eyes of the people, devoid of prudence,<br/>Rehoboam, who led the people to turn away from his counsels,<br/>and Jeroboam, son of Nebat, who made Israel sin,<br/>and opened to Ephraim the way of transgression.<br/>24. And the sins of the Israelites multiplied beyond measure,<br/>so that they were carried far from their land.<br/>25. They pursued every kind of iniquity,<br/>until vengeance came down upon them.</p>

### Chapter 48 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Then arose Elijah, a prophet like fire,<br/>and his word burned like a torch.<br/>2. He brought famine upon Israel,<br/>and, by his zeal, reduced it to a small number.<br/>3. By the word of the Lord, he shut up the heavens;<br/>likewise, he made fire fall from it three times.<br/>4. How glorious you made yourself, O Elijah, by your wonders,<br/>and who could boast of being like you?<br/>5. You who raised up a corpse from the bosom of death,<br/>and from Sheol, by the word of the Most High;<br/>6. you who cast down kings into ruin,<br/>and illustrious men from their beds into death;<br/>7. you who heard on Sinai reproofs,<br/>and on Horeb sentences of vengeance;<br/>8. you who anointed kings to execute vengeance,<br/>and prophets to succeed you;<br/>9. you who were taken up in a whirlwind of flame,<br/>and in a chariot with horses of fire;<br/>10. you who were designated in solemn writings for times to come,<br/>as one who must calm wrath before it kindles,<br/>turn back the heart of the father to the child,<br/>and restore the tribes of Israel.<br/>11. Happy are those who shall see you,<br/>and who shall be adorned with the love of God!<br/>For we too shall surely live.</p>

<p class="v">12. When Elijah had been wrapped in the whirlwind,<br/>Elisha was filled with his spirit.<br/>Throughout his days he was shaken by no prince,<br/>and no one had dominion over him.<br/>13. Nothing was impossible for him,<br/>and his body, laid in the tomb, worked miracles.<br/>14. During his life he wrought wonders,<br/>and, in his death, he performed marvels.<br/>15. In spite of all this, the people did not repent,<br/>and did not turn away from sin,<br/>until they were carried far from their land,<br/>and scattered over all the earth.</p>

<p class="v">Only a small people remained,<br/>with a chief of the house of David.<br/>16. Among these, some did what is pleasing to God,<br/>and others multiplied transgressions.<br/><br/>17. Hezekiah fortified his city,<br/>and brought the Gihon within its walls;<br/>with iron he hewed through the rock,<br/>and built reservoirs for the waters.<br/><br/>18. In his time Sennacherib came up,<br/>and sent Rabshakeh; the latter set out,<br/>and lifted up his hand against Zion,<br/>and boasted in his arrogance.<br/>19. Then their hearts and their hands trembled,<br/>and they were in anguish like women in labor.<br/>20. They called upon the merciful Lord,<br/>stretching out their hands toward him,<br/>and the Holy One heard them at once from heaven,<br/>and delivered them by the ministry of Isaiah.<br/>21. He struck the army of the Assyrians,<br/>and his angel exterminated them.<br/><br/>22. For Hezekiah did what is pleasing to the Lord,<br/>and stood firm in the ways of David his father,<br/>as Isaiah the prophet commanded him,<br/>great and truthful in his visions.<br/>23. In his days the sun turned back,<br/>and Isaiah prolonged the life of the king.</p>

<p class="v">24. Under a powerful inspiration, he saw the times to come,<br/>and consoled the afflicted in Zion.<br/><br/>He announced what must happen even to the end of time,<br/>and hidden things before their fulfillment.</p>

### Chapter 49 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. The memory of Josiah is a perfume compounded of sweet fragrances,<br/>prepared by the art of the perfumer;<br/>in every mouth his memory is sweet as honey,<br/>and like music at a feast.<br/>2. He succeeded in bringing the nation to repentance,<br/>and he made the abominations of impiety disappear.<br/>3. He turned his heart faithfully toward the Lord,<br/>and, in the days of the impious, he made piety strong.</p>

<p class="v">4. With the exception of David, Hezekiah and Josiah,<br/>all the others committed iniquity;<br/>for, having abandoned the law of the Most High,<br/>the kings of Judah went to their ruin.<br/>5. Indeed, they left their power to others,<br/>and their glory to a foreign nation.<br/>6. They burned the chosen city of the sanctuary,<br/>and made its streets desolate,<br/>7. because of Jeremiah, for they mistreated him,<br/>he who was consecrated a prophet from his mother's womb,<br/>to uproot, to destroy and to bring to ruin,<br/>as well as to build and to plant.<br/>8. Ezekiel beheld the vision of glory,<br/>which the Lord showed him upon the chariot of the Cherubim;<br/>9. for he thought of the enemies in the threat of a storm of rain,<br/>and he did good to those who followed the right way.<br/>10. As for the twelve prophets, may their bones<br/>flourish again from their graves!<br/>For they consoled Jacob,<br/>and saved it by a sure hope.</p>

<p class="v">11. How shall we praise Zerubbabel?<br/>For he is like a signet ring on the right hand.<br/>12. So it is also with Jeshua, son of Jehozadak!<br/>Both, in their days, rebuilt the house of God,<br/>and raised up the temple, consecrated to the Lord,<br/>destined for everlasting glory.</p>

<p class="v">13. Of Nehemiah too the memory is great,<br/>he who raised up our ruined walls,<br/>who restored our gates with their bars,<br/>and rebuilt our houses.</p>

<p class="v">14. No man has existed here below like Enoch,<br/>for he too was taken up from this earth.<br/>15. No man was like Joseph either,<br/>the prince of his brothers, the support of his nation;<br/>and his bones were kept with care.<br/>16. Shem and Seth were glorified among men,<br/>but above every being in creation is Adam.</p>
### Chapter 50 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Simon, son of Onias, is the high priest<br/>who, during his life, repaired the house of the Lord,<br/>and, in his days, strengthened the temple.<br/>2. By him were laid the foundations to raise to double height<br/>the lofty wall that supports the enclosure of the temple.<br/>3. In his time was made the reservoir of waters;<br/>the bronze of which it was formed had the circumference of the sea.<br/>4. He took care of his people to preserve them from ruin,<br/>and fortified the city against a siege.<br/><br/>5. How majestic he was in the midst of the people gathered all around,<br/>when he came out of the house of the veil!<br/>6. He was like the morning star glittering through the cloud,<br/>like the moon in the days of her fullness,<br/>7. like the sun shining upon the temple of the Most High,<br/>and like the rainbow gleaming amid the luminous clouds;<br/>8. like the flower of roses in the days of spring,<br/>like lilies on the edge of the waters,<br/>like the branch of the fragrant tree in the days of summer,<br/>9. like frankincense upon the fire of the censer,<br/>like a vessel of massive gold,<br/>adorned with every kind of precious stone,</p>

<p class="v">10. like the olive tree putting forth its fruit,<br/>and like the cypress rising into the clouds.<br/><br/>11. When he had put on the robe of honor,<br/>and clothed himself with all his ornaments,<br/>and went up to the holy altar,<br/>he made the precincts of the sanctuary resplendent.<br/>12. But when he received the portions of the victims from the hands of the priests,<br/>and stood near the hearth of the altar,<br/>his brethren forming a crown around him,<br/>then he appeared like a majestic cedar on Lebanon,<br/>and the priests surrounded him like trunks of palm trees.<br/>13. All the sons of Aaron were clothed in their magnificent ornaments,<br/>and they held in their hands the offering for the Lord,<br/>before the whole assembly of Israel.<br/><br/>14. And when he had finished the service at the altars,<br/>to adorn the offering of the almighty Most High,<br/><br/>he stretched out his hand over the cup of libations,<br/>and poured out the blood of the grape.<br/>15. He poured it upon the base of the altar,<br/>a pleasing odor to the Most High, the great King.<br/>16. Then the sons of Aaron raised shouts,<br/>they sounded their trumpets of beaten metal,<br/>and made a great clamor resound,<br/>as a memorial before the Most High.<br/>17. And all the people together hastened,<br/>and fell with their faces to the ground,<br/>to worship their Lord,<br/>the almighty God, the Most High.<br/>18. And the singers, raising their voices, praised him;<br/>the vast temple resounded with sweet harmonies.<br/>19. And the people entreated the Lord Most High,<br/>standing in prayer before the Merciful One,<br/>until the ceremony of the Lord was completed,<br/>and the priests had accomplished the sacred duties.<br/><br/>20. Then the high priest came down and raised his hand<br/>over the whole assembly of the children of Israel,<br/>to give with his lips the blessing of the Lord,<br/>and to glory in his name.<br/>21. And the people prostrated themselves again<br/>to receive the blessing from the Most High.</p>

<p class="v">22. And now, bless the Lord of the universe,<br/>who everywhere does great things,<br/>who has exalted our days from the beginning,<br/>and has dealt with us according to his mercy.</p>

<p class="v">23. May he give us joy of heart,<br/>and may peace be in our days<br/>in Israel as in the days of old!<br/>24. May his mercy remain with us forever,<br/>and may he deliver us when his day shall come!</p>

<p class="v">25. There are two nations that my soul detests,<br/>and the third is not even a nation:<br/>26. those who dwell on Mount Seir, the Philistines,<br/>and the foolish people who inhabit Shechem.</p>

<p class="v">27. I have set down in this book<br/>a teaching of understanding and knowledge,<br/>I, Jesus, son of Sirach, of Jerusalem,<br/>who have poured forth in streams the wisdom of my heart.<br/>28. Happy is he who devotes himself to these teachings!<br/>He who gathers them into his heart will become wise;<br/>29. for if he puts them into practice, he will triumph over all things,<br/>because the light of the Lord is his path.</p>

### Chapter 51 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. I will celebrate you, Lord, King;<br/>I will praise you, O God my Savior,<br/>I celebrate your name.<br/><br/>2. For you have been for me a protector and a help;<br/>you have saved my body from ruin,<br/>from the snare of the slanderous tongue,<br/>from the lips of those who practice falsehood;<br/>and, in the face of my adversaries,</p>

<p class="v">3. you were my support and you delivered me,<br/>according to the greatness of your mercy and of your name,<br/>from those who gnashed their teeth, ready to devour me;<br/>from the hand of those who sought my life,<br/>from all the tribulations that besieged me;<br/>4. from the suffocation of the fire that surrounded me,<br/>from the midst of a fire that I had not kindled;<br/>5. from the deep abyss of Sheol,<br/>from the impure tongue and the lying word spoken to the king,<br/>from the slander of an unjust tongue.<br/><br/>6. My soul drew near to death,<br/>and my life touched Sheol below.<br/>7. They surrounded me on every side,<br/>and there was no one to help me;<br/>I looked for the help of men, and there was none.<br/>8. Then I remembered your mercy, Lord,<br/>and your works in ancient times;<br/>I remembered that you saved those who hoped in you,<br/>and delivered them from the hands of the idolatrous nations.<br/><br/>9. And, prostrate on the ground, I sent up my prayer,<br/>and I implored you to save me from death.<br/>10. I called upon the Lord, father of my Lord,<br/>that he would not abandon me in the days of my distress,<br/>in the time of the proud, when there was no help:<br/>11. "I will praise your name without ceasing,<br/>and I will sing it in my thankfulness."<br/>And my prayer was heard,<br/>12. for you saved me from ruin,<br/>and delivered me in the time of misfortune.<br/>Therefore I will celebrate you and praise you,<br/>and I will bless the name of the Lord.</p>

<p class="v">13. While I was still young, before I had gone astray,<br/>I openly sought wisdom in my prayer.<br/>14. I asked for her before the temple,<br/>and I will seek her until the end.</p>

<p class="v">15. Seeing her flower, as at the sight of the ripening grape,<br/>my heart rejoiced in her.<br/>With her, my foot walked in the right path;<br/>from my youth I followed her track.<br/>16. I lent her my ear for a little while and I received her,<br/>and I found for myself great instruction.<br/><br/>17. Through her I drew great profit:<br/>to him who gave me wisdom I will render glory!<br/>18. For I resolved to put her into practice,<br/>I applied myself to what is good, and I shall not be put to shame.<br/>19. For her my soul strove,<br/>and I gave great care to my actions.<br/>I lifted up my hands on high,<br/>and I lamented having ignored her.<br/>20. Toward her I directed my soul,<br/>and, in purity of life, I found her.<br/>With her, from the beginning, I acquired understanding;<br/>therefore I shall never be forsaken.<br/>21. My inmost being was stirred in seeking her;<br/>thus I have acquired a precious possession.<br/>22. The Lord gave me as a reward the gift of speech,<br/>and I will use it to praise him.<br/><br/>23. Draw near to me, you who are ignorant,<br/>and take up your dwelling in the house of instruction,<br/>24. since you lack wisdom,<br/>and your souls thirst greatly.<br/>25. I open my mouth and I speak:<br/>Procure her without money;<br/>26. bend your neck under the yoke,<br/>and let your soul receive instruction;<br/>there is no need to go far to find her.<br/>27. See with your own eyes that I have labored little,<br/>and that I have found great rest.<br/>28. Take part in instruction at a great price of silver,<br/>and with her you will have acquired gold in abundance.<br/>29. May your soul rejoice in the mercy of the Lord,<br/>and do not be ashamed of his praise.<br/>30. Do your work before the time,<br/>and, in due time, he will give you your reward.</p>

## Baruch {: .book}

<p class="chap-sub">Jeremiah's secretary speaks to the exiles: confession, wisdom, the consolation of Jerusalem. Chapter 6 is the Letter of Jeremiah against idols.</p>

### Chapter 1 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. These are the words of the book that Baruch wrote, son of Neriah, son of Maasias, son of Zedekiah, son of Sedei, son of Hilkiah, at Babylon, 2. in the fifth year, on the seventh day of the month, at the time when the Chaldeans had taken Jerusalem and burned it. 3. Baruch read the words of this book in the hearing of Jechonias, son of Joakim, king of Judah, and in the hearing of all the people who had come to hear this book, 4. in the hearing of the nobles and the sons of the kings, and in the hearing of the elders, and in the hearing of all the people, from the least to the greatest, of all those who dwelt at Babylon, by the river Sodi. 5. Hearing it, they wept, fasted, and prayed to the Lord. 6. And they collected money, as each could give according to his means. 7. And they sent it to Jerusalem, to Joakim, son of Hilkiah, son of Salom, the priest, to the other priests, and to all the people who were with him at Jerusalem. 8. Baruch had then recovered the vessels of the house of the Lord that had been carried off from the Temple, to send them back to the land of Judah, on the tenth day of the month of Sivan — vessels of silver that Zedekiah, son of Josiah, king of Judah, had had made — 9. after Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had carried off from Jerusalem Jechonias, the princes, the hostages, the nobles, and the people of the land, and had led them away to Babylon. 10. They said: "Behold, we are sending you money; with this money buy victims for the burnt offerings and the sin offerings, and incense; make oblations also, and offer them upon the altar of the Lord our God. 11. Pray for the life of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and for the life of Baltasar, his son, that their days upon the earth may be as the days of heaven; 12. and the Lord will give us strength; he will make light shine in our eyes; we shall live under the shadow of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and under the shadow of Baltasar, his son; we shall serve them for many days and find favor before them. 13. Pray also for us to the Lord our God, because we have sinned against the Lord our God, and the anger of the Lord and his wrath have not turned away from us to this day. 14. Read this book that we are sending you, so that it may be read publicly in the house of the Lord, on the feast days and the days of assembly.</p>

<p class="v">15. And you shall say:</p>

<p class="v">To the Lord our God belongs righteousness,<br/>but to us the shame of face,<br/>as is seen this day,<br/>to the men of Judah<br/>and the inhabitants of Jerusalem,<br/>16. to our kings and our princes,<br/>to our priests and our prophets,<br/>and to our fathers.<br/>17. We have sinned before the Lord<br/>18. and we have disobeyed him.<br/>We have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God,<br/>in following the commandments of the Lord,<br/>which he set before us.<br/><br/>19. From the day the Lord brought our fathers<br/>out of the land of Egypt, until this day,<br/>we have been unruly toward the Lord our God,<br/>and, in our folly, we have turned away,<br/>so as not to hear his voice.<br/>20. Therefore, as is seen this day,<br/>great misfortunes have clung to us,<br/>together with the curse that the Lord pronounced<br/>through Moses his servant,<br/>who brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt,<br/>to give us a land flowing with milk and honey.<br/><br/>21. We have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God,<br/>according to all the words of the prophets<br/>whom he sent to us.<br/>22. And we went, each according to the inclination of his wicked heart,<br/>to serve foreign gods,<br/>to do evil in the eyes of the Lord our God.</p>

### Chapter 2 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Therefore the Lord our God has fulfilled his word,<br/>which he spoke against us,<br/>against our judges who judged Israel,<br/>against our kings, against our rulers,<br/>and against all the men of Israel and Judah,<br/>2. threatening to bring upon us great calamities,<br/>such as have not existed under all of heaven<br/>as have existed at Jerusalem,<br/>according to what is written in the law of Moses,<br/>3. namely, that we would eat, each one, the flesh of his son,<br/>and each one the flesh of his daughter.<br/>4. And he gave them into the hand of all the kings around us,<br/>to be an object of reproach and astonishment,<br/>to all the peoples<br/>among whom the Lord has scattered us.<br/>5. And we have been made subject instead of ruling,<br/>because we have sinned against the Lord our God,<br/>by not obeying his voice.</p>

<p class="v">6. To the Lord our God belongs righteousness,<br/>to us and to our fathers the shame of face,<br/>as is seen this day.<br/>7. All these evils of which the Lord had spoken concerning us<br/>have come upon us.<br/>8. And we have not entreated the face of the Lord,<br/>that each of us might turn back<br/>from the thoughts of his wicked heart.<br/>9. So the Lord watched over the evil,<br/>and the Lord brought it upon us;<br/>for the Lord is righteous in all the works<br/>that he commanded us.<br/>10. And we have not listened to his voice,<br/>by observing the precepts of the Lord,<br/>which he set before us.</p>

<p class="v">11. And now, Lord, God of Israel,<br/>who brought your people out of the land of Egypt<br/>with a strong hand, with signs and wonders,<br/>with great power and an uplifted arm,<br/>and made yourself a name, as is seen this day,<br/>12. we have sinned, we have done impious deeds,<br/>we have committed iniquity, Lord our God,<br/>regarding all your precepts.<br/>13. May your anger turn away from us,<br/>since we are no more than a feeble remnant among the nations<br/>where you have scattered us!<br/><br/>14. Hear, Lord, our prayer and our supplication;<br/>deliver us for your own sake,<br/>and grant us favor before those who have deported us:<br/>15. so that all the earth may know that you are the Lord our God,<br/>since your name has been invoked upon Israel and upon his race.<br/>16. Look down, Lord, from your holy dwelling, think of us,<br/>incline your ear and listen,<br/>17. open your eyes and consider:<br/>it is not the dead in Sheol,<br/>whose spirit has departed from their bodies,<br/>who render glory and justice to the Lord.<br/>18. But the living, grieved by the greatness of their afflictions,<br/>who walk bowed down and without strength,<br/>whose eyes are dim,<br/>whose soul is hungry,<br/>it is he who renders you glory and justice, Lord.<br/><br/>19. For it is not because of the righteousness of our fathers and our kings<br/>that we pour out our prayer before you, Lord our God.<br/>20. For you have sent upon us your anger and your indignation,<br/>as you had proclaimed through your servants the prophets,</p>

<p class="v">21. saying: Thus says the Lord:<br/>"Bend your shoulders and your neck<br/>and serve the king of Babylon,<br/>and you shall dwell in the land<br/>that I gave to your fathers.<br/>22. But if you do not listen to the voice of the Lord your God,<br/>by serving the king of Babylon,<br/>23. I will cause to cease, in the cities of Judah<br/>and outside Jerusalem,<br/>the voice of joy and the voice of gladness,<br/>the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride,<br/>and all the land shall become a desert, without inhabitants."<br/><br/>24. We did not listen to your voice,<br/>by serving the king of Babylon,<br/>and you have fulfilled your words,<br/>spoken through your servants the prophets,<br/>declaring that the bones of our kings<br/>and the bones of our fathers<br/>would be removed from their tombs.<br/>25. And behold, they have indeed been cast out on the ground,<br/>exposed to the heat of the sun and the cold of the night;<br/>and our fathers died in cruel sufferings,<br/>by famine, by the sword, and by pestilence.<br/>26. You have reduced the house upon which your name was invoked<br/>to the state in which it is today,<br/>because of the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Judah.<br/><br/>27. You have dealt with us, Lord our God,<br/>according to all your goodness,<br/>and according to all your great mercy,<br/>28. as you had declared through your servant Moses,<br/>on the day you commanded him to write your law,<br/>in the presence of the children of Israel,<br/>29. saying: "If you do not listen to my voice,<br/>this great and vast multitude<br/>will be reduced to a very small number,<br/>among the nations where I will scatter them.<br/>30. For I know well that they will not listen to me,<br/>because they are a stiff-necked people;<br/>but they will come to themselves<br/>in the land of their exile;<br/>31. and they will know that I am the Lord their God,<br/>and I will give them a heart that understands,<br/>and ears that hear.<br/>32. And they will praise me in the land of their exile,<br/>and they will remember my name.<br/>33. They will give up their stiff neck,<br/>and their perverse maxims,<br/>because they will remember the fate of their fathers,<br/>who sinned before the Lord.<br/>34. And I will bring them back into the land<br/>that I promised by oath to their fathers,<br/>to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob,<br/>and they will be masters of it,<br/>and I will multiply them, and they will not diminish.</p>

<p class="v">35. I will make with them an everlasting covenant,<br/>that I may be their God,<br/>and that they may be my people;<br/>and I will no longer drive out my people Israel<br/>from the land that I have given them.</p>

### Chapter 3 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Almighty Lord, God of Israel,<br/>a soul in anguish and a troubled spirit cries out to you.<br/>2. Hear, Lord, and have pity,<br/>because we have sinned before you;<br/>3. for you sit upon an eternal throne,<br/>and we perish without return.<br/>4. Almighty Lord, God of Israel,<br/>hear the prayer of the dead of Israel,<br/>and of the children of those who sinned before you,<br/>who did not listen to the voice of their God,<br/>and are the cause that these misfortunes have clung to us.<br/>5. Remember no longer the iniquities of our fathers,<br/>but remember, at this hour, your power and your name.<br/>6. For you are the Lord our God,<br/>and we will praise you, Lord.<br/>7. It is for this that you have put your fear into our hearts,<br/>that we might call upon your name;<br/>and we will praise you in our exile;<br/>for we have cast out from our hearts the iniquity of our fathers,<br/>who sinned before you.<br/>8. Behold, we are today in the land of our exile,<br/>where you have scattered us for reproach,<br/>for a curse and an expiation,<br/>according to all the iniquities of our fathers,<br/>who turned away from the Lord our God.</p>

<p class="v">9. Hear, Israel, the commandments of life;<br/>lend your ear to learn prudence.<br/>10. How is it, Israel, how is it that you are in the land of your enemies,<br/>that you languish in a foreign land,<br/>that you defile yourself with the dead,<br/>11. and that you are counted among those who have gone down to Sheol?</p>

<p class="v">12. You have abandoned the fountain of wisdom.<br/>13. For if you had walked in the way of God,<br/>you would dwell forever in peace.<br/>14. Learn where prudence is,<br/>where strength is, where understanding is,<br/>that you may know at the same time<br/>where length of days and life are,<br/>where the light of the eyes and peace are.<br/><br/>15. Who has found the place of wisdom,<br/>and who has entered into her treasures?<br/>16. Where are the leaders of the nations,<br/>and those who tame the beasts of the earth,<br/>17. who make sport of the birds of the sky,<br/>18. who hoard silver and gold,<br/>in which men put their trust,<br/>and whose possessions have no end?<br/><br/>For these men who hoard silver and make it their concern,<br/>no trace of their works would be found.<br/>19. They have vanished and gone down to Sheol,<br/>and others have risen in their place.<br/>20. Young men have seen the light,<br/>and have dwelt upon the earth;<br/>but they have not known the way of wisdom;<br/>21. they have not known her paths;<br/>their children too have not grasped her; they were far from her way!<br/><br/>22. She has not been heard of in the land of Canaan,<br/>nor has she been seen in Teman.<br/>23. And the sons of Hagar who seek the prudence that is of the earth;<br/>the merchants of Merrah and of Teman,<br/>the tellers of parables and the seekers of prudence,<br/>have not known the way of wisdom,<br/>and have not remembered her paths.<br/><br/>24. O Israel, how great is the house of God,<br/>how vast is the place of his domain!<br/>25. It is vast and has no bounds,<br/>it is high and immense.<br/><br/>26. There from the beginning dwelt the renowned giants,<br/>of great stature and skilled in war.<br/>27. It was not they whom God chose,<br/>and he did not teach them the way of wisdom.<br/>28. And they perished because they did not have true knowledge,<br/>they perished because of their folly.<br/><br/>29. Who has gone up into heaven and grasped wisdom,<br/>and brought her down from the clouds?<br/>30. Who has crossed the sea, and, having found her,<br/>brought her back for the price of the purest gold?<br/>31. There is no one who knows her ways,<br/>nor who observes her paths.</p>

<p class="v">32. But he who knows all things knows her;<br/>he discovers her by his understanding,<br/>he who has established the earth forever,<br/>and filled it with four-footed animals,<br/>33. who sends forth the light, and it goes,<br/>who calls it, and it obeys him, trembling.<br/>34. The stars shine at their posts,<br/>and they are glad;<br/><br/>35. he calls them, and they say: "Here we are!"<br/>and they shine joyfully for him who created them.<br/><br/>36. It is he who is our God,<br/>and no other can be compared to him.<br/>37. He found every way of wisdom,<br/>and gave her to Jacob his servant,<br/>and to Israel his beloved.<br/>38. After this he appeared on the earth,<br/>and conversed among men.</p>

### Chapter 4 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Wisdom is the book of the commandments of God,<br/>and the law that endures forever;<br/>all who hold fast to her will come to life,<br/>but those who forsake her will go to death.<br/><br/>2. Return, O Jacob, and embrace her;<br/>walk toward the splendor of her light.<br/>3. Do not give your glory to another,<br/>nor your advantages to a foreign nation.<br/>4. Happy are we, O Israel,<br/>for what is pleasing to God has been revealed to us!</p>

<p class="v">5. Take courage, O my people,<br/>memorial of Israel!<br/>6. You were sold to the nations,<br/>not for ruin;<br/>but because you provoked the anger of God,<br/>you were delivered to your oppressors.<br/>7. For you angered him who made you,<br/>by offering sacrifices to demons, and not to God.<br/>8. You have forgotten him who nourished you,<br/>the eternal God, and you have grieved her who raised you, Jerusalem.<br/>9. For she saw the anger of God falling upon you, and she said:<br/><br/>Listen, neighbors of Zion,<br/>for God has sent me great mourning.<br/>10. I have seen the captivity of my sons and my daughters,<br/>which the LORD brought upon them.<br/>11. I had nourished them in joy,<br/>and I let them go in tears and mourning.</p>

<p class="v">12. Let no one rejoice at seeing me a widow, forsaken by many!<br/>I am left desolate because of the sins of my children,<br/>because they turned away from the law of God,<br/>13. because they disregarded his commandments,<br/>because they did not walk in the way of the precepts of God,<br/>and did not follow the paths of discipline, according to his justice.<br/><br/>14. Let them come, the neighbors of Zion!<br/>Remember the captivity of my sons and my daughters,<br/>which the LORD brought upon them.<br/>15. For he brought against them a distant nation,<br/>a cruel nation, of a barbarous tongue,<br/>16. which had neither respect for the aged,<br/>nor compassion for the child,<br/>which carried off the beloved ones of the widow,<br/>and left me alone, bereft of my daughters.<br/><br/>17. And how could I help you?<br/>18. He who brought these evils upon you,<br/>it is he who will draw you out of the hand of your enemies.<br/>19. Go, my sons, go;<br/>as for me, I remain alone!<br/>20. I have put off the robe of happy days;<br/>I have put on the sackcloth of my supplication;<br/>I will cry to the Most High all the days of my life.<br/>21. Take courage, my sons; cry to the Lord,<br/>and he will snatch you from the power,<br/>from the hands of your enemies.<br/><br/>22. I await your deliverance from the LORD,<br/>and joy comes to me, from the Holy One, for the mercy<br/>that will soon come to you from the LORD, your Savior.<br/>23. I let you go in tears and mourning;<br/>but God will bring you back to me in joy<br/>and gladness, forever.<br/>24. As the neighbors of Zion have seen your captivity,<br/>so shall they soon see your deliverance from God,<br/>which will come to you with great glory<br/>and great splendor from the LORD.<br/><br/>25. My sons, bear with patience the wrath of God that has come upon you; your enemy has persecuted you;<br/>but soon you will see his ruin,<br/>and set your foot upon his neck.<br/>26. My most delicate sons have walked by rough roads;<br/>they have been carried off like a flock stolen by the enemy.<br/>27. Take courage, my sons, and cry to the Lord:<br/>for he who brought these evils upon you will remember you.<br/>28. For, as your thought was to turn away from God,<br/>having returned to him, you will put tenfold more zeal into seeking him.<br/>29. For he who brought misfortune upon you<br/>will bring you, by saving you, an everlasting joy.</p>

<p class="v">30. Take courage, Jerusalem;<br/>he who gave you his name will console you.</p>

<p class="v">31. Wretched are those who mistreated you,<br/>and rejoiced at your fall!<br/>32. Wretched are the cities where your children were slaves!<br/>Wretched is she who received them!<br/>33. Just as she rejoiced at your ruin<br/>and triumphed at your fall,<br/>so shall she grieve at her own devastation.<br/>34. I will take from her the joy caused by her many inhabitants,<br/>and her boasting shall be turned into mourning.<br/>35. A fire shall come upon her from the LORD,<br/>for many days,<br/>and she shall long be the dwelling of evil spirits.<br/><br/>36. Look toward the East, O Jerusalem,<br/>and see the joy that comes to you from God.<br/>37. For behold, they are returning, your sons whom you saw depart;<br/>they come gathered from the East to the West at the voice of the Holy One,<br/>rejoicing in the glory of God.</p>

### Chapter 5 {: .chap}

<p class="v">1. Take off, Jerusalem, the robe of your mourning and your affliction,<br/>and put on the ornaments of the glory that comes to you from God forever;<br/>2. wrap yourself in the mantle of righteousness that comes to you from God;<br/>set upon your head the miter of the glory of the LORD.<br/><br/>3. For God will display your splendor<br/>to every land that is under heaven.<br/>4. Your name shall be spoken by God forever:<br/>"Peace-of-Righteousness" and "Splendor-of-Piety."<br/>5. Arise, Jerusalem, stand upon your height,<br/>and look toward the East;<br/>and see your children gathered from the west to the east,<br/>at the word of the Holy One,<br/>rejoicing that God has remembered them.<br/><br/>6. They had left you on foot, led away by the enemies;<br/>God brings them back to you carried in honor,<br/>like a royal throne.<br/>7. For God has commanded every high mountain<br/>and the everlasting rocks to be brought low,<br/>and the valleys to be filled up to level the ground,<br/>so that Israel may walk in safety,<br/>for the glory of God.<br/>8. The forests themselves, and every fragrant tree,<br/>have given their shade to Israel, at the command of God.<br/>9. For God will lead Israel with joy to the light of his glory,<br/>with mercy and righteousness that come from himself.</p>

### Chapter 6 {: .chap}

<p class="chap-sub">The Letter of Jeremiah</p>

<p class="v">A copy of the letter that Jeremiah sent to those who were about to be led captive to Babylon by the king of the Babylonians, to announce to them what God had commanded them to be told. 1. Because of the sins you have committed before God, you are about to be led captive to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians. 2. Having arrived at Babylon, you will remain there for many years and a long time, up to seven generations; and after that I will bring you out again in peace. 3. Now you will see at Babylon gods of silver, gold, and wood, which are carried upon shoulders and inspire fear in the nations. 4. Take care, then, not to imitate these foreigners yourselves, and not to let yourselves be seized by fear of these gods. 5. When you see a crowd pressing before and behind them, and paying them homage, say in your heart: "It is you, O Master, who must be worshiped." 6. For my angel is with you, and he takes care of your life.</p>

<p class="v">7. For the tongue of these gods has been polished by a craftsman; it is covered with gold and silver, but they are only falsehood, and cannot speak. 8. As for a girl who loves adornment, gold has been taken, and crowns have been prepared to set upon the heads of these gods. 9. The priests go so far as to steal from their gods gold and silver, which they put to their own uses; 10. they will even give some to prostitutes in their house. They deck these gods of silver, gold, and wood with rich garments, as if they were men; 11. but these gods cannot defend themselves from rust or from worms. 12. When they have been clothed in purple garments, their faces still have to be wiped, because of the dust of the house that covers them with a thick layer. 13. Here is one that holds a scepter, like a governor of a province: he will not put to death the one who has offended him. 14. That other one carries in his hand a sword or an axe, but he cannot defend himself against an enemy or against thieves. By this one sees clearly that these are not gods; 15. do not fear them, then.</p>

<p class="v">Like a vessel that a man owns, which, once broken, becomes useless: so it is with their gods. 16. If you place them in a house, their eyes fill with the dust from the feet of those who enter. 17. Just as the doors of a prison are carefully shut upon a man who has offended the king, or upon a man who is being led to death, so the priests guard the dwelling of their gods with solid doors, with locks and bolts, for fear they may be stripped by thieves. 18. They light lamps, even in greater number than for themselves, and these gods can see none of them. 19. They are like one of the beams of the house, and it is said that their hearts are gnawed by the vermin that comes out of the earth and devours them, along with their garments, without their feeling it. 20. Their faces become</p>

<p class="v">black from the smoke that rises from the house. 21. Upon their bodies and upon their heads flutter owls, swallows, and other birds; and likewise cats disport themselves there as well. 22. By this you shall know that these are not gods; do not fear them, then.</p>

<p class="v">23. As for the gold with which they are covered to embellish them, if no one removes the tarnish from it, they will not make it shine; for they felt nothing at all even when they were being cast. 24. These idols have been bought at the highest price, and there is no breath of life in them. 25. Having no feet, they are carried upon shoulders, thus showing men their shameful powerlessness. Let those who serve them be put to shame! 26. If they fall to the ground, they will not rise up by themselves; and if someone sets them upright, they will not move by themselves; and if they lean, they will not straighten themselves. It is as before the dead that offerings are set before them. 27. The priests sell the victims offered to them and make their profit from them; their wives salt them down, and give nothing either to the poor or to the infirm. 28. Women in childbirth or in an unclean state touch their sacrifices. Knowing then, by these things, that they are not gods, do not fear them.</p>

<p class="v">29. And why call them gods? For it is women who come to bring their offerings to these gods of silver, gold, and wood. 30. And, in their temples, the priests sit, their tunics torn, their heads and faces shaved, and their heads uncovered. 31. They roar, shouting before their gods, as at a funeral feast. 32. Their priests take their garments from them, and clothe their wives and children with them. 33. Whether one does them harm or does them good, they can render neither the one nor the other; they are incapable of setting up a king or of deposing him. 34. No more can they give wealth, nor even a single coin. If someone, having made a vow to them, fails to fulfill it, they do not claim it. 35. They will not save a man from death, they will not snatch the weak from the hand of the strong. 36. They will not restore sight to the blind, and will not deliver one who is in distress. 37. They will have no pity on the widow, and will do no good to the orphan. 38. They are like rocks broken off from the mountain, these idols of wood, covered with gold and silver, and those who serve them shall be put to shame. 39. How then can one believe or say that these are gods?</p>

<p class="v">40. The Chaldeans themselves dishonor them, when, seeing a man who cannot speak, they bring him before Bel, asking that the mute may speak, as though the god could hear anything. 41. And although they realize this, they cannot abandon these idols; for they have no feeling. 42.
